      "content":"# 309 — Build system & Makefile orchestration\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nPhase 2 has no compiled binary. The runner is a Lua script\n(`src/007-runner-main.lua`) invoked via `luajit`. Drivers are shell\nscripts that compile per-box C source on demand. There is no\ntop-level Makefile, no vendoring of C dependencies, no link step\nbeyond per-driver compile.\n\nPhase 3 introduces a real C binary (the pool runner) plus a set of\nlanguage spec `.so` files. They need to compile in the right order\nwith the right flags, and the build needs to be reproducible from a\nclean checkout.\n\n## Concept\n\nA top-level `Makefile` at the project root orchestrates the entire\nphase 3 build. It builds:\n\n1. The pool runner binary: `soramech-pool` (statically links the\n   SoraMech-owned task pool, the vendored JSON parser, the slot\n   store, the graph loader, the dispatch layer, the spec registry).\n2. Each language spec: `langs/<name>/spec.so`, built by a small\n   per-spec Makefile.\n3. (Optional) Unit test binaries.\n\nEach component has its own Makefile if it has non-trivial build\nrules. The top-level Makefile delegates to them via `$(MAKE) -C\n<dir>`. A clean checkout becomes a working build with `make`.\n\n## Directory layout\n\n```\nsoramech/\n├── Makefile                       ← top-level orchestration\n├── soramech-pool                  ← built binary (gitignored)\n├── src/\n│   ├── 008-pool-runner.c          ← main entry, pool lifecycle (issue 301)\n│   ├── slot-store.c / .h          ← per-task slot allocator (issue 302)\n│   ├── graph-loader.c / .h        ← C loader, replaces 003-loader.lua (issue 305)\n│   ├── dispatch.c / .h            ← dispatch action (issue 304)\n│   └── spec-registry.c / .h       ← spec dlopen/registry (issue 303)\n├── libs/\n│   ├── task-pool/                 ← SoraMech-built thread pool\n│   │   ├── pool.h\n│   │   └── pool.c\n│   └── json/                      ← vendored JSON parser (cJSON, jsmn, etc.)\n│       ├── cjson.h\n│       └── cjson.c\n├── langs/\n│   ├── lua/\n│   │   ├── Makefile               ← builds spec.so\n│   │   ├── spec.c\n│   │   └── spec.so                ← built (gitignored)\n│   ├── c/\n│   │   ├── Makefile\n│   │   ├── spec.c\n│   │   ├── soramech-c.h           ← user-facing helper header\n│   │   └── spec.so\n│   └── bash/\n│       ├── Makefile\n│       ├── spec.c\n│       ├── bash-server.sh\n│       └── spec.so\n└── build/                         ← intermediate object files (gitignored)\n```\n\n`build/` holds intermediate `.o` files; binaries land alongside their\nsources or at the project root. `.so` and `.o` files are gitignored;\n`make clean` removes them.\n\n## Top-level targets\n\n```make\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: soramech-pool\n\nsoramech-pool: $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t$(CC) -O2 -Wall -pthread -o $@ $^ -ldl\n\nspecs:\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/lua\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/c\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/bash\n\nclean:\n\trm -f soramech-pool\n\trm -rf build/\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/lua clean\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/c clean\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/bash clean\n\ntest: all\n\t./scripts/run-tests.sh\n```\n\n`POOL_OBJECTS` resolves to the `.o` files for every `src/*.c`,\n`libs/task-pool/*.c`, and `libs/json/*.c`. A pattern rule compiles\neach source into `build/`.\n\n## Per-language spec Makefiles\n\nEach `langs/<name>/Makefile` follows the same shape. Lua's:\n\n```make\nLUA_INCLUDE ?= /usr/include/luajit-2.1\nLUA_LIB    ?= /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu\n\nCFLAGS  = -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -I$(LUA_INCLUDE)\nLDFLAGS = -L$(LUA_LIB) -lluajit-5.1\n\nspec.so: spec.c\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $< $(LDFLAGS)\n\nclean:\n\trm -f spec.so\n```\n\nC's spec links `-ldl`. Bash's links nothing beyond libc. The pattern\nis uniform.\n\nLuaJIT's include and lib paths are set via environment variables so\nthe build works on systems where they live elsewhere (macOS via\nhomebrew, Alpine, etc.). Defaults match Debian/Ubuntu.\n\n## Build modes\n\n```\nmake                  ← release: -O2 -Wall\nmake DEBUG=1          ← debug:   -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -Wextra\nmake STRICT=1         ← strict:  release + -Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic\n```\n\n`DEBUG=1` adds `-g` for symbols and `-DDEBUG` for opt-in debug\nprints in the C sources. `STRICT=1` fails the build on any warning;\nuseful in CI.\n\n## Vendoring\n\nVendored libraries live under `libs/` and are checked into the repo\nas plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time. To\nupdate a vendored library, copy the new sources in and commit. The\nvendored directory carries a small `VENDOR.md` noting the upstream\nsource and the version that was copied.\n\nInitial vendored libraries:\n- `libs/task-pool/` — SoraMech-built thread pool (issue 301)\n- `libs/json/` — JSON parser (issue 305 picks cJSON or similar)\n\nFuture additions land alongside these.\n\n## Spec discovery at runtime\n\nThe pool runner finds language specs by scanning the `langs/`\ndirectory at startup, opening each `langs/<name>/spec.so` via\n`dlopen`, and reading the `soramech_lang_spec` symbol via `dlsym`\n(per issue 303). The path to `langs/` is resolved relative to the\nrunner binary's location: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`\n(Linux), follows the symlink, and looks for `langs/` next to it.\n\nThis means the binary is location-flexible: the user can drop the\nproject tree anywhere, and `./soramech-pool` finds its specs\nwithout a config file.\n\nIf the user wants to override (custom spec dirs for development),\n`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs ./soramech-pool` overrides the\nauto-detected location.\n\n## Compile and package a map for standalone execution\n\nFolded in from issue 219 (closed). The build system also handles the\n\"package a map for deployment\" step that the editor's Compile button\n(issue 222) and a CLI tool both invoke.\n\nThe compile step turns an editable map directory into a self-contained\ndeployable directory:\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/compiled/\n    pool-runner          ← copy (or symlink) of soramech-pool\n    src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n    bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n    langs/               ← copy of language spec .so files used\n    manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version\n```\n\nRunning `./compiled/pool-runner` executes the map without reference to\nthe editor, the live `src/` outside `compiled/`, or any external\nSoraMech installation.\n\n### Steps the compile step performs\n\n1. **Walk the graph.** Reuse the C loader (issue 305) to enumerate\n   boxes, languages, and source files.\n2. **Copy source.** Every file referenced by `box.ref` plus\n   transitively-required libs lands in `compiled/src/`. The map's\n   local `src/` is the only path `package.path` searches at runtime\n   (issue 306), so all dependencies must be present.\n3. **Compile per-box artifacts.** For each language present, invoke\n   that spec's `compile` callback (issue 303). The C spec emits a\n   wrapper from the box's signature into `compiled/bin/` (issue 307).\n   Lua and Bash have no compile step; their files are copied verbatim.\n4. **Copy spec libraries.** `langs/<name>/spec.so` for every language\n   used in the map is copied to `compiled/langs/<name>/spec.so`. The\n   pool runner's spec discovery (above) finds them relative to the\n   binary location.\n5. **Copy or symlink the runner binary.** `--portable` copies; the\n   default symlinks to save disk on the dev machine.\n6. **Write the manifest.** `compiled/manifest.json` lists every box,\n   its language, its compiled artifact path (or source file for\n   interpreted languages), and the SoraMech build version.\n\n### Incremental compile\n\nmtime comparison per artifact: if the source is newer than the\ncompiled output, recompile that one; otherwise skip. The C spec's\n`compile` callback (issue 307) implements this per-box; the package\nstep inherits it.\n\n### Editor invocation (issue 222)\n\nThe Compile button calls `POST /maps/<name>/compile`. The server\nshells out to a `soramech-compile` CLI (or invokes the same code\nin-process). Output streams back to the editor for display. The\neditor itself never runs the compiled output; the user invokes\n`./compiled/pool-runner` from a terminal.\n\n### CLI invocation\n\nStandalone `soramech-compile <map-dir>` runs the same pipeline\nwithout the server. Used in CI and headless deployment.\n\n### Errors\n\nAny failure aborts the compile and surfaces a precise message:\nwhich box, which file, what failed. Partial output is left in\n`compiled/` for inspection but the manifest is not written, so the\ndeployment is recognizably broken until a clean compile succeeds.\n\n### Open questions (compile step)\n\n- **Multi-architecture**: a directory built on x86_64 won't run on\n  arm64. Out of scope — users compile on the target. Could later\n  add cross-compile if the SoraMind cluster goes mixed-arch.\n- **Source-copy granularity**: copy the file referenced by `box.ref`\n  plus a static-analysis sweep for `require` / `source` /\n  `#include`, or just copy the entire `libs/` tree. Lean toward\n  static analysis with a fallback whole-tree copy if analysis fails.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- macOS: `.so` becomes `.dylib`, and there's no `/proc/self/exe`.\n  Use `_NSGetExecutablePath`. Cross-platform spec discovery is a\n  small platform-#ifdef. Fold into the spec registry implementation.\n- Out-of-tree build (a separate `build/` directory holding all\n  artifacts): nice-to-have, not blocking. Current layout uses\n  in-tree `.o` files in `build/` already — full out-of-tree means\n  the `.so`s live in `build/langs/lua/spec.so` instead of next to\n  the source. Defer.\n- Static vs dynamic linking of vendored libs: vendored sources\n  compile straight into the runner binary. No separate `.so` for\n  the task pool or JSON parser. Right call given how small they are.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Write the top-level Makefile with empty `runner`, `specs`,\n   `clean` targets. Verify `make` succeeds against an empty source\n   tree.\n2. Build the SoraMech thread pool into `libs/task-pool/` (3d-rts\n   referenced as design inspiration). Add a\n   `VENDOR.md`.\n3. Vendor cJSON (or chosen JSON parser) into `libs/json/`. Add a\n   `VENDOR.md`.\n4. Add the pool-runner build rule. Compiles `src/*.c` plus vendored\n   libs into `soramech-pool`. Initially the runner is just `int\n   main() { return 0; }` to verify the link.\n5. Add `langs/lua/Makefile`. Build `spec.so` from a stub `spec.c`.\n6. Add `langs/c/Makefile`. Same shape.\n7. Add `langs/bash/Makefile`. Same shape.\n8. Add `make DEBUG=1` and `make STRICT=1` modes.\n9. Wire `make test` into a placeholder script (real tests come from\n   issue 311).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `Makefile` — top-level (to be created)\n- `langs/lua/Makefile`, `langs/c/Makefile`, `langs/bash/Makefile`\n  — per-spec (to be created)\n- `libs/task-pool/`, `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be added)\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool runner this\n  builds\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec discovery uses\n  `dlopen`/`dlsym`\n- `issues/306-lua-language-spec.md`, `307-c-language-spec.md`,\n  `308-bash-language-spec.md` — per-spec build details\n- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — `make test`\n  consumers\n- `issues/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` (completed) —\n  the editor button this compile step services\n- `issues/completed/219-map-compiler.md` — original issue, folded\n  into this one\n",
      "startLine":1,

The path to `langs/` is resolved relative to the\n164\trunner binary's location: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`\n165\t(Linux), follows the symlink, and looks for `langs/` next to it.\n166\t\n167\tThis means the binary is location-flexible: the user can drop the\n168\tproject tree anywhere, and `./soramech-pool` finds its specs\n169\twithout a config file.\n170\t\n171\tIf the user wants to override (custom spec dirs for development),\n172\t`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs ./soramech-pool` overrides the\n173\tauto-detected location.\n174\t\n175\t## Compile and package a map for standalone execution\n176\t\n177\tFolded in from issue 219 (closed). The build system also handles the\n178\t\"package a map for deployment\" step that the editor's Compile button\n179\t(issue 222) and a CLI tool both invoke.\n180\t\n181\tThe compile step turns an editable map directory into a self-contained\n182\tdeployable directory:\n183\t\n184\t```\n185\tmaps/<name>/compiled/\n186\t    pool-runner          ← copy (or symlink) of soramech-pool\n187\t    src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n188\t    bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n189\t    langs/               ← copy of language spec .so files used\n190\t    manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version\n191\t```\n192\t\n193\tRunning `./compiled/pool-runner` executes the map without reference to\n194\tthe editor, the live `src/` outside `compiled/`, or any external\n195\tSoraMech installation.\n196\t\n197\t### Steps the compile step performs\n198\t\n199\t1. **Walk the graph.** Reuse the C loader (issue 305) to enumerate\n200\t   boxes, languages, and source files.\n201\t2. **Copy source.** Every file referenced by `box.ref` plus\n202\t   transitively-required libs lands in `compiled/src/`. The map's\n203\t   local `src/` is the only path `package.path` searches at runtime\n204\t   (issue 306), so all dependencies must be present.\n205\t3. **Compile per-box artifacts.** For each language present, invoke\n206\t   that spec's `compile` callback (issue 303). The C spec emits a\n207\t   wrapper from the box's signature into `compiled/bin/` (issue 307).\n208\t   Lua and Bash have no compile step; their files are copied verbatim.\n209\t4. **Copy spec libraries.** `langs/<name>/spec.so` for every language\n210\t   used in the map is copied to `compiled/langs/<name>/spec.so`. The\n211\t   pool runner's spec discovery (above) finds them relative to the\n212\t   binary location.\n213\t5. **Copy or symlink the runner binary.** `--portable` copies; the\n214\t   default symlinks to save disk on the dev machine.\n215\t6. **Write the manifest.** `compiled/manifest.json` lists every box,\n216\t   its language, its compiled artifact path (or source file for\n217\t   interpreted languages), and the SoraMech build version.\n218\t\n219\t### Incremental compile\n220\t\n221\tmtime comparison per artifact: if the source is newer than the\n222\tcompiled output, recompile that one; otherwise skip. The C spec's\n223\t`compile` callback (issue 307) implements this per-box; the package\n224\tstep inherits it.\n225\t\n226\t### Editor invocation (issue 222)\n227\t\n228\tThe Compile button calls `POST /maps/<name>/compile`. The server\n229\tshells out to a `soramech-compile` CLI (or invokes the same code\n230\tin-process). Output streams back to the editor for display. The\n231\teditor itself never runs the compiled output; the user invokes\n232\t`./compiled/pool-runner` from a terminal.\n233\t\n234\t### CLI invocation\n235\t\n236\tStandalone `soramech-compile <map-dir>` runs the same pipeline\n237\twithout the server. Used in CI and headless deployment.\n238\t\n239\t### Errors\n240\t\n241\tAny failure aborts the compile and surfaces a precise message:\n242\twhich box, which file, what failed. Partial output is left in\n243\t`compiled/` for inspection but the manifest is not written, so the\n244\tdeployment is recognizably broken until a clean compile succeeds.\n245\t\n246\t### Open questions (compile step)\n247\t\n248\t- **Multi-architecture**: a directory built on x86_64 won't run on\n249\t  arm64. Out of scope — users compile on the target. Could later\n250\t  add cross-compile if the SoraMind cluster goes mixed-arch.\n251\t- **Source-copy granularity**: copy the file referenced by `box.ref`\n252\t  plus a static-analysis sweep for `require` / `source` /\n253\t  `#include`, or just copy the entire `libs/` tree. Lean toward\n254\t  static analysis with a fallback whole-tree copy if analysis fails.\n255\t\n256\t## Open questions\n257\t\n258\t- macOS: `.so` becomes `.dylib`, and there's no `/proc/self/exe`.\n259\t  Use `_NSGetExecutablePath`. Cross-platform spec discovery is a\n260\t  small platform-#ifdef. Fold into the spec registry implementation.\n261\t- Out-of-tree build (a separate `build/` directory holding all\n262\t  artifacts): nice-to-have, not blocking. Current layout uses\n263\t  in-tree `.o` files in `build/` already — full out-of-tree means\n264\t  the `.so`s live in `build/langs/lua/spec.so` instead of next to\n265\t  the source. Defer.\n266\t- Static vs dynamic linking of vendored libs: vendored sources\n267\t  compile straight into the runner binary. No separate `.so` for\n268\t  the task pool or JSON parser. Right call given how small they are.\n269\t\n270\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n271\t\n272\t1. Write the top-level Makefile with empty `runner`, `specs`,\n273\t   `clean` targets. Verify `make` succeeds against an empty source\n274\t   tree.\n275\t2. Build the SoraMech thread pool into `libs/task-pool/` (3d-rts\n276\t   referenced as design inspiration). Add a\n277\t   `VENDOR.md`.\n278\t3. Vendor cJSON (or chosen JSON parser) into `libs/json/`. Add a\n279\t   `VENDOR.md`.\n280\t4. Add the pool-runner build rule. Compiles `src/*.c` plus vendored\n281\t   libs into `soramech-pool`. Initially the runner is just `int\n282\t   main() { return 0; }` to verify the link.\n283\t5. Add `langs/lua/Makefile`. Build `spec.so` from a stub `spec.c`.\n284\t6. Add `langs/c/Makefile`. Same shape.\n285\t7. Add `langs/bash/Makefile`. Same shape.\n286\t8. Add `make DEBUG=1` and `make STRICT=1` modes.\n287\t9. Wire `make test` into a placeholder script (real tests come from\n288\t   issue 311).\n289\t\n290\t## Relevant files\n291\t\n292\t- `Makefile` — top-level (to be created)\n293\t- `langs/lua/Makefile`, `langs/c/Makefile`, `langs/bash/Makefile`\n294\t  — per-spec (to be created)\n295\t- `libs/task-pool/`, `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be added)\n296\t- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool runner this\n297\t  builds\n298\t- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec discovery uses\n299\t  `dlopen`/`dlsym`\n300\t- `issues/306-lua-language-spec.md`, `307-c-language-spec.md`,\n301\t  `308-bash-language-spec.md` — per-spec build details\n302\t- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — `make test`\n303\t  consumers\n304\t- `issues/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` (completed) —\n305\t  the editor button this compile step services\n306\t- `issues/completed/219-map-compiler.md` — original issue, folded\n307\t  into this one\n308\t"

      "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        -- iterator boxes (issue 221) are a pure routing primitive: input\n        -- copies straight to a chosen output, no language function is\n        -- invoked. Such a box has no ref/fn — only `iterator_outputs`,\n        -- an ordered list of output slot names. Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01W5Z5fG3fNm4fz6XLL6RBEp",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk\nformat: the map directory. None of the three knows about the others\nat runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (assets/index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  src/006-server-main.lua       [map directory]\n                                maps/<name>/\n                                  meta.json\n                                  boxes/\n                                  data/\n                                  src/\n                                  compiled/   (after compile button)\n                                  tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  Runner (one of):\n    src/007-runner-main.lua     ← phase 2, synchronous Lua interpreter\n    soramech-pool (binary)      ← phase 3, C thread pool runner\n```\n\n### src/006-server-main.lua (the editor's HTTP backend)\n\nThin file CRUD proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and\ntranslates them into reads and writes on the map directory. No logic\nbeyond path validation and basic consistency checks (e.g. reject a\ndelete if the box is still referenced by another box's connection\nlist).\n\nStarted with: `luajit src/006-server-main.lua [port]` (default 7700).\nThe `run` script at the project root starts the server and opens the\neditor.\n\nThe editor is editor-only — no run button, no run results display.\nThe runner is invoked separately, by command line. `last-run.jsonl`\nis the runner's output, consumed by external tooling, not by the\neditor.\n\n### Phase 2 runner — `src/007-runner-main.lua`\n\nSynchronous Lua interpreter. Loads a map directory, validates the\ngraph, walks boxes in dependency order, invokes language drivers per\nbox (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/c.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`). Each box\ninvocation is wrapped in a `task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` boundary that\nmatches the phase 3 thread pool's action signature.\n\nThis is the development target while the editor is being built out.\nPhase 2 retires wholesale when phase 3 lands; the editor and the\nmap-directory format are unchanged across the cutover.\n\n### Phase 3 runner — `soramech-pool` (`src/008-pool-runner.c`)\n\nThe phase 3 runner is a single C binary. It owns:\n\n- A **SoraMech-built thread pool** under `libs/task-pool/` (3d-rts at\n  `/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h`\n  is the design reference, not vendored).\n- A **C graph loader** (`src/graph-loader.c`) — replaces\n  `src/003-loader.lua`. The runner has no embedded Lua state at the\n  top level; Lua only appears inside a Lua language spec's per-worker\n  handle.\n- A **per-input-port slot store** (`src/slot-store.c`) — ring-buffer\n  cells in process heap, durable for the run, plus a large-value heap\n  for variable-size payloads.\n- A **dispatch layer** (`src/dispatch.c`) — the single worker-side\n  action: read inputs → invoke spec → pick branch → push outputs.\n- A **language spec registry** (`src/spec-registry.c`) — `dlopen`s\n  every `langs/<name>/spec.so` at startup and registers it by name\n  and file extension.\n- A **run-output writer** — a dedicated thread that drains a\n  multi-producer-single-consumer ring of events and appends one JSON\n  line per event to `tmp/last-run.jsonl`.\n\nOne pool per map run. Created after the graph loads and validates;\ndestroyed after the active-task counter reaches zero. Worker count\ndefaults to logical CPUs (capped at `MAX_WORKERS=16`), overridable\nvia `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N`.\n\nSee \"Execution model — phase 3\" below for the action loop and slot\nmechanics.\n\n### assets/index.html (the editor)\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to `src/006-server-main.lua` for all file operations. No run\nbutton. The Compile button (added in phase 2 as UI only) wires into\nthe phase 3 build/package pipeline once it lands.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, src_dirs?, lang? }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — soramech-data tables; section-level \"constant\" flag\n  src/\n    *.lua, *.c, *.sh — box function source files\n  compiled/          — produced by the compile pipeline (issue 309)\n    pool-runner      — copy or symlink of soramech-pool\n    src/             — every source file the map uses\n    bin/             — compiled .so files (C boxes via the C spec's compile callback)\n    langs/<name>/    — copy of each language spec .so the map uses\n    manifest.json    — every box, its language, its artifact path, build version\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.jsonl   — phase 3 run log (JSON Lines)\n    logs/            — additional run logs\n```\n\nA compiled map runs standalone: `./compiled/pool-runner` looks up its\nspecs in `compiled/langs/`, reads `manifest.json`, and executes\nwithout any reference to the live editor source tree.\n\nPhase 2's `drivers.json` file is gone. Phase 2 resolves drivers by\nfile extension via the `drivers/` directory; phase 3 resolves\nlanguages by file extension via the spec registry (each spec declares\nits `file_ext`). No map-local driver config file is needed in either\nphase.\n\nThe `data/` directory is for `soramech-data` storage (see \"Data\nfiles\" below). It is **not** where file-source boxes read from — those\nread arbitrary paths, see Box kinds.\n\n## Box file format\n\nEvery box is a single JSON file under `boxes/<id>.json`. Every box\nhas exactly **one output wire** (issue 218). There is no `outputs`\narray. Whatever the function returns travels down the single output\nwire as one value; multi-value returns are encoded as JSON (or a\nlanguage-native struct on a same-language wire — see \"Language spec\nsystem\" below) and decoded downstream.\n\n### Box kinds\n\n| `kind`       | Runs a function? | Notes                                                          |\n|--------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `call`       | yes              | Plain call, comparator, iterator, etc. — see `routing` below.  |\n| `data`       | no               | Language-agnostic **file source**. Reads `path` at dispatch.   |\n| `file_write` | no               | Language-agnostic **file sink**. Writes inputs to disk.        |\n\n`data` and `file_write` are dispatch-layer primitives — the runtime\nreads/writes the file directly, no language spec is invoked. Both\nfollow atomic-write semantics where it matters (write to `path.tmp`,\nfsync, rename).\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"config\", \"kind\": \"data\", \"path\": \"config.json\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"save\",   \"kind\": \"file_write\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"path\", \"type\": \"string\" },\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 } }\n```\n\n`data` has `path` (not `ref`), no `fn`, no inputs; emits the file's\nbytes-as-UTF-8 string on its one output wire. `file_write` takes\n`path` and `text` as inputs; the `path` input can be wired (dynamic)\nor filled by a literal (static). Binary files are out of scope for\nboth — non-UTF-8 reads fail with a clear error.\n\n### Call boxes and the `routing` field\n\nA `call` box runs a function (`ref` + `fn`) and produces one output\nvalue. The `routing` field decides where that value goes. Every\ncall box carries `routing` explicitly — there is no implicit default:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\", \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\", \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" },\n  \"connections\": [\n    { \"from_box\": \"plain-call\", \"from_branch\": null,\n      \"to_box\": \"next\", \"to_input\": \"text\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 } }\n```\n\nThe function **always runs**, regardless of routing kind. Routing\ndecides which downstream branch receives the function's output; the\nfunction itself doesn't know.\n\n#### Routing kinds\n\n| `routing.kind`  | Output ports          | Branch picker                                                | Status     |\n|-----------------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|------------|\n| `plain`         | single port           | fan to all outgoing wires                                    | shipped    |\n| `comparator`    | `lt` / `eq` / `gt`    | `compare(output, comparand)` → lt/eq/gt                      | shipped    |\n| `iterator`      | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, N)`                             | shipped    |\n| `randomizer`    | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | `hash(slot_read_inc(counter_slot, MAX)) % N`                 | follow-on  |\n| `weighted`      | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to PRECISION | follow-on  |\n| `distributor`   | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | argmin over downstream slot fill levels                      | follow-on  |\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"0\" }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\",   \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"weighted\",   \"weights\": [0.8, 0.2] }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"distributor\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n```\n\n**Branch-level fan-out**: for `comparator` / `iterator` / etc., each\nbranch port acts like a small plain output of its own. If the\ncomparator's `lt` port has three wires going to three consumers, then\non every invocation where the routing decision picks `lt`, all three\nof those wires fire. The routing decision picks which branch;\nfan-out picks which consumers on that branch receive the value.\n\nPlain output port can fan freely too — multiple connections from\n`from_branch: null` send copies to every wired consumer. Pulling\nmultiple wires from a single output is not a routing decision.\n\n### Input ports\n\n```json\n\"inputs\": [\n  { \"name\": \"text\",        \"type\": \"string\" },\n  { \"name\": \"config_path\", \"type\": \"string\", \"optional\": true,\n    \"value\": \"config.json\" }\n]\n```\n\nEvery input port is in one of three states at compile time:\n\n1. A wire is connected to it.\n2. A literal `value` is set on it.\n3. It carries `optional: true`.\n\n**Compile fails** when any port is in none of those states. The\nerror is precise: which box, which port. Enforced at the Compile\nbutton (phase 2 UI / phase 3 build) and again in the C graph loader\nat runtime — belt and suspenders against hand-edited maps.\n\n`optional: true` does **not** mean \"pass null\" — it means the\nargument doesn't have to be passed. The dispatch layer assembles\n`input_data[]` / `input_sizes[]` from the slots that actually have\nvalues; an absent optional port shortens `n_inputs` by one and the\nlanguage's native short-arg convention handles the rest. Each\nlanguage picks up the convention natively (Lua: missing args are\n`nil`; Bash: positional unset; C: wrapper reads `n_inputs` and\nforwards what's present).\n\nNull as an **explicit** value (typed `null` into the literal field)\nis a different thing: it arrives through the function call as a real\nargument, mapped to the language's native null (Lua `nil`, Bash empty\nstring `\"\"`, C `NULL`).\n\nVariadic inputs (`variadic_inputs`) carry base names whose ports\nexpand to `<base>_0`, `<base>_1`, … in the editor (issue 217).\n\n### Connections\n\nConnections are written to **both** endpoint box files. The loader\nvalidates at load time that both ends agree — disagreement is a\nhard error.\n\n```json\n{ \"from_box\": \"...\",\n  \"from_branch\": null | \"lt\" | \"eq\" | \"gt\" | \"out_0\" | ...,\n  \"to_box\":   \"...\",\n  \"to_input\": \"...\" }\n```\n\n`from_branch` is `null` for `routing: plain` and for boxes without a\nrouting field; otherwise it names the branch port the wire leaves\nfrom.\n\n## Language spec system (phase 3)\n\nEach language is a **spec** — a `.so` library at\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` that exports a `lang_spec_t` symbol. The pool\nrunner loads every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup via `dlopen` and\nregisters it by `name` (for box lookup) and `file_ext` (for source\nresolution). The spec contract is uniform across languages; no\nlanguage is privileged. The runner itself does not link to liblua,\nlibc++, or any language-specific runtime — only specs do.\n\n### `lang_spec_t`\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       // \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ...\n    const char *file_ext;   // \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Pool startup calls init() for every spec on\n    // every worker before unblocking the init barrier; teardown()\n    // runs at shutdown.\n    void *(*init)    (int worker_idx);\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    // Optional: at map-compile time. C uses this to gcc -shared -fPIC.\n    // Lua and Bash leave this NULL.\n    int   (*compile) (const char *src_path, const char *out_path);\n\n    // Universal invoke path: JSON bytes in, JSON bytes out.\n    // Used across every cross-language wire.\n    int   (*invoke_json)  (void *handle,\n                           const char *file_path, const char *fn_name,\n                           const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes, int n_inputs,\n                           void *out_buf, int out_buf_capacity, int *out_size);\n\n    // Fast invoke path: language-native bytes in, language-native bytes out.\n    // Used when producer and consumer share a language (see \"Same-language\n    // wire fast path\" below).\n    int   (*invoke_native)(void *handle, /* same signature */);\n\n    // Bridges used when a value crosses a language boundary.\n    int   (*native_to_json)(const void *src, int src_size,\n                            void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n    int   (*json_to_native)(const void *src, int src_size,\n                            void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n} lang_spec_t;\n\nextern lang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec;\n```\n\nA nonzero return from `invoke_*` is a fatal error. The dispatch\nlayer prints the context (box id, function name, language) and\naborts. There is no recovery, no retry, no per-task \"failed\" state.\nBugs do not belong in production.\n\n### Init barrier\n\nWorkers are not safe to dispatch to until every worker has completed\n`init` for every spec the map uses. Pool startup runs each worker's\n`init` calls, increments a shared `workers_ready` atomic, and blocks\non a condition variable. The main thread waits for\n`workers_ready == n_workers`, then broadcasts — all workers release\ntogether and begin pulling tasks. One-shot; doesn't re-engage.\n\n### Same-language wire fast path\n\nWire format defaults to JSON. At compile time, every wire is\nclassified `fast_path: true` (same language at both ends) or `false`\n(crosses a language boundary). The compile step also records the\nproducer's `output_format` per box — `native` if **all** consumers\nof its output share its language, `json` if any consumer is\ndifferent.\n\nAt runtime:\n\n- `fast_path && output_format=native`: producer writes native bytes;\n  same-language consumers read native bytes directly.\n- `output_format=json`: producer writes JSON bytes; cross-language\n  consumers read directly; same-language consumers call\n  `json_to_native` on the way in.\n\nPer-language native forms:\n- **Lua** — `lua_dump` for closures, `cjson` or msgpack for tables,\n  raw bytes for strings/numbers.\n- **C** — `memcpy` of the typed struct (the C spec's `compile`\n  callback knows the types).\n- **Bash** — strings only; the fast path is an alias of the JSON\n  path.\n\nA spec that only ever talks to itself can stub out `invoke_json`\n(compile error if a cross-language wire ever points at it). A spec\nthat participates in cross-language wires must implement all four\ncallbacks.\n\n### Shipped specs\n\n`langs/lua/spec.so`, `langs/c/spec.so`, `langs/bash/spec.so` ship as\nreference implementations:\n\n- **Lua** — `init` constructs a `lua_State`; `invoke_*` does\n  `luaL_loadfile` (cached) + `lua_pcall`.\n- **C** — `compile` runs `gcc -shared -fPIC -o <out> <src>` (caching\n  by mtime); `invoke_*` does `dlsym` + direct call through a wrapper\n  the compile step generates from the box signature.\n- **Bash** — `init` spawns a persistent bash subprocess and connects\n  to it over a Unix domain socket. `invoke_*` sends a framed request,\n  reads a framed response. The same shape every future\n  non-embeddable-runtime language uses (Python optional, Node\n  optional, etc.).\n\nA user adds a new language by writing a `langs/<name>/spec.c` and a\nsmall Makefile. SoraMech itself does not transpile box source between\nlanguages.\n\n## Execution model — phase 2 (synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the boxes that have all\ntheir inputs satisfied. Each box call:\n\n1. Read wired output values from predecessor boxes.\n2. Shell out to the appropriate driver script (`drivers/<lang>.sh`).\n3. Decode the single JSON value from driver stdout.\n4. Hold the output in runner memory, keyed by box id.\n5. Fire connections — enqueue boxes whose inputs are now met.\n\nSingle-threaded; one process per box call. The `task_fn` boundary\nmatches the phase 3 dispatch action signature, so the executor can\nbe swapped without changing the box execution model.\n\n## Execution model — phase 3 (thread pool)\n\nTasks are ephemeral; box state is durable. Each box owns one slot\nper input port plus optional state (iterator counter, language\nhandle). A **task** is one stack frame on a worker — `box_id` is\nall it carries. Tasks come and go; boxes persist for the run.\n\n### Slots\n\nEvery input port has exactly one slot, allocated at graph load and\nfreed at run end. A wire is a routing declaration; the producer\ndoesn't own a slot — its output is a push event into every\ndownstream input slot it's wired to. Fan-out is N pushes; fan-in is\nN producers pushing into one slot.\n\nSlot modes:\n\n| Mode                    | Cells   | Reads via         | Used for                                    |\n|-------------------------|---------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|\n| 1-cell peek             | 1       | `slot_peek`       | Literals; wires from runs-once producers    |\n| N-cell pop              | N       | `slot_pop`        | Wires whose producer runs many times        |\n| `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`   | 1 atom  | `slot_read_inc`   | Iterator / randomizer / weighted counters   |\n\nCompile-time analysis decides per wire: a producer is \"runs-once\" if\nno transitive ancestor is an iterator, else \"runs-N-times.\" The\nformer gets a 1-cell peek slot (subsequent consumer tasks re-read the\nsame value); the latter gets an N-cell ring (FIFO drain, one cell\nper consumer task).\n\nVariable-size payloads (long LLM outputs, dynamically-sized arrays)\nlive in a separate **large-value heap**. The slot then holds a small\nfixed-size handle `{ uint32_t size; uint32_t offset; }`. The slot\nallocator only ever sees fixed-size slots; the two-tier scheme keeps\nthe hot path simple while supporting unbounded values.\n\n### Cell tagging for parallel iterators\n\nEach cell optionally carries a 4-byte ordering tag alongside its\ndata. Iterator pushes carry their counter value as the tag; slots\ndownstream of an iterator are allocated with `SLOT_TAGGED`, and\n`slot_pop` on a tagged slot returns the **lowest-tag** cell — not\nthe head. This preserves iteration order across parallel iterator\nworkers (task K of iterator A may push before task K-1 if it landed\non a faster worker; the tag makes the consumer see the values in\niteration order regardless).\n\nWhen a consumer has two tagged inputs from two iterators, each port\npops in tag order independently — pairing falls out as `(A_K, B_K)`\nfor every K.\n\n### The dispatch action\n\nOne C function, one phase per worker per task:\n\n1. **Read inputs.** For each input port: `slot_peek` (peek mode) or\n   `slot_pop` (pop mode) into a heap buffer. Tasks are spawned only\n   when every input slot has a value (spawn-on-input-ready rule), so\n   no waiting is needed.\n2. **Invoke spec.** Look up the box's `lang`, find the worker's\n   handle for it, call `invoke_native` or `invoke_json` (per the\n   wire's fast-path classification). Output lands in a heap buffer\n   sized to the box's declared output size, or into the large-value\n   heap if the box's output is variable-size.\n3. **Pick the branch.** Dispatch on `routing.kind`:\n   - `plain`: every outgoing wire fires.\n   - `comparator`: compare to `comparand`, fire only `lt`/`eq`/`gt`.\n   - `iterator`: `idx = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)`,\n     fire `out_idx` only.\n   - `randomizer` / `weighted` / `distributor`: kind-specific rule\n     (computes an `idx` from the counter slot or from downstream\n     fill, fires that branch).\n4. **Push.** For each firing wire, `slot_push` into the consumer's\n   input slot. The push carries the appropriate ordering tag\n   (iterator counter snapshot for iterator-rooted wires; 0 for\n   plain). Each push triggers a spawn-on-input-ready check on the\n   consumer; if the check passes, the dispatch layer spawns a new\n   `dispatch_task_t` and the pool picks it up.\n5. **Done.** The action returns; the pool decrements the active-task\n   counter. The action does not block, does not wait, does not park.\n\n### Startup, quiescence, and termination\n\nStartup: the pool runner pushes literal-input values into the\ncorresponding slots, then spawns first tasks for boxes whose input\nsets are now satisfied. Iterator counter slots start at 0.\n\nQuiescence: the main thread waits on a condition variable that\nsignals when the pool's active-task counter reaches zero with no\npending spawns. That's the run-over signal. The graph validator at\nload time rejects non-iterator cycles, so the run cannot deadlock —\nan iterator with no upstream pushes simply contributes nothing\nfurther, and once the counter drains, termination fires.\n\nHard-crash error policy: a nonzero `invoke_*` return aborts the\nprocess. No retry, no per-task failed state, no fallback executor.\n\n### Blocking-aware iterator pattern\n\nLong-running operations (network calls, LLM inference) hold their\nworker for the duration. Pool size is the budget. The cooperative\npattern for not holding a worker for minutes: split the call into a\n\"kickoff\" box and a \"check-done\" iterator that polls. Each pass\nthrough the iterator releases the worker between checks. Documented\nfully in `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`.\n\n## Run output — `tmp/last-run.jsonl`\n\nPhase 3 writes one JSON object per event, one event per line, to\n`tmp/last-run.jsonl`. The format decouples the runner from the\neditor — the editor never displays run results; the file is for LLM\nconsumption, CLI viewers, and the integration test harness.\n\nEvent types:\n\n```jsonl\n{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":..., \"map\":\"maps/<name>\", \"n_workers\":16}\n{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\"}\n{\"event\":\"task_start\",  \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}\n{\"event\":\"task_end\",    \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}\n{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\",  \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}   // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"slot_free\",   \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}                              // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"run_end\",     \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}\n```\n\nMechanism: a dedicated writer thread drains a multi-producer\nsingle-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size event records, serializes\neach to JSON, and appends to the file. Workers push records into the\nring without contending on a file mutex. The writer joins before\n`pool_destroy`, including a final `run_end` summary.\n\nInputs/outputs per task are off by default (`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`\nto enable; truncated past 4 KB). Slot allocator events are off by\ndefault (`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` to enable). Timestamps are Unix\nepoch floats.\n\nThe file is overwritten on every run. Rotation is out of scope —\nusers who want history copy the file.\n\n## Build & compile pipeline\n\nA top-level `Makefile` builds:\n\n1. `soramech-pool` — statically links the pool, JSON parser, slot\n   store, graph loader, dispatch layer, spec registry.\n2. `langs/<name>/spec.so` — per-spec, via the per-language Makefile\n   (Lua links LuaJIT; C links `-ldl`; Bash links nothing extra).\n\nModes: `make` (release, `-O2 -Wall`), `make DEBUG=1` (`-O0 -g`),\n`make STRICT=1` (release + `-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).\n\nVendored dependencies (the task pool, the JSON parser) live under\n`libs/` as plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time.\n\nSpec discovery at runtime: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`,\nfollows the symlink, and scans for `langs/` next to its own binary.\n`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs` overrides for development.\n\n### Compile a map for standalone execution\n\n`./compiled/pool-runner` runs a map independently of the editor and\nthe surrounding source tree. The compile step (Compile button in the\neditor, or `soramech-compile <map-dir>` from the CLI) produces:\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/compiled/\n  pool-runner          ← copy or symlink of soramech-pool\n  src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n  bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n  langs/<name>/spec.so ← one per language the map uses\n  manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version\n```\n\nSteps: walk the graph (reusing the C loader's validation); copy\nsource files and transitive `require` / `#include` dependencies;\ninvoke each spec's `compile` callback for boxes whose language needs\nit; copy the spec `.so` files used by the map; copy or symlink the\nrunner binary; write the manifest. Per-box artifacts mtime-compare\nso a re-compile recompiles only what changed. Any failure aborts\nthe step and leaves the partial output for inspection but does not\nwrite the manifest, so the deployment is recognizably broken until\na clean compile succeeds.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in `data/<name>.json` and is accessed via\n`libs/soramech-data.lua` (`data.get` / `data.set` / `data.load`).\nFormat:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only;\nfield-level `constant` flags individual fields within an otherwise\nmutable file. This is **separate** from the `data` box kind (which\nreads arbitrary files at the dispatch layer) — `soramech-data` is\nthe per-map structured-table store; `data` boxes are unstructured\nfile sources.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, run logs, `last-run.jsonl`) goes to\n`tmp/`, a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n",

    "content":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk\nformat: the map directory. None of the three knows about the others\nat runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (assets/index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  src/006-server-main.lua       [map directory]\n                                maps/<name>/\n                                  meta.json\n                                  boxes/\n                                  data/\n                                  src/\n                                  compiled/   (after compile button)\n                                  tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  Runner (one of):\n    src/007-runner-main.lua     ← phase 2, synchronous Lua interpreter\n    soramech-pool (binary)      ← phase 3, C thread pool runner\n```\n\n### src/006-server-main.lua (the editor's HTTP backend)\n\nThin file CRUD proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and\ntranslates them into reads and writes on the map directory. No logic\nbeyond path validation and basic consistency checks (e.g. reject a\ndelete if the box is still referenced by another box's connection\nlist).\n\nStarted with: `luajit src/006-server-main.lua [port]` (default 7700).\nThe `run` script at the project root starts the server and opens the\neditor.\n\nThe editor is editor-only — no run button, no run results display.\nThe runner is invoked separately, by command line. `last-run.jsonl`\nis the runner's output, consumed by external tooling, not by the\neditor.\n\n### Phase 2 runner — `src/007-runner-main.lua`\n\nSynchronous Lua interpreter. Loads a map directory, validates the\ngraph, walks boxes in dependency order, invokes language drivers per\nbox (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/c.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`). Each box\ninvocation is wrapped in a `task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` boundary that\nmatches the phase 3 thread pool's action signature.\n\nThis is the development target while the editor is being built out.\nPhase 2 retires wholesale when phase 3 lands; the editor and the\nmap-directory format are unchanged across the cutover.\n\n### Phase 3 runner — `soramech-pool` (`src/008-pool-runner.c`)\n\nThe phase 3 runner is a single C binary. It owns:\n\n- A **SoraMech-built thread pool** under `libs/task-pool/` (3d-rts at\n  `/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h`\n  is the design reference, not vendored).\n- A **C graph loader** (`src/graph-loader.c`) — replaces\n  `src/003-loader.lua`. The runner has no embedded Lua state at the\n  top level; Lua only appears inside a Lua language spec's per-worker\n  handle.\n- A **per-input-port slot store** (`src/slot-store.c`) — ring-buffer\n  cells in process heap, durable for the run, plus a large-value heap\n  for variable-size payloads.\n- A **dispatch layer** (`src/dispatch.c`) — the single worker-side\n  action: read inputs → invoke spec → pick branch → push outputs.\n- A **language spec registry** (`src/spec-registry.c`) — `dlopen`s\n  every `langs/<name>/spec.so` at startup and registers it by name\n  and file extension.\n- A **run-output writer** — a dedicated thread that drains a\n  multi-producer-single-consumer ring of events and appends one JSON\n  line per event to `tmp/last-run.jsonl`.\n\nOne pool per map run. Created after the graph loads and validates;\ndestroyed after the active-task counter reaches zero. Worker count\ndefaults to logical CPUs (capped at `MAX_WORKERS=16`), overridable\nvia `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N`.\n\nSee \"Execution model — phase 3\" below for the action loop and slot\nmechanics.\n\n### assets/index.html (the editor)\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to `src/006-server-main.lua` for all file operations. No run\nbutton. The Compile button (added in phase 2 as UI only) wires into\nthe phase 3 build/package pipeline once it lands.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, src_dirs?, lang? }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — soramech-data tables; section-level \"constant\" flag\n  src/\n    *.lua, *.c, *.sh — box function source files\n  compiled/          — produced by the compile pipeline (issue 309)\n    pool-runner      — copy or symlink of soramech-pool\n    src/             — every source file the map uses\n    bin/             — compiled .so files (C boxes via the C spec's compile callback)\n    langs/<name>/    — copy of each language spec .so the map uses\n    manifest.json    — every box, its language, its artifact path, build version\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.jsonl   — phase 3 run log (JSON Lines)\n    logs/            — additional run logs\n```\n\nA compiled map runs standalone: `./compiled/pool-runner` looks up its\nspecs in `compiled/langs/`, reads `manifest.json`, and executes\nwithout any reference to the live editor source tree.\n\nPhase 2's `drivers.json` file is gone. Phase 2 resolves drivers by\nfile extension via the `drivers/` directory; phase 3 resolves\nlanguages by file extension via the spec registry (each spec declares\nits `file_ext`). No map-local driver config file is needed in either\nphase.\n\nThe `data/` directory is for `soramech-data` storage (see \"Data\nfiles\" below). It is **not** where file-source boxes read from — those\nread arbitrary paths, see Box kinds.\n\n## Box file format\n\nEvery box is a single JSON file under `boxes/<id>.json`. Every box\nhas exactly **one output wire** (issue 218). There is no `outputs`\narray. Whatever the function returns travels down the single output\nwire as one value; multi-value returns are encoded as JSON (or a\nlanguage-native struct on a same-language wire — see \"Language spec\nsystem\" below) and decoded downstream.\n\n### Box kinds\n\n| `kind`       | Runs a function? | Notes                                                          |\n|--------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `call`       | yes              | Plain call, comparator, iterator, etc. — see `routing` below.  |\n| `data`       | no               | Language-agnostic **file source**. Reads `path` at dispatch.   |\n| `file_write` | no               | Language-agnostic **file sink**. Writes inputs to disk.        |\n\n`data` and `file_write` are dispatch-layer primitives — the runtime\nreads/writes the file directly, no language spec is invoked. Both\nfollow atomic-write semantics where it matters (write to `path.tmp`,\nfsync, rename).\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"config\", \"kind\": \"data\", \"path\": \"config.json\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"save\",   \"kind\": \"file_write\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"path\", \"type\": \"string\" },\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 } }\n```\n\n`data` has `path` (not `ref`), no `fn`, no inputs; emits the file's\nbytes-as-UTF-8 string on its one output wire. `file_write` takes\n`path` and `text` as inputs; the `path` input can be wired (dynamic)\nor filled by a literal (static). Binary files are out of scope for\nboth — non-UTF-8 reads fail with a clear error.\n\n### Call boxes and the `routing` field\n\nA `call` box runs a function (`ref` + `fn`) and produces one output\nvalue. The `routing` field decides where that value goes. Every\ncall box carries `routing` explicitly — there is no implicit default:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\", \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\", \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" },\n  \"connections\": [\n    { \"from_box\": \"plain-call\", \"from_branch\": null,\n      \"to_box\": \"next\", \"to_input\": \"text\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 } }\n```\n\nThe function **always runs**, regardless of routing kind. Routing\ndecides which downstream branch receives the function's output; the\nfunction itself doesn't know.\n\n#### Routing kinds\n\n| `routing.kind`  | Output ports          | Branch picker                                                | Status     |\n|-----------------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|------------|\n| `plain`         | single port           | fan to all outgoing wires                                    | shipped    |\n| `comparator`    | `lt` / `eq` / `gt`    | `compare(output, comparand)` → lt/eq/gt                      | shipped    |\n| `iterator`      | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, N)`                             | shipped    |\n| `randomizer`    | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | `hash(slot_read_inc(counter_slot, MAX)) % N`                 | follow-on  |\n| `weighted`      | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to PRECISION | follow-on  |\n| `distributor`   | `out_0` … `out_N-1`   | argmin over downstream slot fill levels                      | follow-on  |\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"0\" }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\",   \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"weighted\",   \"weights\": [0.8, 0.2] }\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"distributor\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n```\n\n**Branch-level fan-out**: for `comparator` / `iterator` / etc., each\nbranch port acts like a small plain output of its own. If the\ncomparator's `lt` port has three wires going to three consumers, then\non every invocation where the routing decision picks `lt`, all three\nof those wires fire. The routing decision picks which branch;\nfan-out picks which consumers on that branch receive the value.\n\nPlain output port can fan freely too — multiple connections from\n`from_branch: null` send copies to every wired consumer. Pulling\nmultiple wires from a single output is not a routing decision.\n\n### Input ports\n\n```json\n\"inputs\": [\n  { \"name\": \"text\",        \"type\": \"string\" },\n  { \"name\": \"config_path\", \"type\": \"string\", \"optional\": true,\n    \"value\": \"config.json\" }\n]\n```\n\nEvery input port is in one of three states at compile time:\n\n1. A wire is connected to it.\n2. A literal `value` is set on it.\n3. It carries `optional: true`.\n\n**Compile fails** when any port is in none of those states. The\nerror is precise: which box, which port. Enforced at the Compile\nbutton (phase 2 UI / phase 3 build) and again in the C graph loader\nat runtime — belt and suspenders against hand-edited maps.\n\n`optional: true` does **not** mean \"pass null\" — it means the\nargument doesn't have to be passed. The dispatch layer assembles\n`input_data[]` / `input_sizes[]` from the slots that actually have\nvalues; an absent optional port shortens `n_inputs` by one and the\nlanguage's native short-arg convention handles the rest. Each\nlanguage picks up the convention natively (Lua: missing args are\n`nil`; Bash: positional unset; C: wrapper reads `n_inputs` and\nforwards what's present).\n\nNull as an **explicit** value (typed `null` into the literal field)\nis a different thing: it arrives through the function call as a real\nargument, mapped to the language's native null (Lua `nil`, Bash empty\nstring `\"\"`, C `NULL`).\n\nVariadic inputs (`variadic_inputs`) carry base names whose ports\nexpand to `<base>_0`, `<base>_1`, … in the editor (issue 217).\n\n### Connections\n\nConnections are written to **both** endpoint box files. The loader\nvalidates at load time that both ends agree — disagreement is a\nhard error.\n\n```json\n{ \"from_box\": \"...\",\n  \"from_branch\": null | \"lt\" | \"eq\" | \"gt\" | \"out_0\" | ...,\n  \"to_box\":   \"...\",\n  \"to_input\": \"...\" }\n```\n\n`from_branch` is `null` for `routing: plain` and for boxes without a\nrouting field; otherwise it names the branch port the wire leaves\nfrom.\n\n## Language spec system (phase 3)\n\nEach language is a **spec** — a `.so` library at\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` that exports a `lang_spec_t` symbol. The pool\nrunner loads every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup via `dlopen` and\nregisters it by `name` (for box lookup) and `file_ext` (for source\nresolution). The spec contract is uniform across languages; no\nlanguage is privileged. The runner itself does not link to liblua,\nlibc++, or any language-specific runtime — only specs do.\n\n### `lang_spec_t`\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       // \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ...\n    const char *file_ext;   // \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Pool startup calls init() for every spec on\n    // every worker before unblocking the init barrier; teardown()\n    // runs at shutdown.\n    void *(*init)    (int worker_idx);\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    // Optional: at map-compile time. C uses this to gcc -shared -fPIC.\n    // Lua and Bash leave this NULL.\n    int   (*compile) (const char *src_path, const char *out_path);\n\n    // Universal invoke path: JSON bytes in, JSON bytes out.\n    // Used across every cross-language wire.\n    int   (*invoke_json)  (void *handle,\n                           const char *file_path, const char *fn_name,\n                           const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes, int n_inputs,\n                           void *out_buf, int out_buf_capacity, int *out_size);\n\n    // Fast invoke path: language-native bytes in, language-native bytes out.\n    // Used when producer and consumer share a language (see \"Same-language\n    // wire fast path\" below).\n    int   (*invoke_native)(void *handle, /* same signature */);\n\n    // Bridges used when a value crosses a language boundary.\n    int   (*native_to_json)(const void *src, int src_size,\n                            void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n    int   (*json_to_native)(const void *src, int src_size,\n                            void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n} lang_spec_t;\n\nextern lang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec;\n```\n\nA nonzero return from `invoke_*` is a fatal error. The dispatch\nlayer prints the context (box id, function name, language) and\naborts. There is no recovery, no retry, no per-task \"failed\" state.\nBugs do not belong in production.\n\n### Init barrier\n\nWorkers are not safe to dispatch to until every worker has completed\n`init` for every spec the map uses. Pool startup runs each worker's\n`init` calls, increments a shared `workers_ready` atomic, and blocks\non a condition variable. The main thread waits for\n`workers_ready == n_workers`, then broadcasts — all workers release\ntogether and begin pulling tasks. One-shot; doesn't re-engage.\n\n### Same-language wire fast path\n\nWire format defaults to JSON. At compile time, every wire is\nclassified `fast_path: true` (same language at both ends) or `false`\n(crosses a language boundary). The compile step also records the\nproducer's `output_format` per box — `native` if **all** consumers\nof its output share its language, `json` if any consumer is\ndifferent.\n\nAt runtime:\n\n- `fast_path && output_format=native`: producer writes native bytes;\n  same-language consumers read native bytes directly.\n- `output_format=json`: producer writes JSON bytes; cross-language\n  consumers read directly; same-language consumers call\n  `json_to_native` on the way in.\n\nPer-language native forms:\n- **Lua** — `lua_dump` for closures, `cjson` or msgpack for tables,\n  raw bytes for strings/numbers.\n- **C** — `memcpy` of the typed struct (the C spec's `compile`\n  callback knows the types).\n- **Bash** — strings only; the fast path is an alias of the JSON\n  path.\n\nA spec that only ever talks to itself can stub out `invoke_json`\n(compile error if a cross-language wire ever points at it). A spec\nthat participates in cross-language wires must implement all four\ncallbacks.\n\n### Shipped specs\n\n`langs/lua/spec.so`, `langs/c/spec.so`, `langs/bash/spec.so` ship as\nreference implementations:\n\n- **Lua** — `init` constructs a `lua_State`; `invoke_*` does\n  `luaL_loadfile` (cached) + `lua_pcall`.\n- **C** — `compile` runs `gcc -shared -fPIC -o <out> <src>` (caching\n  by mtime); `invoke_*` does `dlsym` + direct call through a wrapper\n  the compile step generates from the box signature.\n- **Bash** — `init` spawns a persistent bash subprocess and connects\n  to it over a Unix domain socket. `invoke_*` sends a framed request,\n  reads a framed response. The same shape every future\n  non-embeddable-runtime language uses (Python optional, Node\n  optional, etc.).\n\nA user adds a new language by writing a `langs/<name>/spec.c` and a\nsmall Makefile. SoraMech itself does not transpile box source between\nlanguages.\n\n## Execution model — phase 2 (synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the boxes that have all\ntheir inputs satisfied. Each box call:\n\n1. Read wired output values from predecessor boxes.\n2. Shell out to the appropriate driver script (`drivers/<lang>.sh`).\n3. Decode the single JSON value from driver stdout.\n4. Hold the output in runner memory, keyed by box id.\n5. Fire connections — enqueue boxes whose inputs are now met.\n\nSingle-threaded; one process per box call. The `task_fn` boundary\nmatches the phase 3 dispatch action signature, so the executor can\nbe swapped without changing the box execution model.\n\n## Execution model — phase 3 (thread pool)\n\nTasks are ephemeral; box state is durable. Each box owns one slot\nper input port plus optional state (iterator counter, language\nhandle). A **task** is one stack frame on a worker — `box_id` is\nall it carries. Tasks come and go; boxes persist for the run.\n\n### Slots\n\nEvery input port has exactly one slot, allocated at graph load and\nfreed at run end. A wire is a routing declaration; the producer\ndoesn't own a slot — its output is a push event into every\ndownstream input slot it's wired to. Fan-out is N pushes; fan-in is\nN producers pushing into one slot.\n\nSlot modes:\n\n| Mode                    | Cells   | Reads via         | Used for                                    |\n|-------------------------|---------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|\n| 1-cell peek             | 1       | `slot_peek`       | Literals; wires from runs-once producers    |\n| N-cell pop              | N       | `slot_pop`        | Wires whose producer runs many times        |\n| `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`   | 1 atom  | `slot_read_inc`   | Iterator / randomizer / weighted counters   |\n\nCompile-time analysis decides per wire: a producer is \"runs-once\" if\nno transitive ancestor is an iterator, else \"runs-N-times.\" The\nformer gets a 1-cell peek slot (subsequent consumer tasks re-read the\nsame value); the latter gets an N-cell ring (FIFO drain, one cell\nper consumer task).\n\nVariable-size payloads (long LLM outputs, dynamically-sized arrays)\nlive in a separate **large-value heap**. The slot then holds a small\nfixed-size handle `{ uint32_t size; uint32_t offset; }`. The slot\nallocator only ever sees fixed-size slots; the two-tier scheme keeps\nthe hot path simple while supporting unbounded values.\n\n### Cell tagging for parallel iterators\n\nEach cell optionally carries a 4-byte ordering tag alongside its\ndata. Iterator pushes carry their counter value as the tag; slots\ndownstream of an iterator are allocated with `SLOT_TAGGED`, and\n`slot_pop` on a tagged slot returns the **lowest-tag** cell — not\nthe head. This preserves iteration order across parallel iterator\nworkers (task K of iterator A may push before task K-1 if it landed\non a faster worker; the tag makes the consumer see the values in\niteration order regardless).\n\nWhen a consumer has two tagged inputs from two iterators, each port\npops in tag order independently — pairing falls out as `(A_K, B_K)`\nfor every K.\n\n### The dispatch action\n\nOne C function, one phase per worker per task:\n\n1. **Read inputs.** For each input port: `slot_peek` (peek mode) or\n   `slot_pop` (pop mode) into a heap buffer. Tasks are spawned only\n   when every input slot has a value (spawn-on-input-ready rule), so\n   no waiting is needed.\n2. **Invoke spec.** Look up the box's `lang`, find the worker's\n   handle for it, call `invoke_native` or `invoke_json` (per the\n   wire's fast-path classification). Output lands in a heap buffer\n   sized to the box's declared output size, or into the large-value\n   heap if the box's output is variable-size.\n3. **Pick the branch.** Dispatch on `routing.kind`:\n   - `plain`: every outgoing wire fires.\n   - `comparator`: compare to `comparand`, fire only `lt`/`eq`/`gt`.\n   - `iterator`: `idx = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)`,\n     fire `out_idx` only.\n   - `randomizer` / `weighted` / `distributor`: kind-specific rule\n     (computes an `idx` from the counter slot or from downstream\n     fill, fires that branch).\n4. **Push.** For each firing wire, `slot_push` into the consumer's\n   input slot. The push carries the appropriate ordering tag\n   (iterator counter snapshot for iterator-rooted wires; 0 for\n   plain). Each push triggers a spawn-on-input-ready check on the\n   consumer; if the check passes, the dispatch layer spawns a new\n   `dispatch_task_t` and the pool picks it up.\n5. **Done.** The action returns; the pool decrements the active-task\n   counter. The action does not block, does not wait, does not park.\n\n### Startup, quiescence, and termination\n\nStartup: the pool runner pushes literal-input values into the\ncorresponding slots, then spawns first tasks for boxes whose input\nsets are now satisfied. Iterator counter slots start at 0.\n\nQuiescence: the main thread waits on a condition variable that\nsignals when the pool's active-task counter reaches zero with no\npending spawns. That's the run-over signal. The graph validator at\nload time rejects non-iterator cycles, so the run cannot deadlock —\nan iterator with no upstream pushes simply contributes nothing\nfurther, and once the counter drains, termination fires.\n\nHard-crash error policy: a nonzero `invoke_*` return aborts the\nprocess. No retry, no per-task failed state, no fallback executor.\n\n### Blocking-aware iterator pattern\n\nLong-running operations (network calls, LLM inference) hold their\nworker for the duration. Pool size is the budget. The cooperative\npattern for not holding a worker for minutes: split the call into a\n\"kickoff\" box and a \"check-done\" iterator that polls. Each pass\nthrough the iterator releases the worker between checks. Documented\nfully in `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`.\n\n## Run output — `tmp/last-run.jsonl`\n\nPhase 3 writes one JSON object per event, one event per line, to\n`tmp/last-run.jsonl`. The format decouples the runner from the\neditor — the editor never displays run results; the file is for LLM\nconsumption, CLI viewers, and the integration test harness.\n\nEvent types:\n\n```jsonl\n{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":..., \"map\":\"maps/<name>\", \"n_workers\":16}\n{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\"}\n{\"event\":\"task_start\",  \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}\n{\"event\":\"task_end\",    \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}\n{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\",  \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}   // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"slot_free\",   \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}                              // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"run_end\",     \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}\n```\n\nMechanism: a dedicated writer thread drains a multi-producer\nsingle-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size event records, serializes\neach to JSON, and appends to the file. Workers push records into the\nring without contending on a file mutex. The writer joins before\n`pool_destroy`, including a final `run_end` summary.\n\nInputs/outputs per task are off by default (`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`\nto enable; truncated past 4 KB). Slot allocator events are off by\ndefault (`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` to enable). Timestamps are Unix\nepoch floats.\n\nThe file is overwritten on every run. Rotation is out of scope —\nusers who want history copy the file.\n\n## Build & compile pipeline\n\nA top-level `Makefile` builds:\n\n1. `soramech-pool` — statically links the pool, JSON parser, slot\n   store, graph loader, dispatch layer, spec registry.\n2. `langs/<name>/spec.so` — per-spec, via the per-language Makefile\n   (Lua links LuaJIT; C links `-ldl`; Bash links nothing extra).\n\nModes: `make` (release, `-O2 -Wall`), `make DEBUG=1` (`-O0 -g`),\n`make STRICT=1` (release + `-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).\n\nVendored dependencies (the task pool, the JSON parser) live under\n`libs/` as plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time.\n\nSpec discovery at runtime: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`,\nfollows the symlink, and scans for `langs/` next to its own binary.\n`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs` overrides for development.\n\n### Compile a map for standalone execution\n\n`./compiled/pool-runner` runs a map independently of the editor and\nthe surrounding source tree. The compile step (Compile button in the\neditor, or `soramech-compile <map-dir>` from the CLI) produces:\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/compiled/\n  pool-runner          ← copy or symlink of soramech-pool\n  src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n  bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n  langs/<name>/spec.so ← one per language the map uses\n  manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version\n```\n\nSteps: walk the graph (reusing the C loader's validation); copy\nsource files and transitive `require` / `#include` dependencies;\ninvoke each spec's `compile` callback for boxes whose language needs\nit; copy the spec `.so` files used by the map; copy or symlink the\nrunner binary; write the manifest. Per-box artifacts mtime-compare\nso a re-compile recompiles only what changed. Any failure aborts\nthe step and leaves the partial output for inspection but does not\nwrite the manifest, so the deployment is recognizably broken until\na clean compile succeeds.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in `data/<name>.json` and is accessed via\n`libs/soramech-data.lua` (`data.get` / `data.set` / `data.load`).\nFormat:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only;\nfield-level `constant` flags individual fields within an otherwise\nmutable file. This is **separate** from the `data` box kind (which\nreads arbitrary files at the dispatch layer) — `soramech-data` is\nthe per-map structured-table store; `data` boxes are unstructured\nfile sources.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, run logs, `last-run.jsonl`) goes to\n`tmp/`, a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n",

The slot","+allocator only ever sees fixed-size slots; the two-tier scheme keeps","+the hot path simple while supporting unbounded values.","+","+### Cell tagging for parallel iterators","+","+Each cell optionally carries a 4-byte ordering tag alongside its","+data.
