Output lands in a heap buffer","+   sized to the box's declared output size, or into the large-value","+   heap if the box's output is variable-size.","+3. **Pick the branch.** Dispatch on `routing.kind`:","+   - `plain`: every outgoing wire fires.","+   - `comparator`: compare to `comparand`, fire only `lt`/`eq`/`gt`.","+   - `iterator`: `idx = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)`,","+     fire `out_idx` only.","+   - `randomizer` / `weighted` / `distributor`: kind-specific rule","+     (computes an `idx` from the counter slot or from downstream","+     fill, fires that branch).","+4. **Push.** For each firing wire, `slot_push` into the consumer's","+   input slot. The push carries the appropriate ordering tag","+   (iterator counter snapshot for iterator-rooted wires; 0 for","+   plain). Each push triggers a spawn-on-input-ready check on the","+   consumer; if the check passes, the dispatch layer spawns a new","+   `dispatch_task_t` and the pool picks it up.","+5. **Done.** The action returns; the pool decrements the active-task","+   counter. The action does not block, does not wait, does not park.","+","+### Startup, quiescence, and termination","+","+Startup: the pool runner pushes literal-input values into the","+corresponding slots, then spawns first tasks for boxes whose input","+sets are now satisfied. Iterator counter slots start at 0.","+","+Quiescence: the main thread waits on a condition variable that","+signals when the pool's active-task counter reaches zero with no","+pending spawns. That's the run-over signal. The graph validator at","+load time rejects non-iterator cycles, so the run cannot deadlock —","+an iterator with no upstream pushes simply contributes nothing","+further, and once the counter drains, termination fires.","+","+Hard-crash error policy: a nonzero `invoke_*` return aborts the","+process. No retry, no per-task failed state, no fallback executor.","+","+### Blocking-aware iterator pattern","+","+Long-running operations (network calls, LLM inference) hold their","+worker for the duration. Pool size is the budget. The cooperative","+pattern for not holding a worker for minutes: split the call into a","+\"kickoff\" box and a \"check-done\" iterator that polls. Each pass","+through the iterator releases the worker between checks. Documented","+fully in `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`.","+","+## Run output — `tmp/last-run.jsonl`","+","+Phase 3 writes one JSON object per event, one event per line, to","+`tmp/last-run.jsonl`. The format decouples the runner from the","+editor — the editor never displays run results; the file is for LLM","+consumption, CLI viewers, and the integration test harness.","+","+Event types:","+","+```jsonl","+{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":..., \"map\":\"maps/<name>\", \"n_workers\":16}","+{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\"}","+{\"event\":\"task_start\",  \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}","+{\"event\":\"task_end\",    \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}","+{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\",  \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}   // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1","+{\"event\":\"slot_free\",   \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}                              // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1","+{\"event\":\"run_end\",     \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}","+```","+","+Mechanism: a dedicated writer thread drains a multi-producer","+single-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size event records, serializes","+each to JSON, and appends to the file. Workers push records into the","+ring without contending on a file mutex. The writer joins before","+`pool_destroy`, including a final `run_end` summary.","+","+Inputs/outputs per task are off by default (`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`","+to enable; truncated past 4 KB). Slot allocator events are off by","+default (`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` to enable). Timestamps are Unix","+epoch floats.","+","+The file is overwritten on every run. Rotation is out of scope —","+users who want history copy the file.","+","+## Build & compile pipeline","+","+A top-level `Makefile` builds:","+","+1. `soramech-pool` — statically links the pool, JSON parser, slot","+   store, graph loader, dispatch layer, spec registry.","+2. `langs/<name>/spec.so` — per-spec, via the per-language Makefile","+   (Lua links LuaJIT; C links `-ldl`; Bash links nothing extra).","+","+Modes: `make` (release, `-O2 -Wall`), `make DEBUG=1` (`-O0 -g`),","+`make STRICT=1` (release + `-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).","+","+Vendored dependencies (the task pool, the JSON parser) live under","+`libs/` as plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time.","+","+Spec discovery at runtime: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`,","+follows the symlink, and scans for `langs/` next to its own binary.","+`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs` overrides for development.","+","+### Compile a map for standalone execution","+","+`./compiled/pool-runner` runs a map independently of the editor and","+the surrounding source tree. The compile step (Compile button in the","+editor, or `soramech-compile <map-dir>` from the CLI) produces:","+","+```","+maps/<name>/compiled/","+  pool-runner          ← copy or symlink of soramech-pool","+  src/                 ← every source file the map uses","+  bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)","+  langs/<name>/spec.so ← one per language the map uses","+  manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version","+```","+","+Steps: walk the graph (reusing the C loader's validation); copy","+source files and transitive `require` / `#include` dependencies;","+invoke each spec's `compile` callback for boxes whose language needs","+it; copy the spec `.so` files used by the map; copy or symlink the","+runner binary; write the manifest. Per-box artifacts mtime-compare","+so a re-compile recompiles only what changed. Any failure aborts","+the step and leaves the partial output for inspection but does not","+write the manifest, so the deployment is recognizably broken until","+a clean compile succeeds.","+"," ## Data files"," ","-Persistent data lives in `data/<name>.json`. Format:","+Persistent data lives in `data/<name>.json` and is accessed via","+`libs/soramech-data.lua` (`data.get` / `data.set` / `data.load`).","+Format:"," "," ```json"," {"],

  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/ritz/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/frontend-design/1c81b812991b/skills/frontend-design\n\nThis skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic \"AI slop\" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.\n\nThe user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.\n\n## Design Thinking\n\nBefore coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:\n- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?\n- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.\n- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).\n- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?\n\n**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.\n\nThen implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:\n- Production-grade and functional\n- Visually striking and memorable\n- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view\n- Meticulously refined in every detail\n\n## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines\n\nFocus on:\n- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.\n- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.\n- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.\n- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.\n- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.\n\nNEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.\n\nInterpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.\n\nRemember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision."
      }],
    "role":"user"
  }
}

## [137]

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-12T22:06:07.092Z",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"938955b4-11a6-4776-8e35-a64362f55154",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"585b6e65-7287-44e7-b133-8bdf3479a266",
  "parentUuid":"938955b4-11a6-4776-8e35-a64362f55154",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "promptId":"d0b4df49-5900-46d4-9f44-b3ae588a50ef",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"text",
    "file":{
      "content":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## Two systems, one filename\n\nPhase 2 used **driver scripts** — shell wrappers under `drivers/`\nthat the synchronous runner invoked one process per box call.\n\nPhase 3 uses **language specs** — `.so` libraries under `langs/`\nloaded by the C pool runner via `dlopen`, with persistent per-worker\nruntimes.\n\nSame idea, different mechanism. Phase 3 replaces phase 2 wholesale\nwhen it lands. This document covers both, since the project lives in\nphase 2 today and the phase 3 design is fully specified.\n\n## Phase 2 — Driver scripts (current)\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The synchronous runner looks up the file extension, finds\nthe driver script, and calls it.\n\n### Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n```\n<driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n```\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and decoded by the driver.\n\nThe driver must:\n- Exit 0 on success, nonzero on failure\n- Print one JSON value to stdout — string, number, boolean, object,\n  or null. One output wire per box.\n- Print error messages to stderr on failure\n\nMulti-output tuple returns are not supported. Each box has exactly\none output wire (issue 218).\n\n### Built-in driver scripts\n\nShipped in the project's `drivers/` directory:\n\n- `drivers/lua.sh` — invokes a Lua function via `luajit`\n- `drivers/c.sh` — compiles `.c` (mtime cache) and runs the binary\n- `drivers/bash.sh` — sources the `.sh` and calls the function\n\nUser-added drivers go in the same directory and are picked up by\nextension.\n\n### What's wrong with this model\n\nProcess spawn cost dominates each call (1–10 ms per language).\nStdout is a fragile channel — debug prints inside box code corrupt\nthe wire value. Each invocation is its own fresh interpreter; there\nis no persistent runtime between calls. These are the limitations\nphase 3 fixes.\n\n## Phase 3 — Language specs (planned)\n\nEach language is a small C library implementing the spec interface\ndefined in issue 303. The pool runner loads every\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` at startup; the spec interface is uniform\nacross languages, with no privileged language.\n\n### Spec interface\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;\n    const char *file_ext;\n\n    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n    int   (*compile)(const char *src_path, const char *out_path,\n                     const box_t *box);\n    int   (*invoke)(void *handle,\n                    const char *file_path, const char *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes,\n                    int n_inputs,\n                    void *out_buf, int out_buf_capacity,\n                    int *out_size);\n} lang_spec_t;\n```\n\n`init` runs once per worker thread at pool startup. `teardown` runs\nat shutdown. `compile` runs at map load time for languages that need\nit (C). `invoke` runs once per box invocation.\n\nThe spec receives input bytes and writes output bytes — never\ninteracts with slot IDs. The dispatch layer (issue 304) reads\ninputs from slots into byte buffers, hands them to `invoke`, takes\nback bytes, writes them to the output slot.\n\n### Reference specs\n\n- **Lua** (issue 306) — handle is a `lua_State` per worker. `invoke`\n  loads the box file (cached in the registry), pushes typed\n  arguments, calls via `lua_pcall`, serializes the return value.\n- **C** (issue 307) — handle is a `dlopen`-cache per worker.\n  `compile` generates a wrapper from the box's declared inputs and\n  return type, then runs `cc` to produce the `.so`. `invoke` does\n  `dlsym` and a direct function-pointer call.\n- **Bash** (issue 308) — handle is a Unix domain socket connected\n  to a persistent `bash-server.sh` subprocess. `invoke` sends a\n  framed request, reads a framed response.\n\nThe Lua and C specs are in-process (Option 1 in\n`docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`). The Bash spec is out-of-process\n(Option 3) — proof that the spec interface accommodates languages\nthat cannot be embedded.\n\n### Adding a new language\n\nA user adds Python, Rust, or anything else by writing a new spec:\n\n1. Create `langs/<name>/spec.c` implementing the four callbacks.\n2. Create `langs/<name>/Makefile` that builds `spec.so`.\n3. Add the language to `meta.json src_dirs` if necessary so the\n   editor's file browser can see source files.\n\nThe pool runner picks up the new spec at the next startup. No\nSoraMech code change required.\n\nFor full implementation guidance, see the future\n`docs/005-language-specs.md` (referenced from issue 303). For the\nspec contract itself, issue 303.\n\n## Migration: phase 2 → phase 3\n\nWhen phase 3 lands:\n\n| Phase 2                              | Phase 3                              |\n|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|\n| `drivers/lua.sh`                     | `langs/lua/spec.so`                  |\n| `drivers/c.sh`                       | `langs/c/spec.so`                    |\n| `drivers/bash.sh`                    | `langs/bash/spec.so`                 |\n| `drivers.json` (per-map)             | (none — spec registry is global)     |\n| stdout as channel                    | direct function call / Unix socket   |\n| One process per call                 | Persistent runtimes                  |\n| Single output wire (JSON-encoded)    | Single output slot (typed bytes)     |\n\nBox JSON does not change shape — `lang`, `ref`, `fn`, `inputs`\nremain. Phase 3 reads the same files phase 2 reads. The runtime\nmechanism beneath the box is what changes.\n\n## Relevant issues\n\n- 102 (completed) — phase 2 driver interface\n- 218 (completed) — single-output driver contract\n- 303 — phase 3 language spec contract\n- 306 — Lua language spec\n- 307 — C language spec\n- 308 — Bash language spec\n",
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":157,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/003-driver-system.md",
      "numLines":157
    }
  },
  "uuid":"6f9d614a-cf5d-4312-9bc5-8e493616a373",

The runtime\n147\tmechanism beneath the box is what changes.\n148\t\n149\t## Relevant issues\n150\t\n151\t- 102 (completed) — phase 2 driver interface\n152\t- 218 (completed) — single-output driver contract\n153\t- 303 — phase 3 language spec contract\n154\t- 306 — Lua language spec\n155\t- 307 — C language spec\n156\t- 308 — Bash language spec\n157\t"

      "content":"# SoraMech — IPC and Threading Model\n\n## The problem\n\nThe current executor runs boxes sequentially. Each box invocation shells out to\na driver script, which starts a new process, runs the function, and exits. The\nreturn value passes through stdout. This works but has two structural problems:\n\n1. **Process-per-call cost.** Spawning a process takes roughly 1–10 ms depending\n   on the runtime. For a map with ten boxes, that's dominated by spawn overhead,\n   not by the actual work.\n\n2. **stdout is the wrong channel.** A box function that prints debug output\n   corrupts the wire value. Values are transient — they vanish once the pipe is\n   drained. The channel has no addressing, no framing, and no backpressure.\n\nThe goal is a design where cross-language calls are fast, values are addressable,\nand the execution model is ready to parallelize without redesign.\n\n---\n\n## The threading roadmap\n\nThree stages, each building on the last:\n\n**Stage 1 — Synchronous (current).** A single-threaded ready-queue walks the\ngraph in dependency order. `run_task(box, inputs)` in `src/004-executor.lua` is\nthe task boundary. It blocks until the driver responds.\n\n**Stage 2 — Coroutine-based non-blocking.** The ready-queue becomes a coroutine\nscheduler. Boxes yield when waiting on upstream results or cross-language calls.\nLuaSocket non-blocking I/O lets the scheduler run other boxes while one is\nwaiting for a response. No true parallelism yet, but the graph's natural\nconcurrency is exploited without blocking the whole process.\n\n**Stage 3 — SoraMech-owned thread pool.** A pool implementation\nwritten for SoraMech, with the 3d-rts pool design as a reference.\nThe `task_fn` boundary swaps in the thread pool. Worker threads pull\ntasks from the pool; OS-level scheduling replaces any single-threaded\nordering. Cross-language calls block a worker thread while other\nthreads continue. True parallelism across cores.\n\nEffil-jit is not used. Coroutines are not used. The path goes\nstraight from synchronous (phase 2) to the C pool (phase 3) — no\nintermediate coroutine stage.\n\n---\n\n## Stage 3 detail: pthreads task model\n\nEach box execution in the thread pool is a **task struct** containing:\n\n- **Function pointer** — the language-specific invocation wrapper (a C\n  function, since pthreads requires a C entry point)\n- **Shared memory pointer** — the region holding the input arguments and\n  return value for this invocation\n- **Dependency list** — pointers to the tasks this task is waiting on\n- **Waiting list** — pointers to tasks that are waiting on this task\n- **Counter** (iterator boxes only) — current iteration index, updated\n  in-place when the iterator re-queues itself\n\nTask structs are allocated once at run start, one per box (not one per\ninvocation). They live for the entire run.\n\n### Blocking and unblocking — pointer-only transitions\n\nWhen a task cannot run (upstream output not yet available), it is placed\nin its upstream task's waiting list. This is a pointer move — no\nallocation, no struct copy. The task struct stays exactly where it is.\n\nWhen an upstream task completes and writes its return value to shared\nmemory, it walks its waiting list and re-adds each entry to the main task\nqueue. Again, a pointer move only. The unblocked task's struct is\nunchanged; only its position in the queue changes.\n\nThis means \"blocked\", \"queued\", and \"running\" are states defined by which\nlist a task's pointer currently lives in — not by any field in the struct.\n\n### Per-thread language runtimes\n\nEach worker thread initializes its own language runtimes at startup:\n- **Lua:** one `lua_State` per thread. Lua states are not thread-safe, but\n  one per thread requires no locking. The task wrapper calls the box\n  function via `lua_pcall`.\n- **C:** the compiled box function is called directly through the function\n  pointer. No interpreter, no overhead beyond the call itself.\n- **Bash/other:** a persistent subprocess per thread (Unix domain socket\n  server model — see Option 3 above). The task wrapper sends a request and\n  blocks the thread waiting for the response.\n\n### Iterator self-re-queue\n\nAn iterator task does not terminate after one invocation. When it\ncompletes:\n1. It increments its `counter` field in-place (or wraps to 0).\n2. It checks its input queue for the next pending value.\n3. If a value is waiting: it updates its input pointer and re-adds itself\n   to the main task queue. No allocation — the same task struct re-enters\n   the queue with updated state.\n4. If no value is waiting: it adds itself to the upstream task's waiting\n   list, to be re-added when the next input arrives.\n\nInput values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued\ninputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the\ncounter and firing a different output path each time.\n\n### Blocking semantics for long-running operations\n\nThe pool's parallelism comes from running N worker threads concurrently\non N cores. Each worker is sitting inside a single dispatch task at any\ngiven moment. If a box function does something that takes a long time —\n`sleep`, blocking I/O, a synchronous network request, waiting on a long-\nrunning subprocess — **the worker thread is occupied for the full\nduration**. It cannot pick up other tasks while it waits.\n\nConcretely:\n- 16-worker pool, 1 box sleeping 10 seconds → the other 15 workers\n  continue normally.\n- 16-worker pool, 16 boxes all sleeping → all workers parked, no other\n  task runs until a sleep finishes.\n- The pool size is also the budget for \"blocking activities\". Heavy\n  use of `sleep`-style boxes means raising `SORAMECH_WORKERS`.\n\nWhy the runtime does not have a scheduler: SoraMech is deliberately not\nin the business of \"park this task and wake it at time T.\" There is no\ndelayed-spawn primitive, no timer thread, no polling loop. Adding one\nwould mean a second concurrency model alongside the pool, with its own\nsynchronization story. Instead, we lean on the pool's existing\nmechanism: a task either runs (occupying a worker) or is blocked on a\nslot waiting for a value (parked, no worker held). Long sleeps are an\n\"occupying a worker\" case.\n\nFor users who need many concurrent waits without burning workers, the\ngraph-level pattern is cooperative: split the operation into \"kick off\nthe thing\" (returns immediately) and \"check whether the thing is done\"\n(returns immediately, returns a status), and wire them through an\niterator with a queued input. The iterator polls. No individual box\nblocks for long. Each box completes quickly, freeing its worker.\n\nThis is a documented constraint, not a bug. Box authors should know\nthat an unbounded `sleep` inside a function is the equivalent of\nholding a worker hostage. The cooperative pattern is the way around\nit.\n\n---\n\n## The three IPC options\n\n### Option 1 — LuaJIT FFI (Lua ↔ C, in-process)\n\nThe Foreign Function Interface lets Lua call C functions that live in a shared\nlibrary (`.so`) directly, in the same process, with no subprocess and no channel.\nYou provide a C declaration (`ffi.cdef[[ int add(int a, int b); ]]`), load the\ncompiled library (`ffi.load(\"./mybox.so\")`), and call `lib.add(3, 4)` — the CPU\njumps into native code and returns. Overhead is nanoseconds.\n\nSince the executor already does mtime-based dynamic compilation (see `drivers/c.sh`),\ncompiling to a `.so` instead of a binary is just a flag change (`-shared -fPIC`).\nThe box function signature changes from `main(argc, argv)` to a named function\nwith typed arguments — which is strictly cleaner.\n\n**Limitation:** FFI only works for languages that compile to a C-compatible ABI.\nBash cannot. Python can (via `ctypes` on the other side), but it's awkward.\nFFI is the right answer for Lua ↔ C only.\n\n**Cross-platform:** LuaJIT FFI works on Linux, macOS, and Windows. `.so` becomes\n`.dylib` on macOS and `.dll` on Windows — the `ffi.load()` call is portable if\nyou handle the extension.\n\n---\n\n### Option 2 — Shared memory (`shm_open` + `mmap`)\n\n`shm_open(\"/soramech-wire-0\", ...)` creates a named memory segment managed by\nthe kernel — not a file on disk, but a named object in RAM. `mmap()` maps it\ninto the calling process's address space. Any other process that opens the same\nname gets access to the *same physical memory*. A write in one process is\nimmediately visible in another — no copy, no syscall per access after setup.\n\nFor SoraMech, each wire between two boxes would correspond to a named shared\nmemory slot. The compiler (issue 219) generates the slot names and the read/write\ncalls. Any language that can call POSIX can participate:\n\n- Lua: via LuaJIT FFI calling `shm_open` + `mmap` from libc\n- C: natively\n- Bash: via `/dev/shm/<name>` — on Linux, the tmpfs backing shared memory is\n  exposed as a filesystem path, so bash can `cat /dev/shm/soramech-wire-0`\n\n**Performance:** After the initial `mmap()` setup, reads and writes are pointer\ndereferences — no syscalls, no copies. For small values (strings, numbers) this\nis essentially free.\n\n**Complication:** Shared memory is untyped raw bytes. You need a size header\n(how many bytes is this value?), a type tag (string? number? JSON object?), and\na synchronization mechanism (how does the reader know the writer is done?). None\nof these are hard — a small fixed header in the segment handles all three — but\nthe compiler must generate all of it correctly for every wire.\n\n**Cross-platform:**\n- Linux: full support. `/dev/shm/` filesystem exposure is Linux-specific.\n- macOS: `shm_open()` works, but the objects are NOT exposed as files. No\n  `/dev/shm/` path. Bash access via file path doesn't work.\n- Windows: completely different API (`CreateFileMapping` / `MapViewOfFile`).\n  No POSIX `shm_open` without WSL or Cygwin.\n\nShared memory is powerful but not the most portable option. The bash filesystem\nshortcut that makes it cross-language is Linux-only.\n\n---\n\n### Option 3 — Unix domain socket servers (chosen direction)\n\nA Unix domain socket is a socket addressed by a filesystem path instead of an\nIP address and port. `/tmp/soramech-bash.sock` is a special file; any process\non the same machine connects to it with the standard socket API. The kernel\nroutes data directly between processes in memory — no network stack, no loopback,\nno protocol headers. Performance is bounded by memory bandwidth.\n\nUnlike anonymous pipes, a socket has a name that unrelated processes can find\nwithout inheriting file descriptors. Multiple clients connect simultaneously;\neach gets its own channel. The server handles them with `accept()` in a loop.\n\n**The model for SoraMech:**\n\nEach language runtime runs as a persistent socket server. One server instance\nper language per worker thread:\n\n```\n/tmp/soramech-bash-0.sock   ← worker thread 0's bash runtime\n/tmp/soramech-bash-1.sock   ← worker thread 1's bash runtime\n/tmp/soramech-c-0.sock      ← worker thread 0's C runtime\n```\n\nThe server starts when the program starts, stays alive for the whole run, and\naccepts sequential requests — one box call at a time per instance. A Lua worker\nconnects to its designated socket, sends a framed request (function name +\narguments), and reads back a framed response (return value). The server is a\nsmall script (~50 lines) that sources or compiles the box file, calls the\nfunction, and writes the result.\n\n**Wire protocol:** Length-prefix framing. The sender writes a 4-byte big-endian\ninteger (the message length in bytes), then that many bytes of content. The\nreceiver reads 4 bytes, then reads exactly that many bytes. This handles values\ncontaining newlines or null bytes without ambiguity.\n\n**Cost of idle servers:** An idle server process is blocked on `accept()` — zero\nCPU, approximately 3–5 MB RSS for a bash process. For 10 languages × 4 threads\n= 40 processes ≈ 150–200 MB. Acceptable.\n\n**Integration with the coroutine scheduler (Stage 2):**\n\nWith LuaSocket non-blocking sockets, the coroutine that makes a cross-language\ncall does this:\n1. Connect to the language server socket (non-blocking)\n2. Send the request\n3. `coroutine.yield()` — registers the socket fd with the scheduler\n4. Scheduler polls all pending fds with `select()`\n5. When the fd is readable, scheduler resumes the coroutine\n6. Coroutine reads the response and continues\n\nThe cross-language call never blocks the main Lua thread. Other boxes run in\nother coroutines while the bash/C server is processing.\n\n**Integration with the SoraMech thread pool (Stage 3):**\n\nEach worker thread owns its set of language server sockets. When `run_task` calls\na cross-language box, it sends to the socket and blocks on the read — the thread\nblocks, not the whole program. Other workers continue processing other boxes on\nother cores. The server processes run concurrently on whatever cores the OS\nschedules them to. This gives real parallelism: a bash box and a C box assigned\nto different workers can run simultaneously.\n\n**Cross-platform:**\n- Linux: full support.\n- macOS: full support. Unix domain sockets are POSIX.\n- Windows: supported since Windows 10 1803 (2018). `AF_UNIX` sockets work\n  natively. Most languages abstract this through their socket libraries.\n\nUnix domain sockets are the most portable cross-language IPC mechanism that also\nsupports concurrent connections. They are the chosen direction for the compiler\noutput and the coroutine/thread-pool executor.\n\n---\n\n## Summary comparison\n\n| Property              | FFI (.so)       | Shared memory       | Unix domain socket  |\n|-----------------------|-----------------|---------------------|---------------------|\n| Speed (per call)      | nanoseconds     | nanoseconds*        | microseconds        |\n| Languages supported   | C-ABI only      | any (with caveats)  | any                 |\n| Parallel connections  | N/A (in-process)| yes (with sync)     | yes (natural)       |\n| Linux                 | yes             | yes                 | yes                 |\n| macOS                 | yes             | partial†            | yes                 |\n| Windows               | yes (.dll)      | no (different API)  | yes (Win10+)        |\n| Complexity            | low             | medium              | low-medium          |\n\n*After initial mmap setup. †shm_open works; /dev/shm filesystem path does not.\n\nThe compiler (issue 219) uses FFI for Lua ↔ C wires where the C source is\ncompiled to a `.so`, and Unix domain sockets for all other cross-language wires.\nSame-language Lua wires are direct function calls — no IPC at all.\n\n---\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — `run_task` boundary, ready-queue\n- `src/007-runner-main.lua` — entry point for the interpreter path\n- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — compiler that generates the IPC calls\n- `issues/104-runner-synchronous-executor.md` — task boundary design\n- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queue-per-port, thread pool notes\n- `docs/002-roadmap.md` — phase plan for threading stages\n",
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":313,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md",
      "numLines":313

The cooperative pattern is the way around\n143\tit.\n144\t\n145\t---\n146\t\n147\t## The three IPC options\n148\t\n149\t### Option 1 — LuaJIT FFI (Lua ↔ C, in-process)\n150\t\n151\tThe Foreign Function Interface lets Lua call C functions that live in a shared\n152\tlibrary (`.so`) directly, in the same process, with no subprocess and no channel.\n153\tYou provide a C declaration (`ffi.cdef[[ int add(int a, int b); ]]`), load the\n154\tcompiled library (`ffi.load(\"./mybox.so\")`), and call `lib.add(3, 4)` — the CPU\n155\tjumps into native code and returns. Overhead is nanoseconds.\n156\t\n157\tSince the executor already does mtime-based dynamic compilation (see `drivers/c.sh`),\n158\tcompiling to a `.so` instead of a binary is just a flag change (`-shared -fPIC`).\n159\tThe box function signature changes from `main(argc, argv)` to a named function\n160\twith typed arguments — which is strictly cleaner.\n161\t\n162\t**Limitation:** FFI only works for languages that compile to a C-compatible ABI.\n163\tBash cannot. Python can (via `ctypes` on the other side), but it's awkward.\n164\tFFI is the right answer for Lua ↔ C only.\n165\t\n166\t**Cross-platform:** LuaJIT FFI works on Linux, macOS, and Windows. `.so` becomes\n167\t`.dylib` on macOS and `.dll` on Windows — the `ffi.load()` call is portable if\n168\tyou handle the extension.\n169\t\n170\t---\n171\t\n172\t### Option 2 — Shared memory (`shm_open` + `mmap`)\n173\t\n174\t`shm_open(\"/soramech-wire-0\", ...)` creates a named memory segment managed by\n175\tthe kernel — not a file on disk, but a named object in RAM. `mmap()` maps it\n176\tinto the calling process's address space. Any other process that opens the same\n177\tname gets access to the *same physical memory*. A write in one process is\n178\timmediately visible in another — no copy, no syscall per access after setup.\n179\t\n180\tFor SoraMech, each wire between two boxes would correspond to a named shared\n181\tmemory slot. The compiler (issue 219) generates the slot names and the read/write\n182\tcalls. Any language that can call POSIX can participate:\n183\t\n184\t- Lua: via LuaJIT FFI calling `shm_open` + `mmap` from libc\n185\t- C: natively\n186\t- Bash: via `/dev/shm/<name>` — on Linux, the tmpfs backing shared memory is\n187\t  exposed as a filesystem path, so bash can `cat /dev/shm/soramech-wire-0`\n188\t\n189\t**Performance:** After the initial `mmap()` setup, reads and writes are pointer\n190\tdereferences — no syscalls, no copies. For small values (strings, numbers) this\n191\tis essentially free.\n192\t\n193\t**Complication:** Shared memory is untyped raw bytes. You need a size header\n194\t(how many bytes is this value?), a type tag (string? number? JSON object?), and\n195\ta synchronization mechanism (how does the reader know the writer is done?). None\n196\tof these are hard — a small fixed header in the segment handles all three — but\n197\tthe compiler must generate all of it correctly for every wire.\n198\t\n199\t**Cross-platform:**\n200\t- Linux: full support. `/dev/shm/` filesystem exposure is Linux-specific.\n201\t- macOS: `shm_open()` works, but the objects are NOT exposed as files. No\n202\t  `/dev/shm/` path. Bash access via file path doesn't work.\n203\t- Windows: completely different API (`CreateFileMapping` / `MapViewOfFile`).\n204\t  No POSIX `shm_open` without WSL or Cygwin.\n205\t\n206\tShared memory is powerful but not the most portable option. The bash filesystem\n207\tshortcut that makes it cross-language is Linux-only.\n208\t\n209\t---\n210\t\n211\t### Option 3 — Unix domain socket servers (chosen direction)\n212\t\n213\tA Unix domain socket is a socket addressed by a filesystem path instead of an\n214\tIP address and port. `/tmp/soramech-bash.sock` is a special file; any process\n215\ton the same machine connects to it with the standard socket API. The kernel\n216\troutes data directly between processes in memory — no network stack, no loopback,\n217\tno protocol headers. Performance is bounded by memory bandwidth.\n218\t\n219\tUnlike anonymous pipes, a socket has a name that unrelated processes can find\n220\twithout inheriting file descriptors. Multiple clients connect simultaneously;\n221\teach gets its own channel. The server handles them with `accept()` in a loop.\n222\t\n223\t**The model for SoraMech:**\n224\t\n225\tEach language runtime runs as a persistent socket server. One server instance\n226\tper language per worker thread:\n227\t\n228\t```\n229\t/tmp/soramech-bash-0.sock   ← worker thread 0's bash runtime\n230\t/tmp/soramech-bash-1.sock   ← worker thread 1's bash runtime\n231\t/tmp/soramech-c-0.sock      ← worker thread 0's C runtime\n232\t```\n233\t\n234\tThe server starts when the program starts, stays alive for the whole run, and\n235\taccepts sequential requests — one box call at a time per instance. A Lua worker\n236\tconnects to its designated socket, sends a framed request (function name +\n237\targuments), and reads back a framed response (return value). The server is a\n238\tsmall script (~50 lines) that sources or compiles the box file, calls the\n239\tfunction, and writes the result.\n240\t\n241\t**Wire protocol:** Length-prefix framing. The sender writes a 4-byte big-endian\n242\tinteger (the message length in bytes), then that many bytes of content. The\n243\treceiver reads 4 bytes, then reads exactly that many bytes. This handles values\n244\tcontaining newlines or null bytes without ambiguity.\n245\t\n246\t**Cost of idle servers:** An idle server process is blocked on `accept()` — zero\n247\tCPU, approximately 3–5 MB RSS for a bash process. For 10 languages × 4 threads\n248\t= 40 processes ≈ 150–200 MB. Acceptable.\n249\t\n250\t**Integration with the coroutine scheduler (Stage 2):**\n251\t\n252\tWith LuaSocket non-blocking sockets, the coroutine that makes a cross-language\n253\tcall does this:\n254\t1. Connect to the language server socket (non-blocking)\n255\t2. Send the request\n256\t3. `coroutine.yield()` — registers the socket fd with the scheduler\n257\t4. Scheduler polls all pending fds with `select()`\n258\t5. When the fd is readable, scheduler resumes the coroutine\n259\t6. Coroutine reads the response and continues\n260\t\n261\tThe cross-language call never blocks the main Lua thread. Other boxes run in\n262\tother coroutines while the bash/C server is processing.\n263\t\n264\t**Integration with the SoraMech thread pool (Stage 3):**\n265\t\n266\tEach worker thread owns its set of language server sockets. When `run_task` calls\n267\ta cross-language box, it sends to the socket and blocks on the read — the thread\n268\tblocks, not the whole program. Other workers continue processing other boxes on\n269\tother cores. The server processes run concurrently on whatever cores the OS\n270\tschedules them to. This gives real parallelism: a bash box and a C box assigned\n271\tto different workers can run simultaneously.\n272\t\n273\t**Cross-platform:**\n274\t- Linux: full support.\n275\t- macOS: full support. Unix domain sockets are POSIX.\n276\t- Windows: supported since Windows 10 1803 (2018). `AF_UNIX` sockets work\n277\t  natively. Most languages abstract this through their socket libraries.\n278\t\n279\tUnix domain sockets are the most portable cross-language IPC mechanism that also\n280\tsupports concurrent connections. They are the chosen direction for the compiler\n281\toutput and the coroutine/thread-pool executor.\n282\t\n283\t---\n284\t\n285\t## Summary comparison\n286\t\n287\t| Property              | FFI (.so)       | Shared memory       | Unix domain socket  |\n288\t|-----------------------|-----------------|---------------------|---------------------|\n289\t| Speed (per call)      | nanoseconds     | nanoseconds*        | microseconds        |\n290\t| Languages supported   | C-ABI only      | any (with caveats)  | any                 |\n291\t| Parallel connections  | N/A (in-process)| yes (with sync)     | yes (natural)       |\n292\t| Linux                 | yes             | yes                 | yes                 |\n293\t| macOS                 | yes             | partial†            | yes                 |\n294\t| Windows               | yes (.dll)      | no (different API)  | yes (Win10+)        |\n295\t| Complexity            | low             | medium              | low-medium          |\n296\t\n297\t*After initial mmap setup. †shm_open works; /dev/shm filesystem path does not.\n298\t\n299\tThe compiler (issue 219) uses FFI for Lua ↔ C wires where the C source is\n300\tcompiled to a `.so`, and Unix domain sockets for all other cross-language wires.\n301\tSame-language Lua wires are direct function calls — no IPC at all.\n302\t\n303\t---\n304\t\n305\t## Relevant files\n306\t\n307\t- `src/004-executor.lua` — `run_task` boundary, ready-queue\n308\t- `src/007-runner-main.lua` — entry point for the interpreter path\n309\t- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — compiler that generates the IPC calls\n310\t- `issues/104-runner-synchronous-executor.md` — task boundary design\n311\t- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queue-per-port, thread pool notes\n312\t- `docs/002-roadmap.md` — phase plan for threading stages\n313\t"
      }],
    "role":"user"
  },

}

          "content":"// Sidebar TOC + subnav highlighting.\n// All paths relative to docs/HTML/. The sidebar HTML is identical across pages,\n// and a `data-page` attribute on <body> selects the active entry.\n\n(function () {\n  const pages = [\n    { num: \"00\",  href: \"index.html\",                   title: \"Contents\" },\n    { num: \"01\",  href: \"001-architecture.html\",        title: \"Architecture\" },\n    { num: \"02\",  href: \"002-roadmap.html\",             title: \"Roadmap\" },\n    { num: \"03\",  href: \"003-driver-system.html\",       title: \"Driver System\" },\n    { num: \"04\",  href: \"004-ipc-and-threading.html\",   title: \"IPC & Threading\" },\n    { num: \"05\",  href: \"005-language-specs.html\",      title: \"Language Specs\" },\n  ];\n\n  function build() {\n    const aside = document.querySelector(\".sidebar\");\n    if (!aside) return;\n\n    const current = document.body.dataset.page || \"\";\n\n    const brand = `\n      <a href=\"index.html\" class=\"brand\">\n        <span class=\"mark\"><em class=\"accent\">Sora</em>Mech</span>\n        <span class=\"sub\">Notebook · vol. one</span>\n      </a>`;\n\n    const tocItems = pages.map(p => {\n      const isCurrent = (p.href === current) ? \" current\" : \"\";\n      return `\n        <li>\n          <a class=\"page-link${isCurrent}\" href=\"${p.href}\">\n            <span class=\"num\">§${p.num}</span>\n            <span class=\"title\">${p.title}</span>\n          </a>\n          ${isCurrent ? `<ul class=\"toc-subnav\" data-subnav></ul>` : ``}\n        </li>`;\n    }).join(\"\");\n\n    const foot = `\n      <div class=\"sidebar-foot\">\n        <div>Source: <a href=\"../\">../docs/</a></div>\n        <div>Last assembled by lamplight.</div>\n        <div style=\"margin-top:0.6rem;\">\n          <span class=\"scribble\" style=\"display:block; font-size:0.95rem; transform:rotate(-2deg)\">strings flow like ink ↗</span>\n        </div>\n      </div>`;\n\n    aside.innerHTML = `\n      ${brand}\n      <span class=\"toc-label\">Documents</span>\n      <ul class=\"toc-list\">${tocItems}</ul>\n      ${foot}\n    `;\n\n    // Sub-nav from page <h2> elements\n    const subnav = aside.querySelector(\"[data-subnav]\");\n    if (subnav) {\n      const heads = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(\"main h2[id]\"));\n      subnav.innerHTML = heads.map(h =>\n        `<li><a href=\"#${h.id}\" data-sub-target=\"${h.id}\">${h.textContent.trim()}</a></li>`\n      ).join(\"\");\n\n      // Scroll spy\n      const linkFor = id => subnav.querySelector(`[data-sub-target=\"${CSS.escape(id)}\"]`);\n      const obs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\n        entries.forEach(e => {\n          const a = linkFor(e.target.id);\n          if (!a) return;\n          if (e.isIntersecting) {\n            subnav.querySelectorAll(\"a\").forEach(x => x.classList.remove(\"current\"));\n            a.classList.add(\"current\");\n          }\n        });\n      }, { rootMargin: \"-20% 0px -70% 0px\" });\n      heads.forEach(h => obs.observe(h));\n    }\n\n    // Number every page-level h2 in the document using its data-num if present,\n    // otherwise inject section numbers like \"§01.A\" sequentially.\n    const h2s = document.querySelectorAll(\"main h2\");\n    let n = 0;\n    h2s.forEach(h => {\n      if (h.hasAttribute(\"data-num\")) return;\n      n++;\n      const letter = String.fromCharCode(64 + n); // A, B, C\n      const ts = (document.body.dataset.page || \"\").match(/(\\d{3})/);\n      const docNum = ts ? ts[1].slice(1) : \"00\";\n      h.setAttribute(\"data-num\", `§${docNum}.${letter}`);\n    });\n  }\n\n  document.addEventListener(\"DOMContentLoaded\", build);\n})();\n",

The sidebar HTML is identical across pages,\n// and a `data-page` attribute on <body> selects the active entry.\n\n(function () {\n  const pages = [\n    { num: \"00\",  href: \"index.html\",                   title: \"Contents\" },\n    { num: \"01\",  href: \"001-architecture.html\",        title: \"Architecture\" },\n    { num: \"02\",  href: \"002-roadmap.html\",             title: \"Roadmap\" },\n    { num: \"03\",  href: \"003-driver-system.html\",       title: \"Driver System\" },\n    { num: \"04\",  href: \"004-ipc-and-threading.html\",   title: \"IPC & Threading\" },\n    { num: \"05\",  href: \"005-language-specs.html\",      title: \"Language Specs\" },\n  ];\n\n  function build() {\n    const aside = document.querySelector(\".sidebar\");\n    if (!aside) return;\n\n    const current = document.body.dataset.page || \"\";\n\n    const brand = `\n      <a href=\"index.html\" class=\"brand\">\n        <span class=\"mark\"><em class=\"accent\">Sora</em>Mech</span>\n        <span class=\"sub\">Notebook · vol. one</span>\n      </a>`;\n\n    const tocItems = pages.map(p => {\n      const isCurrent = (p.href === current) ? \" current\" : \"\";\n      return `\n        <li>\n          <a class=\"page-link${isCurrent}\" href=\"${p.href}\">\n            <span class=\"num\">§${p.num}</span>\n            <span class=\"title\">${p.title}</span>\n          </a>\n          ${isCurrent ? `<ul class=\"toc-subnav\" data-subnav></ul>` : ``}\n        </li>`;\n    }).join(\"\");\n\n    const foot = `\n      <div class=\"sidebar-foot\">\n        <div>Source: <a href=\"../\">../docs/</a></div>\n        <div>Last assembled by lamplight.</div>\n        <div style=\"margin-top:0.6rem;\">\n          <span class=\"scribble\" style=\"display:block; font-size:0.95rem; transform:rotate(-2deg)\">strings flow like ink ↗</span>\n        </div>\n      </div>`;\n\n    aside.innerHTML = `\n      ${brand}\n      <span class=\"toc-label\">Documents</span>\n      <ul class=\"toc-list\">${tocItems}</ul>\n      ${foot}\n    `;\n\n    // Sub-nav from page <h2> elements\n    const subnav = aside.querySelector(\"[data-subnav]\");\n    if (subnav) {\n      const heads = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(\"main h2[id]\"));\n      subnav.innerHTML = heads.map(h =>\n        `<li><a href=\"#${h.id}\" data-sub-target=\"${h.id}\">${h.textContent.trim()}</a></li>`\n      ).join(\"\");\n\n      // Scroll spy\n      const linkFor = id => subnav.querySelector(`[data-sub-target=\"${CSS.escape(id)}\"]`);\n      const obs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\n        entries.forEach(e => {\n          const a = linkFor(e.target.id);\n          if (!a) return;\n          if (e.isIntersecting) {\n            subnav.querySelectorAll(\"a\").forEach(x => x.classList.remove(\"current\"));\n            a.classList.add(\"current\");\n          }\n        });\n      }, { rootMargin: \"-20% 0px -70% 0px\" });\n      heads.forEach(h => obs.observe(h));\n    }\n\n    // Number every page-level h2 in the document using its data-num if present,\n    // otherwise inject section numbers like \"§01.A\" sequentially.\n    const h2s = document.querySelectorAll(\"main h2\");\n    let n = 0;\n    h2s.forEach(h => {\n      if (h.hasAttribute(\"data-num\")) return;\n      n++;\n      const letter = String.fromCharCode(64 + n);           "content":"/* SoraMech interactive demos.\n   Drop a <div data-demo=\"<name>\"></div> into a page; this script\n   initializes it on DOMContentLoaded. Each demo is self-contained,\n   uses inline SVG where it makes sense, and shares the design tokens\n   from style.css via CSS variables. */\n\n(function () {\n\n  const NS = \"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\";\n  const svg = (tag, attrs = {}, children = []) => {\n    const el = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) el.setAttribute(k, v);\n    (Array.isArray(children) ? children : [children]).forEach(c => {\n      if (c == null) return;\n      el.appendChild(typeof c === \"string\" ? document.createTextNode(c) : c);\n    });\n    return el;\n  };\n  const el = (tag, attrs = {}, children = []) => {\n    const e = document.createElement(tag);\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) {\n      if (k === \"class\") e.className = v;\n      else if (k === \"html\") e.innerHTML = v;\n      else if (k.startsWith(\"on\") && typeof v === \"function\") e.addEventListener(k.slice(2), v);\n      else e.setAttribute(k, v);\n    }\n    (Array.isArray(children) ? children : [children]).forEach(c => {\n      if (c == null) return;\n      e.appendChild(typeof c === \"string\" ? document.createTextNode(c) : c);\n    });\n    return e;\n  };\n  const frame = (label, hint, body, foot) => {\n    const wrap = el(\"div\", { class: \"demo\" });\n    const head = el(\"div\", { class: \"demo-head\" }, [\n      el(\"span\", { class: \"label\" }, label),\n      hint ? el(\"span\", { class: \"hint\" }, hint) : null,\n    ]);\n    const b = el(\"div\", { class: \"demo-body\" }, body);\n    const f = foot ? el(\"div\", { class: \"demo-foot\" }, foot) : null;\n    wrap.append(head, b);\n    if (f) wrap.appendChild(f);\n    return wrap;\n  };\n\n  const demos = {};\n\n  /* ─── three-program architecture diagram ─────────────────── */\n  demos.threeProgram = (host) => {\n    const W = 720, H = 360;\n    const root = svg(\"svg\", { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${H}` });\n\n    // Lamp glow\n    root.appendChild(svg(\"defs\", {}, [\n      (() => {\n        const r = svg(\"radialGradient\", { id: \"tp-glow\", cx: \"20%\", cy: \"0%\", r: \"70%\" });\n        r.appendChild(svg(\"stop\", { offset: \"0%\", \"stop-color\": \"var(--amber)\", \"stop-opacity\": \"0.12\" }));\n        r.appendChild(svg(\"stop\", { offset: \"100%\", \"stop-color\": \"var(--amber)\", \"stop-opacity\": \"0\" }));\n        return r;\n      })()\n    ]));\n    root.appendChild(svg(\"rect\", { x: 0, y: 0, width: W, height: H, fill: \"url(#tp-glow)\" }));\n\n    // Nodes\n    const nodes = [\n      { id: \"browser\",  x: 100, y: 60,  w: 180, h: 70, title: \"Browser\",            sub: \"assets/index.html\", role: \"Editor — canvas, inspector, file browser. Talks HTTP to the server.\" },\n      { id: \"server\",   x: 100, y: 200, w: 180, h: 70, title: \"src/006-server-main.lua\", sub: \"HTTP file CRUD\",     role: \"Thin file proxy. No logic beyond path validation. No runner knowledge.\" },\n      { id: \"map\",      x: 340, y: 130, w: 200, h: 110, title: \"[ map directory ]\",  sub: \"maps/<name>/\",       role: \"boxes/  data/  src/  compiled/  tmp/.  The only shared contract.\" },\n      { id: \"runner\",   x: 590, y: 60,  w: 130, h: 100, title: \"Phase 2\",            sub: \"007-runner-main.lua\", role: \"Synchronous Lua interpreter. Drivers via shell-out.\" },\n      { id: \"pool\",     x: 590, y: 220, w: 130, h: 100, title: \"Phase 3\",            sub: \"soramech-pool (C)\",   role: \"C thread pool. Specs via dlopen. Per-input-port slot store.\" },\n    ];\n\n    const nodeEls = {};\n\n    nodes.forEach(n => {\n      const g = svg(\"g\", { class: \"tp-node\", \"data-id\": n.id, style: \"cursor:pointer\" });\n      const r = svg(\"rect\", {\n        x: n.x, y: n.y, width: n.w, height: n.h,\n        rx: 2, ry: 2,\n        fill: \"var(--ink-card)\",\n        stroke: \"var(--ink-rim)\",\n        \"stroke-width\": 1\n      });\n      const t = svg(\"text\", { x: n.x + 14, y: n.y + 26, class: \"label-serif\", \"font-size\": 15, fill: \"var(--cream)\" }, n.title);\n      const s = svg(\"text\", { x: n.x + 14, y: n.y + 44, class: \"label-mono\" }, n.sub);\n      g.append(r, t, s);\n      root.appendChild(g);\n      nodeEls[n.id] = { g, r, n };\n    });\n\n    // Wires\n    const wires = [\n      { from: \"browser\", to: \"server\",  curve: \"down\",   label: \"HTTP\" },\n      { from: \"server\",  to: \"map\",     curve: \"right\",  label: \"reads / writes\" },\n      { from: \"map\",     to: \"runner\",  curve: \"right\",  label: \"map dir\" },\n      { from: \"map\",     to: \"pool\",    curve: \"right\",  label: \"map dir\" },\n      { from: \"pool\",    to: \"map\",     curve: \"left\",   label: \"tmp/last-run.jsonl\", dashed: true },\n    ];\n\n    const wireGroup = svg(\"g\", {});\n    root.appendChild(wireGroup);\n\n    const wirePath = (a, b, kind) => {\n      const sx = a.x + a.w, sy = a.y + a.h / 2;\n      const tx = b.x,        ty = b.y + b.h / 2;\n      // simple S curve\n      const dx = (tx - sx) / 2;\n      return `M ${sx} ${sy} C ${sx + dx} ${sy}, ${tx - dx} ${ty}, ${tx} ${ty}`;\n    };\n\n    wires.forEach(w => {\n      const a = nodeEls[w.from].n, b = nodeEls[w.to].n;\n      let d;\n      if (w.from === \"browser\" && w.to === \"server\") {\n        d = `M ${a.x + a.w / 2} ${a.y + a.h} L ${b.x + b.w / 2} ${b.y}`;\n      } else if (w.from === \"pool\" && w.to === \"map\") {\n        const sx = b.x + b.w, sy = a.y + a.h / 2;\n        const tx = a.x,        ty = sy;\n        d = `M ${a.x} ${a.y + a.h / 2} C ${a.x - 40} ${a.y + a.h / 2}, ${b.x + b.w + 60} ${b.y + b.h + 30}, ${b.x + b.w / 2 + 20} ${b.y + b.h}`;\n      } else {\n        d = wirePath(a, b);\n      }\n      const p = svg(\"path\", {\n        d,\n        stroke: w.dashed ? \"var(--copper)\" : \"var(--amber)\",\n        \"stroke-width\": 1.4,\n        \"stroke-dasharray\": w.dashed ? \"4 3\" : \"none\",\n        fill: \"none\",\n        opacity: 0.55,\n        \"data-wire\": `${w.from}-${w.to}`\n      });\n      wireGroup.appendChild(p);\n      if (w.label) {\n        const m = p.getPointAtLength ? null : null; // skip — set after mount\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Side panel detail\n    const detail = el(\"div\", { class: \"tp-detail\" }, [\n      el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [\n        el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"selected\"), el(\"span\", { class: \"v amber\" }, \"hover a node ↗\")\n      ]),\n      el(\"p\", { class: \"tiny dim\", style: \"margin:0.6rem 0 0; min-height: 4.5em; line-height:1.5\" }, \"Three independent programs share the map directory. None knows about the others at runtime — the directory format is the only shared contract.\"),\n    ]);\n\n    Object.values(nodeEls).forEach(({ g, r, n }) => {\n      g.addEventListener(\"mouseenter\", () => {\n        r.setAttribute(\"stroke\", \"var(--amber)\");\n        r.setAttribute(\"fill\", \"var(--ink-paper)\");\n        wireGroup.querySelectorAll(\"path\").forEach(p => {\n          const wid = p.getAttribute(\"data-wire\");\n          if (wid && (wid.startsWith(n.id + \"-\") || wid.endsWith(\"-\" + n.id))) {\n            p.setAttribute(\"opacity\", \"1\");\n            p.setAttribute(\"stroke-width\", \"2.2\");\n          } else {\n            p.setAttribute(\"opacity\", \"0.18\");\n          }\n        });\n        detail.querySelector(\".kvline .v\").textContent = n.title;\n        detail.querySelector(\"p\").textContent = n.role;\n      });\n      g.addEventListener(\"mouseleave\", () => {\n        r.setAttribute(\"stroke\", \"var(--ink-rim)\");\n        r.setAttribute(\"fill\", \"var(--ink-card)\");\n        wireGroup.querySelectorAll(\"path\").forEach(p => {\n          p.setAttribute(\"opacity\", \"0.55\");\n          p.setAttribute(\"stroke-width\", \"1.4\");\n        });\n      });\n    });\n\n    host.appendChild(frame(\n      \"FIG · three-program architecture\",\n      \"hover the parts ↘\",\n      [\n        el(\"div\", { style: \"display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 220px;gap:1.3rem\" }, [\n          el(\"div\", {}, root),\n          detail,\n        ])\n      ],\n      el(\"span\", {}, [\n        document.createTextNode(\"Server never knows about runner. Runner never knows about server. \"),\n        el(\"span\", { class: \"amber\" }, \"Phase 2\"),\n        document.createTextNode(\" retires when \"),\n        el(\"span\", { class: \"amber\" }, \"Phase 3\"),\n        document.createTextNode(\" lands; box JSON unchanged.\"),\n      ])\n    ));\n  };\n\n  /* ─── routing kinds explorer ─────────────────────────────── */\n  demos.routingExplorer = (host) => {\n    const state = {\n      kind: \"plain\",\n      counter: 0,\n      lastValue: 4,\n      lastBranch: -1,\n      log: [],\n    };\n\n    const kinds = [\n      { id: \"plain\",       label: \"plain\",       n: 1 },\n      { id: \"comparator\",  label: \"comparator\",  n: 3, comparand: 4 },\n      { id: \"iterator\",    label: \"iterator\",    n: 4 },\n      { id: \"randomizer\",  label: \"randomizer\",  n: 4 },\n      { id: \"weighted\",    label: \"weighted\",    n: 3, weights: [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] },\n      { id: \"distributor\", label: \"distributor\", n: 3, fills: [2, 0, 1] },\n    ];\n\n    const branchNames = (k) => {\n      if (k.id === \"plain\") return [\"out\"];\n      if (k.id === \"comparator\") return [\"lt\", \"eq\", \"gt\"];\n      return Array.from({ length: k.n }, (_, i) => `out_${i}`);\n    };\n\n    const seg = el(\"div\", { class: \"seg\" }, kinds.map(k => {\n      const b = el(\"button\", { type: \"button\" }, k.label);\n      if (k.id === state.kind) b.classList.add(\"active\");\n      b.addEventListener(\"click\", () => {\n        state.kind = k.id;\n        state.counter = 0;\n        state.log = [];\n        seg.querySelectorAll(\"button\").forEach(x => x.classList.remove(\"active\"));\n        b.classList.add(\"active\");\n        redraw();\n      });\n      return b;\n    }));\n\n    const stage = el(\"div\", {});\n    const sidebar = el(\"div\", {});\n\n    const fire = () => {\n      const k = kinds.find(x => x.id === state.kind);\n      const branches = branchNames(k);\n      let idx;\n      if (k.id === \"plain\") {\n        idx = \"*\"; // all\n      } else if (k.id === \"comparator\") {\n        const v = state.lastValue;\n        idx = v < k.comparand ? 0 : (v === k.comparand ? 1 : 2);\n      } else if (k.id === \"iterator\") {\n        idx = state.counter % k.n;\n        state.counter++;\n      } else if (k.id === \"randomizer\") {\n        const c = state.counter++;\n        // small mixing hash\n        let h = (c ^ 0x9e3779b9) >>> 0;\n        h = ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) * 0x85ebca6b) >>> 0;\n        idx = h % k.n;\n      } else if (k.id === \"weighted\") {\n        const c = state.counter++;\n        const PR = 1000;\n        const r = c % PR;\n        let acc = 0;\n        idx = 0;\n        for (let i = 0; i < k.n; i++) {\n          acc += k.weights[i] * PR;\n          if (r < acc) { idx = i; break; }\n        }\n      } else if (k.id === \"distributor\") {\n        let min = Infinity;\n        idx = 0;\n        for (let i = 0; i < k.n; i++) if (k.fills[i] < min) { min = k.fills[i]; idx = i; }\n        k.fills[idx]++;\n      }\n      state.lastBranch = idx;\n      state.log.unshift({ step: state.log.length + 1, k: k.id, idx, v: state.lastValue });\n      if (state.log.length > 5) state.log.pop();\n      redraw();\n    };\n\n    const redraw = () => {\n      const k = kinds.find(x => x.id === state.kind);\n      const branches = branchNames(k);\n\n      // Stage SVG\n      const W = 460, H = 230;\n      const root = svg(\"svg\", { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${H}` });\n\n      // Producer box\n      const px = 30, py = H/2 - 30, pw = 110, ph = 60;\n      const pg = svg(\"g\", {});\n      pg.appendChild(svg(\"rect\", { x: px, y: py, width: pw, height: ph, fill: \"var(--ink-card)\", stroke: \"var(--amber)\", \"stroke-width\": 1.4, rx: 2 }));\n      pg.appendChild(svg(\"text\", { x: px + 12, y: py + 24, class: \"label-serif\", \"font-size\": 13, fill: \"var(--cream)\" }, \"score()\"));\n      pg.appendChild(svg(\"text\", { x: px + 12, y: py + 42, class: \"label-mono\" }, `routing: ${k.id}`));\n      root.appendChild(pg);\n\n      // Output dot(s)\n      const outX = px + pw;\n      const branchY = (i) => 40 + (i + 0.5) * (H - 80) / branches.length;\n\n      branches.forEach((bn, i) => {\n        const cy = branchY(i);\n        const cx = outX + 8;\n        const isFired = state.lastBranch === i || (state.lastBranch === \"*\" && k.id === \"plain\");\n        const colour = isFired ? \"var(--amber)\" : \"var(--cream-faint)\";\n\n        // wire\n        root.appendChild(svg(\"path\", {\n          d: `M ${outX} ${py + ph/2} C ${outX + 40} ${py + ph/2}, ${cx + 50} ${cy}, ${cx + 120} ${cy}`,\n          stroke: colour,\n          \"stroke-width\": isFired ? 2.2 : 1,\n          fill: \"none\",\n          opacity: isFired ? 0.95 : 0.4\n        }));\n\n        // branch port\n        root.appendChild(svg(\"circle\", { cx: cx, cy: py + ph/2, r: 4, fill: colour }));\n\n        // consumer box\n        const conX = cx + 120, conY = cy - 16;\n        root.appendChild(svg(\"rect\", { x: conX, y: conY, width: 96, height: 32, fill: \"var(--ink-card)\", stroke: isFired ? \"var(--amber)\" : \"var(--ink-rim)\", rx: 2 }));\n        root.appendChild(svg(\"text\", { x: conX + 10, y: conY + 20, class: \"label-mono\", fill: isFired ? \"var(--amber)\" : \"var(--cream-faint)\" }, `→ ${bn}`));\n\n        // animated pulse along wire when fired\n        if (isFired) {\n          const pulse = svg(\"circle\", { r: 3.5, fill: \"var(--gold)\" });\n          pulse.appendChild(svg(\"animateMotion\", {\n            dur: \"0.6s\",\n            repeatCount: \"1\",\n            path: `M ${outX} ${py + ph/2} C ${outX + 40} ${py + ph/2}, ${cx + 50} ${cy}, ${cx + 120} ${cy}`\n          }));\n          root.appendChild(pulse);\n        }\n      });\n\n      stage.replaceChildren(root);\n\n      // Sidebar\n      const lines = [\n        el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"kind\"),     el(\"span\", { class: \"v amber\" }, k.id)]),\n        el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"branches\"), el(\"span\", { class: \"v\" }, branches.join(\" / \"))]),\n      ];\n      if (k.id === \"comparator\") {\n        lines.push(el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"comparand\"), el(\"span\", { class: \"v\" }, String(k.comparand))]));\n        lines.push(el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"f(x)\"), el(\"span\", { class: \"v copper\" }, String(state.lastValue))]));\n      }\n      if (k.id === \"iterator\" || k.id === \"randomizer\" || k.id === \"weighted\") {\n        lines.push(el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, \"counter\"), el(\"span\", { class: \"v amber\" }, String(state.counter))]));\n      }\n      if (k.id === \"weighted\") {\n        k.weights.forEach((w, i) => lines.push(\n          el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, `out_${i}`), el(\"span\", { class: \"v\" }, `${(w*100)|0}%`)])\n        ));\n      }\n      if (k.id === \"distributor\") {\n        k.fills.forEach((v, i) => lines.push(\n          el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, `out_${i} fill`), el(\"span\", { class: \"v copper\" }, String(v))])\n        ));\n      }\n      sidebar.replaceChildren(...lines);\n    };\n\n    // Comparator input\n    const cmpInput = el(\"div\", { style: \"display:flex; gap:0.8rem; align-items:center; margin-top:0.7rem;\" }, [\n      el(\"span\", { class: \"mono dim tiny\" }, \"f(x) returns:\"),\n      (() => {\n        const inp = el(\"input\", { type: \"number\", value: \"4\", style: \"width:64px; background:var(--ink-card); color:var(--cream); border:1px solid var(--ink-rim); padding:0.3rem 0.5rem; font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:0.85rem;\" });\n        inp.addEventListener(\"input\", () => { state.lastValue = Number(inp.value) || 0; redraw(); });\n        return inp;\n      })(),\n    ]);\n\n    const controls = el(\"div\", { class: \"row\", style: \"margin-top:0.6rem\" }, [\n      el(\"button\", { class: \"btn solid\", onclick: fire }, \"↺ spawn task\"),\n      el(\"button\", { class: \"btn ghost\", onclick: () => { state.counter = 0; state.log = []; redraw(); } }, \"reset\"),\n    ]);\n\n    const body = el(\"div\", { style: \"display:grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 200px; gap:1.4rem\" }, [\n      el(\"div\", {}, [\n        el(\"p\", { class: \"tiny dim\", style: \"margin-bottom:0.8rem\" }, \"Pick a routing kind, then fire the box. The same function runs every time — only the routing decision changes.\"),\n        seg,\n        stage,\n        cmpInput,\n        controls,\n      ]),\n      el(\"div\", {}, [\n        el(\"h4\", {}, \"live state\"),\n        sidebar,\n      ])\n    ]);\n\n    host.appendChild(frame(\n      \"WORKBENCH · routing kinds\",\n      \"fire the box ↘\",\n      [body],\n      \"Issue 233 unified the schema. Every call box carries routing.kind explicitly.\"\n    ));\n\n    redraw();\n  };\n\n  /* ─── weighted slider ────────────────────────────────────── */\n  demos.weighted = (host) => {\n    let weights = [0.55, 0.25, 0.20]; // initial\n    const N = 3;\n    const COLOURS = [\"var(--amber)\", \"var(--copper)\", \"var(--gold)\"];\n\n    const draw = () => {\n      const total = weights.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);\n      const norm = weights.map(w => w / total);\n      bar.replaceChildren();\n      let acc = 0;\n      norm.forEach((w, i) => {\n        const seg = el(\"div\", {\n          style: `width:${w*100}%; background:${COLOURS[i]}; height:100%; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; color:var(--ink-deep); font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:0.74rem; font-weight:600; transition:width 200ms;`\n        }, w > 0.06 ? `out_${i}` : \"\");\n        bar.appendChild(seg);\n        acc += w;\n      });\n\n      // breakdown\n      rows.replaceChildren();\n      norm.forEach((w, i) => {\n        const row = el(\"div\", { style: \"display:grid; grid-template-columns: 70px 1fr 60px; gap:0.6rem; align-items:center; margin: 0.4rem 0;\" });\n        row.append(\n          el(\"span\", { class: \"mono tiny\", style: `color:${COLOURS[i]}` }, `out_${i}`),\n          (() => {\n            const r = el(\"input\", { type: \"range\", min: \"0\", max: \"100\", value: String((w*100)|0) });\n            r.addEventListener(\"input\", () => {\n              const v = Number(r.value);\n              const others = weights.reduce((a, b, j) => a + (j === i ? 0 : b), 0);\n              if (others > 0) {\n                const remain = 1 - v/100;\n                weights = weights.map((w0, j) => j === i ? v/100 : (w0 / others) * remain);\n              } else {\n                weights[i] = v/100;\n              }\n              draw();\n            });\n            return r;\n          })(),\n          el(\"span\", { class: \"mono tiny amber\", style: \"text-align:right\" }, `${(w*100).toFixed(1)}%`)\n        );\n        rows.appendChild(row);\n      });\n\n      // simulate 1000 invocations, count the histogram\n      const counts = new Array(N).fill(0);\n      const PR = 1000;\n      for (let c = 0; c < 1000; c++) {\n        const r = c % PR;\n        let acc2 = 0, idx = 0;\n        for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n          acc2 += norm[i] * PR;\n          if (r < acc2) { idx = i; break; }\n        }\n        counts[idx]++;\n      }\n      hist.replaceChildren();\n      counts.forEach((c, i) => {\n        hist.appendChild(el(\"div\", { class: \"kvline\" }, [\n          el(\"span\", { class: \"k\" }, `out_${i} (1000 runs)`),\n          el(\"span\", { class: \"v amber\" }, `${c} hits`)\n        ]));\n      });\n    };\n\n    const bar = el(\"div\", { style: \"display:flex; width:100%; height:34px; border:1px solid var(--ink-rim); border-radius:2px; overflow:hidden;\" });\n    const rows = el(\"div\", { style: \"margin-top:1rem;\" });\n    const hist = el(\"div\", { style: \"margin-top:1rem; padding-top:0.8rem; border-top:1px dashed var(--ink-rule);\" });\n\n    host.appendChild(frame(\n      \"INSPECTOR · weighted routing\",\n      \"drag the knobs ↘\",\n      [\n        el(\"p\", { class: \"tiny dim\" }, \"Each output port takes a fraction of invocations.
