    "content":"/* src/009-slot-store.c — per-input-port slot store, implementation.\n *\n * Three slot shapes coexist behind one set of APIs:\n *\n *   - Ring-buffer slots (peek and pop modes) — a header followed by\n *     n_cells cells laid out contiguously. Each cell is a 4-byte\n *     filled_size, optionally a 4-byte tag (for SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED),\n *     then cell_capacity bytes of payload. Untagged slots use the\n *     standard head/tail ring discipline; tagged slots use head/tail\n *     for the bookkeeping of \"where to put the next push\" but pop\n *     scans for the lowest-tag filled cell.\n *\n *   - Atomic-counter slots — no header bookkeeping, no payload cells;\n *     just one atomic_uint that slot_read_inc fetches-and-adds. No\n *     lock needed.\n *\n * Per-slot concurrency is a single atomic_flag spinlock for the\n * ring-buffer slots. Inside the lock the header and cells are mutated\n * without atomics; outside the lock no header bytes are touched.\n *\n * The store itself owns a flat array of slot pointers indexed by\n * slot_id_t. The array grows on demand. Ids are never reused — there\n * is no slot_free; slots live for the run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302. This file implements the API declared in\n * 009-slot-store.h. Free-list optimization and the large-value heap\n * are deferred per the header's \"what's not in this version\" note.\n */\n\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal slot record */\ntypedef struct slot_rec {\n    uint32_t    cell_capacity;   /* bytes per cell payload (ring slots) */\n    uint32_t    n_cells;         /* ring size (ring slots)              */\n    _Atomic uint32_t head;       /* read index, mod n_cells             */\n    _Atomic uint32_t tail;       /* write index, mod n_cells            */\n    atomic_flag lock;            /* per-slot spinlock for header+cells  */\n    uint32_t    flags;           /* SLOT_FLAG_*                         */\n    uint32_t    cell_record;     /* derived: 4 (+4 if tagged) + cap     */\n\n    /* For atomic-counter slots: a single atomic uint, used by\n     * slot_read_inc. Lives separately from `cells` so the two slot\n     * shapes don't share storage interpretation. */\n    _Atomic uint32_t counter;\n\n    /* For ring slots: n_cells * cell_record bytes. Flexible array. */\n    uint8_t     cells[];\n} slot_rec_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Internal store */\nstruct slot_store {\n    slot_rec_t **slots;        /* dynamic array, indexed by slot_id_t */\n    int32_t      count;\n    int32_t      capacity;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — locking */\nstatic inline void lock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n{\n    while (atomic_flag_test_and_set_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_acquire)) {\n        /* spin — contention is expected to be brief because the\n         * locked section is just a header update plus a memcpy. */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline void unlock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n{\n    atomic_flag_clear_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_release);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — cell layout */\n/* Pointer to the i-th cell within the slot's flexible array. The cell\n * record layout for ring slots is:\n *\n *   bytes 0..3   : filled_size (uint32_t; 0 means empty)\n *   bytes 4..7   : tag         (uint32_t; only if SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED)\n *   bytes (4|8)..: payload     (cell_capacity bytes)\n */\nstatic inline uint8_t *cell_ptr(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    return r->cells + (size_t)i * r->cell_record;\n}\n\nstatic inline uint32_t cell_filled(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    uint32_t v;\n    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i), sizeof v);\n    return v;\n}\n\nstatic inline uint32_t cell_tag(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    uint32_t v;\n    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i) + 4, sizeof v);\n    return v;\n}\n\nstatic inline uint8_t *cell_data(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    return cell_ptr(r, i) + ((r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) ? 8 : 4);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_create() */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);\n    if (!s) return NULL;\n    s->capacity = 16;\n    s->slots    = calloc((size_t)s->capacity, sizeof *s->slots);\n    if (!s->slots) { free(s); return NULL; }\n    return s;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_destroy() */\nvoid slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (!s) return;\n    for (int32_t i = 0; i < s->count; i++) {\n        free(s->slots[i]);\n    }\n    free(s->slots);\n    free(s);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_size() */\nint32_t slot_store_size(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    return s ? s->count : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — grow_store_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_store_if_needed(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (s->count < s->capacity) return 0;\n    int32_t new_cap = s->capacity * 2;\n    slot_rec_t **grown = realloc(s->slots, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *grown);\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    memset(grown + s->capacity, 0,\n           (size_t)(new_cap - s->capacity) * sizeof *grown);\n    s->slots    = grown;\n    s->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_alloc() */\nslot_id_t slot_alloc(slot_store_t *s,\n                     int32_t cell_capacity,\n                     int32_t n_cells,\n                     int32_t flags)\n{\n    if (!s) return SLOT_INVALID;\n\n    size_t bytes_cells = 0;\n    uint32_t cell_record = 0;\n\n    if (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) {\n        /* Atomic-counter slot: no ring cells. cell_capacity and\n         * n_cells are ignored. */\n        bytes_cells = 0;\n    } else {\n        if (cell_capacity <= 0 || n_cells <= 0) return SLOT_INVALID;\n        cell_record = (uint32_t)(4\n                                  + ((flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) ? 4 : 0)\n                                  + cell_capacity);\n        bytes_cells = (size_t)n_cells * cell_record;\n    }\n\n    slot_rec_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof(slot_rec_t) + bytes_cells);\n    if (!r) return SLOT_INVALID;\n\n    r->cell_capacity = (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) ? 0 : (uint32_t)cell_capacity;\n    r->n_cells       = (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) ? 0 : (uint32_t)n_cells;\n    r->cell_record   = cell_record;\n    r->flags         = (uint32_t)flags;\n    atomic_init(&r->head,    0u);\n    atomic_init(&r->tail,    0u);\n    atomic_init(&r->counter, 0u);\n    /* atomic_flag has no atomic_flag_init in C11; ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT is\n     * for initializers. Clearing it leaves it in the \"not set\" state. */\n    atomic_flag_clear(&r->lock);\n\n    if (grow_store_if_needed(s) != 0) { free(r); return SLOT_INVALID; }\n    slot_id_t id = s->count++;\n    s->slots[id] = r;\n    return id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0 || id >= s->count) return NULL;\n    return s->slots[id];\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_push() */\nint slot_push(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id,\n              const void *data, int32_t size, uint32_t tag)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                      return -1;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER)     return -1;\n    if (size < 0 || (uint32_t)size > r->cell_capacity) return -1;\n    if (!data && size > 0)                       return -1;\n\n    lock_slot(r);\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_relaxed);\n    if (tail - head >= r->n_cells) {\n        /* Ring full. */\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t i = tail % r->n_cells;\n    uint8_t *cp = cell_ptr(r, i);\n\n    /* filled_size */\n    uint32_t fs = (uint32_t)size;\n    memcpy(cp, &fs, sizeof fs);\n    /* tag (only if tagged) */\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        memcpy(cp + 4, &tag, sizeof tag);\n    }\n    /* payload */\n    if (size > 0) {\n        memcpy(cell_data(r, i), data, (size_t)size);\n    }\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&r->tail, tail + 1u, memory_order_release);\n    unlock_slot(r);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_peek() */\nint32_t slot_peek(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id,\n                  void *buf, int32_t buf_size)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                  return -1;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return -1;\n    if (buf_size < 0 || (!buf && buf_size > 0)) return -1;\n\n    lock_slot(r);\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n    if (head == tail) {\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t i = head % r->n_cells;\n    uint32_t fs = cell_filled(r, i);\n    if (fs == 0) {\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if ((uint32_t)buf_size < fs) {\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (fs > 0) memcpy(buf, cell_data(r, i), fs);\n    /* head not advanced — peek leaves the cell in place. */\n    unlock_slot(r);\n    return (int32_t)fs;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — find_lowest_tag_index() */\n/* Return the in-ring cell index with the lowest tag among filled\n * cells. The caller holds the slot lock. Returns UINT32_MAX if no\n * filled cells exist. */\nstatic uint32_t find_lowest_tag_index(slot_rec_t *r)\n{\n    uint32_t best     = UINT32_MAX;\n    uint32_t best_tag = UINT32_MAX;\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r->n_cells; i++) {\n        if (cell_filled(r, i) == 0) continue;\n        uint32_t t = cell_tag(r, i);\n        if (best == UINT32_MAX || t < best_tag) {\n            best     = i;\n            best_tag = t;\n        }\n    }\n    return best;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_pop() */\nint32_t slot_pop(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id,\n                 void *buf, int32_t buf_size)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                  return -1;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return -1;\n    if (buf_size < 0 || (!buf && buf_size > 0)) return -1;\n\n    lock_slot(r);\n\n    uint32_t pick;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        pick = find_lowest_tag_index(r);\n        if (pick == UINT32_MAX) { unlock_slot(r); return -1; }\n    } else {\n        uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n        uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n        if (head == tail) { unlock_slot(r); return -1; }\n        pick = head % r->n_cells;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t fs = cell_filled(r, pick);\n    if (fs == 0)                  { unlock_slot(r); return -1; }\n    if ((uint32_t)buf_size < fs)  { unlock_slot(r); return -1; }\n\n    if (fs > 0) memcpy(buf, cell_data(r, pick), fs);\n\n    /* Mark cell empty. */\n    uint32_t zero = 0;\n    memcpy(cell_ptr(r, pick), &zero, sizeof zero);\n\n    /* For untagged: advance head by one. For tagged: walk head\n     * forward over any contiguous empty cells (the head/tail\n     * relationship is preserved so further pushes still land at the\n     * right spot, but stale empties at the front of the ring don't\n     * block future pushes that wrap). */\n    if (!(r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED)) {\n        uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_relaxed);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&r->head, head + 1u, memory_order_release);\n    } else {\n        uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_relaxed);\n        uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_relaxed);\n        while (head < tail && cell_filled(r, head % r->n_cells) == 0) {\n            head++;\n        }\n        atomic_store_explicit(&r->head, head, memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    unlock_slot(r);\n    return (int32_t)fs;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_read_inc() */\nuint32_t slot_read_inc(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, uint32_t mod)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                     return UINT32_MAX;\n    if (!(r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER)) return UINT32_MAX;\n    if (mod == 0)                               return UINT32_MAX;\n\n    uint32_t prev = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&r->counter, 1u,\n                                              memory_order_relaxed);\n    return prev % mod;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_has_value() */\nint slot_has_value(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r) return 0;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return 1;\n\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        /* Tagged: any filled cell counts. Cheap scan; tagged slots\n         * are usually small. */\n        lock_slot(r);\n        int found = 0;\n        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r->n_cells; i++) {\n            if (cell_filled(r, i) != 0) { found = 1; break; }\n        }\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return found;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n    return head != tail;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_fill_count() */\nint32_t slot_fill_count(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                  return 0;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return 0;\n\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        lock_slot(r);\n        int32_t n = 0;\n        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r->n_cells; i++) {\n            if (cell_filled(r, i) != 0) n++;\n        }\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return n;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n    return (int32_t)(tail - head);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

The dispatch\nlayer reads and writes through this API; language specs never see\nslot IDs (issue 303 keeps that boundary clean).\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `slot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)` — empty store; NULL on OOM.\n- `void slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)` — frees every slot.\n\n## Allocation\n\n- `slot_id_t slot_alloc(store, cell_capacity, n_cells, flags)`\n  - Returns `SLOT_INVALID` on bad args / OOM.\n  - Flags: `SLOT_FLAG_NONE`, `SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED`, `SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER`.\n  - `cell_capacity` and `n_cells` are ignored for atomic-counter slots.\n\n## Ring-buffer ops (push / peek / pop / has_value / fill_count)\n\n- `int slot_push(store, id, data, size, tag)` — 0 on success, -1 on\n  full / wrong type / size too big.\n- `int32_t slot_peek(store, id, buf, buf_size)` — returns the cell's\n  filled_size on success; -1 on empty / wrong type / buf too small.\n  Does not advance head. Used for 1-cell peek slots.\n- `int32_t slot_pop(store, id, buf, buf_size)` — drains. Untagged\n  pops head FIFO; tagged pops the lowest-tag filled cell.\n- `int slot_has_value(store, id)` — 1 if a value is available.\n- `int32_t slot_fill_count(store, id)` — number of filled cells.\n\n## Atomic-counter slot\n\n- `uint32_t slot_read_inc(store, id, mod)` — fetch-and-add. Returns\n  the pre-increment counter value mod the supplied bound.\n  `UINT32_MAX` on wrong type or `mod == 0`.\n\n## Thread safety\n\n- The atomic-counter slot uses `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`; no lock.\n- Ring-buffer slots use a per-slot `atomic_flag` spinlock around\n  header + cell mutations.\n- The store itself is single-threaded for allocation (graph-load\n  phase); after that, the slot array is read-only and per-slot\n  operations run concurrently.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- Size-class free lists / coalescing — plain `malloc` per slot for\n  now. The current usage pattern doesn't reuse slot memory, so\n  optimization buys nothing yet.\n- Large-value heap for variable-size payloads. Follow-on within\n  issue 302.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 302 — design.\n- Issue 304 — the dispatch layer that calls this API.\n- Issue 301 — the pool whose workers contend on these slots.\n",

idempotent.\n *   - N-cell pop slot (untagged, FIFO): push N values, pop them\n *     out in order, ring is empty.\n *   - Ring-full / empty edge cases.\n *   - Tagged pop: out-of-order pushes are popped in tag order.\n *   - Atomic-counter slot: read-and-increment, modulus, concurrent\n *     unique-value guarantee.\n *   - Concurrent push/pop on an N-cell untagged ring across two\n *     threads (smoke test for the per-slot spinlock).\n */\n\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_peek_1cell() */\nstatic int test_peek_1cell(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    ASSERT(s);\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 32, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n    ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n    ASSERT(slot_has_value(s, id) == 0);\n\n    const char *msg = \"hello\";\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, msg, 5, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_has_value(s, id) == 1);\n\n    char buf[32];\n    /* Peek as many times as we like — head doesn't move. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {\n        memset(buf, 0, sizeof buf);\n        int32_t got = slot_peek(s, id, buf, sizeof buf);\n        ASSERT(got == 5);\n        ASSERT(memcmp(buf, \"hello\", 5) == 0);\n        ASSERT(slot_has_value(s, id) == 1);\n    }\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pop_fifo_ncell() */\nstatic int test_pop_fifo_ncell(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 8, 4, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n    ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n\n    const char *vals[] = {\"a\", \"bb\", \"ccc\", \"dddd\"};\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n        ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, vals[i], (int)strlen(vals[i]), 0) == 0);\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_fill_count(s, id) == 4);\n    /* Ring full — fifth push should fail. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, \"eeeee\", 5, 0) == -1);\n\n    char buf[16];\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n        memset(buf, 0, sizeof buf);\n        int32_t got = slot_pop(s, id, buf, sizeof buf);\n        ASSERT(got == (int32_t)strlen(vals[i]));\n        ASSERT(memcmp(buf, vals[i], (size_t)got) == 0);\n    }\n    /* Empty — pop fails. */\n    ASSERT(slot_pop(s, id, buf, sizeof buf) == -1);\n    ASSERT(slot_has_value(s, id) == 0);\n\n    /* Push again after drain — wrap-around. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, \"wrap\", 4, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_pop(s, id, buf, sizeof buf) == 4);\n    ASSERT(memcmp(buf, \"wrap\", 4) == 0);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_buf_too_small() */\nstatic int test_buf_too_small(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 16, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, \"hello world\", 11, 0) == 0);\n\n    char buf[4];\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, id, buf, 4) == -1);\n    /* But large enough should succeed. */\n    char big[32];\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, id, big, sizeof big) == 11);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_size_too_big_push() */\nstatic int test_size_too_big_push(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 2, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n    /* cell_capacity = 4, ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, \"B\", 1, 2) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, \"D\", 1, 4) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_fill_count(s, id) == 4);\n\n    char buf[2];\n    /* Pop should return in tag order: 1, 2, for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {\n        uint32_t v = slot_read_inc(s, id, 3);\n        ASSERT(v == (uint32_t)(i % 3));\n    }\n    /* push / peek / pop must reject this slot type. */\n    char  slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 0, 0, SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n    ASSERT(slot_read_inc(s, id, 0) == UINT32_MAX);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return    ASSERT(slot_pop (s, -1, buf, 4)    == -1);\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, 99, buf, 4)    == -1);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Concurrent counter — N threads, M reads each, all unique */\nstruct counter_args {\n    slot_store_t *store;\n    slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n    uint32_t     *out;\n};\n\nstatic void *counter_worker(void *arg)\n{\n    struct counter_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        a->out[i] = slot_read_inc(a->store, a->id, UINT32_MAX);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int cmp_u32(const void *l, const void *r)\n{\n    uint32_t lv = *(const uint32_t *)l, rv = *(const uint32_t *)r;\n    return (lv < rv) ? -1 : (lv > rv) ? 1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_counter(void)\n{\n    enum { N_THREADS = 8, N_READS = 1000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 0, 0, SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n\n    pthread_t   threads[N_THREADS];\n    uint32_t    out[N_THREADS * N_READS];\n    struct counter_args args[N_THREADS];\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        args[t].store = s;\n        args[t].id    = id;\n        args[t].n     = N_READS;\n        args[t].out   = out + t * N_READS;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, counter_worker, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    /* Every value must be unique and cover 0..N_THREADS*N_READS-1. */\n    qsort(out, N_THREADS * N_READS, sizeof out[0], cmp_u32);\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < N_THREADS * N_READS; i++) slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n};\n\nstatic void *producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* Spin if ring full; producer/consumer race intentionally. */\n        while (slot_push(a->store, a->id, &i, (int)sizeof i, 0) != 0) {\n            /* busy-wait */\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void *consumer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    int seen = 0;\n    int sum  = 0;\n    while (seen < a->n) {\n        int v;\n        if (slot_pop(a->store, a->id, &v, (int)sizeof v) > 0) test_concurrent_push_pop(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, (int)sizeof(int), 16, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n\n    struct prod_args pa = { s, id, N };\n    struct prod_args ca = { s, id, N };\n    pthread_t tp, tc;\n    pthread_create(&tp, NULL, producer, &pa);\n    pthread_create(&tc, NULL, consumer, &ca);\n    pthread_join(tp, NULL);\n    pthread_join(tc, NULL);\n\n    /* Consumer summed every value it read. The producer pushed\n     * 0..N-1, so the expected total is N*(N-1)/2. The \"sum\" was\n     * stashed into ca.n (yes, ugly). */\n    int expected = N * (N - 1) / 2;\n    ASSERT(ca.n == expected);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"009-slot-store-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(peek_1cell);\n    RUN(pop_fifo_ncell);\n    RUN(buf_too_small);\n    RUN(size_too_big_push);\n    RUN(tagged_pop_lowest_first);\n    RUN(tagged_interleaved);\n    RUN(atomic_counter);\n    RUN(atomic_counter_mod_zero);\n    RUN(bad_slot_id);\n    RUN(concurrent_counter);\n    RUN(concurrent_push_pop);\n    RUN(store_size_growth);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "type":"create",

Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n# }}}\n",

          "old_string":"/* {{{ Concurrent push/pop on an N-cell ring */\nstruct prod_args {\n    slot_store_t *store;\n    slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n};\n\nstatic void *producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* Spin if ring full; producer/consumer race intentionally. */\n        while (slot_push(a->store, a->id, &i, (int)sizeof i, 0) != 0) {\n            /* busy-wait */\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void *consumer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    int seen = 0;\n    int sum  = 0;\n    while (seen < a->n) {\n        int v;\n        if (slot_pop(a->store, a->id, &v, (int)sizeof v) > 0) {\n            sum += v;\n            seen++;\n        }\n    }\n    *(int *)arg = sum;   /* abuse: write sum back through arg.n field */\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_push_pop(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, (int)sizeof(int), 16, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n\n    struct prod_args pa = { s, id, N };\n    struct prod_args ca = { s, id, N };\n    pthread_t tp, tc;\n    pthread_create(&tp, NULL, producer, &pa);\n    pthread_create(&tc, NULL, consumer, &ca);\n    pthread_join(tp, NULL);\n    pthread_join(tc, NULL);\n\n    /* Consumer summed every value it read. The producer pushed\n     * 0..N-1, so the expected total is N*(N-1)/2. The \"sum\" was\n     * stashed into ca.n (yes, ugly). */\n    int expected = N * (N - 1) / 2;\n    ASSERT(ca.n == expected);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ Concurrent push/pop on an N-cell ring */\nstruct prod_args {\n    slot_store_t *store;\n    slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n    int           sum;   /* consumer writes the running total here */\n};\n\nstatic void *producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* Spin if ring full; producer/consumer race intentionally. */\n        while (slot_push(a->store, a->id, &i, (int)sizeof i, 0) != 0) {\n            /* busy-wait */\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void *consumer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    int seen = 0;\n    while (seen < a->n) {\n        int v;\n        if (slot_pop(a->store, a->id, &v, (int)sizeof v) > 0) {\n            a->sum += v;\n            seen++;\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_push_pop(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, (int)sizeof(int), 16, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n\n    struct prod_args pa = { s, id, N, 0 };\n    struct prod_args ca = { s, id, N, 0 };\n    pthread_t tp, tc;\n    pthread_create(&tp, NULL, producer, &pa);\n    pthread_create(&tc, NULL, consumer, &ca);\n    pthread_join(tp, NULL);\n    pthread_join(tc, NULL);\n\n    /* Producer pushed 0..N-1; consumer's running sum must match. */\n    int expected = N * (N - 1) / 2;\n    ASSERT(ca.sum == expected);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

          "new_string":"- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queued input model that\n  ring-buffer slots implement\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — IPC options; shm_open + mmap is Option 2\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Core milestone — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — the public API exactly as the design\n  describes: `slot_alloc` / `slot_push` / `slot_peek` / `slot_pop` /\n  `slot_read_inc` / `slot_has_value` / `slot_fill_count`. Plus the\n  store lifecycle pair and a small inspection helper for tests.\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — implementation. Plain-malloc per slot\n  (size-class free lists deferred); ring slots and atomic-counter\n  slots both supported; the SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED variant of pop scans\n  for the lowest-tag filled cell. Per-slot spinlock via\n  `atomic_flag`. Atomic counter via `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`,\n  no lock.\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — 12 unit tests covering peek\n  semantics, FIFO pop, tagged pop ordering (in-order and\n  interleaved), atomic counter (sequential + 8-thread concurrent),\n  bad-argument paths, ring-full / empty edge cases, and a\n  multi-thread producer/consumer race over 5000 values.\n- Makefile additions: `test` target builds test binaries via a\n  pattern rule and runs them. Per-test prerequisites listed\n  explicitly so each binary links the minimal set of source `.o`s.\n- File index counter advanced to `009`.\n\nVerified clean build and 12/12 tests pass in `make STRICT=1`\n(`-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).\n\nWhat's deferred to a follow-on within 302:\n- **Size-class free lists with coalescing.** The current\n  implementation `malloc`s each slot independently. That's correct\n  but unoptimized. Slots are allocated once at graph load and never\n  freed until run end, so under the current usage pattern free-list\n  reuse buys nothing. Lands once profiling justifies it (or once\n  long-running maps surface allocation pressure).\n- **Large-value heap for variable-size payloads.** Slots currently\n  store fixed-size cells; very large outputs (multi-MB LLM\n  responses, dynamically-sized arrays) will need the two-tier\n  scheme described under \"Large-value heap\" above. Blocks no\n  in-flight phase 3 work until a graph wants variable-size outputs.\n\nNeither deferred item blocks 301 / 304 / 305 / 306 / 307 / 308.",

    "newString":"- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queued input model that\n  ring-buffer slots implement\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — IPC options; shm_open + mmap is Option 2\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Core milestone — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — the public API exactly as the design\n  describes: `slot_alloc` / `slot_push` / `slot_peek` / `slot_pop` /\n  `slot_read_inc` / `slot_has_value` / `slot_fill_count`. Plus the\n  store lifecycle pair and a small inspection helper for tests.\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — implementation. Plain-malloc per slot\n  (size-class free lists deferred); ring slots and atomic-counter\n  slots both supported; the SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED variant of pop scans\n  for the lowest-tag filled cell. Per-slot spinlock via\n  `atomic_flag`. Atomic counter via `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`,\n  no lock.\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — 12 unit tests covering peek\n  semantics, FIFO pop, tagged pop ordering (in-order and\n  interleaved), atomic counter (sequential + 8-thread concurrent),\n  bad-argument paths, ring-full / empty edge cases, and a\n  multi-thread producer/consumer race over 5000 values.\n- Makefile additions: `test` target builds test binaries via a\n  pattern rule and runs them. Per-test prerequisites listed\n  explicitly so each binary links the minimal set of source `.o`s.\n- File index counter advanced to `009`.\n\nVerified clean build and 12/12 tests pass in `make STRICT=1`\n(`-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).\n\nWhat's deferred to a follow-on within 302:\n- **Size-class free lists with coalescing.** The current\n  implementation `malloc`s each slot independently. That's correct\n  but unoptimized. Slots are allocated once at graph load and never\n  freed until run end, so under the current usage pattern free-list\n  reuse buys nothing. Lands once profiling justifies it (or once\n  long-running maps surface allocation pressure).\n- **Large-value heap for variable-size payloads.** Slots currently\n  store fixed-size cells; very large outputs (multi-MB LLM\n  responses, dynamically-sized arrays) will need the two-tier\n  scheme described under \"Large-value heap\" above. Blocks no\n  in-flight phase 3 work until a graph wants variable-size outputs.\n\nNeither deferred item blocks 301 / 304 / 305 / 306 / 307 / 308."

    "originalFile":"# Phase 3 Progress\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel.\n\nThe phase is fully designed; implementation is now underway.\nIssues 301–313 are the architectural specification. spec implementation                           | designed |\n| 309 | build system & Makefile orchestration                       | in progress · scaffolding done |\n| 310 | priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally                | designed |\n| 311 | integration tests & run output (`last-run.jsonl`)           | designed |\n| 312 | same-language wire fast path (skip JSON for Lua→Lua etc.)   | designed |\n| 313 | research: whole-program same-language merge                 | research / blocked |\n\n## Phase goal checklist\n\n- [ ] SoraMech-owned task pool builds clean (3d-rts as design reference)\n- [ ] Slot store unit-tested (single-value + ring buffer + refcounting)\n- [ ] C graph loader passes phase 2's existing maps\n- [ ] Lua spec runs `maps/hello` end-to-end\n- [ ] C spec compiles and runs a typed-signature box\n- [ ] Bash spec runs an out-of-process box via the socket protocol\n- [ ] Pool runner runs a multi-language map with concurrent workers\n- [ ] Iterator box routes via dispatch layer (no spec invoked)\n- [ ] Comparator box routes via dispatch layer (no spec invoked)\n- [ ] Variable-size outputs work via the large-value heap\n- [ ] `last-run.jsonl` written for every run\n- [ ] All 11 integration test maps pass\n- [ ] Phase 3 demo map runs and produces expected output\n- [ ] Phase 2 synchronous runner retired (`src/004-executor.lua`,\n           "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nPhase 3 foundation — build system scaffolding and the slot store\n\nLay the groundwork for the C pool runner. Three pieces land together\nsince they're meaningless apart: there's a Makefile to build with,\nthe first real piece of runtime code (the slot store), and the\nworking directory swept clean of the user content that was\naccidentally tracked.\n\nThe build orchestration grows a top-level Makefile that turns the\nrunner sources into a single binary and each language directory\ninto its own shared library. Three modes — release by default,\ndebug with symbols, and a strict mode that promotes warnings to\nerrors — share the same source discovery: a glob over the source\ntree picks up new files automatically as future issues land them.\nThe runner is currently a single-file stub that parses argv,\nprints what it would do, and exits, and each of the three reference\nlanguage stubs exports the expected symbol with NULL callbacks —\njust enough that the spec registry can dlopen and inspect them once\nthat lands. A small editor config matches the include paths so\nLSP integrations resolve the same way the compiler does.\n\nThe slot store is the first real runtime component. It owns three\nshapes of slot behind one API: a one-cell peek mode for literals\nand run-once wires, an N-cell pop ring for queued and multi-push\nwires, and an atomic-counter mode that backs iterator and weighted\nrouting. The pop ring optionally honours an ordering tag — a push\ncarries the producer's counter snapshot, and pop returns the\nlowest-tag filled cell, preserving iteration order under parallel\niterator workers. Concurrency is per-slot: a one-byte spinlock\nguards header and cell mutations on the ring slots, while the\natomic counter goes straight through fetch-and-add with no lock.\n\nTwelve unit tests exercise every read mode, the buffer-too-small\nand ring-full edge cases, the bad-id path, the tagged ordering\nguarantee, and two threaded races — eight threads pulling a\nmillion-value-range counter and a producer/consumer pair shuffling\nfive thousand integers through a sixteen-cell ring. All pass under\nstrict-mode warnings-as-errors.\n\nTwo pieces of the slot store design are deferred to follow-ons:\nthe size-class free list with coalescing, and the large-value\nheap that backs variable-size payloads. Neither blocks 301 / 304 /\n305 / 306 / 307 / 308; the first is a pure optimization and the\nsecond only matters once a graph wants outputs whose size isn't\nknown at compile time.\n\nMaps stop being tracked as well. The user content that had\naccumulated under maps/* gets removed from the index; the working\ntree is untouched, and the blanket gitignore from the previous\ncommit keeps future contents out.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"\necho \"---\"\ngit log --oneline -5",
          "description":"Commit phase 3 foundation"
        }
      }],

    "content":"# 314 — A small C JSON parser, written for SoraMech\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe phase 3 design assumes a vendored JSON parser sits under\n`libs/json/` — issues 305 (graph loader), 311 (JSONL run output),\nand 309 (build system) all reference it. The original plan was to\ndrop in cJSON / jsmn / similar.\n\nAfter thinking about it: a vendored generic parser is one more\nexternal surface to learn and to debug, with idioms that don't\nmatch the rest of the runtime, and complications around large\ninputs / streaming / arena allocation that we'd want to special-case\nanyway. SoraMech needs JSON in two specific places:\n\n1. **Reading** map files (`meta.json`, `boxes/*.json`,\n   `data/*.json`) at graph load. Inputs are kilobyte-scale, parsed\n   once, validated immediately. The output is a tree that the\n   graph loader walks once.\n2. **Writing** run-log events into `tmp/last-run.jsonl` (issue\n   311). Output is per-event, line-oriented, ASCII-safe; the writer\n   thread serialises one event struct per call.\n\nBoth are narrow enough that a small, opinionated parser tailored to\nthe project beats a general-purpose library on every dimension that\nmatters to us.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA C library under `libs/json/`, vendored as plain source, that\nSoraMech owns end to end. Two halves:\n\n### Parser (DOM, arena-allocated)\n\n```c\ntypedef struct json_arena json_arena_t;\ntypedef struct json_node  json_node_t;\n\ntypedef enum {\n    JSON_NULL, JSON_BOOL, JSON_NUMBER,\n    JSON_STRING, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_OBJECT\n} json_kind_t;\n\njson_arena_t *json_arena_create(void);\nvoid          json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a);\n\n/* Parse a NUL-terminated string into a tree owned by the arena.\n * Returns NULL on syntax error; *err_offset and *err_msg are filled\n * with the position and a short diagnostic. */\njson_node_t *json_parse(json_arena_t *a,\n                        const char *src,\n                        int *err_offset, const char **err_msg);\n\n/* Parse a file. Convenience over json_parse + a file read. */\njson_node_t *json_parse_file(json_arena_t *a,\n                             const char *path,\n                             int *err_line, const char **err_msg);\n\n/* Inspect. */\njson_kind_t   json_kind        (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_is_null     (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_bool_value  (const json_node_t *n);\ndouble        json_number_value(const json_node_t *n);\nconst char   *json_string_value(const json_node_t *n);   /* NUL-terminated */\nint           json_array_size  (const json_node_t *n);\njson_node_t  *json_array_at    (const json_node_t *n, int i);\nint           json_object_size (const json_node_t *n);\nconst char   *json_object_key  (const json_node_t *n, int i);\njson_node_t  *json_object_value(const json_node_t *n, int i);\njson_node_t  *json_object_get  (const json_node_t *n, const char *key);\n```\n\nAll strings, arrays, and objects are arena-allocated. The whole\nparse tree lives in one `json_arena_t`; destroying the arena\nfrees every node and every string in one go. No per-node `free`.\n\n`json_object_get` is the common path for \"pull the `id` field off\nthis box\" — linear scan over the object's keys; object sizes in\nthis project are < 20, so the simplicity wins over a hash map.\n\n### Writer (streaming, no DOM)\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    char  *buf;\n    int    cap;\n    int    used;\n    int    err;       /* 0 ok; nonzero = truncation / OOM */\n} json_writer_t;\n\nvoid json_writer_init    (json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap);\nvoid json_writer_object  (json_writer_t *w);   /* '{' */\nvoid json_writer_end     (json_writer_t *w);   /* '}' or ']' */\nvoid json_writer_array   (json_writer_t *w);\nvoid json_writer_key     (json_writer_t *w, const char *key);\nvoid json_writer_string  (json_writer_t *w, const char *s);\nvoid json_writer_int     (json_writer_t *w, long long v);\nvoid json_writer_number  (json_writer_t *w, double v);\nvoid json_writer_bool    (json_writer_t *w, int v);\nvoid json_writer_null    (json_writer_t *w);\n\n/* Returns the number of bytes written (excludes NUL terminator),\n * or -1 if w->err is set. */\nint  json_writer_finish  (json_writer_t *w);\n```\n\nThe writer maintains a small state stack (depth ≤ 16 is plenty\nfor our event records) so it knows when to emit commas between\nelements. The writer never allocates — the caller hands in a fixed\nbuffer, the writer reports overflow via `w->err`. This matches the\nJSONL event-writer design (issue 311): one record per fixed-size\nstruct, serialised into a per-write buffer of bounded size.\n\n### What the parser supports\n\n- JSON per RFC 8259: objects, arrays, strings, numbers (parsed as\n  `double`), `true`, `false`, `null`.\n- UTF-8 strict. Escape sequences `\\\"`, `\\\\`, `\\/`, `\\b`, `\\f`,\n  `\\n`, `\\r`, `\\t`. `\\uXXXX` for BMP code points; surrogate pairs\n  handled. Decoded strings are NUL-terminated; embedded NULs in\n  source strings are rejected (we don't need them and they make\n  the strings interaction with the rest of the C code awkward).\n- Strict syntax. Trailing commas, comments, unquoted keys: all\n  errors with a precise message.\n\n### What it does NOT support\n\n- **Streaming / SAX**. Our inputs are small and parsed once. If\n  some future use case wants streaming (a 10-MB LLM response that\n  is itself JSON), revisit then.\n- **No integer / no big-number type**. Numbers are `double`. The\n  graph loader's integer-looking fields (`output_capacity`,\n  `n_outputs`) are read via `(int)json_number_value(n)`. Documented\n  in the loader, not in the parser.\n- **No pretty-print**. The writer emits compact JSON only (one\n  whitespace token between primitives, no spaces, no newlines).\n  JSONL needs compact lines anyway.\n- **No mutation API on parsed trees**. Trees are read-only; if a\n  caller wants to construct JSON, it uses the writer.\n\n### Errors\n\n`json_parse` returns NULL on syntax error and fills `*err_offset`\nwith the byte offset where parsing failed, and `*err_msg` with a\nshort static-string description (\"expected ':' after key\",\n\"unterminated string\", \"invalid escape sequence\"). The graph loader\nturns this into a precise diagnostic (\"maps/<name>/boxes/<id>.json:\nline 12: unterminated string\").\n\nOOM during parsing (arena out of memory) is a fatal error — the\narena uses a chunked-buffer allocator that calls `malloc` when it\ngrows; if that fails, the parser reports `*err_msg = \"out of\nmemory\"` and returns NULL. The hard-crash policy of the rest of\nthe runtime (issue 303) applies upstream.\n\n## Why now\n\nThe graph loader (issue 305) is the immediate consumer. The JSONL\nwriter (issue 311) is the next one. Building the parser ourselves\nkeeps the dependency surface to zero and gives us idioms (arenas,\nerror reporting style, allocation policy) that match the slot\nstore and the dispatch layer.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Arena allocator** (`libs/json/arena.c` + `.h`). Chunked\n   bump allocator: each chunk is a `malloc`'d buffer; allocate by\n   advancing an offset; chain chunks when one fills. Free chunks\n   in `json_arena_destroy`.\n2. **Parser** (`libs/json/json.c` + `.h`). Hand-rolled recursive\n   descent. ~600 lines. One internal struct per kind, packed into\n   a `json_node_t` union with a small tag.\n3. **Writer** (in `libs/json/json.c` alongside). State stack for\n   comma placement; bounded buffer; clean error reporting via\n   `w->err`.\n4. **Unit tests** (`tests/314-json-test.c`). Conformance cases:\n   nesting, escapes, surrogate pairs, error positions, writer\n   bracket-comma correctness, round-trip for a meta.json-shaped\n   input.\n5. **Wire into the Makefile.** `libs/json/*.c` is already in the\n   wildcard from issue 309; no Makefile edit needed beyond\n   confirming it picks up.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be created here, not\n  imported from upstream).\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — the immediate consumer.\n- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — the writer's\n  consumer (JSONL events).\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — Makefile already discovers\n  `libs/json/*.c` via wildcard.\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — references the JSON parser in the\n  phase 3 runtime layout.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Comments.** RFC 8259 forbids them; cJSON optionally allows\n  `//` and `/* */`. Box files are produced by the editor, not\n  hand-written, so we don't need them. Stay strict.\n- **`json_node_t` storage layout.** Tagged union (`json_kind_t` +\n  union of payloads) is simplest. Could also pack the kind into\n  low bits of a pointer for size — defer until profiling shows\n  node-count pressure.\n- **Object key lookup performance.** Linear scan is fine for\n  objects with 2–20 keys (every object in a SoraMech map). If\n  data files ever grow to thousands of keys, add an optional\n  hash-table mode.\n",

Building the parser ourselves\nkeeps the dependency surface to zero and gives us idioms (arenas,\nerror reporting style, allocation policy) that match the slot\nstore and the dispatch layer.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Arena allocator** (`libs/json/arena.c` + `.h`). Chunked\n   bump allocator: each chunk is a `malloc`'d buffer; allocate by\n   advancing an offset; chain chunks when one fills. Free chunks\n   in `json_arena_destroy`.\n2. **Parser** (`libs/json/json.c` + `.h`). Hand-rolled recursive\n   descent. ~600 lines. One internal struct per kind, packed into\n   a `json_node_t` union with a small tag.\n3. **Writer** (in `libs/json/json.c` alongside). State stack for\n   comma placement; bounded buffer; clean error reporting via\n   `w->err`.\n4. **Unit tests** (`tests/314-json-test.c`). Conformance cases:\n   nesting, escapes, surrogate pairs, error positions, writer\n   bracket-comma correctness, round-trip for a meta.json-shaped\n   input.\n5. **Wire into the Makefile.** `libs/json/*.c` is already in the\n   wildcard from issue 309; no Makefile edit needed beyond\n   confirming it picks up.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be created here, not\n  imported from upstream).\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — the immediate consumer.\n- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — the writer's\n  consumer (JSONL events).\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — Makefile already discovers\n  `libs/json/*.c` via wildcard.\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — references the JSON parser in the\n  phase 3 runtime layout.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Comments.** RFC 8259 forbids them; cJSON optionally allows\n  `//` and `/* */`. Box files are produced by the editor, not\n  hand-written, so we don't need them. Stay strict.\n- **`json_node_t` storage layout.** Tagged union (`json_kind_t` +\n  union of payloads) is simplest. Could also pack the kind into\n  low bits of a pointer for size — defer until profiling shows\n  node-count pressure.\n- **Object key lookup performance.** Linear scan is fine for\n  objects with 2–20 keys (every object in a SoraMech map). If\n  data files ever grow to thousands of keys, add an optional\n  hash-table mode.\n",

          "content":"/* libs/json/json.h — small DOM JSON parser + streaming writer.\n *\n * Written for SoraMech, not vendored. Designed in issue 314. Two\n * halves: a DOM parser with arena-allocated nodes (used by the\n * phase 3 graph loader, issue 305), and a streaming writer with a\n * fixed buffer (used by the JSONL run-log writer, issue 311).\n *\n * The parser is hand-rolled recursive descent. The DOM is read-only\n * once parsed; constructing JSON goes through the writer, not the\n * DOM. Numbers are doubles; integer-shaped fields read via\n * (int)json_number_value(...). UTF-8 strict, BMP \\uXXXX with\n * surrogate-pair handling. No comments, no trailing commas.\n *\n * Errors: json_parse returns NULL on failure, with *err_offset\n * and *err_msg filled. The graph loader maps the offset to a\n * filename:line:column diagnostic before surfacing it.\n *\n * Memory: every parse tree lives in one json_arena_t. Destroying\n * the arena frees every node and every string in one call. There\n * is no per-node free.\n *\n * Threading: single-threaded — the parser is meant to run on the\n * graph-load thread before the pool spins up. Concurrency comes in\n * at the writer side, where each writer call is independent and the\n * caller owns the buffer.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_JSON_H\n#define SORAMECH_JSON_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef enum {\n    JSON_NULL,\n    JSON_BOOL,\n    JSON_NUMBER,\n    JSON_STRING,\n    JSON_ARRAY,\n    JSON_OBJECT,\n} json_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct json_arena json_arena_t;\ntypedef struct json_node  json_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Arena lifecycle */\n/* Construct an empty arena. Returns NULL on allocation failure. */\njson_arena_t *json_arena_create(void);\n\n/* Free every chunk in the arena. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid          json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a);\n\n/* Bytes currently allocated across all chunks (for diagnostics). */\nsize_t        json_arena_bytes(const json_arena_t *a);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Parser */\n/* Parse a NUL-terminated UTF-8 source into a tree owned by the\n * arena. Returns NULL on syntax error; *err_offset (if non-NULL)\n * receives the byte offset where parsing failed, and *err_msg\n * (if non-NULL) receives a static-string description. */\njson_node_t *json_parse(json_arena_t *a,\n                        const char  *src,\n                        int         *err_offset,\n                        const char **err_msg);\n\n/* Read a file end-to-end and parse it. *err_line (if non-NULL) is\n * the 1-based line number where parsing failed, computed from the\n * byte offset against the file contents. */\njson_node_t *json_parse_file(json_arena_t *a,\n                             const char  *path,\n                             int         *err_line,\n                             const char **err_msg);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\njson_kind_t   json_kind        (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_is_null     (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_bool_value  (const json_node_t *n);\ndouble        json_number_value(const json_node_t *n);\n\n/* NUL-terminated; lives in the arena. */\nconst char   *json_string_value(const json_node_t *n);\n\nint           json_array_size  (const json_node_t *n);\njson_node_t  *json_array_at    (const json_node_t *n, int i);\n\nint           json_object_size (const json_node_t *n);\nconst char   *json_object_key  (const json_node_t *n, int i);\njson_node_t  *json_object_value(const json_node_t *n, int i);\n\n/* Linear scan; returns NULL if key not present. */\njson_node_t  *json_object_get  (const json_node_t *n, const char *key);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Writer (declared; implementation deferred) */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *buf;\n    int   cap;\n    int   used;\n    int   err;        /* 0 ok; nonzero = truncation or bad call */\n    /* Internal: depth stack (commas + bracket pairing). */\n    unsigned char depth;\n    unsigned char first[16];\n} json_writer_t;\n\nvoid json_writer_init   (json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap);\nvoid json_writer_object (json_writer_t *w);\nvoid json_writer_array  (json_writer_t *w);\nvoid json_writer_end    (json_writer_t *w);\nvoid json_writer_key    (json_writer_t *w, const char *key);\nvoid json_writer_string (json_writer_t *w, const char *s);\nvoid json_writer_int    (json_writer_t *w, long long v);\nvoid json_writer_number (json_writer_t *w, double v);\nvoid json_writer_bool   (json_writer_t *w, int v);\nvoid json_writer_null   (json_writer_t *w);\n/* Returns used bytes (excluding NUL), or -1 if w->err. */\nint  json_writer_finish (json_writer_t *w);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_JSON_H */\n",

          "content":"/* libs/json/json.c — DOM JSON parser + streaming writer.\n *\n * Sections, top to bottom:\n *\n *   - Arena allocator (chunked bump).\n *   - Internal node types and tagged-union layout.\n *   - Parser (hand-rolled recursive descent).\n *   - Accessors.\n *   - File loader (json_parse_file).\n *   - Writer (declared; body deferred per the implementation log on\n *     issue 314 — JSONL writer lands when 311 needs it).\n *\n * Designed in issue 314. The parser supports JSON per RFC 8259 with\n * a few tightenings: no comments, no trailing commas, no embedded\n * NULs in strings, BMP-only \\uXXXX with surrogate-pair handling.\n * Numbers are doubles; integer-shaped fields are read via\n * (int)json_number_value.\n *\n * Memory model: every node and every string lives in the arena\n * passed to json_parse. json_arena_destroy frees the lot in one\n * call. There is no per-node free. During parsing, temporary\n * linked-list scaffolding for array/object construction is also\n * allocated in the arena and left \"abandoned\" once the final\n * fixed-size arrays are emitted — abandoned bytes are reclaimed\n * when the arena is destroyed.\n */\n\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Arena allocator */\ntypedef struct json_chunk {\n    struct json_chunk *next;\n    size_t size;\n    size_t used;\n    /* Followed by `size` bytes of storage. */\n    char data[];\n} json_chunk_t;\n\nstruct json_arena {\n    json_chunk_t *head;\n    size_t total_bytes;\n};\n\n#define JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT 16384\n\n/* {{{ arena_new_chunk() */\nstatic json_chunk_t *arena_new_chunk(size_t min_size)\n{\n    size_t sz = (min_size > JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT) ? min_size : JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT;\n    json_chunk_t *c = malloc(sizeof(json_chunk_t) + sz);\n    if (!c) return NULL;\n    c->next = NULL;\n    c->size = sz;\n    c->used = 0;\n    return c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_create() */\njson_arena_t *json_arena_create(void)\n{\n    json_arena_t *a = calloc(1, sizeof *a);\n    if (!a) return NULL;\n    a->head = arena_new_chunk(JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT);\n    if (!a->head) { free(a); return NULL; }\n    a->total_bytes = a->head->size;\n    return a;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_destroy() */\nvoid json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a)\n{\n    if (!a) return;\n    json_chunk_t *c = a->head;\n    while (c) {\n        json_chunk_t *next = c->next;\n        free(c);\n        c = next;\n    }\n    free(a);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_bytes() */\nsize_t json_arena_bytes(const json_arena_t *a)\n{\n    return a ? a->total_bytes : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ arena_alloc() — aligned to 8 bytes */\nstatic void *arena_alloc(json_arena_t *a, size_t bytes)\n{\n    if (bytes == 0) bytes = 1;\n    /* 8-byte alignment for everything; the union contains a double\n     * and pointers, both of which want at least 8-byte alignment on\n     * 64-bit targets. */\n    size_t aligned = (bytes + 7u) & ~(size_t)7u;\n\n    if (a->head->used + aligned > a->head->size) {\n        json_chunk_t *c = arena_new_chunk(aligned);\n        if (!c) return NULL;\n        c->next = a->head;\n        a->head = c;\n        a->total_bytes += c->size;\n    }\n    void *p = a->head->data + a->head->used;\n    a->head->used += aligned;\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ arena_strdup() — copy a length-counted byte run, NUL-terminate */\nstatic char *arena_strdup(json_arena_t *a, const char *s, size_t len)\n{\n    char *out = arena_alloc(a, len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(out, s, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Node layout */\ntypedef struct kv_link {\n    struct kv_link *next;\n    const char     *key;     /* arena-allocated; NULL for array items */\n    json_node_t    *value;\n} kv_link_t;\n\nstruct json_node {\n    json_kind_t kind;\n    union {\n        int           b;\n        double        n;\n        const char   *s;\n        struct {\n            json_node_t **items;\n            int           count;\n        } arr;\n        struct {\n            const char  **keys;\n            json_node_t **values;\n            int           count;\n        } obj;\n    } u;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Parser state */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char  *src;\n    int          pos;     /* current byte offset into src */\n    json_arena_t *arena;\n    const char  *err_msg; /* set on first failure */\n    int          err_pos;\n} parser_t;\n\nstatic json_node_t *parse_value(parser_t *p);\nstatic int          parse_string_into(parser_t *p, const char **out);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — error reporting & character classes */\nstatic void fail(parser_t *p, const char *msg)\n{\n    if (!p->err_msg) {\n        p->err_msg = msg;\n        p->err_pos = p->pos;\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int is_ws(int c)   { return c == ' ' || c == '\\t' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r'; }\nstatic int is_digit(int c){ return c >= '0' && c <= '9'; }\nstatic int is_hex(int c)\n{\n    return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F');\n}\n\nstatic int hex_val(int c)\n{\n    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') return c - '0';\n    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') return c - 'a' + 10;\n    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') return c - 'A' + 10;\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic int peek(parser_t *p)\n{\n    return (unsigned char)p->src[p->pos];\n}\n\nstatic void skip_ws(parser_t *p)\n{\n    while (is_ws((unsigned char)p->src[p->pos])) p->pos++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — node makers */\nstatic json_node_t *mk_node(parser_t *p, json_kind_t k)\n{\n    json_node_t *n = arena_alloc(p->arena, sizeof *n);\n    if (!n) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n    memset(n, 0, sizeof *n);\n    n->kind = k;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_string_into() — read \"...\", decode escapes into arena */\n/* Reads from the opening '\"' at p->pos. On success advances p past\n * the closing '\"' and sets *out to an arena-owned NUL-terminated\n * UTF-8 string. */\nstatic int parse_string_into(parser_t *p, const char **out)\n{\n    if (peek(p) != '\"') { fail(p, \"expected string\"); return 0; }\n    p->pos++;\n\n    /* First pass: scan to closing quote, count decoded bytes. */\n    int start = p->pos;\n    int decoded_len = 0;\n    while (1) {\n        int c = peek(p);\n        if (c == 0) { fail(p, \"unterminated string\"); return 0; }\n        if (c == '\"') break;\n        if (c == '\\\\') {\n            p->pos++;\n            int e = peek(p);\n            switch (e) {\n                case '\"': case '\\\\': case '/':\n                case 'b': case 'f': case 'n': case 'r': case 't':\n                    decoded_len += 1; p->pos++; break;\n                case 'u': {\n                    /* 4 hex digits → 1..4 UTF-8 bytes; surrogate pairs\n                     * combine to 4 bytes. long sz = ftell(fp);\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    if (sz < 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = \"cannot size file\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    char *buf = malloc((size_t)sz + 1);\n    if (!buf) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = \"out of memory\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    size_t got = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)sz, fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n    buf[got] = '\\0';\n\n    int off = 0;\n    const char *m = NULL;\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, buf, &off, &m);\n    if (!n) {\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = m;\n        if (err_line) {\n            int line = 1;\n            for (int i = 0; i < off && i < (int)got; i++) {\n                if (buf[i] == '\\n') line++;\n            }\n            *err_line = line;\n        }\n    }\n    free(buf);\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\njson_kind_t json_kind(const json_node_t *n)         { return n ? n->kind : JSON_NULL; }\nint         json_is_null(const json_node_t *n)      { return n && n->kind == JSON_NULL; }\nint         json_bool_value(const json_node_t *n)   { return (n && n->kind == JSON_BOOL)   ? n->u.b : 0; }\ndouble      json_number_value(const json_node_t *n) { return (n && n->kind == JSON_NUMBER) ? n->u.n : 0.0; }\nconst char *json_string_value(const json_node_t *n) { return (n && n->kind == JSON_STRING) ? n->u.s : NULL; }\nint         json_array_size(const json_node_t *n)   { return (n && n->kind == JSON_ARRAY)  ? n->u.arr.count : 0; }\nint         json_object_size(const json_node_t *n)  { return (n && n->kind == JSON_OBJECT) ? n->u.obj.count : 0; }\n\njson_node_t *json_array_at(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_ARRAY) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.arr.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.arr.items[i];\n}\n\nconst char *json_object_key(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.obj.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.obj.keys[i];\n}\n\njson_node_t *json_object_value(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.obj.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.obj.values[i];\n}\n\njson_node_t *json_object_get(const json_node_t *n, const char *key)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT || !key) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n->u.obj.count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(n->u.obj.keys[i], key) == 0) return n->u.obj.values[i];\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Writer — declared, body deferred */\n/* The writer half is exercised once the JSONL run-log writer\n * (issue 311) lands. The signatures are declared in json.h so other\n * components can link against this object even before the writer\n * body is implemented. For now each entrypoint sets w->err and\n * returns; json_writer_finish returns -1 if the writer has been\n * touched, 0 if untouched. */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_init() */\nvoid json_writer_init(json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    w->buf   = buf;\n    w->cap   = cap;\n    w->used  = 0;\n    w->err   = 0;\n    w->depth = 0;\n    memset(w->first, 0, sizeof w->first);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_object() */\nvoid json_writer_object(json_writer_t *w) { (void)w; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_array() */\nvoid json_writer_array (json_writer_t *w) { (void)w; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_end() */\nvoid json_writer_end   (json_writer_t *w) { (void)w; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_key() */\nvoid json_writer_key   (json_writer_t *w, const char *k) { (void)k; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_string() */\nvoid json_writer_string(json_writer_t *w, const char *s) { (void)s; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_int() */\nvoid json_writer_int   (json_writer_t *w, long long v)   { (void)v; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_number() */\nvoid json_writer_number(json_writer_t *w, double v)      { (void)v; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_bool() */\nvoid json_writer_bool  (json_writer_t *w, int v)         { (void)v; if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_null() */\nvoid json_writer_null  (json_writer_t *w)                { if (w) w->err = -1; }\n/* }}} */\n/* {{{ json_writer_finish() */\nint json_writer_finish(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    return w->err ? -1 : w->used;\n}\n/* }}} */\n/* }}} */\n",

test_error_positions(void)\n{\n    ARENA();\n    int off; const char *msg;\n\n    /* trailing comma in array */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"[1, 2, ]\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"trailing comma\") != NULL);\n\n    /* missing colon */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"{\\\"k\\\" \\\"v\\\"}\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"expected ':'\") != NULL);\n\n    /* unterminated string */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"\\\"unfinished\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"unterminated\") != NULL);\n\n    /* bad escape */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"\\\"\\\\q\\\"\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"invalid escape\") != NULL);\n\n    /* trailing garbage */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"42xyz\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"trailing garbage\") != NULL);\n\n    /* lone control char */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"\\\"\\x01\\\"\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(msg, \"control\") != NULL);\n\n    /* leading zero followed by digit -- spec violates `0\\d` */\n    /* (Our parser accepts \"0\" but stops at the next char; with strict\n     * RFC compliance \"01\" should fail at the next-value lookup. We\n     * test the easier case: a non-number that starts with 'x'.) */\n    ASSERT(json_parse(a, \"xyz\", &off, &msg) == NULL);\n    END_ARENA();\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_meta_shape() */\n/* Realistic test: the shape of a meta.json file. */\nstatic int test_meta_shape(void)\n{\n    ARENA();\n    const char *src =\n        \"{\"\n        \"  \\\"name\\\": \\\"hello\\\",\"\n        \"  \\\"description\\\": \\\"Minimal example map\\\",\"\n        \"  \\\"entry_box_id\\\": \\\"greet\\\",\"\n        \"  \\\"src_dirs\\\": [\\\"libs\\\", \\\"maps/hello/src\\\"]\"\n        \"}\";\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, src, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"name\")),         \"hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"entry_box_id\")), \"greet\") == 0);\n    json_node_t *dirs = json_object_get(n, \"src_dirs\");\n    ASSERT(json_array_size(dirs) == 2);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_array_at(dirs, 0)), \"libs\") == 0);\n    END_ARENA();\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_parse_file() */\nstatic int test_parse_file(void)\n{\n    /* Write a tiny test file, parse it, verify. */\n    char path[] = \"/tmp/soramech-json-test-XXXXXX\";\n    int fd = mkstemp(path);\n    ASSERT(fd >= 0);\n    FILE *fp = fdopen(fd, \"w\");\n    fprintf(fp, \"\\n\\n{\\\"answer\\\": 42,\\n  \\\"broken\\\": true\\n}\\n\");\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse_file(a, path, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(json_number_value(json_object_get(n, \"answer\")) == 42.0);\n    ASSERT(json_bool_value(json_object_get(n, \"broken\")) == 1);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_parse_file_error_line() */\nstatic int test_parse_file_error_line(void)\n{\n    /* Write a file with an error on line 3. */\n    char path[] = \"/tmp/soramech-json-err-XXXXXX\";\n    int fd = mkstemp(path);\n    ASSERT(fd >= 0);\n    FILE *fp = fdopen(fd, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\n  \\\"x\\\": 1,\\n  bad\\n}\\n\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n ASSERT(msg != NULL);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_arena_grows() */\nstatic int test_arena_grows(void)\n{\n    /* Force the arena to add     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. {
