If","   data files ever grow to thousands of keys, add an optional","   hash-table mode.","+","+## Implementation log","+","+### Parser milestone — 2026-05-12","+","+What shipped:","+- `libs/json/json.h` — full public surface for both halves.","+- `libs/json/json.c` — arena allocator (chunked bump, 16 KB","+  default chunk), recursive-descent parser, every accessor. The","+  parser handles every JSON kind, all escape sequences including","+  BMP `\\uXXXX` and surrogate pairs, with precise error positions.","+  Numbers go through `strtod` after a small NUL-terminated scratch","+  buffer (heap fallback for literals over 64 bytes — exceptionally","+  rare). Arrays and objects build via a temporary linked list in","+  the arena, finalized to fixed-size pointer arrays at close time;","+  the link nodes are abandoned (recovered when the arena is","+  destroyed).","+- `tests/314-json-test.c` — 14 unit tests: every primitive,","+  string escapes, U+00E9 single-escape, U+1F600 surrogate pair,","+  empty / non-empty / nested arrays and objects, whitespace","+  insensitivity, six distinct error-position cases, a realistic","+  meta.json-shaped parse, file loading with line-numbered errors,","+  arena growth across the 16 KB chunk boundary, and accessor","+  safety on the wrong kind.","+- Makefile per-test dependency line for `314-json-test`.","+","+Verified `make STRICT=1` (`-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`) builds","+cleanly; 14/14 parser tests and the 12 slot-store tests all pass.","+","+What's deferred:","+- **The writer half.** Declared in `json.h`; every entrypoint in","+  `json.c` currently sets `w->err`. Lands alongside the JSONL","+  run-log writer (issue 311) since that's the first real consumer","+  — no point implementing it before there's a struct shape to","+  serialize.","+- **Stricter leading-zero rule.** RFC 8259 disallows `0\\d+`; we","+  currently accept `01` as `1`. None of our inputs produce that","+  shape, so it's a tightening that lands when something needs it.","+","+Neither blocks 305 — the graph loader uses the parser half only."],
        "oldStart":209
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 314 — A small C JSON parser, written for SoraMech\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe phase 3 design assumes a vendored JSON parser sits under\n`libs/json/` — issues 305 (graph loader), 311 (JSONL run output),\nand 309 (build system) all reference it. The original plan was to\ndrop in cJSON / jsmn / similar.\n\nAfter thinking about it: a vendored generic parser is one more\nexternal surface to learn and to debug, with idioms that don't\nmatch the rest of the runtime, and complications around large\ninputs / streaming / arena allocation that we'd want to special-case\nanyway. SoraMech needs JSON in two specific places:\n\n1. **Reading** map files (`meta.json`, `boxes/*.json`,\n   `data/*.json`) at graph load. Inputs are kilobyte-scale, parsed\n   once, validated immediately. The output is a tree that the\n   graph loader walks once.\n2. **Writing** run-log events into `tmp/last-run.jsonl` (issue\n   311). Output is per-event, line-oriented, ASCII-safe; the writer\n   thread serialises one event struct per call.\n\nBoth are narrow enough that a small, opinionated parser tailored to\nthe project beats a general-purpose library on every dimension that\nmatters to us.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA C library under `libs/json/`, vendored as plain source, that\nSoraMech owns end to end. Two halves:\n\n### Parser (DOM, arena-allocated)\n\n```c\ntypedef struct json_arena json_arena_t;\ntypedef struct json_node  json_node_t;\n\ntypedef enum {\n    JSON_NULL, JSON_BOOL, JSON_NUMBER,\n    JSON_STRING, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_OBJECT\n} json_kind_t;\n\njson_arena_t *json_arena_create(void);\nvoid          json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a);\n\n/* Parse a NUL-terminated string into a tree owned by the arena.\n * Returns NULL on syntax error; *err_offset and *err_msg are filled\n * with the position and a short diagnostic. */\njson_node_t *json_parse(json_arena_t *a,\n                        const char *src,\n                        int *err_offset, const char **err_msg);\n\n/* Parse a file. Convenience over json_parse + a file read. */\njson_node_t *json_parse_file(json_arena_t *a,\n                             const char *path,\n                             int *err_line, const char **err_msg);\n\n/* Inspect. */\njson_kind_t   json_kind        (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_is_null     (const json_node_t *n);\nint           json_bool_value  (const json_node_t *n);\ndouble        json_number_value(const json_node_t *n);\nconst char   *json_string_value(const json_node_t *n);   /* NUL-terminated */\nint           json_array_size  (const json_node_t *n);\njson_node_t  *json_array_at    (const json_node_t *n, int i);\nint           json_object_size (const json_node_t *n);\nconst char   *json_object_key  (const json_node_t *n, int i);\njson_node_t  *json_object_value(const json_node_t *n, int i);\njson_node_t  *json_object_get  (const json_node_t *n, const char *key);\n```\n\nAll strings, arrays, and objects are arena-allocated. The whole\nparse tree lives in one `json_arena_t`; destroying the arena\nfrees every node and every string in one go. No per-node `free`.\n\n`json_object_get` is the common path for \"pull the `id` field off\nthis box\" — linear scan over the object's keys; object sizes in\nthis project are < 20, so the simplicity wins over a hash map.\n\n### Writer (streaming, no DOM)\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    char  *buf;\n    int    cap;\n    int    used;\n    int    err;       /* 0 ok; nonzero = truncation / OOM */\n} json_writer_t;\n\nvoid json_writer_init    (json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap);\nvoid json_writer_object  (json_writer_t *w);   /* '{' */\nvoid json_writer_end     (json_writer_t *w);   /* '}' or ']' */\nvoid json_writer_array   (json_writer_t *w);\nvoid json_writer_key     (json_writer_t *w, const char *key);\nvoid json_writer_string  (json_writer_t *w, const char *s);\nvoid json_writer_int     (json_writer_t *w, long long v);\nvoid json_writer_number  (json_writer_t *w, double v);\nvoid json_writer_bool    (json_writer_t *w, int v);\nvoid json_writer_null    (json_writer_t *w);\n\n/* Returns the number of bytes written (excludes NUL terminator),\n * or -1 if w->err is set. */\nint  json_writer_finish  (json_writer_t *w);\n```\n\nThe writer maintains a small state stack (depth ≤ 16 is plenty\nfor our event records) so it knows when to emit commas between\nelements. The writer never allocates — the caller hands in a fixed\nbuffer, the writer reports overflow via `w->err`. This matches the\nJSONL event-writer design (issue 311): one record per fixed-size\nstruct, serialised into a per-write buffer of bounded size.\n\n### What the parser supports\n\n- JSON per RFC 8259: objects, arrays, strings, numbers (parsed as\n  `double`), `true`, `false`, `null`.\n- UTF-8 strict. Escape sequences `\\\"`, `\\\\`, `\\/`, `\\b`, `\\f`,\n  `\\n`, `\\r`, `\\t`. `\\uXXXX` for BMP code points; surrogate pairs\n  handled. Decoded strings are NUL-terminated; embedded NULs in\n  source strings are rejected (we don't need them and they make\n  the strings interaction with the rest of the C code awkward).\n- Strict syntax. Trailing commas, comments, unquoted keys: all\n  errors with a precise message.\n\n### What it does NOT support\n\n- **Streaming / SAX**. Our inputs are small and parsed once. If\n  some future use case wants streaming (a 10-MB LLM response that\n  is itself JSON), revisit then.\n- **No integer / no big-number type**. Numbers are `double`. The\n  graph loader's integer-looking fields (`output_capacity`,\n  `n_outputs`) are read via `(int)json_number_value(n)`. Documented\n  in the loader, not in the parser.\n- **No pretty-print**. The writer emits compact JSON only (one\n  whitespace token between primitives, no spaces, no newlines).\n  JSONL needs compact lines anyway.\n- **No mutation API on parsed trees**. Trees are read-only; if a\n  caller wants to construct JSON, it uses the writer.\n\n### Errors\n\n`json_parse` returns NULL on syntax error and fills `*err_offset`\nwith the byte offset where parsing failed, and `*err_msg` with a\nshort static-string description (\"expected ':' after key\",\n\"unterminated string\", \"invalid escape sequence\"). The graph loader\nturns this into a precise diagnostic (\"maps/<name>/boxes/<id>.json:\nline 12: unterminated string\").\n\nOOM during parsing (arena out of memory) is a fatal error — the\narena uses a chunked-buffer allocator that calls `malloc` when it\ngrows; if that fails, the parser reports `*err_msg = \"out of\nmemory\"` and returns NULL. The hard-crash policy of the rest of\nthe runtime (issue 303) applies upstream.\n\n## Why now\n\nThe graph loader (issue 305) is the immediate consumer. The JSONL\nwriter (issue 311) is the next one. Building the parser ourselves\nkeeps the dependency surface to zero and gives us idioms (arenas,\nerror reporting style, allocation policy) that match the slot\nstore and the dispatch layer.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Arena allocator** (`libs/json/arena.c` + `.h`). Chunked\n   bump allocator: each chunk is a `malloc`'d buffer; allocate by\n   advancing an offset; chain chunks when one fills. Free chunks\n   in `json_arena_destroy`.\n2. **Parser** (`libs/json/json.c` + `.h`). Hand-rolled recursive\n   descent. ~600 lines. One internal struct per kind, packed into\n   a `json_node_t` union with a small tag.\n3. **Writer** (in `libs/json/json.c` alongside). State stack for\n   comma placement; bounded buffer; clean error reporting via\n   `w->err`.\n4. **Unit tests** (`tests/314-json-test.c`). Conformance cases:\n   nesting, escapes, surrogate pairs, error positions, writer\n   bracket-comma correctness, round-trip for a meta.json-shaped\n   input.\n5. **Wire into the Makefile.** `libs/json/*.c` is already in the\n   wildcard from issue 309; no Makefile edit needed beyond\n   confirming it picks up.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be created here, not\n  imported from upstream).\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — the immediate consumer.\n- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — the writer's\n  consumer (JSONL events).\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — Makefile already discovers\n  `libs/json/*.c` via wildcard.\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — references the JSON parser in the\n  phase 3 runtime layout.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Comments.** RFC 8259 forbids them; cJSON optionally allows\n  `//` and `/* */`. Box files are produced by the editor, not\n  hand-written, so we don't need them. Stay strict.\n- **`json_node_t` storage layout.** Tagged union (`json_kind_t` +\n  union of payloads) is simplest. Could also pack the kind into\n  low bits of a pointer for size — defer until profiling shows\n  node-count pressure.\n- **Object key lookup performance.** Linear scan is fine for\n  objects with 2–20 keys (every object in a SoraMech map). If\n  data files ever grow to thousands of keys, add an optional\n  hash-table mode.\n",

Implement the parser\nhalf this round; the writer half is declared in the header but\ndeferred until the run-log writer (issue 311) needs it.\n\nSingle file plus header under libs/json/. The arena is a chunked\nbump allocator that hands out 8-byte-aligned bytes from a 16 KB\ndefault chunk and grows as needed; destroying the arena reclaims\nevery node and every string in one call. Parsing is recursive\ndescent — six functions in a loop, one per JSON kind — with array\nand object items built into a temporary linked list in the same\narena and finalised to fixed-size pointer arrays at close time.\nThe link nodes are abandoned after finalise; the arena reclaims\nthem at destroy time, so there is no per-node free anywhere.\n\nStrings decode in two passes. The first scans to the closing quote\nand counts a worst-case decoded length; the second writes the\ndecoded bytes into an arena buffer sized to that count. Escape\nhandling covers the standard suite plus BMP \\uXXXX with surrogate\npairs combining to four-byte UTF-8 sequences. Unescaped control\ncharacters and embedded NULs in strings are rejected with precise\npositions, since we don't need them and they'd break the rest of\nthe C code's interaction with these strings.\n\nNumbers go through strtod after copying the literal into a small\nNUL-terminated scratch buffer; literals over 64 bytes (vanishingly\nrare in our maps) get a heap fallback. Errors set a static-string\ndiagnostic and a byte offset on the parser state; the file loader\nwalks the source once more to convert the offset into a 1-based\nline number for diagnostic surfaces.\n\nFourteen unit tests cover every primitive, escape, surrogate pair,\nnested structure, six distinct error-position cases, the\nrealistic-meta-json shape, file loading with line-numbered errors,\narena growth across the chunk boundary, and accessor safety on the\nwrong kind. All twenty-six tests across the two suites pass under\nstrict-mode warnings-as-errors.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"\necho \"---\"\ngit log --oneline -5",

        }

  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01E6uvLARHbLPG9TY31DC3aP",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* For routing kinds that need them later — weights, thresholds —\n     * the parser leaves their fields zero in this iteration and adds\n     * them when those kinds are implemented. */\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection (string refs; resolved in phase 4) */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Data boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (data only)          */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n} box_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.h"
        }
      }],

    "content":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* For routing kinds that need them later — weights, thresholds —\n     * the parser leaves their fields zero in this iteration and adds\n     * them when those kinds are implemented. */\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection (string refs; resolved in phase 4) */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Data boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (data only)          */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n} box_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",
    "type":"create",

json_string_value(kind_n);\n\n    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);\n\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"plain\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_PLAIN;\n        out->n_outputs = 1;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"comparator\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_COMPARATOR;\n        out->n_outputs = 3;\n        json_node_t *c = json_object_get(r, \"comparand\");\n        if (!c) {\n double. */\n            const char *s = json_string_value(c);\n            char *endp = NULL;\n            out->comparand = strtod(s, &endp);\n            if (endp == s) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand '%s' is not a number\", box_id, s);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        } else {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand must be number or string\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"iterator\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n        json_node_t *n =       }\n        out->n_outputs = (int)json_number_value(n);\n        if (out->n_outputs < 1) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': iterator n_outputs must be >= 1\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': unknown routing.kind '%s' \"\n                   \"(this iteration supports plain, comparator, iterator)\",\n                   box_id, kind);\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_inputs() — input port array */\nstatic int parse_inputs(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                        const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_inputs = 0;\n        box->inputs = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'inputs' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_inputs = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->inputs = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->inputs = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(input_decl_t));\n    if (!box->inputs) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *item = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!item || json_kind(item) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': input port %d is not an object\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(item, \"name\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': input port %d missing 'name'\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->inputs[i].name = json_string_value(name_n);\n\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(item, \"type\");\n        box->inputs[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                ? json_string_value(type_n) : \"string\";\n\n        /* `value`: only string literals supported in this iteration. */\n        json_node_t *val_n = json_object_get(item, \"value\");\n        box->inputs[i].literal = (val_n && json_kind(val_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                    ? json_string_value(val_n) : NULL;\n\n        json_node_t *opt_n = json_object_get(item, \"optional\");\n        box->inputs[i].optional = (opt_n && json_kind(opt_n) == JSON_BOOL)\n                                    ? json_bool_value(opt_n) : 0;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_connections() — outgoing connection array */\nstatic int parse_connections(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                             const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_connections = 0;\n        box->connections = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'connections' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_connections = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->connections = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->connections = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(connection_t));\n    if (!box->connections) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *c = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!c || json_kind(c) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = return -1;\n        }\n        if (!to_input_n || json_kind(to_input_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': connection %d missing 'to_input'\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->connections[i].to_box   = json_string_value(to_box_n);\n        box->connections[i].to_input = json_string_value(to_input_n);\n\n        /* from_branch is optional: NULL for plain output ports, or\n         * \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\" for comparator, or branch name for\n         * iterator. The validation that the branch matches the\n         * routing kind lives in phase 4 (topology). */\n        json_node_t *fb = json_object_get(c, \"from_branch\");\n        box->connections[i].from_branch =\n            (fb && json_kind(fb) == JSON_STRING) ? json_string_value(fb) : NULL;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_box_file() — read one boxes/<id>.json into a box_t */\nstatic int parse_box_file(graph_t *g, box_t *box,\n                          const char *path, char **err)\n{\n    int err_line = 0;\n    const char *err_msg = NULL;\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse_file(g->arena, path, &err_line, &err_msg);\n    if (!n) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s:%d: %s\", path, err_line, err_msg ? err_msg : \"parse error\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: top-level must be a JSON object\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    memset(box, 0, sizeof *box);\n\n    /* id */\n    json_node_t *id_n = json_object_get(n, \"id\");\n    if (!id_n || json_kind(id_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: missing or non-string 'id'\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    box->id = json_string_value(id_n);\n\n    /* kind */\n    json_node_t *kind_n = json_object_get(n, \"kind\");\n    if (!kind_n || json_kind(kind_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: box '%s' missing 'kind'\", path, box->id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    const char *kind_str = json_string_value(kind_n);\n    if      (strcmp(kind_str, \"call\")       == 0) box->kind = BOX_CALL;\n    else if (strcmp(kind_str, \"data\")       == 0) box->kind = BOX_DATA;\n    else if (strcmp(kind_str, \"file_write\") == 0) box->kind = BOX_FILE_WRITE;\n    else {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: box '%s': unknown kind '%s'\", path, box->id, kind_str);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Kind-specific required fields */\n    if (box->kind == BOX_CALL) {\n        json_node_t *ref_n = json_object_get(n, \"ref\");\n        if (!ref_n || json_kind(ref_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"%s: call box '%s' missing 'ref'\", path, box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->ref = json_string_value(ref_n);\n\n        json_node_t *fn_n = json_object_get(n, \"fn\");\n        if (fn_n && json_kind(fn_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->fn = json_string_value(fn_n);\n        }\n\n        json_node_t *lang_n = json_object_get(n, \"lang\");\n        if (lang_n && json_kind(lang_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->lang = json_node_t *oc_n = json_object_get(n, \"output_capacity\");\n        if (oc_n && json_kind(oc_n) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n            box->output_capacity = (int)json_number_value(oc_n);\n        }\n    } else if (box->kind == BOX_DATA) {\n        json_node_t *path_n = json_object_get(n, \"path\");\n        if (!path_n || json_kind(path_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"%s: data box '%s' missing 'path'\", path, box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->path = json_string_value(path_n);\n    }\n    /* file_write boxes: nothing additional beyond inputs. */\n\n    if (parse_inputs(json_object_get(n, \"inputs\"),\n                     box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n    if (parse_connections(json_object_get(n, \"connections\"),\n                          box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ count_json_files_in_dir() — first pass, count .json entries */\nstatic int count_json_files_in_dir(const char *dir, char **err)\n{\n    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = 0;\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        if (ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\")) n++;\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_meta() — parse map_dir/meta.json into the graph */\nstatic int load_meta(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", map_dir);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"meta.json path too long\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int err_line = 0; const char *err_msg = NULL;\n    json_node_t *meta = json_parse_file(g->arena, path, &err_line, &err_msg);\n    if (!meta) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s:%d: %s\", path, err_line, err_msg ? err_msg : \"parse error\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(meta) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: top-level must be a JSON object\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *name = json_object_get(meta, \"name\");\n    if (!name || json_kind(name) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: missing 'name'\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    g->name = json_string_value(name);\n\n    json_node_t *entry = json_object_get(meta, \"entry_box_id\");\n    if (entry && json_kind(entry) == JSON_STRING) {\n        g->entry_box_id = json_string_value(entry);\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *desc = json_object_get(meta, \"description\");\n    if (desc && json_kind(desc) == JSON_STRING) {\n        g->description = json_string_value(desc);\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_boxes() — walk boxes/, parse every .json into g->boxes */\nstatic int load_boxes(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n{\n    char dir[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, \"%s/boxes\", map_dir);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof dir) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"boxes path too long\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int n = count_json_files_in_dir(dir, err);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n\n    g->n_boxes = n;\n    if (n == 0) { g->boxes = NULL; return 0; }\n    g->boxes = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(box_t));\n    if (!g->boxes) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n    if (!d) { *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir); return -1; }\n\n    int i = 0;\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.')              continue;\n        if (!ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\"))   continue;\n\n        char path[4096];\n        int wp = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s\", dir, e->d_name);\n        if (wp < 0 || wp >= (int)sizeof path) {\n            closedir(d);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box path too long\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n\n        if (parse_box_file(g, &g->boxes[i], path, err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        i++;\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n\n    /* Validate id uniqueness (O(n^2) scan; n is small). */\n    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {\n        for (int k = j + 1; k < n; k++) {\n            if (strcmp(g->boxes[j].id, g->boxes[k].id) == 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"duplicate (!g) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n\n    g->arena = json_arena_create();\n    if (!g->arena) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        free(g);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    if (load_meta(g, map_dir, err) != 0)  { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n    if (load_boxes(g, map_dir, err) != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n    return g;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_destroy() */\nvoid graph_destroy(graph_t *g)\n{\n    if (!g) return;\n    if (g->boxes) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            free(g->boxes[i].inputs);\n            free(g->boxes[i].connections);\n        }\n        free(g->boxes);\n    }\n    json_arena_destroy(g->arena);\n    free(g);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors *g, int i)\n{\n    if (!g || i < 0 || i >= g->n_boxes) return NULL;\n    return &g->boxes[i];\n}\n\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n{\n    if (!g || !id) return NULL;\n     "content":"/* tests/010-graph-loader-test.c — unit tests for the graph loader.\n *\n * Exercises the phase 1 + phase 2 + early phase 3 work shipped in\n * this iteration: directory walk, JSON parse, per-box schema\n * validation. Topology / cycle / language-enumeration tests land\n * with their iterations.\n *\n * Fixtures live under tests/maps/. Tests cd to the project root so\n * relative paths work regardless of where the test binary is run.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Path resolution — find tests/maps/ relative to cwd */\nstatic const char *FIXTURE_DIR = \"tests/maps\";\n\n/* If tests are run from project root: tests/maps/ exists.\n * If run from build/tests/: the binary was started by make test,\n * which cd's to project root first. We don't try to be clever here. */\nstatic int has_fixtures(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    return stat(FIXTURE_DIR, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_hello() */\nstatic int test_load_hello(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_name(g), \"hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_entry_box_id(g), \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(graph_description(g) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    /* greet box */\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet != NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->kind == BOX_CALL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->lang, \"lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->ref,  \"src/hello.lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->fn,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->routing.kind == ROUTING_PLAIN);\n    ASSERT(greet->output_capacity == 256);\n    ASSERT(greet->n_inputs == 2);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[0].name, \"name\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].literal == NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].optional == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].name, \"salutation\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].literal, \"Hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[1].optional == 1);\n\n    /* who box */\n    const box_t *who = graph_box_by_id(g, \"who\");\n    ASSERT(who != NULL);\n    ASSERT(who->kind == BOX_DATA);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->path, \"names.txt\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->n_connections == 1);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_box,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_input, \"name\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->connections[0].from_branch == NULL);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_branching() — comparator + iterator routing kinds */\nstatic int test_load_branching(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/branching\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    const box_t *src = graph_box_by_id(g, \"source\");\n    ASSERT(src != NULL);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.n_outputs == 3);\n\n    const box_t *cls = graph_box_by_id(g, \"classify\");\n    ASSERT(cls != NULL);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.kind == ROUTING_COMPARATOR);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.comparand == 5.0);\n    ASSERT(cls->n_connections == 3);\n    /* All three branches reachable. */\n    int seen_lt = 0, seen_eq = 0, seen_gt = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < cls->n_connections; i++) {\n        const char *b = cls->connections[i].from_branch;\n        if      (b && strcmp(b, \"lt\") == 0) seen_lt = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"eq\") == 0) seen_eq = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"gt\") == 0) seen_gt = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lt && seen_eq && seen_gt);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_map_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_map_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/does-not-exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    /* Error mentions the path. */\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"does-not-exist\") != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_argument() */\nstatic int test_null_argument(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Helpers for malformed-fixture tests */\n/* Make a temp map directory with a given meta.json and a single\n * box file. Caller frees `out_dir` (or just lets it leak — tests\n * are short-lived). */\nstatic int make_temp_map(const char *meta_json,\n                         const char *box_name,\n                         const char *box_json,\n                         char **out_dir)\n{\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-loader-test-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    if (!dir) return -1;\n    *out_dir = strdup(dir);\n\n    char path[4096];\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\"); if (!fp) return -1;\n    fputs(meta_json, fp); fclose(fp);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir);\n    mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir, box_name);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\"); if (!fp) return -1;\n    fputs(box_json, fp); fclose(fp);\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void cleanup_temp_map(const char *dir, const char *box_name)\n{\n    char p[4096];\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir, box_name); unlink(p);\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);              unlink(p);\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/boxes\", dir);                  rmdir(p);\n    rmdir(dir);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_unknown_kind() */\nstatic int test_unknown_kind(void)\n{\n    char *dir = NULL;\n    ASSERT(make_temp_map(\n        \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"t\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\n        \"x\",\n        \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"frobnicate\\\"}\",\n        &dir) == 0);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"frobnicate\") != NULL);\n\n    free(err);\n    cleanup_temp_map(dir, \"x\");\n    free(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_routing() */\nstatic int test_missing_routing(void)\n{\n    char *dir = NULL;\n    ASSERT(make_temp_map(\n        \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"t\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\n        \"x\",\n        \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"ref\\\":\\\"foo.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"foo\\\"}\",\n        &dir) == 0);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"routing\") != NULL);\n\n    free(err);\n    cleanup_temp_map(dir, \"x\");\n    free(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_duplicate_id() */\nstatic int test_duplicate_id(void)\n{\n    /* Use a temp dir with two boxes whose JSON declares the same id. */\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-dup-test-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    ASSERT(dir);\n\n    char path[4096];\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"t\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir);\n    mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/a.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"ref\\\":\\\"f.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"f\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"plain\\\"}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/b.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"ref\\\":\\\"g.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"g\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"plain\\\"}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err && strstr(err, \"duplicate\") != NULL);\n    free(err);\n\n    /* Cleanup. */\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/a.json\", dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/b.json\", dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\",   dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\",       dir); rmdir(path);\n    rmdir(dir);\n\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The test runner is invoked from the project root by `make test`. */\n    if (!has_fixtures()) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"010-graph-loader-test: tests/maps/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"010-graph-loader-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_hello);\n    RUN(load_branching);\n    RUN(missing_map_dir);\n    RUN(null_argument);\n    RUN(unknown_kind);\n    RUN(missing_routing);\n    RUN(duplicate_id);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

Topology / cycle / language-enumeration tests land\n * with their iterations.\n *\n * Fixtures live under tests/maps/. Tests cd to the project root so\n * relative paths work regardless of where the test binary is run.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Path resolution — find tests/maps/ relative to cwd */\nstatic const char *FIXTURE_DIR = \"tests/maps\";\n\n/* If tests are run from project root: tests/maps/ exists.\n * If run from build/tests/: the binary was started by make test,\n * which cd's to project root first. We don't try to be clever here. */\nstatic int has_fixtures(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    return stat(FIXTURE_DIR, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_hello() */\nstatic int test_load_hello(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_name(g), \"hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_entry_box_id(g), \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(graph_description(g) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    /* greet box */\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet != NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->kind == BOX_CALL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->lang, \"lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->ref,  \"src/hello.lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->fn,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->routing.kind == ROUTING_PLAIN);\n    ASSERT(greet->output_capacity == 256);\n    ASSERT(greet->n_inputs == 2);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[0].name, \"name\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].literal == NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].optional == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].name, \"salutation\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].literal, \"Hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[1].optional == 1);\n\n    /* who box */\n    const box_t *who = graph_box_by_id(g, \"who\");\n    ASSERT(who != NULL);\n    ASSERT(who->kind == BOX_DATA);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->path, \"names.txt\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->n_connections == 1);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_box,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_input, \"name\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->connections[0].from_branch == NULL);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_branching() — comparator + iterator routing kinds */\nstatic int test_load_branching(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/branching\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    const box_t *src = graph_box_by_id(g, \"source\");\n    ASSERT(src != NULL);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.n_outputs == 3);\n\n    const box_t *cls = graph_box_by_id(g, \"classify\");\n    ASSERT(cls != NULL);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.kind == ROUTING_COMPARATOR);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.comparand == 5.0);\n    ASSERT(cls->n_connections == 3);\n    /* All three branches reachable. */\n    int seen_lt = 0, seen_eq = 0, seen_gt = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < cls->n_connections; i++) {\n        const char *b = cls->connections[i].from_branch;\n        if      (b && strcmp(b, \"lt\") == 0) seen_lt = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"eq\") == 0) seen_eq = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"gt\") == 0) seen_gt = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lt && seen_eq && seen_gt);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_map_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_map_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/does-not-exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    /* Error mentions the path. */\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"does-not-exist\") != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_argument() */\nstatic int test_null_argument(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Helpers for malformed-fixture tests */\n/* Make a temp map directory with a given meta.json and a single\n * box file. snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir);\n    mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir, box_name);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\"); if (!fp) return -1;\n    fputs(box_json, fp); fclose(fp);\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void cleanup_temp_map(const char *dir, const char *box_name)\n{\n    char p[4096];\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir,    \"x\",\n        \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"frobnicate\\\"}\",\n        &dir) == 0);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"frobnicate\") != NULL);\n\n    free(err);\n    cleanup_temp_map(dir, \"x\");\n    free(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"routing\") != NULL);\n\n    free(err);\n    cleanup_temp_map(dir, \"x\");\n    free(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_duplicate_id() */\nstatic int test_duplicate_id(void)\n{\n    /* Use a temp dir with two boxes whose JSON declares the same id. */\n    char tmpl[] = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/a.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"ref\\\":\\\"f.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"f\\\",\"\n As each test lands,"," # add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit"," # is clearer than clever for tests).","-$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o","-$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o","+$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o","+$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\","+                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o","+$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o"," "," # Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared"," # above plus the test's own .o file."],
        "oldStart":115
      }],
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o",
    "newString":"$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o",

          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 010-graph-loader.c — public surface\n\nC graph loader (phase 3). Reads a map directory, parses every\nJSON file, and produces an in-memory `graph_t` the dispatch layer\nand pool runner consume. Replaces `src/003-loader.lua`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `graph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err)` — read +\n  parse + validate. Returns NULL on any failure and sets `*err` to\n  a malloc'd `\"<file>:<line>: <message>\"` diagnostic. The caller\n  frees `*err`.\n- `void graph_destroy(graph_t *g)` — frees every byte the graph\n  owns (the box and connection arrays, the input declarations, the\n  underlying JSON arena holding every string).\n\n## Accessors\n\n- `const char *graph_name(g)`\n- `const char *graph_description(g)`\n- `const char *graph_entry_box_id(g)`\n- `int          graph_n_boxes(g)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box(g, i)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box_by_id(g, id)`\n\n## Public types\n\n- `box_kind_t` — `BOX_CALL` / `BOX_DATA` / `BOX_FILE_WRITE`.\n- `routing_kind_t` — `ROUTING_PLAIN` / `ROUTING_COMPARATOR` /\n  `ROUTING_ITERATOR`; randomizer / weighted / distributor enum\n  values exist but the parser doesn't accept them yet.\n- `routing_t` — `kind` plus per-kind params (`n_outputs`,\n  `comparand`).\n- `input_decl_t` — `name`, `type`, `literal`, `optional`.\n- `connection_t` — outgoing connection. Stores string refs\n  (`to_box`, `to_input`); resolved-to-integer-index forms come in\n  the topology iteration.\n- `box_t` — all of the above per box.\n\n## Schema currently enforced\n\n- `meta.json` must be a JSON object containing at least `name`.\n- Every file under `boxes/` ending in `.json` is a box file with a\n  top-level object, `id` (string), `kind` ∈ `{call, data, file_write}`.\n- `call` boxes: require `ref` and `routing`. `fn` is optional (a\n  language without function-name dispatch is fine). `lang` is\n  optional too — falls back to inference from `ref` extension once\n  the spec registry lands.\n- `data` boxes: require `path`; no `ref` / `fn` / `routing`.\n- `file_write` boxes: no kind-specific required fields beyond\n  inputs.\n- `routing.kind` ∈ `{plain, comparator, iterator}` (issue 233's\n  shipped surface). `comparator` requires `comparand` (number or\n  string-form number per the issue's example shape).\n  `iterator` requires `n_outputs` (>= 1).\n- Box ids must be unique across the map. O(n²) scan; n is small.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred to follow-on iterations within 305)\n\n- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints aren't\n  resolved to integer indices yet; we don't verify that every\n  `to_box` refers to a real box, nor that the `to_input` matches a\n  declared port. Cycle detection (excluding iterator-rooted\n  cycles) lands here too.\n- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The slot store's\n  `slot_alloc` consumes a `cell_capacity`; the loader's job is to\n  scan box outputs and enumerate the distinct sizes the graph\n  needs.\n- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** Boxes with no inputs (or\n  inputs fed only by `data` boxes) get auto-detected as entry\n  points.\n- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Walk every call box,\n  collect distinct `lang` values, hand the set to the spec\n  registry.\n- The remaining routing kinds (`randomizer`, `weighted`,\n  `distributor`) — issue 233 deferred them to their own\n  follow-ons; the parser rejects them with a precise message.\n\nNone of these block issues 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 305 — design.\n- Issue 233 — unified routing schema this loader implements.\n- Issue 229 — data / file_write box kinds.\n- Issue 314 — the JSON parser this depends on.\n- Issue 302 — slot store; the loader will eventually hand size\n  class enumeration to it.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.info.md"
        }
      }],
    "role":"assistant",
    "id":"msg_01AUcyi7DJpSqreBapaNY2Hf",
    "model":"claude-opus-4-7",
    "type":"message",
    "stop_reason":"tool_use",
    "usage":{

          "new_string":"- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — the compiler is the other consumer of\n  the same validation logic; the C loader and the compiler should\n  share validation code if possible\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Phase 1 + 2 + early phase 3 — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `src/010-graph-loader.h` — public types and API. `graph_t` is\n  opaque; the box / connection / input declaration shapes are\n  public so the dispatch layer (issue 304) can walk them directly.\n  Routing kinds align with issue 233 — `routing_t` with `kind`\n  plus per-kind parameters, no legacy `comparand` /\n  `iterator_outputs` top-level fields.\n- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — implementation. Pipeline: open the\n  map dir, parse `meta.json` via the project JSON parser\n  (issue 314), walk every `.json` under `boxes/`, parse each into\n  a `box_t`, enforce kind-specific required fields (ref/routing\n  for call; path for data; inputs only for file_write), validate\n  id uniqueness across boxes. Errors return a malloc'd\n  `<file>:<line>: <message>` diagnostic via the `**err`\n  out-parameter; the pool runner's main is expected to print and\n  abort.\n- `tests/maps/hello/` and `tests/maps/branching/` — fixture maps\n  exercising the call/data combo, comparator routing (lt/eq/gt\n  branches all present), and iterator routing (n_outputs=3).\n- `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c` — 7 unit tests covering\n  successful loads of both fixtures, missing map directory,\n  NULL argument, unknown box kind, missing routing, and\n  duplicate box id. Malformed-shape tests use mkdtemp scratch\n  dirs so the tracked fixtures stay valid.\n- Memory model: one `json_arena_t` per loaded graph holds every\n  string and every parsed tree from every file; the box,\n  connection, and input declaration arrays are plain malloc.\n  `graph_destroy` releases all of it.\n- `.gitignore` anchored to `/maps/` so `tests/maps/` is tracked.\n- Makefile per-test dependency line for `010-graph-loader-test`\n  linking the loader and the JSON parser.\n\nVerified `make STRICT=1` builds cleanly; 33 tests across three\nsuites (slot store 12, graph loader 7, JSON 14) all pass.\n\nWhat's deferred to follow-on iterations within 305:\n- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints store\n  string refs only. The next pass resolves `to_box` to integer\n  indices, verifies endpoints exist, and detects non-iterator\n  cycles via DFS.\n- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The loader needs to\n  walk every box output and produce the distinct `cell_capacity`\n  values the slot store's allocator pre-populates.\n- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** A box with zero inputs or\n  with all inputs fed only by `data` boxes is an entry. The pool\n  runner spawns initial tasks for these.\n- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Distinct `lang` values\n  across call boxes, handed to the spec registry (issue 303).\n- The remaining routing kinds from issue 233 (randomizer,\n  weighted, distributor) — the parser currently rejects them with\n  a precise message.\n\nNone of those block 301 / 303 / 306. Topology and language\nenumeration land before 304 (the dispatch layer) since the\ndispatch action needs both.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/305-c-graph-loader.md"

          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nGraph loader — directory walk, JSON parse, per-box schema (issue 305)\n\nFirst substantive bite of the C graph loader. Reads a map\ndirectory off disk, parses every JSON file in it with the project\nparser from 314, and produces an in-memory graph describing the\nboxes, their routing kinds, their input ports, and their outgoing\nconnections. Topology validation, slot size class enumeration,\nentry-box detection, and language enumeration are deferred to\nfollow-on iterations within the same issue.\n\nThe shape on disk: meta.json at the top with the map name,\ndescription, and the entry box id; one .json file per box under\nboxes/; for call boxes, the unified routing schema from issue 233\n(plain / comparator / iterator), with the other three kinds\nreserved in the enum but rejected at parse with a precise message.\nThe data and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are recognised\nand validated. Input ports carry the optional flag from issue 230;\nliteral values are accepted as strings (other primitive literal\nforms land when something needs them).\n\nMemory model leans on the JSON arena from 314. One arena per\nloaded graph holds every parsed tree and every string the graph\npoints at across every file; the box, connection, and input\ndeclaration arrays are plain malloc, sized once after the\ndiscovery walk. graph_destroy frees the whole stack in one call.\n\nErrors return through an out-parameter as a malloc'd diagnostic\nof the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The pool runner's main is\nexpected to print and abort upstream, per the hard-crash policy;\nthe loader stays a library so the test harness can verify\nfailures without aborting.\n\nTwo tracked fixture maps under tests/maps/ — one minimal call +\ndata pair, one with comparator and iterator routing exercising\nall three lt/eq/gt branches and n_outputs=3. Seven loader tests\ncover both fixtures plus the malformed shapes (unknown kind,\nmissing routing, duplicate id, missing directory, NULL input).\nMalformed cases use mkdtemp scratch directories so the tracked\nfixtures stay valid for future iterations to read against. The\ngitignore is now anchored to /maps/ so user content at the\nproject root stays out of source control while tests/maps/\nremains tracked.\n\nThirty-three tests across the three suites pass under strict-mode\nwarnings-as-errors.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"\necho \"---\"\ngit log --oneline -6",

        }

    "content":"# libs/task-pool/pool.c — public surface\n\nSoraMech-owned thread pool. N pthread workers pulling tasks off a\nsingle FIFO queue. Designed in issue 301. The 3d-rts pool at\n`/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h`\nwas the design reference; nothing was vendored.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `pool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)` — spawns workers and parks\n  them at the init barrier. `n_workers <= 0` uses\n  `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)` capped at `POOL_MAX_WORKERS`\n  (16). `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N` env var overrides. NULL on\n  allocation / pthread failure.\n- `void pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)` — blocks until every worker\n  reaches the barrier, then releases them all simultaneously.\n  One-shot; the spec-registry plug-in point sits between\n  `pool_create` and `pool_init_barrier`.\n- `void pool_destroy(pool_t *p)` — flips shutdown, drains the\n  queue, joins every worker, frees.\n\n## Submission\n\n- `void pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg)` —\n  safe from any thread, including from inside another action.\n- `void pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)` — blocks until the\n  active-task counter reaches zero.\n- `int  pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)` — count.\n\n## Worker context\n\n- `extern __thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker` — set on\n  every worker before the barrier; readable from any action.\n- `worker_ctx_t.thread_idx` — 0-based worker index.\n- `worker_ctx_t.pool` — back-pointer.\n- `worker_ctx_t.handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS]` — reserved for the\n  spec registry (issue 303).\n\n## Concurrency model\n\n- One mutex for the FIFO queue (`q_mtx`), one CV (`q_cv`) for\n  workers waiting on work.\n- Atomic active-task counter; one mutex/CV pair (`quiet_mtx`,\n  `quiet_cv`) for the quiescence waiter.\n- One mutex/CV pair (`init_mtx`, `init_cv`) for the init barrier.\n- The three pairs never nest. Lock-ordering is moot.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- **Per-worker spec init** between `pool_create` and\n  `pool_init_barrier`. Lands with issue 303's spec registry.\n- **Priority queue** (issue 310): the current queue is a plain\n  singly-linked FIFO. The priority work is \"wired in, no-op\n  behaviorally\" until something distinguishes task priorities.\n- **Frame-ring scheduling / park-on-slot**: the 3d-rts pool's\n  design has these; we don't need them for the dispatch model\n  (issue 304), which always spawns tasks when inputs are ready\n  rather than parking on slot wait lists.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 301 — design.\n- Issue 302 — slot store, the thing tasks read and write through.\n- Issue 303 — spec registry; per-worker init hook.\n- Issue 304 — dispatch action, the function `pool_spawn`'d on\n  every task.\n- Issue 310 — priority queue (open).\n",

          "content":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.h — SoraMech-owned thread pool, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: N worker threads pulling tasks off a\n * single mutex-protected queue, with a one-shot init barrier and a\n * condition-variable-based quiescence wait.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. Reference: the 3d-rts pool at\n * /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h\n * (design only, not vendored).\n *\n * Lifecycle:\n *\n *   1. pool_create(n_workers)\n *        - spawns the worker threads\n *        - each worker sets its TLS context and parks at the init\n *          barrier (no init work to do yet; 303 plugs spec init in\n *          here later)\n *   2. pool_init_barrier(pool)\n *        - blocks until every worker has reached the barrier\n *        - releases them all simultaneously\n *        - one-shot; returns; barrier never engages again\n *   3. pool_spawn / pool_wait_quiescent — main loop of work\n *   4. pool_destroy(pool)\n *        - flips the shutdown flag, broadcasts the queue cv,\n *          joins every worker, frees the pool\n *\n * Per-worker context is reachable from inside any task action via\n * the `pool_current_worker` TLS pointer. The handle slots are\n * reserved for the spec registry (issue 303); ignore them for now.\n *\n * Thread safety: every public function is safe to call from any\n * thread. pool_spawn from inside an action is fine and is how\n * iterators and graph traversal will work.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_POOL_H\n#define SORAMECH_POOL_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct pool pool_t;\n\n/* A pool action takes one void* argument and returns nothing.\n * Errors are the action's business — the pool just dispatches. */\ntypedef void (*pool_action_t)(void *arg);\n\n/* Per-worker context. Reserved for issue 303's per-language runtime\n * handles; the pool itself only uses thread_idx and pool. */\n#define POOL_LANG_SLOTS 16\n\ntypedef struct worker_ctx {\n    int     thread_idx;\n    pool_t *pool;\n    void   *handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS];\n} worker_ctx_t;\n\n/* Set on every worker thread before the init barrier; readable from\n * any pool action. */\nextern __thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker;\n\n#define POOL_MAX_WORKERS 16\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Create a pool with n_workers threads. If n_workers <= 0, defaults\n * to sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) capped at POOL_MAX_WORKERS. The\n * SORAMECH_WORKERS environment variable, if set and >0, overrides\n * the default. Returns NULL on allocation or pthread_create failure. */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers);\n\n/* Block until every worker has finished its (currently empty) init\n * sequence and is parked at the barrier; then release them all. The\n * 303 spec-registry plug-in point lives between pool_create and\n * pool_init_barrier. One-shot. */\nvoid    pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p);\n\n/* Stop accepting tasks, drain whatever's queued, join every worker,\n * free the pool. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid    pool_destroy(pool_t *p);\n\nint     pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Submission and wait */\n/* Submit a task. Safe from any thread (including from inside another\n * action). Increments the active-task counter; the worker that runs\n * the task decrements it on return. */\nvoid    pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg);\n\n/* Block until the active-task counter reaches zero. Calling this\n * before pool_init_barrier with pending tasks is a programming\n * error — workers haven't been released yet, so nothing will drain. */\nvoid    pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_POOL_H */\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/task-pool/pool.h"
        }
