    "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.c — SoraMech thread pool, implementation.\n *\n * Pthreads, a singly-linked FIFO task queue under one mutex, a\n * condition variable for \"queue has work or we're shutting down\",\n * an atomic active-task counter with its own mutex/cv for the\n * quiescence wait, and a one-shot init barrier under a third\n * mutex/cv.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. The three sync primitives never nest —\n * pool_spawn takes the queue mutex, pool_wait_quiescent takes the\n * quiet mutex, pool_init_barrier takes the init mutex. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked FIFO */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its (currently empty) per-thread setup; main thread\n     * waits for workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released\n     * and broadcasts. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point — issue 303 plugs spec->init calls here\n     * for every language the map uses. Empty for now. */\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready, notify the main thread, then park at\n     * the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) pthread_join(p->threads[j], NULL);\n            goto fail;\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n\nfail:\n    if (p) {\n        free(p->threads);\n        free(p->contexts);\n        free(p);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_init_barrier() */\nvoid pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    while (p->workers_ready < p->n_workers) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    p->init_released = 1;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn   = fn;\n    t->arg  = arg;\n    t->next = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    if (p->q_tail) p->q_tail->next = t;\n    else           p->q_head       = t;\n    p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_wait_quiescent() */\nvoid pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    while (atomic_load_explicit(&p->active, memory_order_acquire) > 0) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->quiet_cv, &p->quiet_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_n_workers() */\nint pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)\n{\n    return p ? p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < p->n_workers; i++) {\n        pthread_join(p->threads[i], NULL);\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->quiet_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->init_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->init_cv);\n\n    free(p->threads);\n    free(p->contexts);\n    free(p);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

Spawning + quiescence work — verifiable by running the\n * binary against tests/maps/hello.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        free(err);\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!p) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: cannot create thread pool\\n\");\n        graph_destroy(g);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' loaded — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g),\n        graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(p));\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: dispatch layer not yet wired (issue 304); \"\n        \"quiescing with no tasks.\\n\");\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

The eventual main\n * body, in pseudocode (see docs/HTML/001-architecture.html):\n *\n *   1.  parse map path from argv\n *   2.  load and validate graph    (issue 305 graph loader)\n *   3.  determine languages used   (issue 305)\n *   4.  allocate per-port slots    (issue 302 slot store)\n *   5.  pool = pool_create(N)      (issue 301 pool lifecycle)\n *   6.  init per-worker handles    (issue 303 spec registry)\n *   7.  pool_init_barrier(pool)    (issue 301)\n *   8.  push literal input values  (issue 304 dispatch)\n *   9.  spawn entry-box tasks      (issue 304)\n *   10. pool_wait_quiescent(pool)  (issue 301)\n *   11. write last-run.jsonl       (issue 311)\n *   12. pool_destroy(pool)         (issue 301)\n *\n * At this scaffolding stage we just parse argv, print a banner so\n * the build link is verified end-to-end, and exit 0.\n */\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map.           "content":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1));\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1));\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

          "new_string":"- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — replaces 004-executor.lua\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — threading roadmap and IPC options\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Pool skeleton — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `libs/task-pool/pool.h` + `pool.c` — SoraMech-owned pool with N\n  pthread workers, a singly-linked FIFO queue under one mutex,\n  atomic active-task counter with its own cv for quiescence wait,\n  one-shot init barrier with workers_ready / init_released\n  predicates under a third mutex. Worker count defaults to logical\n  CPUs (capped at `POOL_MAX_WORKERS=16`), overridable via\n  `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N`. Recursive `pool_spawn` from inside an\n  action works — the queue mutex is re-entered cleanly.\n- TLS `pool_current_worker` for actions that need their worker\n  index or the back-pointer to the pool.\n- `tests/301-pool-test.c` — 8 unit tests: create/destroy with no\n  tasks, default worker count, cap-at-max, single spawn, 1000-task\n  spawn-and-quiesce, TLS context observable from inside actions,\n  recursive spawn (depth 10 → 11 invocations), and 8 concurrent\n  producer threads each pushing 500 tasks while 4 workers drain\n  (4000 total). All pass under STRICT.\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` now loads the graph via 305 and stands up\n  the pool: `./soramech-pool tests/maps/hello` prints the box count,\n  entry box, and worker count, then quiesces cleanly with no tasks.\n\nWhat's deferred to follow-ons within 301:\n- **Per-worker spec init** between `pool_create` and\n  `pool_init_barrier`. The hook is documented in `worker_main`;\n  lands with issue 303 once specs can be `dlopen`ed and\n  per-worker handles allocated.\n- **Priority queue.** Issue 310 covers the \"wired in, no-op\n  behaviorally\" upgrade. Current queue is plain FIFO.\n\nNeither blocks 304 (dispatch) from starting.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md"
        }

    "originalFile":"# 301 — Thread pool lifecycle and per-worker initialization\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe executor (`src/004-executor.lua`) runs boxes synchronously in a\nsingle Lua coroutine. There is no thread pool, no pthreads, and no\nper-thread language runtime state.\n\n## Phase model\n\nPhase 2 is the synchronous interpreter path. It is the development\ntarget while editor work is in progress.\n\nPhase 3 is the thread pool path. It is the only execution path going\nforward. The synchronous interpreter does not stay around as an\nalternative entry point — once phase 3 lands, the pool runner\nreplaces it. There is no \"fallback to synchronous\" mode.\n\n### Phase 2 → 3 refactor surface\n\nThe following components are replaced (not extended) in phase 3:\n\n| Phase 2 file                  | Phase 3 replacement                  |\n|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------|\n| `src/003-loader.lua`          | C loader inside `src/008-pool-runner.c` |\n| `src/004-executor.lua`        | C task dispatch layer (issue 304)    |\n| `src/007-runner-main.lua`     | `src/008-pool-runner.c`              |\n| `drivers/*.sh`                | Language runtime spec (issue 303)    |\n\nAll threading-pool-adjacent functionality is C code that lives next to\nthe pool. There is no embedded Lua runtime for graph loading or\ndispatch — Lua appears only as a language runtime that boxes can use,\non equal footing with C, Bash, and any future language.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Pool source\nThe thread pool is **SoraMech-owned**, written from scratch under\n`libs/task-pool/`. The 3d-rts pool at\n`/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h`\nis the **design reference**, not a dependency. We need full control\nover the spawn primitive, the worker context, the init barrier\n(below), and iterator-pinning extensions — all reasons not to inherit\nan external implementation.\n\nThe pool exposes (at minimum):\n\n```c\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers);\nvoid    pool_destroy(pool_t *p);\nvoid    pool_spawn(pool_t *p, action_fn_t fn, void *arg);\nvoid    pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p);   // blocks until active count hits zero\nvoid    pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p);     // see \"Init barrier\" below\n```\n\n3d-rts's frame-ring + park-on-slot machinery is referenced for\npatterns; we don't reimplement features we don't need.\n\n### Where the pool lives in the process\nThe pool is owned by the map runner's C entry point. One pool per map\nrun. It is created after the graph is loaded and validated, and\ndestroyed after the run completes.\n\nThe C entry point (`src/008-pool-runner.c`):\n\n```c\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    // 1. parse map path from argv\n    // 2. load and validate graph (C loader, no Lua involved)\n    // 3. determine which language runtimes the map uses\n    // 4. allocate per-input-port slots for every box (issue 302)\n    // 5. pool = pool_create(n_workers)\n    // 6. init per-worker language runtime handles for each language present\n    // 7. pool_init_barrier(pool)  ← block until every worker is fully initialized\n    // 8. push every input port's literal value into its slot\n    // 9. spawn tasks for boxes whose input set is now satisfied\n    // 10. pool_wait_quiescent(pool)\n    // 11. write last-run.jsonl\n    // 12. pool_destroy(pool)\n}\n```\n\n### Init barrier\n\nWorkers are not safe to dispatch tasks to until **every worker has\nfully completed init for every language spec the map uses**. If the\nmain thread spawns a task before a worker's `lua_State` is up, the\ntask lands on a null handle.\n\n`pool_init_barrier` is the join point:\n\n1. Each worker's startup runs all `lang->init(worker_idx)` calls in\n   a defined order, populating its `worker_ctx_t.handles[]`.\n2. After completing its inits, each worker increments a shared\n   atomic `workers_ready` counter and blocks on a condition\n   variable.\n3. The main thread waits until `workers_ready == n_workers`.\n4. Main thread broadcasts the condition variable; all workers\n   release simultaneously and begin pulling tasks.\n\nThis is a one-shot barrier — it runs once at pool startup. After\nquiescence it doesn't re-engage; teardown takes a different path.\n\nThe barrier also protects against partial init failures: if any\nworker's `init` returns an error, the barrier never completes and\nthe main thread can detect it via a timeout or per-worker status\nflag.\n\n### Graph loading: ported to C\nThe graph loader is ported from `src/003-loader.lua` to C and lives\ninside (or alongside) `008-pool-runner.c`. The pool runner has no\nembedded Lua state for loader purposes. JSON parsing uses a small\nvendored C JSON library (cJSON or similar; decision deferred to\nimplementation).\n\nLua appears in the runner only when a box's language is Lua — and even\nthen, only inside that worker's language runtime handle. The pool\nrunner itself does not link to liblua at the top level.\n\n### Per-worker language runtimes\nNo language is treated as the \"native\" or preferred language at the\nthread level. Every box — regardless of language — goes through the\nsame task dispatch path. The per-box cost is determined by that box's\ninvocation wrapper, not by any map-level language setting.\n\nEach worker thread holds a set of language runtime handles, one per\nlanguage it may be asked to run. These are initialized once at pool\nstartup, before any tasks are submitted, and torn down at shutdown:\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    void   *handles[N_LANGS];   // opaque per-language runtime state\n    int     thread_idx;\n} worker_ctx_t;\n```\n\nOnly the language handles actually needed by the map are initialized.\nIf the map contains no Bash boxes, no Bash handle is started for any\nworker. The graph loader determines which languages are present and\npasses that set to the pool runner at startup.\n\nThe per-language initialization protocol is defined by the language\nruntime spec (issue 303). The pool runner calls each spec's `init`\nfunction at startup and its `teardown` function at shutdown.\n\n### Worker context access\nWorker context is stored in thread-local storage (`__thread\nworker_ctx_t *current_worker`), set by each worker immediately after\nthe thread is started. This avoids per-task `pthread_self()` lookups.\n\n### Pool size\nNumber of worker threads defaults to the number of logical CPUs\n(`sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`), capped at a compile-time maximum\n(`MAX_WORKERS`, initially 16). Can be overridden by an environment\nvariable `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N`.\n\n### Slots are owned by input ports (issue 302)\nEach box has one ring-buffer slot per input port, allocated at\ngraph load time and durable for the run. The pool runner walks\nevery box during the load step and populates a per-box slot table.\nSlots are not allocated per-task; tasks pop and push but never\nallocate. See issue 302 for the slot lifecycle and lifetime model.\n\n### Quiescence\nThe runner tracks an active-task counter, incremented on `pool_spawn`\nand decremented when a task reaches `ACT_DONE`. The main thread waits\non a condition variable that signals when the counter reaches zero.\n\nThis naturally handles iterators that re-queue themselves: each\nre-queue increments the counter, each completion decrements. When the\ncounter reaches zero, the run is over.\n\nDeadlock is not a concern at runtime. The graph validator (running at\nload) rejects non-iterator cycles and inputs without producers. Errors\ninside a task crash the program (issue 303), so there is no\nhalf-completed-producer case to worry about. An iterator parking\nbecause its upstream queue is empty is not deadlock — it is the\nnatural end-of-stream condition; once the active-task counter reaches\nzero with the iterator parked, the run ends cleanly.\n\n## Open questions\n- Vendored JSON library: cJSON, jsmn, or hand-rolled. cJSON is heavier\n  but easiest. Decision deferred.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Vendor `900-task-pool.h` + `.c` into `libs/task-pool/`.\n2. Vendor a JSON parser into `libs/json/`.\n3. Port `003-loader.lua` to C inside `src/008-pool-runner.c`.\n4. Write the pool lifecycle skeleton: pool_create, worker context TLS,\n   active-task counter, quiescence wait.\n5. Add `Makefile` target `soramech-pool` that compiles the C runner and\n   links against the vendored pool and JSON parser.\n6. Smoke test: single-box Lua map, pool with 2 workers, box runs, result\n   written. No task graph complexity yet.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/task-pool/` — SoraMech-built pool (to be created)\n- `/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h` — design reference only\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — current Lua loader, to be ported to C\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — current synchronous executor, to be replaced\n- `src/007-runner-main.lua` — current Lua runner, to be replaced\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — per-port slot model\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — per-language init/call/teardown\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — replaces 004-executor.lua\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — threading roadmap and IPC options\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — replaces 004-executor.lua\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — threading roadmap and IPC options",
    "newString":"- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — replaces 004-executor.lua\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — threading roadmap and IPC options\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Pool skeleton — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `libs/task-pool/pool.h` + `pool.c` — SoraMech-owned pool with N\n  pthread workers, a singly-linked FIFO queue under one mutex,\n  atomic active-task counter with its own cv for quiescence wait,\n  one-shot init barrier with workers_ready / init_released\n  predicates under a third mutex. Worker count defaults to logical\n  CPUs (capped at `POOL_MAX_WORKERS=16`), overridable via\n  `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N`. Recursive `pool_spawn` from inside an\n  action works — the queue mutex is re-entered cleanly.\n- TLS `pool_current_worker` for actions that need their worker\n  index or the back-pointer to the pool.\n- `tests/301-pool-test.c` — 8 unit tests: create/destroy with no\n  tasks, default worker count, cap-at-max, single spawn, 1000-task\n  spawn-and-quiesce, TLS context observable from inside actions,\n  recursive spawn (depth 10 → 11 invocations), and 8 concurrent\n  producer threads each pushing 500 tasks while 4 workers drain\n  (4000 total). All pass under STRICT.\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` now loads the graph via 305 and stands up\n  the pool: `./soramech-pool tests/maps/hello` prints the box count,\n  entry box, and worker count, then quiesces cleanly with no tasks.\n\nWhat's deferred to follow-ons within 301:\n- **Per-worker spec init** between `pool_create` and\n  `pool_init_barrier`. The hook is documented in `worker_main`;\n  lands with issue 303 once specs can be `dlopen`ed and\n  per-worker handles allocated.\n- **Priority queue.** Issue 310 covers the \"wired in, no-op\n  behaviorally\" upgrade.     "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.h — SoraMech-owned thread pool, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: N worker threads pulling tasks off a\n * single mutex-protected queue, with a one-shot init barrier and a\n * condition-variable-based quiescence wait.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. Reference: the 3d-rts pool at\n * /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h\n * (design only, not vendored).\n *\n * Lifecycle:\n *\n *   1. pool_create(n_workers)\n *        - spawns the worker threads\n *        - each worker sets its TLS context and parks at the init\n *          barrier (no init work to do yet; 303 plugs spec init in\n *          here later)\n *   2. pool_init_barrier(pool)\n *        - blocks until every worker has reached the barrier\n *        - releases them all simultaneously\n *        - one-shot; returns; barrier never engages again\n *   3. pool_spawn / pool_wait_quiescent — main loop of work\n *   4. pool_destroy(pool)\n *        - flips the shutdown flag, broadcasts the queue cv,\n *          joins every worker, frees the pool\n *\n * Per-worker context is reachable from inside any task action via\n * the `pool_current_worker` TLS pointer. The handle slots are\n * reserved for the spec registry (issue 303); ignore them for now.\n *\n * Thread safety: every public function is safe to call from any\n * thread. pool_spawn from inside an action is fine and is how\n * iterators and graph traversal will work.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_POOL_H\n#define SORAMECH_POOL_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct pool pool_t;\n\n/* A pool action takes one void* argument and returns nothing.\n * Errors are the action's business — the pool just dispatches. */\ntypedef void (*pool_action_t)(void *arg);\n\n/* Per-worker context. Reserved for issue 303's per-language runtime\n * handles; the pool itself only uses thread_idx and pool. */\n#define POOL_LANG_SLOTS 16\n\ntypedef struct worker_ctx {\n    int     thread_idx;\n    pool_t *pool;\n    void   *handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS];\n} worker_ctx_t;\n\n/* Set on every worker thread before the init barrier; readable from\n * any pool action. */\nextern __thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker;\n\n#define POOL_MAX_WORKERS 16\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Create a pool with n_workers threads. If n_workers <= 0, defaults\n * to sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) capped at POOL_MAX_WORKERS. The\n * SORAMECH_WORKERS environment variable, if set and >0, overrides\n * the default. Returns NULL on allocation or pthread_create failure. */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers);\n\n/* Block until every worker has finished its (currently empty) init\n * sequence and is parked at the barrier; then release them all. The\n * 303 spec-registry plug-in point lives between pool_create and\n * pool_init_barrier. One-shot. */\nvoid    pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p);\n\n/* Stop accepting tasks, drain whatever's queued, join every worker,\n * free the pool. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid    pool_destroy(pool_t *p);\n\nint     pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Submission and wait */\n/* Submit a task. Safe from any thread (including from inside another\n * action). Increments the active-task counter; the worker that runs\n * the task decrements it on return. */\nvoid    pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg);\n\n/* Block until the active-task counter reaches zero. Calling this\n * before pool_init_barrier with pending tasks is a programming\n * error — workers haven't been released yet, so nothing will drain. */\nvoid    pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_POOL_H */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"/* Submit a task. Safe from any thread (including from inside another\n * action). Increments the active-task counter; the worker that runs\n * the task decrements it on return. */\nvoid    pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg);",
    "newString":"/* Submit a task. Safe from any thread (including from inside another\n * action). Increments the active-task counter; the worker that runs\n * the task decrements it on return.\n *\n * `priority` is a signed-int weight; higher priorities are dequeued\n * before lower ones.     "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.c — SoraMech thread pool, implementation.\n *\n * Pthreads, a singly-linked FIFO task queue under one mutex, a\n * condition variable for \"queue has work or we're shutting down\",\n * an atomic active-task counter with its own mutex/cv for the\n * quiescence wait, and a one-shot init barrier under a third\n * mutex/cv.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked FIFO */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its (currently empty) per-thread setup; main thread\n     * waits for workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released\n     * and broadcasts. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point — issue 303 plugs spec->init calls here\n     * for every language the map uses. Empty for now. */\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready, notify the main thread, then park at\n     * the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn   = fn;\n    t->arg  = arg;\n    t->next = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    if (p->q_tail) p->q_tail->next = t;\n    else           p->q_head       = t;\n    p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_wait_quiescent() */\nvoid pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    while (atomic_load_explicit(&p->active, memory_order_acquire) > 0) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->quiet_cv, &p->quiet_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_n_workers() */\nint pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)\n{\n    return p ? p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0;     "oldString":"/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn   = fn;\n    t->arg  = arg;\n    t->next = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    if (p->q_tail) p->q_tail->next = t;\n    else           p->q_head       = t;\n    p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg, int priority)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn       = fn;\n    t->arg      = arg;\n    t->priority = priority;\n    t->next     = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    /* Priority-ordered insertion. Walk from head until finding the\n     * first node with strictly-lower priority; insert before it.\n     * Strict less-than gives FIFO tiebreaking on equal priority.\n     * The queue is small in practice (bounded by ready tasks), so\n     * linear scan is fine. */\n    task_node_t **link = &p->q_head;\n    while (*link && (*link)->priority >= priority) {\n        link = &(*link)->next;\n    }\n    t->next = *link;\n    *link = t;\n    if (t->next == NULL) p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */",

g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1), 0);\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1), 0);\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority. Single-worker pool is\n * used so dequeue order maps directly to execution order. */\nstatic pthread_mutex_t g_seq_mtx = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\nstatic int g_seq[16];\nstatic int g_seq_len;\n\nstatic void seq_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int id = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_seq_mtx);\n    g_seq[g_seq_len++] = id;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_seq_mtx);\n}\n\nstatic int test_priority_order(void)\n{\n    g_seq_len = 0;\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(1);\n    ASSERT(p);\n\n    /* Queue 6 tasks BEFORE the worker is released. ids encode order\n     * of spawn; the test asserts on order of execution. */\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)1, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)2, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)3, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)4, 9);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)5, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)6, -1);\n\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    /* Expected order:\n     *   4 (prio 9)\n     *   2, 5 (prio 5, FIFO)\n     *   1, 3 (prio 0, FIFO)\n     *   6 (prio -1)\n     */\n    static const int expected[] = { 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, 6 };\n    ASSERT(g_seq_len == 6);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) ASSERT(g_seq[i] == expected[i]);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    RUN(priority_order);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/301-pool-test.c"
  },

    "newString":"/* {{{ Writer — bounded streaming emitter\n *\n * The writer fills the caller's buffer one token at a time. State is\n * a small stack of depth markers: low bit is \"next element will be\n * the first,\" high bit is \"this level is an object\" (vs an array).\n * That's enough to handle comma placement and choose the right\n * close bracket. Depth is capped at 16 — plenty for the event\n * records issue 311 will emit.\n *\n * Errors are sticky: once w->err is set, every subsequent op is a\n * no-op until json_writer_finish reports the failure. Overruns of\n * the bounded buffer flip w->err; the caller is expected to size\n * the buffer for the worst case (or detect overflow and retry with\n * a bigger one).\n */\n\n#define WRITER_FLAG_FIRST    1u\n#define WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT   2u\n\n/* {{{ writer_emit() — append `n` bytes, or set err on overflow */\nstatic void writer_emit(json_writer_t *w, const char *s, int n)\n{\n    if (w->err) return;\n    if (w->used + n > w->cap) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    memcpy(w->buf + w->used, s, (size_t)n);\n    w->used += n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_pre_value() — comma before next array element if needed */\nstatic void writer_pre_value(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (w->depth == 0) return;\n    unsigned char st = w->first[w->depth - 1];\n    if (st & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT) {\n        /* In an object: a value follows a key, which already wrote\n         * its colon. No comma here. */\n        return;\n    }\n    /* In an array. */\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_FIRST)) writer_emit(w, \",\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth - 1] = (unsigned char)(st & (unsigned char)~WRITER_FLAG_FIRST);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_emit_string_literal() — \"...\" with JSON escapes */\nstatic void writer_emit_string_literal(json_writer_t *w, const char *s)\n{\n    writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1);\n    if (!s) { writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1); return; }\n    for (const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s; *p; p++) {\n        unsigned char c = *p;\n        switch (c) {\n            case '\"':  writer_emit(w, \"\\\\\\\"\", 2); break;\n            case '\\\\': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\\\\\\", 2); break;\n            case '\\n': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\n\",  2); break;\n            case '\\r': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\r\",  2); break;\n            case '\\t': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\t\",  2); break;\n            case '\\b': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\b\",  2); break;\n            case '\\f': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\f\",  2); break;\n            default:\n                if (c < 0x20) {\n                    char buf[8];\n                    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"\\\\u%04x\", c);\n                    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n                } else {\n                    char ch = (char)c;\n                    writer_emit(w, &ch, 1);\n                }\n        }\n    }\n    writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_init() */\nvoid json_writer_init(json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    w->buf   = buf;\n    w->cap   = cap;\n    w->used  = 0;\n    w->err   = 0;\n    w->depth = 0;\n    memset(w->first, 0, sizeof w->first);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_object() */\nvoid json_writer_object(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth >= 16) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"{\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth] = WRITER_FLAG_FIRST | WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT;\n    w->depth++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_array() */\nvoid json_writer_array(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth >= 16) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"[\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth] = WRITER_FLAG_FIRST;     /* array, no OBJECT bit */\n    w->depth++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_end() */\nvoid json_writer_end(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth == 0) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    w->depth--;\n    writer_emit(w, (w->first[w->depth] & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT) ? \"}\" : \"]\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_key() */\nvoid json_writer_key(json_writer_t *w, const char *key)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err || !key) { if (w) w->err = 1; return; }\n    if (w->depth == 0) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    unsigned char st = w->first[w->depth - 1];\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT)) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_FIRST)) writer_emit(w, \",\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth - 1] = (unsigned char)(st & (unsigned char)~WRITER_FLAG_FIRST);\n    writer_emit_string_literal(w, key);\n    writer_emit(w, \":\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_string() */\nvoid json_writer_string(json_writer_t *w, const char *s)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit_string_literal(w, s);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_int() */\nvoid json_writer_int(json_writer_t *w, long long v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    char buf[32];\n    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%lld\", v);\n    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_number() */\nvoid json_writer_number(json_writer_t *w, double v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    char buf[40];\n    /* %.17g preserves round-trip for IEEE-754 doubles. */\n    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%.17g\", v);\n    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_bool() */\nvoid json_writer_bool(json_writer_t *w, int v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    if (v) writer_emit(w, \"true\",  4);\n    else   writer_emit(w, \"false\", 5);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_null() */\nvoid json_writer_null(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"null\", 4);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_finish() */\nint json_writer_finish(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w)          return -1;\n    if (w->err)      return -1;\n    if (w->depth != 0) { w->err = 1; return -1; }\n    /* NUL-terminate in any spare byte (not counted in `used`). */\n    if (w->used < w->cap) w->buf[w->used] = '\\0';\n    return w->used;\n}\n/* }}} */\n/* }}} */"

Depth is capped at 16 — plenty for the event\n * records issue 311 will emit.\n *\n * Errors are sticky: once w->err is set, every subsequent op is a\n * no-op until json_writer_finish reports the failure. Overruns of\n * the bounded buffer flip w->err; the caller is expected to size\n * the buffer for the worst case (or detect overflow and retry with\n * a bigger one).\n */\n\n#define WRITER_FLAG_FIRST    1u\n#define WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT   2u\n\n/* {{{ writer_emit() — append `n` bytes, or set err on overflow */\nstatic void writer_emit(json_writer_t *w, const char *s, int n)\n{\n    if (w->err) return;\n    if (w->used + n > w->cap) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    memcpy(w->buf + w->used, s, (size_t)n);\n    w->used += n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_pre_value() — comma before next array element if needed */\nstatic void writer_pre_value(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (w->depth == 0) return;\n    unsigned char st = w->first[w->depth - 1];\n    if (st & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT) {\n        /* In an object: a value follows a key, which already wrote\n         * its colon. No comma here. */\n        return;\n    }\n    /* In an array. */\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_FIRST)) writer_emit(w, \",\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth - 1] = (unsigned char)(st & (unsigned char)~WRITER_FLAG_FIRST);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_emit_string_literal() — \"...\" with JSON escapes */\nstatic void writer_emit_string_literal(json_writer_t *w, const char *s)\n{\n    writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1);\n    if (!s) { writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1); return; }\n    for (const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s; *p; p++) {\n        unsigned char c = *p;\n        switch (c) {\n            case '\"':  writer_emit(w, \"\\\\\\\"\", 2); break;\n            case '\\\\': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\\\\\\", 2); break;\n            case '\\n': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\n\",  2); break;\n            case '\\r': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\r\",  2); break;\n            case '\\t': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\t\",  2); break;\n            case '\\b': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\b\",  2); break;\n            case '\\f': writer_emit(w, \"\\\\f\",  2); break;\n            default:\n                if (c < 0x20) {\n                    char buf[8];\n                    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"\\\\u%04x\", c);\n                    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n                } else {\n                    char ch = (char)c;\n                    writer_emit(w, &ch, 1);\n                }\n        }\n    }\n    writer_emit(w, \"\\\"\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_init() */\nvoid json_writer_init(json_writer_t *w, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    w->buf   = buf;\n    w->cap   = cap;\n    w->used  = 0;\n    w->err   = 0;\n    w->depth = 0;\n    memset(w->first, 0, sizeof w->first);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_object() */\nvoid json_writer_object(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth >= 16) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"{\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth] = WRITER_FLAG_FIRST | WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT;\n    w->depth++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_array() */\nvoid json_writer_array(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth >= 16) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"[\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth] = WRITER_FLAG_FIRST;     /* array, no OBJECT bit */\n    w->depth++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_end() */\nvoid json_writer_end(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    if (w->depth == 0) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    w->depth--;\n    writer_emit(w, (w->first[w->depth] & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT) ? \"}\" : \"]\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_key() */\nvoid json_writer_key(json_writer_t *w, const char *key)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err || !key) { if (w) w->err = 1; return; }\n    if (w->depth == 0) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    unsigned char st = w->first[w->depth - 1];\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_OBJECT)) { w->err = 1; return; }\n    if (!(st & WRITER_FLAG_FIRST)) writer_emit(w, \",\", 1);\n    w->first[w->depth - 1] = (unsigned char)(st & (unsigned char)~WRITER_FLAG_FIRST);\n    writer_emit_string_literal(w, key);\n    writer_emit(w, \":\", 1);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_string() */\nvoid json_writer_string(json_writer_t *w, const char *s)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit_string_literal(w, s);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_int() */\nvoid json_writer_int(json_writer_t *w, long long v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    char buf[32];\n    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%lld\", v);\n    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_number() */\nvoid json_writer_number(json_writer_t *w, double v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    char buf[40];\n    /* %.17g preserves round-trip for IEEE-754 doubles. */\n    int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%.17g\", v);\n    if (n > 0) writer_emit(w, buf, n);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_bool() */\nvoid json_writer_bool(json_writer_t *w, int v)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    if (v) writer_emit(w, \"true\",  4);\n    else   writer_emit(w, \"false\", 5);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_null() */\nvoid json_writer_null(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w || w->err) return;\n    writer_pre_value(w);\n    writer_emit(w, \"null\", 4);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_writer_finish() */\nint json_writer_finish(json_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w)          return -1;\n    if (w->err)      return -1;\n    if (w->depth != 0) { w->err = 1; return -1; }\n    /* NUL-terminate in any spare byte (not counted in `used`). */\n    if (w->used < w->cap) w->buf[w->used] = '\\0';\n    return w->used;\n}\n/* }}} */\n/* }}} */",
