Tests cd to the project root so\n * relative paths work regardless of where the test binary is run.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Path resolution — find tests/maps/ relative to cwd */\nstatic const char *FIXTURE_DIR = \"tests/maps\";\n\n/* If tests are run from project root: tests/maps/ exists.\n * If run from build/tests/: the binary was started by make test,\n * which cd's to project root first. We don't try to be clever here. */\nstatic int has_fixtures(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    return stat(FIXTURE_DIR, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_hello() */\nstatic int test_load_hello(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_name(g), \"hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_entry_box_id(g), \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(graph_description(g) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    /* greet box */\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet != NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->kind == BOX_CALL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->lang, \"lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->ref,  \"src/hello.lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->fn,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->routing.kind == ROUTING_PLAIN);\n    ASSERT(greet->output_capacity == 256);\n    ASSERT(greet->n_inputs == 2);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[0].name, \"name\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].literal == NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].optional == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].name, \"salutation\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[1].literal, \"Hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[1].optional == 1);\n\n    /* who box */\n    const box_t *who = graph_box_by_id(g, \"who\");\n    ASSERT(who != NULL);\n    ASSERT(who->kind == BOX_DATA);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->path, \"names.txt\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->n_connections == 1);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_box,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(who->connections[0].to_input, \"name\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(who->connections[0].from_branch == NULL);\n\n    /* Topology resolution: who's connection resolves to greet's\n     * `name` input. greet is index 0 or 1; name is greet.inputs[0]. */\n    int greet_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        if (strcmp(graph_box(g, i)->id, \"greet\") == 0) { greet_idx = i; break; }\n    }\n    ASSERT(greet_idx >= 0);\n    ASSERT(who->connections[0].to_box_idx == greet_idx);\n    ASSERT(who->connections[0].to_input_idx == 0);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_branching() — comparator + iterator routing kinds */\nstatic int test_load_branching(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/branching\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    const box_t *src = graph_box_by_id(g, \"source\");\n    ASSERT(src != NULL);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR);\n    ASSERT(src->routing.n_outputs == 3);\n\n    const box_t *cls = graph_box_by_id(g, \"classify\");\n    ASSERT(cls != NULL);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.kind == ROUTING_COMPARATOR);\n    ASSERT(cls->routing.comparand == 5.0);\n    ASSERT(cls->n_connections == 3);\n    /* All three branches reachable. */\n    int seen_lt = 0, seen_eq = 0, seen_gt = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < cls->n_connections; i++) {\n        const char *b = cls->connections[i].from_branch;\n        if      (b && strcmp(b, \"lt\") == 0) seen_lt = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"eq\") == 0) seen_eq = 1;\n        else if (b && strcmp(b, \"gt\") == 0) seen_gt = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lt && seen_eq && seen_gt);\n\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_map_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_map_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/does-not-exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    /* Error mentions the path. */\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"does-not-exist\") != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_argument() */\nstatic int test_null_argument(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Helpers for malformed-fixture tests */\n/* Make a temp map directory with a given meta.json and a single\n * box file. Caller frees `out_dir` (or just lets it leak — tests\n * are short-lived). */\nstatic int make_temp_map(const char *meta_json,\n                         const char *box_name,\n                         const char *box_json,\n                         char **out_dir)\n{\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-loader-test-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    if (!dir) return -1;\n    *out_dir = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir);\n    mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir, box_name);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\"); if (!fp) return -1;\n    fputs(box_json, fp); fclose(fp);\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void cleanup_temp_map(const char *dir, const char *box_name)\n{\n    char p[4096];\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/boxes/%s.json\", dir, box_name); unlink(p);\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);              unlink(p);\n    snprintf(p, sizeof p, \"%s/boxes\", dir);                  rmdir(p);\n    rmdir(dir);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_unknown_kind() */\nstatic int test_unknown_kind(void)\n{\n    char *dir = NULL;\n    ASSERT(make_temp_map(\n        \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"t\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\n        \"x\",\n        \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"frobnicate\\\"}\",\n        &dir) == 0);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    ASSERT(g == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strstr(err, \"frobnicate\") != NULL);\n\n    free(err);\n    cleanup_temp_map(dir, \"x\");\n    free(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_routing() */\nstatic int test_missing_routing(void)\n{\n    char *dir = NULL;\n    ASSERT(make_temp_map(\n        \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"t\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\n           "content":"/* src/011-spec-registry.h — language spec registry, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: scans langs/<name>/ at startup,\n * dlopens every spec.so it finds, and exposes a name- and\n * extension-keyed lookup to the rest of the runtime.\n *\n * Designed in issue 303. The pool runner (issue 301) consults the\n * registry during per-worker init — for every language the map\n * uses, the worker's per-language handle is initialised via the\n * spec's `init` callback. The dispatch layer (issue 304) looks the\n * spec up at runtime to invoke a box's function.\n *\n * Lifetime: created at process startup, alive for the run, freed\n * at shutdown. dlclose() is called on every handle in destroy.\n *\n * Errors: spec_registry_load returns NULL and sets *err on failure\n * (cannot open langs_dir, dlopen failure, missing required symbol).\n * The caller frees *err.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_SPEC_REGISTRY_H\n#define SORAMECH_SPEC_REGISTRY_H\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct spec_registry spec_registry_t;\n\n/* Open every langs_dir/<name>/spec.so and read its\n * soramech_lang_spec symbol. Returns NULL on failure with *err set. */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err);\n\n/* dlclose every handle, free the registry. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid             spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r);\n\nint              spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r);\n\n/* Look up by spec.name (\"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\"). NULL if not found. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name);\n\n/* Look up by file_ext (\".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\"). Used by the graph\n * loader / dispatch when a box's lang isn't explicit. NULL if not\n * found. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext);\n\n/* Enumerate registered specs by index for diagnostics / iteration. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i);\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_SPEC_REGISTRY_H */\n",

        }

  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_012iMES1DKz1hjwr82VABKMR",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/011-spec-registry.c — language spec registry, implementation.\n *\n * Scans the langs/ directory at startup, dlopens every <name>/spec.so\n * it finds, reads the exported `soramech_lang_spec` symbol, and\n * stores name + file_ext + dl handle + spec pointer. Registry stays\n * alive for the run; spec_registry_destroy walks the entries and\n * dlcloses every handle.\n *\n * Per-worker spec init (running each spec's init callback once per\n * worker thread) lives in the pool, not here — issue 301's worker_main\n * gets the hook in a follow-on. This file just produces the lookup\n * table that the hook will iterate.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal entry */\ntypedef struct spec_entry {\n    void             *dl_handle;\n    const lang_spec_t *spec;\n} spec_entry_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Registry */\nstruct spec_registry {\n    int           count;\n    int           capacity;\n    spec_entry_t *entries;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ grow_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_if_needed(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (r->count < r->capacity) return 0;\n    int new_cap = r->capacity ? r->capacity * 2 : 4;\n    spec_entry_t *grown = realloc(r->entries, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(spec_entry_t));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    r->entries  = grown;\n    r->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ try_load_one() — open one langs/<name>/spec.so */\n/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with *err set. Skips entries\n * that don't contain a spec.so silently (a subdirectory without a\n * built spec just means that language isn't available). */\nstatic int try_load_one(spec_registry_t *r, const char *langs_dir,\n                        const char *name, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s/spec.so\", langs_dir, name);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"spec path too long: %s/%s\", langs_dir, name);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) return 0;   /* no spec.so; silent skip */\n\n    /* RTLD_LOCAL keeps symbols from one spec from leaking into\n     * another — a spec's internal helpers shouldn't be visible to\n     * any other dlopen'd module. RTLD_NOW catches missing-symbol\n     * errors immediately rather than deferring them to the first\n     * call. */\n    void *h = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!h) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"dlopen('%s') failed: %s\", path, dlerror());\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* dlerror's \"clear the queue\" idiom: call it once before dlsym\n     * to flush any pending error, then again after to read it. */\n    (void)dlerror();\n    const lang_spec_t *spec = dlsym(h, \"soramech_lang_spec\");\n    const char *dl_err = dlerror();\n    if (!spec || dl_err) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' is missing 'soramech_lang_spec': %s\",\n                       path, dl_err ? dl_err : \"symbol not found\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (!spec->name || !spec->file_ext) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' exports a spec with NULL name or file_ext\", path);\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    if (grow_if_needed(r) != 0) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    r->entries[r->count].dl_handle = h;\n    r->entries[r->count].spec      = spec;\n    r->count++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_load() */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err)\n{\n    if (err) *err = NULL;\n    if (!langs_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"spec_registry_load: NULL langs_dir\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(langs_dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open langs directory '%s'\", langs_dir);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof *r);\n    if (!r) {\n        closedir(d);\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        /* Probe the subdir as a directory; ignore plain files. */\n        char sub[4096];\n        int w = snprintf(sub, sizeof sub, \"%s/%s\", langs_dir, e->d_name);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub) continue;\n        struct stat st;\n        if (stat(sub, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) continue;\n\n        char *one_err = NULL;\n        if (try_load_one(r, langs_dir, e->d_name, &one_err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            spec_registry_destroy(r);\n            if (err) *err = one_err;\n            else     free(one_err);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return r;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_destroy() */\nvoid spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!r) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (r->entries[i].dl_handle) dlclose(r->entries[i].dl_handle);\n    }\n    free(r->entries);\n    free(r);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nint spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    return r ? r->count : 0;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name)\n{\n    if (!r || !name) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->name, name) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext)\n{\n    if (!r || !file_ext) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->file_ext, file_ext) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "content":"/* src/011-spec-registry.c — language spec registry, implementation.\n *\n * Scans the langs/ directory at startup, dlopens every <name>/spec.so\n * it finds, reads the exported `soramech_lang_spec` symbol, and\n * stores name + file_ext + dl handle + spec pointer. Registry stays\n * alive for the run; spec_registry_destroy walks the entries and\n * dlcloses every handle.\n *\n * Per-worker spec init (running each spec's init callback once per\n * worker thread) lives in the pool, not here — issue 301's worker_main\n * gets the hook in a follow-on. This file just produces the lookup\n * table that the hook will iterate.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal entry */\ntypedef struct spec_entry {\n    void             *dl_handle;\n    const lang_spec_t *spec;\n} spec_entry_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Registry */\nstruct spec_registry {\n    int           count;\n    int           capacity;\n    spec_entry_t *entries;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ grow_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_if_needed(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (r->count < r->capacity) return 0;\n    int new_cap = r->capacity ? r->capacity * 2 : 4;\n    spec_entry_t *grown = realloc(r->entries, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(spec_entry_t));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    r->entries  = grown;\n    r->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ try_load_one() — open one langs/<name>/spec.so */\n/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with *err set. Skips entries\n * that don't contain a spec.so silently (a subdirectory without a\n * built spec just means that language isn't available). */\nstatic int try_load_one(spec_registry_t *r, const char *langs_dir,\n                        const char *name, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s/spec.so\", langs_dir, name);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"spec path too long: %s/%s\", langs_dir, name);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) return 0;   /* no spec.so; silent skip */\n\n    /* RTLD_LOCAL keeps symbols from one spec from leaking into\n     * another — a spec's internal helpers shouldn't be visible to\n     * any other dlopen'd module. RTLD_NOW catches missing-symbol\n     * errors immediately rather than deferring them to the first\n     * call. */\n    void *h = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!h) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"dlopen('%s') failed: %s\", path, dlerror());\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* dlerror's \"clear the queue\" idiom: call it once before dlsym\n     * to flush any pending error, then again after to read it. */\n    (void)dlerror();\n    const lang_spec_t *spec = dlsym(h, \"soramech_lang_spec\");\n    const char *dl_err = dlerror();\n    if (!spec || dl_err) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' is missing 'soramech_lang_spec': %s\",\n                       path, dl_err ? dl_err : \"symbol not found\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (!spec->name || !spec->file_ext) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' exports a spec with NULL name or file_ext\", path);\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    if (grow_if_needed(r) != 0) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    r->entries[r->count].dl_handle = h;\n    r->entries[r->count].spec      = spec;\n    r->count++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_load() */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err)\n{\n    if (err) *err = NULL;\n    if (!langs_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"spec_registry_load: NULL langs_dir\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(langs_dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open langs directory '%s'\", langs_dir);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof *r);\n    if (!r) {\n        closedir(d);\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        /* Probe the subdir as a directory; ignore plain files. */\n        char sub[4096];\n        int w = snprintf(sub, sizeof sub, \"%s/%s\", langs_dir, e->d_name);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub) continue;\n        struct stat st;\n        if (stat(sub, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) continue;\n\n        char *one_err = NULL;\n        if (try_load_one(r, langs_dir, e->d_name, &one_err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            spec_registry_destroy(r);\n            if (err) *err = one_err;\n            else     free(one_err);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return r;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_destroy() */\nvoid spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!r) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (r->entries[i].dl_handle) dlclose(r->entries[i].dl_handle);\n    }\n    free(r->entries);\n    free(r);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nint spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    return r ? r->count : 0;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name)\n{\n    if (!r || !name) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->name, name) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext)\n{\n    if (!r || !file_ext) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->file_ext, file_ext) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

          "content":"/* tests/011-spec-registry-test.c — unit tests for the spec\n * registry.\n *\n * Exercises directory scan, dlopen, symbol lookup, and the name /\n * extension accessors. Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"011-spec-registry-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_three_specs);\n    RUN(missing_dir);\n    RUN(null_dir);\n    RUN(null_safety);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "content":"/* tests/011-spec-registry-test.c — unit tests for the spec\n * registry.\n *\n * Exercises directory scan, dlopen, symbol lookup, and the name /\n * extension accessors. Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"011-spec-registry-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_three_specs);\n    RUN(missing_dir);\n    RUN(null_dir);\n    RUN(null_safety);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "type":"create",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

{

        "oldLines":3,

        "lines":["   runs spec `compile` for every box"," - `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — Option 1 (FFI) and Option 3 (Unix","   socket) describe the two execution models specs implement","+","+## Implementation log","+","+### Registry — 2026-05-12","+","+`src/011-spec-registry.{c,h}` scans a `langs/` directory, dlopens","+every `<name>/spec.so` it finds with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL`, and","+exposes name + extension lookup plus enumeration. The three","+shipped stubs (lua/c/bash) load cleanly and round-trip through","+`spec_registry_get` and `spec_registry_for_ext`. Four unit tests","+in `tests/011-spec-registry-test.c` cover the load, missing dir,","+null inputs, and accessor safety.","+","+Deferred: hooking `spec->init(worker_idx)` into the pool's","+`worker_main` between TLS setup and the init barrier. That's the","+final piece that makes 303 fully wired; lands in a follow-on once","+a spec has a real `init` body to call (issue 306 onward)."],
        "oldStart":214
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 303 — Language runtime spec: pluggable per-language invocation\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nEach language has an ad-hoc driver script (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`,\n`drivers/c.sh`). The driver is invoked per box call: spawn a process, run\nthe function, read stdout, exit. Adding a new language means writing a new\ndriver script and modifying the executor to know about it.\n\nThere is no shared interface, no persistent runtime, and no way for a user\nto add a language without touching SoraMech internals.\n\n## Concept\n\nThe language runtime spec is the user-extensible interface that defines how\na language's functions are invoked from inside the thread pool. Every\nlanguage goes through this interface — there is no special path for any\nlanguage. Lua is a spec. C is a spec. Bash is a spec. A user adding Python\nwrites another spec.\n\nThe pool runner does not know how to \"run a Lua function.\" It knows how to\ncall `lang->invoke(...)`. The Lua spec is the thing that knows how to run a\nLua function.\n\nThe user provides the bridging code. SoraMech does not transpile, rewrite,\nor convert box source between languages. If the user wants Rust, the user\nwrites a Rust spec.\n\n## The interface\n\nEach language spec is a C library that exports a single symbol:\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       // \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ...\n    const char *file_ext;   // \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\" — for box file resolution\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Returns an opaque handle stored in worker_ctx.\n    // Called at pool startup, before any tasks run.\n    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Called at pool shutdown.\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    // Optional: called once per box source file at map load.\n    // For languages that compile (C → .so), this is where compilation\n    // happens. For languages that don't (Lua, Bash), this is NULL.\n    int   (*compile)(const char *src_path, const char *out_path);\n\n    // The invocation. Inputs are arrays of (bytes, size) pairs,\n    // already read from slots by the dispatch layer. The spec writes\n    // its return value into out_buf and sets *out_size.\n    //\n    // Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.\n    int   (*invoke)(void *handle,\n                    const char *file_path,\n                    const char *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes, int n_inputs,\n                    void *out_buf, int out_buf_capacity, int *out_size);\n} lang_spec_t;\n\nextern lang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec;\n```\n\nThe spec library is built as a `.so` and loaded by the pool runner at\nstartup via `dlopen` / `dlsym`. The runner iterates `langs/*/spec.so`,\nloads each, and registers it under its `name`.\n\n## Slot access boundary\n\nSpecs do not see slot IDs. The dispatch layer (issue 304) reads input\nvalues from slots into raw byte buffers, hands them to `invoke`, receives\nthe output bytes, and writes them to the output slot. This decouples\nspecs from slot internals — a spec only deals with values.\n\nIf a future language wants zero-copy access (e.g. memory-mapping a slot\ndirectly into a Python bytearray), the interface can be extended. Do not\nadd it preemptively.\n\n## Per-language layout\n\nSpecs live under `langs/<name>/`:\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c              ← implements lang_spec_t (handles → lua_State)\n    Makefile            ← builds spec.so\n    spec.so             ← built artifact\n\nlangs/bash/\n    spec.c              ← bridges to bash-server.sh via Unix domain socket\n    bash-server.sh      ← persistent subprocess started by spec.init\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/c/\n    spec.c              ← uses dlopen/dlsym; compile = gcc -shared -fPIC\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/python/           ← user-added; not shipped\n    spec.c\n    Makefile\n```\n\nThe pool runner has no compiled-in knowledge of any specific language.\nEven Lua is loaded as a `.so` at startup. This keeps the boundary honest\n— there is no temptation to special-case the \"shipped\" languages.\n\n## Built-in specs (shipped, not privileged)\n\nSoraMech ships specs for:\n- **Lua** — handle is a `lua_State`. `invoke` calls `luaL_loadfile` (cached)\n  + `lua_pcall`. Args pushed as Lua strings; return read as Lua string.\n- **C** — handle is a small `dlopen` handle cache. `compile` runs\n  `gcc -shared -fPIC -o <out_path> <src_path>`. `invoke` does\n  `dlsym` + direct call.\n- **Bash** — handle is a Unix domain socket connected to a persistent\n  bash subprocess (`bash-server.sh`). `invoke` sends a framed request,\n  reads a framed response.\n\nThese are the reference implementations. They demonstrate the spec\ninterface for in-process FFI (Lua, C) and for out-of-process socket\nservers (Bash, and any future language whose runtime cannot be embedded).\n\n## Compilation\n\nThe optional `compile` hook runs at map load (or at editor compile-button\ntime, issue 219). For C, it produces a `.so` next to the source. For\nLua and Bash, no compilation step is needed; `compile` is `NULL`.\n\nCompilation outputs go in the map's `compiled/bin/` directory (issue\n222). The dispatch layer passes the compiled artifact path to `invoke`,\nnot the original source path, when a compiled artifact exists.\n\n## Iterator counter prepending\n\nThe iterator counter (issue 221) is prepended to the input array by the\ndispatch layer, not by the spec. From the spec's perspective, an\niterator box just has one extra input. The spec doesn't know which\ninput is the counter — that's a graph-level concept.\n\n## Errors crash the program\n\nA nonzero return from `invoke` is a fatal error. The dispatch layer\nprints the error context (box id, function name, language) to stderr\nand aborts the process. There is no recovery, no retry, no per-task\n\"failed\" state, no fallback. There are no timeouts on stalled tasks,\nno wait-list garbage collection, no failure propagation through the\ngraph.\n\nThe reasoning: a task that cannot produce a correct return value is a\nbug. Bugs do not belong in production. Building in detection and\nrecovery for bug states adds runtime cost and complexity to handle a\ncase that should not exist. If a bug surfaces in production, the\nprogram crashes loudly; the developer fixes the bug and redeploys.\n\nThe spec is still responsible for catching language-level errors (Lua\n`error()`, C signals it can intercept, Bash nonzero exit) and\ntranslating them into a nonzero return — so that the dispatch layer\nsees a clean signal instead of an undefined post-error state. Once\nreturned, the program ends.\n\n## User-facing documentation\n\nThe interface is published in `langs/lang-spec.h`, which every spec\nimplementation includes. That header is the source of truth for the\ncontract.\n\nUser-facing docs that mention the language spec system:\n- `README.md` — short paragraph in the features list pointing out that\n  any language can be added by writing a spec, with a one-line example\n  of what that means\n- `docs/005-language-specs.md` (to be written) — the long-form guide\n  on writing a spec: walk through the Lua spec as a small reference,\n  show what `init` / `invoke` / `teardown` do, point at the C spec for\n  the `compile`-using case and the Bash spec for the\n  socket-server case\n- `docs/000-table-of-contents.md` — index entry for the new doc\n\nWithout these the spec system is invisible — users would never know it\nexists or how to extend it.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently)\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Write `langs/lang-spec.h` — the public interface header.\n2. Write `langs/lua/spec.c` first. Lua is the easiest because it's already\n   our default language and the existing driver gives a reference behavior.\n3. Write `langs/c/spec.c` — adds `compile` callback, exercises the dlopen\n   path.\n4. Write `langs/bash/spec.c` + `langs/bash/bash-server.sh` — exercises\n   the out-of-process socket model. This is the proof that languages\n   without an embeddable runtime fit the same interface.\n5. Pool runner registry: `dlopen` every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup,\n   register by `name`. Box files are routed to specs by `file_ext`.\n6. Smoke test: a map with one Lua box, one C box, one Bash box, all\n   running in the pool, all going through the spec interface.       "content":"# 310 — Priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe SoraMech thread pool's `pool_spawn` (modeled on 3d-rts's API)\ntakes a priority parameter:\n\n```c\ntask_id_t pool_spawn(task_pool_t *pool,\n                     action_fn_t  *actions,\n                     void        **action_args,\n                     int           n_actions,\n                     int           priority);\n```\n\nHigher priority tasks are dispatched ahead of lower priority tasks\nwhen multiple are ready. The pool's queue handles the ordering.\n\nPhase 3 needs to specify what SoraMech does with this knob. The\nsimplest answer is the right one for now: do nothing.\n\n## Decision\n\nEvery dispatch task is submitted at priority `1`. The compile-time\nconstant `MAX_PRIORITY` is set to `1`. There is no graph-level or\nbox-level concept of priority. The runner does not expose any user-\nfacing knob for it.\n\nThe mechanism is wired through the codebase — every `pool_spawn`\ncall passes a priority, the constant is referenced rather than\nhard-coded inline — but the behavior is identical to a single-\npriority pool. Tasks run in submission order (modulo whatever\nordering the pool guarantees within a single priority level).\n\n## Why wire it in if it does nothing\n\nTwo reasons:\n\n1. **Future hooks land as config changes, not refactors.** When a\n   real priority use case appears (allocator cleanup at lowest\n   priority; user-marked urgent boxes; iterator queue draining\n   prioritized over new entry submission), raising `MAX_PRIORITY`\n   and emitting different priorities at the right call sites is a\n   line edit, not a structural change. If the priority parameter\n   were stripped out, adding it later means going back through every\n   `pool_spawn` callsite and threading a new argument.\n\n2. **The pool's API requires it.** `pool_spawn` takes a priority.\n   Callers must pass something. Passing `1` consistently is the\n   straightforward expression of \"no priority concept yet.\"\n\n## Specific call sites\n\n```c\n// src/dispatch.c — every dispatch task\npool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// src/008-pool-runner.c — entry-box submission at startup\npool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// src/slot-store.c — deferred allocator cleanup task (issue 302)\npool_spawn(pool, &cleanup_action, &cleanup_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// langs/bash/spec.c — ... none, the spec doesn't spawn pool tasks\n```\n\n`SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` is `1`. Defined in `src/008-pool-runner.h` (or\na sibling header) so all callers use the same name.\n\n## Future hooks (not in scope, but called out)\n\nWhen `MAX_PRIORITY` is raised, the natural assignments are:\n\n| Future use case                                     | Priority |\n|-----------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| User-marked \"urgent\" boxes (UI / interactive)       | 3        |\n| Iterator continuation when its queue is non-empty   | 2        |\n| Default dispatch task                               | 1        |\n| Allocator cleanup task (deferred coalescing, 302)   | 0        |\n\nThese are speculative. The actual priority schema is decided when\nthere is a workload that demonstrates the need.\n\nA box-level priority field could go in the box JSON (`\"priority\":\n2`) and be plumbed through `dispatch_task_t`. The dispatch action\nreads it, passes it to `pool_spawn` for any successor tasks. This\nis a future change.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently — this is intentionally a small change to the call\nsites. The design conversation about what priorities should mean is\ndeferred until concrete need.)\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Define `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` (= 1) and `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (= 1)\n   in a runner-wide header.\n2. Make every `pool_spawn` call site pass `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT`.\n3. Set the pool's max priority at `pool_create` time using\n   `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (if the pool API takes a max-priority hint).\n4. That's it. No tests required beyond verifying the constants\n   compile and the pool runs.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for entry boxes\n- `src/dispatch.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for successor tasks\n- `src/slot-store.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for deferred cleanup\n- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — `pool_spawn` priority parameter\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch task submission\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — deferred cleanup tasks\n",
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":116,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/310-priority-queue.md",
      "numLines":116
    }

    "originalFile":"# 310 — Priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe SoraMech thread pool's `pool_spawn` (modeled on 3d-rts's API)\ntakes a priority parameter:\n\n```c\ntask_id_t pool_spawn(task_pool_t *pool,\n                     action_fn_t  *actions,\n                     void        **action_args,\n                     int           n_actions,\n                     int           priority);\n```\n\nHigher priority tasks are dispatched ahead of lower priority tasks\nwhen multiple are ready. The pool's queue handles the ordering.\n\nPhase 3 needs to specify what SoraMech does with this knob. The\nsimplest answer is the right one for now: do nothing.\n\n## Decision\n\nEvery dispatch task is submitted at priority `1`. The compile-time\nconstant `MAX_PRIORITY` is set to `1`. There is no graph-level or\nbox-level concept of priority. The runner does not expose any user-\nfacing knob for it.\n\nThe mechanism is wired through the codebase — every `pool_spawn`\ncall passes a priority, the constant is referenced rather than\nhard-coded inline — but the behavior is identical to a single-\npriority pool. Tasks run in submission order (modulo whatever\nordering the pool guarantees within a single priority level).\n\n## Why wire it in if it does nothing\n\nTwo reasons:\n\n1. **Future hooks land as config changes, not refactors.** When a\n   real priority use case appears (allocator cleanup at lowest\n   priority; user-marked urgent boxes; iterator queue draining\n   prioritized over new entry submission), raising `MAX_PRIORITY`\n   and emitting different priorities at the right call sites is a\n   line edit, not a structural change. If the priority parameter\n   were stripped out, adding it later means going back through every\n   `pool_spawn` callsite and threading a new argument.\n\n2. **The pool's API requires it.** `pool_spawn` takes a priority.\n   Callers must pass something. Passing `1` consistently is the\n   straightforward expression of \"no priority concept yet.\"\n\n## Specific call sites\n\n```c\n// src/dispatch.c — every dispatch task\npool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// src/008-pool-runner.c — entry-box submission at startup\npool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// src/slot-store.c — deferred allocator cleanup task (issue 302)\npool_spawn(pool, &cleanup_action, &cleanup_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);\n\n// langs/bash/spec.c — ... none, the spec doesn't spawn pool tasks\n```\n\n`SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` is `1`. Defined in `src/008-pool-runner.h` (or\na sibling header) so all callers use the same name.\n\n## Future hooks (not in scope, but called out)\n\nWhen `MAX_PRIORITY` is raised, the natural assignments are:\n\n| Future use case                                     | Priority |\n|-----------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| User-marked \"urgent\" boxes (UI / interactive)       | 3        |\n| Iterator continuation when its queue is non-empty   | 2        |\n| Default dispatch task                               | 1        |\n| Allocator cleanup task (deferred coalescing, 302)   | 0        |\n\nThese are speculative. The actual priority schema is decided when\nthere is a workload that demonstrates the need.\n\nA box-level priority field could go in the box JSON (`\"priority\":\n2`) and be plumbed through `dispatch_task_t`. The dispatch action\nreads it, passes it to `pool_spawn` for any successor tasks. This\nis a future change.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently — this is intentionally a small change to the call\nsites. The design conversation about what priorities should mean is\ndeferred until concrete need.)\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Define `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` (= 1) and `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (= 1)\n   in a runner-wide header.\n2. Make every `pool_spawn` call site pass `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT`.\n3. Set the pool's max priority at `pool_create` time using\n   `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (if the pool API takes a max-priority hint).\n4. That's it. No tests required beyond verifying the constants\n   compile and the pool runs.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for entry boxes\n- `src/dispatch.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for successor tasks\n- `src/slot-store.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for deferred cleanup\n- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — `pool_spawn` priority parameter\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch task submission\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — deferred cleanup tasks\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — `pool_spawn` priority parameter\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch task submission\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — deferred cleanup tasks",
    "newString":"- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — `pool_spawn` priority parameter\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch task submission\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — deferred cleanup tasks\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### API + ordering — 2026-05-12\n\n`pool_spawn` gained a fourth argument: `int priority`. Higher\npriorities dequeue first; ties between equal priorities resolve\nto FIFO. Linear-scan insertion (strict less-than at the\ncomparison) on the singly-linked queue — small queue, O(n) walk\nis fine. A unit test in `tests/301-pool-test.c` queues six tasks\nof varied priority before the init barrier releases the\nsingle-worker pool, and verifies the execution order matches the\npriority/FIFO rule.\n\nExisting call sites all pass priority 0; behaviorally the queue\nis still a plain FIFO. 304's dispatch action can grow into\npriority-aware scheduling without another signature change.",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "id":"toolu_011AECuneH2FyJuHQ2AjDv1K",

          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ box_is_iterator() — true iff this is a call box whose routing\n * kind cuts cycles. Cycles passing through an iterator are\n * legitimate (the iterator's input queue eventually empties and\n * the cycle terminates); cycles that don't are deadlocks at\n * load time and must be rejected. */\nstatic int box_is_iterator(const box_t *b)\n{\n    return b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dfs_cycle() — recursive DFS for non-iterator cycle detection */\n/* colors: 0 = white (not seen), 1 = gray (on current stack),\n * 2 = black (finished). Returns 0 on success, -1 if a cycle was\n * found; *culprit_box is the box where the back-edge was detected. */\nstatic int dfs_cycle(const graph_t *g, int box_id, char *color,\n                     int *culprit_box)\n{\n    color[box_id] = 1;\n    const box_t *src = &g->boxes[box_id];\n\n    /* Skip outgoing edges from iterator boxes. The iterator naturally\n     * terminates on input-queue empty, so cycles that loop through\n     * one are legal. Skipping is the cleanest way to express\n     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */\n    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {\n            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;\n            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }\n            if (color[dst] == 0) {\n                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    color[box_id] = 2;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */\nstatic int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    if (g->n_boxes == 0) return 0;\n    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);\n    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (color[i] != 0) continue;\n        int culprit = -1;\n        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"\n                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"\n                           \"iterator-routing box\",\n                           g->boxes[culprit].id);\n            free(color);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    free(color);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"
        }
      }],

Skipping is the cleanest way to express","+     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */","+    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {","+        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {","+            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;","+            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }","+            if (color[dst] == 0) {","+                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;","+            }","+        }","+    }","+    color[box_id] = 2;","+    return 0;","+}","+/* }}} */","+","+/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */","+static int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)","+{","+    if (g->n_boxes == 0) return 0;","+    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);","+    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }","+","+    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {","+        if (color[i] != 0) continue;","+        int culprit = -1;","+        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {","+            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"","+                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"","+                           \"iterator-routing box\",","+                           g->boxes[culprit].id);","+            free(color);","+            return -1;","+        }","+    }","+    free(color);","+    return 0;","+}","+/* }}} */","+"," /* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */"," /* Walks every outgoing connection on every box. Looks up `to_box`","  * as a box id and `to_input` as one of that box's declared input"],

      }],
    "newString":"/* {{{ box_is_iterator() — true iff this is a call box whose routing\n * kind cuts cycles. Cycles passing through an iterator are\n * legitimate (the iterator's input queue eventually empties and\n * the cycle terminates); cycles that don't are deadlocks at\n * load time and must be rejected. */\nstatic int box_is_iterator(const box_t *b)\n{\n    return b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dfs_cycle() — recursive DFS for non-iterator cycle detection */\n/* colors: 0 = white (not seen), 1 = gray (on current stack),\n * 2 = black (finished). Returns 0 on success, -1 if a cycle was\n * found; *culprit_box is the box where the back-edge was detected. */\nstatic int dfs_cycle(const graph_t *g, int box_id, char *color,\n                     int *culprit_box)\n{\n    color[box_id] = 1;\n    const box_t *src = &g->boxes[box_id];\n\n    /* Skip outgoing edges from iterator boxes. The iterator naturally\n     * terminates on input-queue empty, so cycles that loop through\n     * one are legal. Skipping is the cleanest way to express\n     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */\n    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {\n            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;\n            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }\n            if (color[dst] == 0) {\n                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    color[box_id] = 2;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */\nstatic int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    if (g->n_boxes == 0) return 0;\n    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);\n    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (color[i] != 0) continue;\n        int culprit = -1;\n        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"\n                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"\n                           \"iterator-routing box\",\n                           g->boxes[culprit].id);\n            free(color);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    free(color);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */"

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

{

        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* langs/lua/spec.c — Lua language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a `lua_State` with the standard libraries\n * opened. Invocation convention: the box's source file is expected\n * to return a Lua table (`return M` at the bottom), and the\n * fn_name is a key into that table. Inputs arrive as byte arrays;\n * each one is pushed as a Lua string. The function's single return\n * value is converted to a string (via tostring semantics) and\n * memcpy'd into the caller's output buffer.\n *\n * Designed in issue 306. Implementation choices that matter:\n *\n *  - One lua_State per worker thread. lua_State is not\n *    thread-safe, but per-thread requires no locking.\n *  - The state's stack is rewound to its baseline depth at every\n *    invoke entry/exit so cross-call leaks don't accumulate.\n *  - File caching (luaL_loadfile once, replayed via lua_call) is\n *    deferred — this iteration loads the chunk on every invoke.\n *    Lands as a follow-on once profiling justifies it.\n *  - The chunk's side effects run on every invoke too (since\n *    we re-load and re-execute). Box source files should be pure\n *    \"return M\" modules for now.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <lua.h>\n#include <lauxlib.h>\n#include <lualib.h>\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_teardown() */\nstatic void lua_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (handle) lua_close((lua_State *)handle);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_invoke() */\nstatic int lua_invoke(void *handle,\n                      const char  *file_path,\n                      const char  *fn_name,\n                      const void **input_data,\n                      const int   *input_sizes,\n                      int          n_inputs,\n                      void        *out_buf,\n                      int          out_buf_capacity,\n                      int         *out_size)\n{\n    lua_State *L = (lua_State *)handle;\n    if (!L || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    int baseline = lua_gettop(L);\n\n    /* Load and execute the file.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           langs/lua/spec.so\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"/* src/011-spec-registry.h — language spec registry, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: scans langs/<name>/ at startup,\n * dlopens every spec.so it finds, and exposes a name- and\n * extension-keyed lookup to the rest of the runtime.\n *\n * Designed in issue 303.           "new_string":"const lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_init_worker() */\nint spec_registry_init_worker(spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                              void **handles, int handles_capacity)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return -1;\n    if (handles_capacity < r->count) return -1;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) handles[i] = NULL;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (!s->init) continue;          /* spec opts out of init */\n        void *h = s->init(worker_idx);\n        if (!h) {\n            /* Teardown anything we've already created. */\n            spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, handles, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        handles[i] = h;\n    }\n    return r->count;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_teardown_worker() */\nvoid spec_registry_teardown_worker(spec_registry_t *r,\n                                   void **handles, int n_handles)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return;\n    if (n_handles > r->count) n_handles = r->count;\n    /* Walk in reverse — symmetric with init order. */\n    for (int i = n_handles - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (s->teardown && handles[i]) {\n            s->teardown(handles[i]);\n        }\n        handles[i] = NULL;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */",

This file just produces the lookup\n * table that the hook will iterate.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal entry */\ntypedef struct spec_entry {\n    void             *dl_handle;\n    const lang_spec_t *spec;\n} spec_entry_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Registry */\nstruct spec_registry {\n    int           count;\n    int           capacity;\n    spec_entry_t *entries;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ grow_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_if_needed(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (r->count < r->capacity) return 0;\n    int new_cap = r->capacity ? r->capacity * 2 : 4;\n    spec_entry_t *grown = realloc(r->entries, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(spec_entry_t));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    r->entries  = grown;\n    r->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ try_load_one() — open one langs/<name>/spec.so */\n/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with *err set.
