    "originalFile":"/* tests/011-spec-registry-test.c — unit tests for the spec\n * registry.\n *\n * Exercises directory scan, dlopen, symbol lookup, and the name /\n * extension accessors. Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found;     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, picks a branch per routing.kind, and pushes the\n * output to downstream input slots, triggering spawn-on-input-\n * ready checks on the consumers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. This iteration ships the skeleton: data\n * types, the action's signature, and a stub body that records\n * dispatch events on the context (so tests can verify the pool +\n * spawn path works end-to-end) without yet reading slots,\n * invoking specs, or pushing outputs.\n *\n * The dispatch_ctx_t bundle is the durable runtime state — the\n * graph, slot store, spec registry, and pool. The action increments a per-context\n * counter for every task that flows through it — enough to verify\n * the pool/spawn/action plumbing end-to-end before the real\n * dispatch logic lands.\n *\n * The real action, in pseudocode (per issue 304):\n *\n *   1. Look up `box = graph_box(ctx->graph, task->box_id)`.\n *   2. For each input port: slot_peek or slot_pop into a buffer.\n *   3. Call the language spec via the per-worker handle.\n *   4. Dispatch on `box->routing.kind` to pick the output branch.\n *   5. For each firing wire: slot_push to the consumer's input\n *      slot, then run the spawn-on-input-ready check.\n *\n * Plumbing each of those onto a real graph involves the per-port\n * slot table (from issue 305's slot-class enumeration pass, still\n * deferred), per-worker spec handles (303's worker hook), and the\n * graph's resolved connection endpoints (305, done).\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_spawn() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx || !ctx->pool) return;\n    dispatch_task_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;\n    t->box_id = box_id;\n    t->ctx    = ctx;\n    pool_spawn(ctx->pool, dispatch_action, t, priority);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — skeleton */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n\n    /* Mutable cast — `ctx` is `const` to callers, but the diagnostic\n     * counter is the action's job. */\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    if (ctx) {\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1,\n                                  memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    /* Real action body lands here:\n     *\n     *   const box_t *box = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n     *   read_inputs(box);\n     *   invoke_spec(box);\n     *   pick_branch(box);\n     *   push_outputs(box);\n     */\n\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

        }

        "input":{
          "content":"/* tests/012-dispatch-test.c — skeleton tests for the dispatch\n * layer.\n *\n * Builds the full runtime context (graph + slot store + spec\n * registry + pool) and submits one task per box. Verifies the\n * counter on the context goes up by exactly n_boxes — the pool /\n * spawn / action plumbing works.\n *\n * Run from the project root; the graph fixture lives under\n * tests/maps/hello/ and the spec registry walks langs/.\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\");     "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.c — task dispatch layer, implementation.\n *\n * Currently a skeleton. The action increments a per-context\n * counter for every task that flows through it — enough to verify\n * the pool/spawn/action plumbing end-to-end before the real\n * dispatch logic lands.\n *\n * The real action, in pseudocode (per issue 304):\n *\n *   1. Look up `box = graph_box(ctx->graph, task->box_id)`.\n *   2. For each input port: slot_peek or slot_pop into a buffer.\n *   3. Call the language spec via the per-worker handle.\n *   4. Dispatch on `box->routing.kind` to pick the output branch.\n *   5. For each firing wire: slot_push to the consumer's input\n *      slot, then run the spawn-on-input-ready check.\n *\n * Plumbing each of those onto a real graph involves the per-port\n * slot table (from issue 305's slot-class enumeration pass, still\n * deferred), per-worker spec handles (303's worker hook), and the\n * graph's resolved connection endpoints (305, done).\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_spawn() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx || !ctx->pool) return;\n    dispatch_task_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;\n    t->box_id = box_id;\n    t->ctx    = ctx;\n    pool_spawn(ctx->pool, dispatch_action, t, priority);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — skeleton */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n\n    /* Mutable cast — `ctx` is `const` to callers, but the diagnostic\n     * counter is the action's job. */\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    if (ctx) {\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1,\n                                  memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    /* Real action body lands here:\n     *\n     *   const box_t *box = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n     *   read_inputs(box);\n     *   invoke_spec(box);\n     *   pick_branch(box);\n     *   push_outputs(box);\n     */\n\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>",
    "newString":"#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdlib.h>",

    "originalFile":"# 303 — Language runtime spec: pluggable per-language invocation\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nEach language has an ad-hoc driver script (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`,\n`drivers/c.sh`). The driver is invoked per box call: spawn a process, run\nthe function, read stdout, exit. Adding a new language means writing a new\ndriver script and modifying the executor to know about it.\n\nThere is no shared interface, no persistent runtime, and no way for a user\nto add a language without touching SoraMech internals.\n\n## Concept\n\nThe language runtime spec is the user-extensible interface that defines how\na language's functions are invoked from inside the thread pool. Every\nlanguage goes through this interface — there is no special path for any\nlanguage. Lua is a spec. C is a spec. Bash is a spec. A user adding Python\nwrites another spec.\n\nThe pool runner does not know how to \"run a Lua function.\" It knows how to\ncall `lang->invoke(...)`. The Lua spec is the thing that knows how to run a\nLua function.\n\nThe user provides the bridging code. SoraMech does not transpile, rewrite,\nor convert box source between languages. If the user wants Rust, the user\nwrites a Rust spec.\n\n## The interface\n\nEach language spec is a C library that exports a single symbol:\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       // \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ...\n    const char *file_ext;   // \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\" — for box file resolution\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Returns an opaque handle stored in worker_ctx.\n    // Called at pool startup, before any tasks run.\n    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Called at pool shutdown.\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    // Optional: called once per box source file at map load.\n    // For languages that compile (C → .so), this is where compilation\n    // happens. For languages that don't (Lua, Bash), this is NULL.\n    int   (*compile)(const char *src_path, const char *out_path);\n\n    // The invocation. Inputs are arrays of (bytes, size) pairs,\n    // already read from slots by the dispatch layer. The spec writes\n    // its return value into out_buf and sets *out_size.\n    //\n    // Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.\n    int   (*invoke)(void *handle,\n                    const char *file_path,\n                    const char *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes, int n_inputs,\n                    void *out_buf, int out_buf_capacity, int *out_size);\n} lang_spec_t;\n\nextern lang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec;\n```\n\nThe spec library is built as a `.so` and loaded by the pool runner at\nstartup via `dlopen` / `dlsym`. The runner iterates `langs/*/spec.so`,\nloads each, and registers it under its `name`.\n\n## Slot access boundary\n\nSpecs do not see slot IDs. The dispatch layer (issue 304) reads input\nvalues from slots into raw byte buffers, hands them to `invoke`, receives\nthe output bytes, and writes them to the output slot. This decouples\nspecs from slot internals — a spec only deals with values.\n\nIf a future language wants zero-copy access (e.g. memory-mapping a slot\ndirectly into a Python bytearray), the interface can be extended. Do not\nadd it preemptively.\n\n## Per-language layout\n\nSpecs live under `langs/<name>/`:\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c              ← implements lang_spec_t (handles → lua_State)\n    Makefile            ← builds spec.so\n    spec.so             ← built artifact\n\nlangs/bash/\n    spec.c              ← bridges to bash-server.sh via Unix domain socket\n    bash-server.sh      ← persistent subprocess started by spec.init\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/c/\n    spec.c              ← uses dlopen/dlsym; compile = gcc -shared -fPIC\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/python/           ← user-added; not shipped\n    spec.c\n    Makefile\n```\n\nThe pool runner has no compiled-in knowledge of any specific language.\nEven Lua is loaded as a `.so` at startup. This keeps the boundary honest\n— there is no temptation to special-case the \"shipped\" languages.\n\n## Built-in specs (shipped, not privileged)\n\nSoraMech ships specs for:\n- **Lua** — handle is a `lua_State`. `invoke` calls `luaL_loadfile` (cached)\n  + `lua_pcall`. Args pushed as Lua strings; return read as Lua string.\n- **C** — handle is a small `dlopen` handle cache. `compile` runs\n  `gcc -shared -fPIC -o <out_path> <src_path>`. `invoke` does\n  `dlsym` + direct call.\n- **Bash** — handle is a Unix domain socket connected to a persistent\n  bash subprocess (`bash-server.sh`). `invoke` sends a framed request,\n  reads a framed response.\n\nThese are the reference implementations. They demonstrate the spec\ninterface for in-process FFI (Lua, C) and for out-of-process socket\nservers (Bash, and any future language whose runtime cannot be embedded).\n\n## Compilation\n\nThe optional `compile` hook runs at map load (or at editor compile-button\ntime, issue 219). For C, it produces a `.so` next to the source. For\nLua and Bash, no compilation step is needed; `compile` is `NULL`.\n\nCompilation outputs go in the map's `compiled/bin/` directory (issue\n222). The dispatch layer passes the compiled artifact path to `invoke`,\nnot the original source path, when a compiled artifact exists.\n\n## Iterator counter prepending\n\nThe iterator counter (issue 221) is prepended to the input array by the\ndispatch layer, not by the spec. From the spec's perspective, an\niterator box just has one extra input. The spec doesn't know which\ninput is the counter — that's a graph-level concept.\n\n## Errors crash the program\n\nA nonzero return from `invoke` is a fatal error. The dispatch layer\nprints the error context (box id, function name, language) to stderr\nand aborts the process. There is no recovery, no retry, no per-task\n\"failed\" state, no fallback. There are no timeouts on stalled tasks,\nno wait-list garbage collection, no failure propagation through the\ngraph.\n\nThe reasoning: a task that cannot produce a correct return value is a\nbug. Bugs do not belong in production. Building in detection and\nrecovery for bug states adds runtime cost and complexity to handle a\ncase that should not exist. If a bug surfaces in production, the\nprogram crashes loudly; the developer fixes the bug and redeploys.\n\nThe spec is still responsible for catching language-level errors (Lua\n`error()`, C signals it can intercept, Bash nonzero exit) and\ntranslating them into a nonzero return — so that the dispatch layer\nsees a clean signal instead of an undefined post-error state. Once\nreturned, the program ends.\n\n## User-facing documentation\n\nThe interface is published in `langs/lang-spec.h`, which every spec\nimplementation includes. That header is the source of truth for the\ncontract.\n\nUser-facing docs that mention the language spec system:\n- `README.md` — short paragraph in the features list pointing out that\n  any language can be added by writing a spec, with a one-line example\n  of what that means\n- `docs/005-language-specs.md` (to be written) — the long-form guide\n  on writing a spec: walk through the Lua spec as a small reference,\n  show what `init` / `invoke` / `teardown` do, point at the C spec for\n  the `compile`-using case and the Bash spec for the\n  socket-server case\n- `docs/000-table-of-contents.md` — index entry for the new doc\n\nWithout these the spec system is invisible — users would never know it\nexists or how to extend it.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently)\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Write `langs/lang-spec.h` — the public interface header.\n2. Write `langs/lua/spec.c` first. Lua is the easiest because it's already\n   our default language and the existing driver gives a reference behavior.\n3. Write `langs/c/spec.c` — adds `compile` callback, exercises the dlopen\n   path.\n4. Write `langs/bash/spec.c` + `langs/bash/bash-server.sh` — exercises\n   the out-of-process socket model. This is the proof that languages\n   without an embeddable runtime fit the same interface.\n5. Pool runner registry: `dlopen` every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup,\n   register by `name`. Box files are routed to specs by `file_ext`.\n6. Smoke test: a map with one Lua box, one C box, one Bash box, all\n   running in the pool, all going through the spec interface. No\n   special-cased code paths.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`, `drivers/c.sh` — current ad-hoc\n  drivers, replaced by `langs/<name>/spec.c`\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool startup invokes\n  spec `init` per worker per language\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — dispatch layer reads slots and\n  passes raw bytes to specs (specs do not touch slots)\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — calls `invoke` per task\n- `issues/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` — compile button\n  runs spec `compile` for every box\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — Option 1 (FFI) and Option 3 (Unix\n  socket) describe the two execution models specs implement\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Registry — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/011-spec-registry.{c,h}` scans a `langs/` directory, dlopens\nevery `<name>/spec.so` it finds with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL`, and\nexposes name + extension lookup plus enumeration. The three\nshipped stubs (lua/c/bash) load cleanly and round-trip through\n`spec_registry_get` and `spec_registry_for_ext`. Four unit tests\nin `tests/011-spec-registry-test.c` cover the load, missing dir,\nnull inputs, and accessor safety.\n\nDeferred: hooking `spec->init(worker_idx)` into the pool's\n`worker_main` between TLS setup and the init barrier. That's the\nfinal piece that makes 303 fully wired; lands in a follow-on once\na spec has a real `init` body to call (issue 306 onward).\n",

    "newString":"- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queued-input slot semantics\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Skeleton — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/012-dispatch.{c,h,info.md}` ships the types and the action's\nsignature with a stub body that increments a diagnostic counter\non the context and frees the task. `dispatch_ctx_t` bundles the\ngraph, slot store, spec registry, and pool — every task carries a\npointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\nwithout globals. `dispatch_spawn(ctx, box_id, priority)`\nallocates a task and calls `pool_spawn`.\n\nTwo skeleton tests in `tests/012-dispatch-test.c` build the full\nruntime (graph + slots + registry + pool) and submit either one\ntask per box, or 200 tasks at varied priorities, and assert that\nthe counter advances by the right amount.\n\nWhat's still ahead inside 304:\n- Reading inputs from per-port slots (peek vs pop based on\n  compile-time wire classification — that classification work\n  itself is the deferred size-class step in 305).\n- Invoking the per-worker spec handle. Needs 303's pool hook in\n  place so each worker has its handles populated; right now the\n  context's `specs` registry is reachable but worker handles\n  aren't routed through the worker context.\n- Picking the output branch per `routing.kind` and pushing to\n  consumer slots; this is the routing-table dispatch from the\n  unified schema in issue 233.\n- Spawn-on-input-ready chaining: each push to a consumer slot\n  triggers a check, which may spawn the consumer's next task."
  },

      "content":"# 306 — Lua language spec implementation (reference spec)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nLua boxes today run via `drivers/lua.sh`, which spawns a fresh `luajit`\nprocess per box invocation, feeds it stdin, and reads stdout. Process\nspawn cost dominates; each call is its own fresh interpreter. There is\nno persistent Lua state between calls.\n\n## Concept\nThe Lua language spec implements `lang_spec_t` (issue 303) for Lua. It\nis the first reference implementation of the spec interface and the\nproof that the in-process FFI model works. It is also the simplest\ncase — no compile step, no out-of-process server.\n\nEach worker thread gets its own `lua_State`. States are not shared.\nPer-thread states need no locking on the call path; the state's\ninternals are only ever touched by the worker that owns it.\n\n`langs/lua/spec.c` is built into `langs/lua/spec.so` and loaded by\nthe pool runner via `dlopen` at startup, like any other spec.\n\n## Per-worker state\n\nInit creates a fresh `lua_State` and configures it:\n\n```c\nvoid *lua_init(int worker_idx) {",

There is\n10\tno persistent Lua state between calls.\n11\t\n12\t## Concept\n13\tThe Lua language spec implements `lang_spec_t` (issue 303) for Lua. It\n14\tis the first reference implementation of the spec interface and the\n15\tproof that the in-process FFI model works. It is also the simplest\n16\tcase — no compile step, no out-of-process server.\n17\t\n18\tEach worker thread gets its own `lua_State`. States are not shared.\n19\tPer-thread states need no locking on the call path; the state's\n20\tinternals are only ever touched by the worker that owns it.\n21\t\n22\t`langs/lua/spec.c` is built into `langs/lua/spec.so` and loaded by\n23\tthe pool runner via `dlopen` at startup, like any other spec.\n24\t\n25\t## Per-worker state\n26\t\n27\tInit creates a fresh `lua_State` and configures it:\n28\t\n29\t```c\n30\tvoid *lua_init(int worker_idx) {"

    "originalFile":"# 306 — Lua language spec implementation (reference spec)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nLua boxes today run via `drivers/lua.sh`, which spawns a fresh `luajit`\nprocess per box invocation, feeds it stdin, and reads stdout. Process\nspawn cost dominates; each call is its own fresh interpreter. There is\nno persistent Lua state between calls.\n\n## Concept\nThe Lua language spec implements `lang_spec_t` (issue 303) for Lua. It\nis the first reference implementation of the spec interface and the\nproof that the in-process FFI model works. It is also the simplest\ncase — no compile step, no out-of-process server.\n\nEach worker thread gets its own `lua_State`. States are not shared.\nPer-thread states need no locking on the call path; the state's\ninternals are only ever touched by the worker that owns it.\n\n`langs/lua/spec.c` is built into `langs/lua/spec.so` and loaded by\nthe pool runner via `dlopen` at startup, like any other spec.\n\n## Per-worker state\n\nInit creates a fresh `lua_State` and configures it:\n\n```c\nvoid *lua_init(int worker_idx) {\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    set_package_path(L);   // libs/, map src/, meta.json src_dirs\n    return L;\n}\n\nvoid lua_teardown(void *handle) {\n    lua_close((lua_State *)handle);\n}\n```\n\n`set_package_path` writes `package.path` and `package.cpath` to\ninclude exactly one directory: the map's own `src/`. Everything the\nmap needs — vendored libs, helper modules, anything — is copied into\n`src/` by the compile step (issue 222). The compiled map is then a\nself-contained directory: ship the directory to someone else and it\nruns without further setup.\n\nThis is a tightening of the phase 2 path, which also included\nSoraMech's central `libs/` and any `meta.json src_dirs`. The new rule\nis: one place to look for functions, the map's own `src/`, full stop.\nCompile is the step that resolves dependencies into that location.\n\n## File-and-function caching\n\nA naive `invoke` would `luaL_loadfile` and look up the function on\nevery call. Both are unnecessary work — the file's chunk does not\nchange during a run, and the function reference is stable.\n\nThe Lua spec keeps a per-handle cache: for each box source file\nloaded, store the table returned by the file's chunk as a Lua\nregistry key (`LUA_REGISTRYINDEX`). On first invocation:\n1. `luaL_loadfile(L, file_path)` — loads the chunk.\n2. `lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0)` — runs the chunk, expecting a returned\n   table.\n3. Store the table in the registry under a key derived from `file_path`.\n\nOn subsequent invocations:\n1. Look up the registry entry by `file_path`.\n2. Index it by `fn_name` to get the function reference.\n3. Skip `luaL_loadfile` entirely.\n\nThe cache is per-`lua_State` and therefore per-worker; no\nsynchronization is needed.\n\n## Box file convention\n\nA Lua box file returns a table whose keys are the box's exported\nfunction names:\n\n```lua\n-- maps/<name>/src/classify.lua\nlocal M = {}\n\nfunction M.classify(text)\n    if text:match(\"^%d+$\") then return \"numeric\"\n    elseif text:match(\"[a-z]\") then return \"alpha\"\n    else return \"other\"\n    end\nend\n\nreturn M\n```\n\nThe box JSON references it by `ref = \"classify.lua\"`, `fn = \"classify\"`.\nThe spec loads `classify.lua`, stores its returned table, and indexes\ninto it with `\"classify\"` to get the function.\n\nThis is the existing phase 2 convention — kept as-is.\n\n## Input marshalling\n\nInputs arrive at `invoke` as `(void *bytes, int size)` pairs. The\nspec is responsible for converting each input's bytes into the Lua\nvalue type the user's function expects. The user's function sees\narguments as native Lua values — never a raw byte buffer that the\nfunction has to parse itself.\n\nEach input has a declared type in the box JSON\n(`{\"name\": \"count\", \"type\": \"number\"}`). The graph loader (issue 305)\nrecords this type on the `input_decl_t` and passes the type alongside\nthe bytes when calling `invoke`. The Lua spec dispatches on type:\n\n| Declared type | Lua spec action                                             |\n|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `string`      | `lua_pushlstring(L, bytes, size)`                           |\n| `number`      | parse with `strtod`, `lua_pushnumber`                       |\n| `integer`     | parse with `strtoll`, `lua_pushinteger`                     |\n| `boolean`     | strcmp against `\"true\"` / `\"false\"`, `lua_pushboolean`      |\n| `json`        | call `dkjson.decode` on the bytes, push the resulting table |\n| `bytes`       | `lua_pushlstring` (raw, may contain nulls)                  |\n| `any`         | treat as `string` for now                                   |\n\nThe Lua function then takes typed arguments:\n\n```lua\nfunction M.add(a, b)            -- both already numbers\n    return a + b\nend\n\nfunction M.classify(payload)    -- payload is already a table\n    return payload.kind\nend\n```\n\nThe user does not write `tonumber` or `dkjson.decode` calls inside\ntheir box function. The spec did that work before the function was\ncalled.\n\nIf a parse fails (`json` input that isn't valid JSON, `number` input\nthat isn't a number), the spec returns nonzero and the dispatch layer\naborts (per issue 303).\n\n## Return marshalling\n\nThe Lua function returns one or more values. The spec converts the\nreturn into bytes for the output slot:\n\n| Return shape           | Spec action                                                   |\n|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Single string          | `lua_tolstring` → copy into `out_buf`                         |\n| Single number          | `snprintf(\"%.17g\", ...)` into `out_buf`                       |\n| Single boolean         | write `\"true\"` or `\"false\"`                                   |\n| Single table           | `dkjson.encode` into `out_buf`                                |\n| Single nil             | `*out_size = 0` (zero-byte output)                            |\n| Multiple values        | wrap into a table `{v1, v2, ...}` and `dkjson.encode`         |\n\n`nil` is a valid return. The spec writes zero bytes and sets\n`*out_size = 0`. Downstream consumers receive a zero-byte slot value;\nhow they interpret it depends on their declared input type (typed\n`number` consumer fails to parse; typed `string` consumer gets an\nempty string; typed `json` consumer parses zero bytes as `null` via\ndkjson). We cannot demand that user functions never return nil, so we\nhandle it.\n\nMultiple return values are wrapped into a table and JSON-encoded.\nPhase 2 silently dropped extra returns; phase 3 keeps them — the\nserialized form is `[v1, v2, ...]`.\n\nOutput buffer is sized to the box's declared `output_capacity`\n(issue 305's `box_t`). If the serialized value exceeds that, abort\n(per the hard-crash policy in issue 303). For variable-size outputs\nthe box declares `output_capacity = 0` and uses the large-value heap\n(issue 302); the spec writes into that heap and stores the handle in\n`out_buf`.\n\ndkjson is the table serializer in both directions (input parsing\nabove and output serialization here). It is already vendored.\n\n## Error handling\n\nEvery `lua_pcall` is wrapped:\n```c\nint rc = lua_pcall(L, n_args, 1, 0);\nif (rc != LUA_OK) {\n    fprintf(stderr, \"[lua spec] %s:%s — %s\\n\",\n            file_path, fn_name, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n    lua_pop(L, 1);\n    return 1;  // dispatch layer aborts the program\n}\n```\n\nLua errors (`error(...)`, runtime errors, syntax errors during file\nload) all surface here as nonzero `pcall` returns. The spec prints\nthe box context and the Lua error message to stderr, then returns\nnonzero. The dispatch layer aborts.\n\nThere is no try-and-recover. Per issue 303, errors crash the program.\n\n## Build\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c          ← lang_spec_t implementation\n    Makefile        ← builds spec.so\n    spec.so         ← built artifact (gitignored)\n```\n\nThe Makefile target:\n```make\nspec.so: spec.c\n\t$(CC) -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall \\\n\t    -I$(LUA_INCLUDE) \\\n\t    -o $@ $< \\\n\t    -L$(LUA_LIB) -lluajit-5.1\n```\n\nLuaJIT is the assumed runtime — it matches the phase 2 driver and the\nproject preference (LuaJIT-compatible Lua, no 5.4 syntax). The build\nlinks against the system LuaJIT shared library.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently — earlier questions resolved as follows:)\n\n- nil return: valid. Zero-byte output, downstream consumers\n  interpret per their declared input type.\n- Multiple return values: wrapped into a table and JSON-encoded via\n  dkjson. No values dropped.\n- Table serializer: dkjson, already vendored. Used in both\n  directions (input parsing and output serialization).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Set up `langs/lua/` directory with a Makefile that builds an empty\n   `spec.so` exporting a stub `soramech_lang_spec`.\n2. Implement `init` and `teardown`. Verify the pool runner can\n   `dlopen` the spec and call `init` per worker without errors.\n3. Implement file-and-function caching — load a file, store its\n   returned table in the registry, look it up later.\n4. Implement input marshalling: push bytes as strings, count args.\n5. Implement `lua_pcall` invocation with error wrapping.\n6. Implement string return marshalling. Smoke test: `maps/hello`\n   end-to-end through the pool.\n7. Implement number return marshalling.\n8. Implement table-via-JSON return marshalling.\n9. Add `package.path` resolution for libs/, src/, and `meta.src_dirs`.\n10. Test against `maps/classify-demo` and `maps/driver-test` (Lua\n    portions).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `drivers/lua.sh` — phase 2 Lua driver, retired by this spec\n- `langs/lang-spec.h` — interface header (issue 303)\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec contract this implements\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer that calls\n  `invoke`\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — large-value heap for\n  variable-size returns\n- `libs/dkjson` (vendored) — table-to-JSON serialization\n- `maps/hello`, `maps/classify-demo` — Lua-only smoke test maps\n",
    "userModified":false,

Returns the state as the per-\n  worker handle.\n- `teardown(handle)` calls `lua_close`.\n- `invoke(handle, file_path, fn_name, inputs, sizes, n, out_buf,\n  out_cap, out_size)` loads the file with `luaL_loadfile`,\n  executes the chunk (which is expected to return a module\n  table), pulls the named function out of that table, pushes each\n  input as a Lua string, calls via `lua_pcall`, and copies the\n  return as a string into the caller's buffer.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"/* langs/c/spec.c — C language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a small dlopen cache. `compile` runs gcc\n * to turn a box source file into a .so; `invoke` dlopens the .so\n * (caching the handle), dlsyms the named function, and calls it\n * through a fixed signature.\n *\n * Designed in issue 307. C box functions follow a single\n * convention that matches the spec's `invoke` shape minus the\n * per-worker handle:\n *\n *     int box_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n *                void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n *\n * Return 0 on success, nonzero (fatal) on failure. This iteration\n * does not generate per-box wrappers from declared signatures\n * (issue 307's optional advanced mode) — every C box uses the\n * fixed signature above. Wrapper generation can land as a follow-on\n * once we have a box whose declared types diverge from the byte-\n * array shape.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define C_CACHE_SIZE 32\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker dlopen cache */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *path;     /* strdup'd; identifies the cache entry         */\n    void *dl;       /* dlopen handle                                */\n} c_cache_entry_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    c_cache_entry_t entries[C_CACHE_SIZE];\n    int             count;\n} c_handle_t;\n\ntypedef int (*c_box_fn_t)(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n                          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_init() */\nstatic void *c_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    c_handle_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_teardown() */\nstatic void c_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (h->entries[i].dl) dlclose(h->entries[i].dl);\n        free(h->entries[i].path);\n    }\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ get_or_load() — find a cached .so or dlopen and add */\nstatic void *get_or_load(c_handle_t *h, const char *path)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(h->entries[i].path, path) == 0) return h->entries[i].dl;\n    }\n    if (h->count >= C_CACHE_SIZE) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen cache full (%d entries)\\n\", C_CACHE_SIZE);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    void *dl = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!dl) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen('%s'): %s\\n\", path, dlerror());\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    h->entries[h->count].path = strdup(path);\n    h->entries[h->count].dl   = dl;\n    h->count++;\n    return dl;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_invoke() */\nstatic int c_invoke(void *handle,\n                    const char  *file_path,    /* path to a .so */\n                    const char  *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data,\n                    const int   *input_sizes,\n                    int          n_inputs,\n                    void        *out_buf,\n                    int          out_capacity,\n                    int         *out_size)\n{\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    if (!h || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    void *dl = get_or_load(h, file_path);\n    if (!dl) return -1;\n\n    /* dlsym returns void*, but the cast to a function pointer is\n     * formally implementation-defined; POSIX requires it to work.\n     * The union trick avoids -Wpedantic noise. */\n    union { void *p; c_box_fn_t fn; } u;\n    (void)dlerror();\n    u.p = dlsym(dl, fn_name);\n    const char *err = dlerror();\n    if (!u.p || err) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlsym('%s' in '%s'): %s\\n\",\n                fn_name, file_path, err ? err : \"symbol not found\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return u.fn(input_data, input_sizes, n_inputs,\n                out_buf, out_capacity, out_size);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name     = \"c\",\n    .file_ext = \".c\",\n    .init     = c_init,\n    .teardown = c_teardown,\n    .compile  = c_compile,\n    .invoke   = c_invoke,\n};\n/* }}} */\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/langs/c/spec.c"
        }
      }],

    "originalFile":"/* tests/011-spec-registry-test.c — unit tests for the spec\n * registry.\n *\n * Exercises directory scan, dlopen, symbol lookup, and the name /\n * extension accessors. Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_teardown() */\n/* Calls spec_registry_init_worker against the real shipped specs.\n * The Lua spec has a real init that returns a lua_State; C and\n * Bash currently have NULL init pointers (stubs), so they\n * contribute NULL handles. Verifies the lua handle is non-NULL,\n * the others are NULL, and teardown walks cleanly. */\nstatic int test_worker_init_teardown(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    int n = spec_registry_size(r);\n    ASSERT(n == 3);\n\n    void *handles[8] = {0};\n    int got = spec_registry_init_worker(r, 0, handles, (int)(sizeof handles / sizeof *handles));\n    ASSERT(got == 3);\n\n    /* Find the lua spec's index and assert its handle is non-NULL. */\n    int lua_idx = -1, c_idx = -1, bash_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) lua_idx = i;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) c_idx = i;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) bash_idx = i;\n    }\n    ASSERT(lua_idx >= 0);\n    ASSERT(handles[lua_idx] != NULL);\n    /* C and Bash stubs have NULL init, so no handle. */\n    ASSERT(handles[c_idx]    == NULL);\n    ASSERT(handles[bash_idx] == NULL);\n\n    spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, handles, got);\n    /* After teardown, all slots are NULL. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < got; i++) ASSERT(handles[i] == NULL);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"011-spec-registry-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_three_specs);\n    RUN(missing_dir);\n    RUN(null_dir);\n    RUN(null_safety);\n    RUN(worker_init_teardown);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:        $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_teardown() */\n/* Calls spec_registry_init_worker against the real shipped specs.\n * The Lua spec has a real init that returns a lua_State; C and\n * Bash currently have NULL init pointers (stubs), so they\n * contribute NULL handles. Verifies the lua handle is non-NULL,\n * the others are NULL, and teardown walks cleanly. */\nstatic int test_worker_init_teardown(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    int n = spec_registry_size(r);\n    ASSERT(n == 3);\n\n    void *handles[8] = {0};\n    int got = spec_registry_init_worker(r, 0, handles, (int)(sizeof handles / sizeof *handles));\n    ASSERT(got == 3);\n\n    /* Find the lua spec's index and assert its handle is non-NULL. */\n    int lua_idx = -1, c_idx = -1, bash_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) lua_idx = i;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) c_idx = i;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) bash_idx = i;\n    }\n    ASSERT(lua_idx >= 0);\n    ASSERT(handles[lua_idx] != NULL);\n    /* C spec now has a real init (issue 307) and returns a non-NULL\n     * handle. The Bash spec is still a stub at this point. */\n    ASSERT(handles[c_idx]    != NULL);\n    ASSERT(handles[bash_idx] == NULL);\n\n    spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, handles, got);\n    /* After teardown, all slots are NULL. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < got; i++) ASSERT(handles[i] == NULL);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"011-spec-registry-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_three_specs);\n    RUN(missing_dir);\n    RUN(null_dir);\n    RUN(null_safety);\n    RUN(worker_init_teardown);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

Failures don't cascade: the writer keeps going,\n * and the caller can check by re-emitting or by closing.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H\n#define SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct jsonl_writer jsonl_writer_t;\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Open `path` for writing (truncates). All emits are thread-safe. */\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_start  (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *map, int n_workers);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_submit(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_start (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_end   (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                           long duration_us, int output_size);\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_end    (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           long duration_us, int n_tasks);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H */\n",

  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01L8YBLv1nt69SFM8GB47qYe",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/013-jsonl-events.c — phase 3 run-log event writer.\n *\n * Each emit serializes one event into a 512-byte buffer via the\n * bounded JSON writer (issue 314), appends a newline, then writes\n * the line to the underlying FILE under a per-writer mutex. The\n * mutex is what the MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread\n * will replace once dispatch is producing events at rate.\n *\n * Buffer size is fixed at 512 bytes. Every event the architecture\n * doc defines fits comfortably; if a future event needs more it\n * can be bumped or made dynamic.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#define EVENT_BUF 512\n\n/* {{{ Writer struct */\nstruct jsonl_writer {\n    FILE            *fp;\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_open() */\njsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    jsonl_writer_t *w = calloc(1, sizeof *w);\n    if (!w) { fclose(fp); return NULL; }\n    w->fp = fp;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&w->mtx, NULL) != 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        free(w);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return w;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_close() */\nvoid jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    if (w->fp) { fflush(w->fp); fclose(w->fp); w->fp = NULL; }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&w->mtx);\n    free(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ flush_line() — finalize the writer, append \\n, write under lock */\nstatic int flush_line(jsonl_writer_t *w, json_writer_t *jw, char *buf)\n{\n    int n = json_writer_finish(jw);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    if (n >= EVENT_BUF) return -1;   /* would overrun the newline byte */\n    buf[n] = '\\n';\n    int total = n + 1;\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    int written = 0;\n    if (w->fp) {\n        written = (int)fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)total, w->fp);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    return (written == total) ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ emit helpers — common event prologue */\nstatic void begin_event(json_writer_t *jw, const char *type, double ts)\n{\n    json_writer_object(jw);\n    json_writer_key(jw, \"event\"); json_writer_string(jw, type);\n    json_writer_key(jw, \"ts\");    json_writer_number(jw, ts);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_emit_run_start() */\nint jsonl_emit_run_start(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                         const char *map, int n_workers)\n{\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    char buf[EVENT_BUF];\n    json_writer_t jw;\n    json_writer_init(&jw, buf, EVENT_BUF);\n    begin_event(&jw, \"run_start\", ts);\n    json_writer_key(&jw, \"map\"); Emits one JSON object per event,\none event per line, to a writable file.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `jsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)` — opens\n  `path` for writing (truncates). NULL on failure.\n- `void jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)` — fflush+fclose,\n  free.\n\n## Event emitters\n\nEach returns 0 on success, -1 on write or encode failure.\nAll emitters are thread-safe via a per-writer mutex.\n\n- `jsonl_emit_run_start  (w, ts, map, n_workers)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_submit(w, ts, task_id, box_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_start (w, ts, task_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_end   (w, ts, task_id, worker_idx, duration_us, output_size)`\n- `jsonl_emit_run_end    (w, ts, duration_us, n_tasks)`\n\nTimestamps are Unix epoch seconds as doubles, matching the\narchitecture doc.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- **Slot allocator events** (`slot_alloc` / `slot_free`) under\n  `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`. Adds when 302's allocator is\n  instrumented.\n- **Per-task input/output bytes** under `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`.\n- **MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread.** Current\n  implementation locks a mutex around `fwrite`. The proper\n  pipeline is many producers pushing fixed-size event records\n  onto a lock-free ring while one writer thread drains and\n  serializes. Lands once dispatch is producing events at rate.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 311 — design.\n- Issue 314 — bounded JSON writer this builds on.\n- Issue 304 — dispatch produces task_start / task_end.\n- Issue 301 — pool runner produces run_start / run_end.\n",

Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:        $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.c — SoraMech thread pool, implementation.\n *\n * Pthreads, a singly-linked FIFO task queue under one mutex, a\n * condition variable for \"queue has work or we're shutting down\",\n * an atomic active-task counter with its own mutex/cv for the\n * quiescence wait, and a one-shot init barrier under a third\n * mutex/cv.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. The three sync primitives never nest —\n * pool_spawn takes the queue mutex, pool_wait_quiescent takes the\n * quiet mutex, pool_init_barrier takes the init mutex. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked, priority-ordered */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    int                priority;     /* higher = earlier; FIFO on ties */\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its (currently empty) per-thread setup; main thread\n     * waits for workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released\n     * and broadcasts. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point — issue 303 plugs spec->init calls here\n     * for every language the map uses. j < i; j++) pthread_join(p->threads[j], NULL);\n            goto fail;\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n\nfail:\n    if (p) {\n        free(p->threads);\n        free(p->contexts);\n        free(p);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_init_barrier() */\nvoid pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    while (p->workers_ready < p->n_workers) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    p->init_released = 1;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg, int priority)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;
