p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < p->n_workers; i++) {\n        pthread_join(p->threads[i], NULL);\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->quiet_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->init_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->init_cv);\n\n    free(p->threads);\n    free(p->contexts);\n    free(p);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.c — SoraMech thread pool, implementation.\n *\n * Pthreads, a singly-linked FIFO task queue under one mutex, a\n * condition variable for \"queue has work or we're shutting down\",\n * an atomic active-task counter with its own mutex/cv for the\n * quiescence wait, and a one-shot init barrier under a third\n * mutex/cv.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. The three sync primitives never nest —\n * pool_spawn takes the queue mutex, pool_wait_quiescent takes the\n * quiet mutex, pool_init_barrier takes the init mutex. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked, priority-ordered */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    int                priority;     /* higher = earlier; FIFO on ties */\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Per-worker init callback (issue 303 plumbing). */\n    pool_init_cb_t   init_cb;\n    void            *init_user;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its per-thread setup runs; main thread waits for\n     * workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released and\n     * broadcasts. init_fail is set if any worker's init callback\n     * returns nonzero; pool_init_barrier reports it. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    int              init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point — issue 303 plugs spec->init calls here\n     * for every language the map uses. Empty for now. */\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready, notify the main thread, then park at\n     * the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) pthread_join(p->threads[j], NULL);\n            goto fail;\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n\nfail:\n    if (p) {\n        free(p->threads);\n        free(p->contexts);\n        free(p);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_init_barrier() */\nvoid pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    while (p->workers_ready < p->n_workers) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    p->init_released = 1;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg, int priority)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn       = fn;\n    t->arg      = arg;\n    t->priority = priority;\n    t->next     = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    /* Priority-ordered insertion. Walk from head until finding the\n     * first node with strictly-lower priority; insert before it.\n     * Strict less-than gives FIFO tiebreaking on equal priority.\n     * The queue is small in practice (bounded by ready tasks), so\n     * linear scan is fine. */\n    task_node_t **link = &p->q_head;\n    while (*link && (*link)->priority >= priority) {\n        link = &(*link)->next;\n    }\n    t->next = *link;\n    *link = t;\n    if (t->next == NULL) p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_wait_quiescent() */\nvoid pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    while (atomic_load_explicit(&p->active, memory_order_acquire) > 0) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->quiet_cv, &p->quiet_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_n_workers() */\nint pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)\n{\n    return p ? p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < p->n_workers; i++) {\n        pthread_join(p->threads[i], NULL);\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->quiet_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->init_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->init_cv);\n\n    free(p->threads);\n    free(p->contexts);\n    free(p);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

The three sync primitives never nest —\n * pool_spawn takes the queue mutex, pool_wait_quiescent takes the\n * quiet mutex, pool_init_barrier takes the init mutex. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked, priority-ordered */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    int                priority;     /* higher = earlier; FIFO on ties */\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Per-worker init callback (issue 303 plumbing). */\n    pool_init_cb_t   init_cb;\n    void            *init_user;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its per-thread setup runs; main thread waits for\n     * workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released and\n     * broadcasts. init_fail is set if any worker's init callback\n     * returns nonzero; pool_init_barrier reports it. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    int              init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point. Issue 303's spec_registry helper\n     * registers itself via pool_set_worker_init; this is where it\n     * runs, populating ctx->handles[] before the worker is allowed\n     * to pull tasks. */\n    int cb_rc = 0;\n    if (p->init_cb) cb_rc = p->init_cb(ctx->thread_idx, ctx, p->init_user);\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready (or mark failure), notify the main\n     * thread, then park at the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (cb_rc != 0) p->init_fail = 1;\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    int fail = p->init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* If anyone's init failed, every worker bails before touching\n     * the task queue; the pool is unusable until destroyed. */\n    if (fail) return NULL;\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) pthread_join(p->threads[j], NULL);\n            goto fail;\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n\nfail:\n    if (p) {\n        free(p->threads);\n        free(p->contexts);\n        free(p);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_init_barrier() */\nvoid pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    while (p->workers_ready < p->n_workers) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    p->init_released = 1;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg, int priority)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn       = fn;\n    t->arg      = arg;\n    t->priority = priority;\n    t->next     = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    /* Priority-ordered insertion. Walk from head until finding the\n     * first node with strictly-lower priority; insert before it.\n     * Strict less-than gives FIFO tiebreaking on equal priority.\n     * The queue is small in practice (bounded by ready tasks), so\n     * linear scan is fine. */\n    task_node_t **link = &p->q_head;\n    while (*link && (*link)->priority >= priority) {\n        link = &(*link)->next;\n    }\n    t->next = *link;\n    *link = t;\n    if (t->next == NULL) p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_wait_quiescent() */\nvoid pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    while (atomic_load_explicit(&p->active, memory_order_acquire) > 0) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->quiet_cv, &p->quiet_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_n_workers() */\nint pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)\n{\n    return p ? p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < p->n_workers; i++) {\n        pthread_join(p->threads[i], NULL);\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->quiet_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->init_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->init_cv);\n\n    free(p->threads);\n    free(p->contexts);\n    free(p);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1), 0);\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority. {

    "content":[{

        "id":"toolu_01YSELjcyD7eoeDK4r16r26o",

        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* tests/303-pool-spec-init-test.c — end-to-end test of the\n * spec_registry → pool worker-init plumbing.\n *\n * Loads the spec registry, registers a per-worker init callback\n * with the pool that invokes spec_registry_init_worker on each\n * worker's handles[] array, runs the barrier, then spawns one\n * task per worker that reads pool_current_worker->handles[lua_idx]\n * and stashes it for the main thread to verify. Every worker\n * should have a non-NULL Lua handle after the barrier releases.\n *\n * Run from the project root so `langs/` is reachable.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() — the canonical pool init callback */\n/* Wires spec_registry_init_worker into pool_set_worker_init.\n * user is the spec_registry_t *. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Shared state for the read-back-from-worker tests */\n#define MAX_OBS 32\nstatic struct {\n    int   thread_idx;\n    void *lua_handle;\n} g_obs[MAX_OBS];\nstatic atomic_int g_obs_count;\nstatic int        g_lua_idx;\n\nstatic void observe_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    int slot = atomic_fetch_add(&g_obs_count, 1);\n    if (slot < MAX_OBS) {\n        g_obs[slot].thread_idx = pool_current_worker->thread_idx;\n        g_obs[slot].lua_handle = pool_current_worker->handles[g_lua_idx];\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_handles_populated() */\nstatic int test_handles_populated(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    /* Find the lua spec's index. */\n    g_lua_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0;     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/013-jsonl-events-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:        $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"/* libs/task-pool/pool.c — SoraMech thread pool, implementation.\n *\n * Pthreads, a singly-linked FIFO task queue under one mutex, a\n * condition variable for \"queue has work or we're shutting down\",\n * an atomic active-task counter with its own mutex/cv for the\n * quiescence wait, and a one-shot init barrier under a third\n * mutex/cv.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301. The three sync primitives never nest —\n * pool_spawn takes the queue mutex, pool_wait_quiescent takes the\n * quiet mutex, pool_init_barrier takes the init mutex. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked, priority-ordered */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    int                priority;     /* higher = earlier; FIFO on ties */\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Per-worker init callback (issue 303 plumbing). */\n    pool_init_cb_t   init_cb;\n    void            *init_user;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its per-thread setup runs; main thread waits for\n     * workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released and\n     * broadcasts. init_fail is set if any worker's init callback\n     * returns nonzero; pool_init_barrier reports it. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    int              init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point. Issue 303's spec_registry helper\n     * registers itself via pool_set_worker_init; this is where it\n     * runs, populating ctx->handles[] before the worker is allowed\n     * to pull tasks. */\n    int cb_rc = 0;\n    if (p->init_cb) cb_rc = p->init_cb(ctx->thread_idx, ctx, p->init_user);\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready (or mark failure), notify the main\n     * thread, then park at the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (cb_rc != 0) p->init_fail = 1;\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    int fail = p->init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* If anyone's init failed, every worker bails before touching\n     * the task queue; the pool is unusable until destroyed. */\n    if (fail) return NULL;\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0; Issue 303's spec_registry\n     * helper registers itself via pool_set_worker_init; this is\n     * where it runs, populating ctx->handles[] before the worker\n     * is allowed to pull tasks. */\n    int cb_rc = 0;\n    if (p->init_cb) cb_rc = p->init_cb(ctx->thread_idx, ctx, p->init_user);\n\n    /* Stage 3: report ready (or failure) and park on init_released. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (cb_rc != 0) p->init_fail = 1;\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    int fail = p->init_fail;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* If anyone's init failed, every worker bails before touching\n     * the task queue; the pool is unusable until destroyed. */\n    if (fail) return NULL;"
  },

Every worker\n * should have a non-NULL Lua handle after the barrier releases.\n *\n * Run from the project root so `langs/` is reachable.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() — the canonical pool init callback */\n/* Wires spec_registry_init_worker into pool_set_worker_init.\n * user is the spec_registry_t *. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Shared state for the read-back-from-worker tests */\n#define MAX_OBS 32\nstatic struct {\n    int   thread_idx;\n    void *lua_handle;\n} g_obs[MAX_OBS];\nstatic atomic_int g_obs_count;\nstatic int        g_lua_idx;\n\nstatic void observe_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    int slot = atomic_fetch_add(&g_obs_count, 1);\n    if (slot < MAX_OBS) {\n        g_obs[slot].thread_idx = pool_current_worker->thread_idx;\n        g_obs[slot].lua_handle = pool_current_worker->handles[g_lua_idx];\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_handles_populated() */\nstatic int test_handles_populated(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    /* Find the lua spec's index. */\n    g_lua_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        if (strcmp(spec_registry_at(r, i)->name, \"lua\") == 0) {\n            g_lua_idx = i;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    ASSERT(g_lua_idx >= 0);\n\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, spec_pool_init_cb, r);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == 0);\n\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker sees one. */\n    atomic_store(&g_obs_count, 0);\n    enum { N_TASKS = 64 };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_TASKS; i++) pool_spawn(p, observe_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    int n = atomic_load(&g_obs_count);\n    ASSERT(n == N_TASKS);\n\n    /* Every observation must have a non-NULL Lua handle and a\n     * thread_idx in range. */\n    int seen_per_thread[POOL_MAX_WORKERS] = {0};\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        ASSERT(g_obs[i].thread_idx >= 0);\n        ASSERT(g_obs[i].thread_idx < pool_n_workers(p));\n        ASSERT(g_obs[i].lua_handle != NULL);\n        if (g_obs[i].thread_idx < POOL_MAX_WORKERS)\n            seen_per_thread[g_obs[i].thread_idx]++;\n    }\n    /* All four workers should have been observed at least once. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < pool_n_workers(p); i++) ASSERT(seen_per_thread[i] > 0);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_handles_distinct_per_worker() */\n/* Each worker should get its own lua_State, not a shared one. */\nstatic int test_handles_distinct_per_worker(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    g_lua_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        if (strcmp(spec_registry_at(r, i)->name, \"lua\") == 0) {\n            g_lua_idx = i; break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, spec_pool_init_cb, r);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == 0);\n\n    atomic_store(&g_obs_count, 0);\n    /* Burst enough tasks to cover every worker. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) pool_spawn(p, observe_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    int n = atomic_load(&g_obs_count);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    /* Collect distinct handles per thread_idx. */\n    void *per_thread[POOL_MAX_WORKERS] = {0};\n    for (int i = 0; i < n && i < MAX_OBS; i++) {\n        int t = g_obs[i].thread_idx;\n        if (t < 0 || t >= POOL_MAX_WORKERS) continue;\n        if (per_thread[t] == NULL) {\n            per_thread[t] = g_obs[i].lua_handle;\n        } else {\n            ASSERT(per_thread[t] == g_obs[i].lua_handle);\n        }\n    }\n    /* Different workers have different handles. */\n    for (int i = 0; Small\nchange; lives in `libs/task-pool/pool.c` and needs the runner to\npass a `spec_registry_t *` into `pool_create` (or to a new\n`pool_init_specs` API). Lands in the next pass.",
          "new_string":"What's still ahead inside 303: actually calling the helper from\nthe pool's `worker_main` so each worker thread populates its\n`worker_ctx_t.handles[]` before crossing the init barrier. Small\nchange; lives in `libs/task-pool/pool.c` and needs the runner to\npass a `spec_registry_t *` into `pool_create` (or to a new\n`pool_init_specs` API). Lands in the next pass.\n\n### Pool worker hook — 2026-05-12\n\n`libs/task-pool/pool.{c,h}` grew a per-worker init callback:\n`pool_set_worker_init(p, cb, user)` and `pool_init_barrier` now\nreturns an int (0 ok, -1 if any worker's callback failed). The\ninit barrier became a three-stage handshake so callbacks\nregistered between `pool_create` and `pool_init_barrier` can't\nrace the workers — stage 1 parks workers until the barrier\nauthorises them, stage 2 runs each worker's callback, stage 3\nreleases everyone into the task loop.\n\n`tests/303-pool-spec-init-test.c` wires `spec_registry_init_worker`\ninto the pool callback (a two-line trampoline) and asserts that\nspawned tasks see a non-NULL `lua_State` in\n`pool_current_worker->handles[lua_idx]`, with each worker getting\nits own distinct state. The pool-internal callback test in\n`tests/301-pool-test.c` covers the success and failure paths\nwithout the registry. 303 is now functionally complete end to\nend — the registry loads specs, the helper inits them per\nworker, and the pool's worker_main calls them through the hook.",

    "newString":"What's still ahead inside 303: actually calling the helper from\nthe pool's `worker_main` so each worker thread populates its\n`worker_ctx_t.handles[]` before crossing the init barrier. Small\nchange; lives in `libs/task-pool/pool.c` and needs the runner to\npass a `spec_registry_t *` into `pool_create` (or to a new\n`pool_init_specs` API). Lands in the next pass.\n\n### Pool worker hook — 2026-05-12\n\n`libs/task-pool/pool.{c,h}` grew a per-worker init callback:\n`pool_set_worker_init(p, cb, user)` and `pool_init_barrier` now\nreturns an int (0 ok, -1 if any worker's callback failed). The\ninit barrier became a three-stage handshake so callbacks\nregistered between `pool_create` and `pool_init_barrier` can't\nrace the workers — stage 1 parks workers until the barrier\nauthorises them, stage 2 runs each worker's callback, stage 3\nreleases everyone into the task loop.\n\n`tests/303-pool-spec-init-test.c` wires `spec_registry_init_worker`\ninto the pool callback (a two-line trampoline) and asserts that\nspawned tasks see a non-NULL `lua_State` in\n`pool_current_worker->handles[lua_idx]`, with each worker getting\nits own distinct state. The pool-internal callback test in\n`tests/301-pool-test.c` covers the success and failure paths\nwithout the registry. 303 is now functionally complete end to\nend — the registry loads specs, the helper inits them per\nworker, and the pool's worker_main calls them through the hook."
  },

The","+persistent Unix-domain-socket model lands as a follow-on.","+","+Limitations: inputs containing NUL bytes can't be passed as","+positional args (base64-encode if needed); output is bounded by","+`out_capacity`.","+","+`tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh` ships three fixture functions.","+Five tests in `tests/308-bash-spec-test.c` cover happy paths","+plus the missing-function failure mode."],
        "oldStart":297
      }],
    "newString":"- `maps/driver-test` — multi-language test map including Bash boxes\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### fork+exec invoke — 2026-05-12\n\nFirst-pass implementation: every invoke forks bash with an inline\n`-c` script that sources the box file and calls the named\nfunction with the inputs as positional args. Child's stdout is\nread through a pipe — that becomes the output bytes. Slow (~1 ms\nper call), but it gets bash boxes running end-to-end. The\npersistent Unix-domain-socket model lands as a follow-on.\n\nLimitations: inputs containing NUL bytes can't be passed as\npositional args (base64-encode if needed); output is bounded by\n`out_capacity`.\n\n`tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh` ships three fixture functions.\nFive tests in `tests/308-bash-spec-test.c` cover happy paths\nplus the missing-function failure mode."

Working tree uncommitted.**\n\n```\n009-slot-store-test       12\n010-graph-loader-test     11\n011-spec-registry-test     5\n012-dispatch-test          2\n013-jsonl-events-test      3   ← new\n301-pool-test             11   (was 9: +worker_init_callback, +worker_init_failure)\n303-pool-spec-init-test    2   ← new\n306-lua-spec-test          5\n307-c-spec-test            5   ← new\n308-bash-spec-test         5   ← new\n314-json-test             22\n```\n\n**Progress now:**\n\n| Issue | Status |\n|-------|--------|\n| 301 | in progress · pool skeleton done |\n| 302 | in progress · core complete |\n| 303 | in progress · registry + per-worker init + pool hook done |\n| 304 | in progress · skeleton done |\n| 305 | in progress · parse + schema + endpoint resolution + cycle detection done |\n| 306 | in progress · init + invoke + teardown done, file caching pending |\n| 307 | in progress · compile + invoke done, typed wrapper deferred |\n| 308 | in progress · fork+exec invoke done, persistent socket deferred |\n| 309 | in progress · scaffolding done |\n| 310 | in progress · API + ordering done |\n| 311 | in progress · json writer + event emitters done |\n| 314 | in progress · parser + writer complete |\n\n**Highlights this round:**\n- **307 C spec** — fork+exec gcc compile, dlopen+dlsym invoke, 32-entry cache per worker, fixed `int fn(const void **, const int *, int, void *, int, int *)` signature. Compiles `tests/maps/hello/src/echo.c` and runs both `echo` and `concat` correctly.\n- **308 Bash spec** — fork+exec bash per invoke with inline `bash -c '. \"$1\" && \"$2\" \"${@:3}\"'`. Real Bash functions running through the spec interface.\n- **311 event emitters** — `jsonl_emit_*` functions over the JSON writer, mutex-serialized file writes. Concurrent emit test runs 8 producers × 200 events through it; every line round-trips.\n- **303 pool worker hook** — `pool_set_worker_init(p, cb, user)` + three-stage init barrier so callbacks registered between `pool_create` and `pool_init_barrier` don't race past workers. Integration test confirms each worker gets its own non-NULL `lua_State` populated through `spec_registry_init_worker`.\n\nThe race fix in the pool was the interesting subtlety. **303 is now end-to-end done** — registry loads specs, helper inits them per worker, pool hook calls them at the right moment in worker startup. Want another round?"

i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return &g->boxes[i];\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nint graph_box_index(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n{\n    if (!g || !id) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return i;\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_spec_for_box() — find the spec index by box->lang */\n/* Returns the spec's index in the registry, or -1 if not found. */\nstatic int resolve_spec_for_box(const box_t *box, spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!box || !r) return -1;\n    if (box->kind != BOX_CALL) return -1;\n    if (box->lang) {\n        for (int i = 0;   "toolUseResult":{

    "structuredPatch":[{
        "oldLines":6,

        "lines":[" # is clearer than clever for tests)."," $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o"," $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\","+                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\","+                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\","                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o"," $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o"," $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\"],
        "oldStart":117
      }],
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/013-jsonl-events-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:        $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

          "content":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

Read each input port's value from its slot (peek mode for\n *      this iteration; pop mode + iterator multi-spawn land later).\n *   3. Do the box's work:\n *        - BOX_CALL — invoke the resolved language spec via the\n *          worker's per-language handle.\n *        - BOX_DATA — read the file at `box->path` (resolved\n *          relative to `graph_map_dir` if non-absolute) and use\n *          its contents as the output.\n *        - BOX_FILE_WRITE — write the second input (\"text\") to the\n *          path given by the first input or by box->path.\n *   4. Push the resulting bytes to every outgoing connection's\n *      consumer input slot.\n *   5. For each consumer, fire the spawn-on-input-ready check,\n *      which spawns the consumer iff it has all required inputs\n *      and hasn't been spawned yet (single-spawn guard via an\n *      atomic CAS).\n *\n * The optional `capture_outputs` mode also memcpy's the output\n * bytes into `ctx->last_outputs[box_id]` so tests can verify\n * what each box produced after the pool quiesces.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304.\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() — malloc'd diagnostic string */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[512];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_ctx_init() */\nint dispatch_ctx_init(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                      const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                      spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                      int enable_output_capture, char **err)\n{\n    if (!ctx || !g) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"dispatch_ctx_init: NULL ctx or graph\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    memset(ctx, 0, sizeof *ctx);\n    ctx->graph = g;\n    ctx->slots = s;\n    ctx->specs = r;\n    ctx->pool  = p;\n    atomic_init(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 0);\n    ctx->n_boxes              = graph_n_boxes(g);\n    ctx->default_out_capacity = 4096;\n\n    if (ctx->n_boxes > 0) {\n        ctx->box_ever_spawned = calloc((size_t)ctx->n_boxes, sizeof(_Atomic int));\n        if (!ctx->box_ever_spawned) {\n            if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n            atomic_init(&ctx->box_ever_spawned[i], 0);\n        }\n\n        if (enable_output_capture) {\n            ctx->capture_outputs    = 1;\n            ctx->last_outputs       = calloc((size_t)ctx->n_boxes, sizeof(char *));\n            ctx->last_output_sizes  = calloc((size_t)ctx->n_boxes, sizeof(int));\n            if (!ctx->last_outputs || !ctx->last_output_sizes) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_ctx_destroy() */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    if (ctx->last_outputs) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) free(ctx->last_outputs[i]);\n        free(ctx->last_outputs);\n    }\n    free(ctx->last_output_sizes);\n    free(ctx->box_ever_spawned);\n    memset(ctx, 0, sizeof *ctx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ box_is_ready() — every required input has a value */\nstatic int box_is_ready(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id)\n{\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, box_id);\n    if (!b) return 0;\n    if (b->n_inputs == 0) return 1;\n    if (!b->input_slot_ids) return 0;        /* runtime not attached */\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (b->inputs[i].optional) continue;\n        if (!slot_has_value(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i])) return 0;\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_spawn() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx || !ctx->pool) return;\n    dispatch_task_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;\n    t->box_id = box_id;\n    t->ctx    = ctx;\n    pool_spawn(ctx->pool, dispatch_action, t, priority);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_spawn_if_ready() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    if (box_id < 0 || box_id >= ctx->n_boxes) return;\n    if (!box_is_ready(ctx, box_id)) return;\n\n    /* CAS the per-box spawn guard. 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime — bundles every piece of phase 3 state */\ntypedef struct {\n    graph_t         *graph;\n    slot_store_t    *slots;\n    spec_registry_t *specs;\n    pool_t          *pool;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n} runtime_t;\n\nstatic int runtime_setup(runtime_t *rt, const char *map_dir,\n                         int n_workers, int capture_outputs)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    memset(rt, 0, sizeof *rt);\n\n    rt->graph = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!rt->graph) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    rt->pool = pool_create(n_workers);\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(rt->graph, rt->slots, rt->specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_attach_runtime: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&rt->ctx, rt->graph, rt->slots, rt->specs,\n                          rt->pool, capture_outputs, &err) != 0) {\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(rt->pool, spec_pool_init_cb, rt->specs);\n    if (pool_init_barrier(rt->pool) != 0) return -1;\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void runtime_teardown(runtime_t *rt)\n{\n    if (rt->pool) pool_destroy(rt->pool);\n    dispatch_ctx_destroy(&rt->ctx);\n    if (rt->specs) spec_registry_destroy(rt->specs);\n    if (rt->slots) slot_store_destroy(rt->slots);\n    if (rt->graph) graph_destroy(rt->graph);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_dispatch_skeleton_run() */\n/* The original skeleton test: a dispatch run that's only checking\n * the action plumbing. Now uses the proper setup so the dispatch\n * action's real logic is exercised (even though the hello fixture\n * needs file IO for the data box, which we don't push literals\n * for — the data box just reads names.txt). All read the same input slots\n     * (1-cell peek), all compute 17 + 25 = 42. */\n    enum { N = 8 };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, entry, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&rt.ctx.tasks_dispatched) == N);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry], \"42\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "originalFile":"/* tests/012-dispatch-test.c — skeleton tests for the dispatch\n * layer.\n *\n * Builds the full runtime context (graph + slot store + spec\n * registry + pool) and submits one task per box. \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_dispatch_one_per_box() */\nstatic int test_dispatch_one_per_box(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g);\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    ASSERT(s);\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    ASSERT(p);\n\n    dispatch_ctx_t ctx = {\n        .graph = g, .slots = s, .specs = r, .pool = p,\n    };\n    atomic_store(&ctx.tasks_dispatched, 0);\n\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    /* Submit one task per box. */\n    int n = graph_n_boxes(g);\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) dispatch_spawn(&ctx, i, 0);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&ctx.tasks_dispatched) == n);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_dispatch_burst() */\n/* Many tasks, varied priorities, all should run. */\nstatic int test_dispatch_burst(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g);\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n\n    dispatch_ctx_t ctx = {\n        .graph = g, .slots = s, .specs = r, .pool = p,\n    };\n    atomic_store(&ctx.tasks_dispatched, 0);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    enum { N = 200 };\n    for (int i = 0;           "content":"/* src/008-pool-runner.c — phase 3 runner entry point.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C binary that loads a map\n * directory, stands up the slot store + spec registry + thread\n * pool, runs the dispatch loop to quiescence, and prints what\n * each box produced.\n *\n * As of this iteration the runner actually runs maps end-to-end:\n *\n *   1. Load and validate the graph (305).\n *   2. Create the slot store (302) and spec registry (303).\n *   3.
