Attach runtime — allocate one slot per input port and\n *      resolve each call box's spec (305 phase 5+7).\n *   5. Initialize the dispatch context with output capture.\n *   6. pool_init_barrier — releases workers from their init\n *      stage into the task loop.\n *   7. Push literal input values to slots, then spawn every box\n *      that's ready (every input either literal or optional).\n *      Wired-input boxes spawn automatically when an upstream\n *      push triggers spawn-on-ready.\n *   8. pool_wait_quiescent.\n *   9. Print each box's captured output, tear down.\n *\n * The JSONL run log (issue 311) and the dispatch action's\n * iterator multi-spawn path (issue 304) are still ahead.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() */\n/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language\n * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g     = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int ctx_initialised = 0;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s)).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

          "content":"/* src/014-event-queue.h — multi-producer event queue with a\n * dedicated writer thread.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: every worker thread (and the main\n * thread) calls into one of the emit functions; the queue\n * appends a small event record under a brief mutex and signals\n * the writer thread, which drains the queue in batches and writes\n * each event as a JSONL line to a file.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311. Decouples event emission from the JSON\n * encoding + fwrite hot path: every producer's critical section\n * is one node allocation plus a couple of pointer updates. The\n * MPSC-ring-with-sequence-numbers variant from the design doc is\n * the next refinement once profiling justifies it.\n *\n * Lifecycle: `event_queue_create(\"tmp/last-run.jsonl\")` opens the\n * file, spawns the writer thread, and is ready to receive events.\n * `event_queue_destroy` signals shutdown, joins the writer thread,\n * closes the file, and frees the queue. Any events still in the\n * queue at shutdown drain to the file before the thread exits.\n *\n * The emit functions are non-blocking from the producer's\n * perspective (modulo brief mutex contention). They never write to\n * the file directly.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n#define SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct event_queue event_queue_t;\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Open `path` for writing (truncates), spawn the writer thread.\n * Returns NULL on failure. */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path);\n\n/* Signal shutdown, drain remaining events, join the writer thread,\n * fflush+fclose, free the queue. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid           event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit (producer side) */\n/* Every emit clones its arguments into the queued event record;\n * the caller's pointers don't need to outlive the call. Strings\n * are bounded by event-record buffers (typically 64–128 bytes);\n * longer values are truncated. */\n\nvoid event_queue_run_start  (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             const char *map, int n_workers);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_submit(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_start (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, int worker_idx);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_end   (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                             long duration_us, int output_size);\n\nvoid event_queue_run_end    (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             long duration_us, int n_tasks);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Inspection */\n/* Best-effort: returns the count of events currently queued\n * (between produce and drain). Mostly useful for diagnostics. */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H */\n",

Decouples event emission from the JSON\n * encoding + fwrite hot path: every producer's critical section\n * is one node allocation plus a couple of pointer updates. The\n * MPSC-ring-with-sequence-numbers variant from the design doc is\n * the next refinement once profiling justifies it.\n *\n * Lifecycle: `event_queue_create(\"tmp/last-run.jsonl\")` opens the\n * file, spawns the writer thread, and is ready to receive events.\n * `event_queue_destroy` signals shutdown, joins the writer thread,\n * closes the file, and frees the queue. Any events still in the\n * queue at shutdown drain to the file before the thread exits.\n *\n * The emit functions are non-blocking from the producer's\n * perspective (modulo brief mutex contention). They never write to\n * the file directly.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n#define SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct event_queue event_queue_t;\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Open `path` for writing (truncates), spawn the writer thread.\n * Returns NULL on failure. */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path);\n\n/* Signal shutdown, drain remaining events, join the writer thread,\n * fflush+fclose, free the queue. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid           event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit (producer side) */\n/* Every emit clones its arguments into the queued event record;\n * the caller's pointers don't need to outlive the call. Strings\n * are bounded by event-record buffers (typically 64–128 bytes);\n * longer values are truncated. */\n\nvoid event_queue_run_start  (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             const char *map, int n_workers);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_submit(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_start (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, int worker_idx);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_end   (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                             long duration_us, int output_size);\n\nvoid event_queue_run_end    (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             long duration_us, int n_tasks);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Inspection */\n/* Best-effort: returns the count of events currently queued\n * (between produce and drain). Mostly useful for diagnostics. */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H */\n",

Multi-producer, single-consumer.\nProducers (worker threads, main thread) call emit functions that\nappend small event records under a brief mutex; a dedicated\nwriter thread drains in batches and writes JSONL through the\nissue-311 emit helpers.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `event_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path)` — open\n  the file, spawn the writer thread, return ready-to-use.\n- `void event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q)` — signal shutdown,\n  drain remaining events, join the writer thread, close the file,\n  free. Safe on NULL.\n\n## Emit\n\n- `event_queue_run_start  (q, ts, map, n_workers)`\n- `event_queue_task_submit(q, ts, task_id, box_id, worker_idx)`\n- `event_queue_task_start (q, ts, task_id, worker_idx)`\n- `event_queue_task_end   (q, ts, task_id, worker_idx, duration_us, output_size)`\n- `event_queue_run_end    (q, ts, duration_us, n_tasks)`\n\nProducer side is non-blocking (modulo brief append-mutex\ncontention). String arguments are clone-copied into a bounded\nbuffer inside the event record (128 bytes for `map`, 64 for\n`box_id`); callers' pointers don't need to outlive the call.\n\n## Diagnostics\n\n- `int event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q)` — best-effort\n  count of events queued between produce and drain.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- **Vyukov-style lock-free MPSC ring**. The architecture doc's\n  preferred design. Current implementation uses a singly-linked\n  queue under one mutex; the writer thread snapshots `head` and\n  drains outside the lock, so encoding + fwrite happens with zero\n  producer contention. Producer's critical section is one node\n  alloc plus two pointer updates — minimal. Upgrade once\n  profiling justifies it.\n- **Verbosity gates** (`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`,\n  `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`). Slot-allocator and per-task value\n  events are opt-in per the issue; not exposed yet.\n- **Backpressure on a full ring**. The current linked-list queue\n  has no hard bound; a slow writer just grows the queue.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 311 — design.\n- Issue 313-jsonl-events — per-event serializers this thread calls.\n- Issue 314 — bounded JSON writer underneath.\n- Issue 304 — dispatch action emits task_start / task_end.\n- Issue 301 — pool runner emits run_start / run_end.\n",

          "content":"/* tests/014-event-queue-test.c — concurrent producer + dedicated\n * writer thread tests.\n *\n * Single-producer sanity, multi-thread burst, ordering check\n * (within a producer, events stay in submission order), shutdown\n * drain (events queued at shutdown still hit the file).\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ tmp_path() / slurp_file() */\nstatic void tmp_path(char *out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-evq-%d-XXXXXX\", (int)getpid());\n    int fd = mkstemp(out);\n    if (fd >= 0) close(fd);\n}\n\nstatic char *slurp_file(const char *path, size_t *out_len)\n{\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"r\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);\n    long sz = ftell(fp);\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    char *buf = malloc((size_t)sz + 1);\n    fread(buf, 1, (size_t)sz, fp);\n    buf[sz] = '\\0';\n    fclose(fp);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = (size_t)sz;\n    return buf;\n}\n\nstatic int count_lines(const char *body, size_t len)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) if (body[i] == '\\n') n++;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_single_producer() */\nstatic int test_single_producer(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    event_queue_run_start  (q, 1.0, \"calc\", 4);\n    event_queue_task_submit(q, 1.1, 0, \"add\", -1);\n    event_queue_task_start (q, 1.2, 0, 2);\n    event_queue_task_end   (q, 1.3, 0, 2, 127, 2);\n    event_queue_run_end    (q, 1.4, 1850, 1);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);   /* drain + join */\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 5);\n\n    /* Spot-check by parsing the first and last line. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *first_nl = strchr(body, '\\n');\n    *first_nl = '\\0';\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, body, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_start\") == 0);\n    *first_nl = '\\n';\n\n    /* Find the last line (skip trailing newline). */\n    char *p = body + len - 1;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p--;\n    while (p > body && *p != '\\n') p--;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p++;\n    n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_end\") == 0);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_burst() — many producers, one writer */\nstruct producer_args { event_queue_t *q; int n; int worker_idx; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(a->q, (double)i, i, a->worker_idx);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_burst(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 250 };\n    pthread_t threads[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args[N_PROD];\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) {\n        args[t].q = q; args[t].n = PER; args[t].worker_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, producer_thread, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    int lines = count_lines(body, len);\n    ASSERT(lines == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    /* Every line must be parsable JSON. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *p = body;\n    int ok = 0;\n    while (*p) {\n        char *nl = strchr(p, '\\n');\n        if (!nl) break;\n        *nl = '\\0';\n        json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n        ASSERT(n);\n        ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")),\n                      \"task_start\") == 0);\n        ok++;\n        p = nl + 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(ok == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_shutdown_drains_late_events() */\n/* Emit events right before destroy; they must end up in the file. */\nstatic int test_shutdown_drains_late_events(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* Emit a small burst without giving the writer time to drain\n     * before destroy. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(q, (double)i, i, 0);\n    }\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 50);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pending_count() */\nstatic int test_pending_count(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* pending is best-effort; the writer might drain between emit\n     * and our read. Just verify it's a small bounded value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) event_queue_task_start(q, 0.0, i, 0);\n    int pending = event_queue_pending(q);\n    ASSERT(pending >= 0);\n    ASSERT(pending <= 10);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n    ASSERT(event_queue_pending(NULL) == 0);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"014-event-queue-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(single_producer);\n    RUN(concurrent_burst);\n    RUN(shutdown_drains_late_events);\n    RUN(pending_count);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

        }

i < len; i++) if (body[i] == '\\n') n++;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_single_producer() */\nstatic int test_single_producer(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    event_queue_run_start  (q, 1.0, \"calc\", 4);\n    event_queue_task_submit(q, 1.1, 0, \"add\", -1);\n    event_queue_task_start (q, 1.2, 0, 2);\n    event_queue_task_end   (q, 1.3, 0, 2, 127, 2);\n    event_queue_run_end    (q, 1.4, 1850, 1);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);   /* drain + join */\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 5);\n\n    /* Spot-check by parsing the first and last line. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *first_nl = strchr(body, '\\n');\n    *first_nl = '\\0';\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, body, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_start\") == 0);\n    *first_nl = '\\n';\n\n    /* Find the last line (skip trailing newline). */\n    char *p = body + len - 1;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p--;\n    while (p > body && *p != '\\n') p--;\n    if (*p == '\\n') p++;\n    n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n    ASSERT(n);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")), \"run_end\") == 0);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_burst() — many producers, one writer */\nstruct producer_args { event_queue_t *q; int n; int worker_idx; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(a->q, (double)i, i, a->worker_idx);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_burst(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n    ASSERT(q);\n\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 250 };\n    pthread_t threads[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args[N_PROD];\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) {\n        args[t].q = q; args[t].n = PER; args[t].worker_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, producer_thread, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_PROD; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    int lines = count_lines(body, len);\n    ASSERT(lines == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    /* Every line must be parsable JSON. */\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    char *p = body;\n    int ok = 0;\n    while (*p) {\n        char *nl = strchr(p, '\\n');\n        if (!nl) break;\n        *nl = '\\0';\n        json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, p, NULL, NULL);\n        ASSERT(n);\n        ASSERT(strcmp(json_string_value(json_object_get(n, \"event\")),\n                      \"task_start\") == 0);\n        ok++;\n        p = nl + 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(ok == N_PROD * PER);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_shutdown_drains_late_events() */\n/* Emit events right before destroy; they must end up in the file. */\nstatic int test_shutdown_drains_late_events(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* Emit a small burst without giving the writer time to drain\n     * before destroy. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        event_queue_task_start(q, (double)i, i, 0);\n    }\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n\n    size_t len = 0;\n    char *body = slurp_file(path, &len);\n    ASSERT(body);\n    ASSERT(count_lines(body, len) == 50);\n    free(body);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pending_count() */\nstatic int test_pending_count(void)\n{\n    char path[256]; tmp_path(path, sizeof path);\n    event_queue_t *q = event_queue_create(path);\n\n    /* pending is best-effort; the writer might drain between emit\n     * and our read. Just verify it's a small bounded value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) event_queue_task_start(q, 0.0, i, 0);\n    int pending = event_queue_pending(q);\n    ASSERT(pending >= 0);\n    ASSERT(pending <= 10);\n\n    event_queue_destroy(q);\n    ASSERT(event_queue_pending(NULL) == 0);\n    unlink(path);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"014-event-queue-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(single_producer);\n    RUN(concurrent_burst);\n    RUN(shutdown_drains_late_events);\n    RUN(pending_count);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/012-dispatch-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/012-dispatch.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/013-jsonl-events-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:      $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:        $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action.     "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

    "newString":"/* {{{ now_secs() / mono_us() — timestamps */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n\nstatic long mono_us(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);\n    return (long)ts.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts.tv_nsec / 1000;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int task_id = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->next_task_id, 1,\n                                            memory_order_relaxed);\n    int worker_idx = pool_current_worker ? pool_current_worker->thread_idx : -1;\n\n    long start_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events)\n        event_queue_task_start(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx);\n\n    int out_size = 0;\n    int out_capacity = ctx->default_out_capacity > 0\n                        ? ctx->default_out_capacity : 4096;\n    char *out_buf = malloc((size_t)out_capacity);\n    int rc = -1;\n    if (out_buf && b) {\n        switch (b->kind) {\n            case BOX_CALL:\n                rc = do_call_box(ctx, b, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;\n            case BOX_DATA:\n                rc = do_data_box(ctx, b, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;\n            case BOX_FILE_WRITE:\n                rc = do_file_write_box(ctx, b, &out_size);\n                break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (rc == 0 && b) {\n        capture(ctx, t->box_id, out_buf, out_size);\n        /* file_write boxes don't push (they're sinks). */\n        if (b->kind != BOX_FILE_WRITE) {\n            push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_buf, out_size);\n        }\n    } else if (b) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: box '%s' failed (rc=%d)\\n\", b->id, rc);\n    }\n\n    long end_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events) {\n        event_queue_task_end(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx,\n                             end_us - start_us, out_size);\n    }\n\n    free(out_buf);\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */"

pool_current_worker->thread_idx : -1;\n\n    long start_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events)\n        event_queue_task_start(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx);\n\n    int out_size = 0;\n    int out_capacity = ctx->default_out_capacity > 0\n                        ?           "new_string":"/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ now_secs() */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ open_event_queue() — try map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl */\n/* Returns NULL silently if the path can't be opened (e.g. tmp\n * symlink missing). The runner still works, just without a JSONL\n * log. */\nstatic event_queue_t *open_event_queue(const char *map_dir, char *path_out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(path_out, cap, \"%s/tmp/last-run.jsonl\", map_dir);\n    /* Ensure the parent dir exists. */\n    struct stat st;\n    char tmpdir[4096];\n    snprintf(tmpdir, sizeof tmpdir, \"%s/tmp\", map_dir);\n    if (stat(tmpdir, &st) != 0) {\n        /* No tmp/ dir; fall back to a system path. */\n        const char *base = graph_map_dir(NULL); (void)base;   /* silence unused */\n        snprintf(path_out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\");\n    }\n    return event_queue_create(path_out);\n}\n/* }}} */",

The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() */\n/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language\n * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g     = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int ctx_initialised = 0;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s)).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test:  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                  $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n     "originalFile":"/* langs/c/spec.c — C language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a small dlopen cache. `compile` runs gcc\n * to turn a box source file into a .so; `invoke` dlopens the .so\n * (caching the handle), dlsyms the named function, and calls it\n * through a fixed signature.\n *\n * Designed in issue 307. C box functions follow a single\n * convention that matches the spec's `invoke` shape minus the\n * per-worker handle:\n *\n *     int box_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n *                void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n *\n * Return 0 on success, nonzero (fatal) on failure. This iteration\n * does not generate per-box wrappers from declared signatures\n * (issue 307's optional advanced mode) — every C box uses the\n * fixed signature above. Wrapper generation can land as a follow-on\n * once we have a box whose declared types diverge from the byte-\n * array shape.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define C_CACHE_SIZE 32\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker dlopen cache */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *path;     /* strdup'd; identifies the cache entry         */\n    void *dl;       /* dlopen handle                                */\n} c_cache_entry_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    c_cache_entry_t entries[C_CACHE_SIZE];\n    int             count;\n} c_handle_t;\n\ntypedef int (*c_box_fn_t)(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n                          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_init() */\nstatic void *c_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    c_handle_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_teardown() */\nstatic void c_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (h->entries[i].dl) dlclose(h->entries[i].dl);\n        free(h->entries[i].path);\n    }\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ends_in_dot_c() */\nstatic int ends_in_dot_c(const char *p)\n{\n    size_t n = strlen(p);\n    return n >= 2 && p[n - 2] == '.' && p[n - 1] == 'c';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ hash_path() — small DJB2-like hash for deriving cache filenames */\nstatic unsigned long hash_path(const char *p)\n{\n    unsigned long h = 5381;\n    for (; *p; p++) h = h * 33u + (unsigned char)*p;\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ maybe_lazy_compile() — if file_path is a .c source, compile it\n * to a /tmp .so and return that path; otherwise return file_path\n * unchanged. The output buffer is the caller-supplied so_buf. */\nstatic const char *maybe_lazy_compile(const char *file_path,\n                                      char *so_buf, size_t so_cap)\n{\n    if (!ends_in_dot_c(file_path)) return file_path;\n    /* Hash the source path so repeat opens of the same source file\n     * pick up the same .so. Concurrent invokes will race on gcc but\n     * the inputs are identical, so the output converges. */\n    unsigned long h = hash_path(file_path);\n    int n = snprintf(so_buf, so_cap, \"/tmp/soramech-c-%lx.so\", h);\n    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= so_cap) return NULL;\n    if (c_compile(file_path, so_buf) != 0) return NULL;\n    return so_buf;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ get_or_load() — find a cached .so or dlopen and add */\nstatic void *get_or_load(c_handle_t *h, const char *path)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(h->entries[i].path, path) == 0) return h->entries[i].dl;\n    }\n    if (h->count >= C_CACHE_SIZE) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen cache full (%d entries)\\n\", C_CACHE_SIZE);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    void *dl = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!dl) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen('%s'): %s\\n\", path, dlerror());\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    h->entries[h->count].path = strdup(path);\n    h->entries[h->count].dl   = dl;\n    h->count++;\n    return dl;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_invoke() */\nstatic int c_invoke(void *handle,\n                    const char  *file_path,    /* path to a .so */\n                    const char  *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data,\n                    const int   *input_sizes,\n                    int          n_inputs,\n                    void        *out_buf,\n                    int          out_capacity,\n                    int         *out_size)\n{\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    if (!h || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    void *dl = get_or_load(h, file_path);\n    if (!dl) return -1;\n\n    /* dlsym returns void*, but the cast to a function pointer is\n     * formally implementation-defined;     "originalFile":"/* langs/c/spec.c — C language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a small dlopen cache. `compile` runs gcc\n * to turn a box source file into a .so; `invoke` dlopens the .so\n * (caching the handle), dlsyms the named function, and calls it\n * through a fixed signature.\n *\n * Designed in issue 307. C box functions follow a single\n * convention that matches the spec's `invoke` shape minus the\n * per-worker handle:\n *\n *     int box_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n *                void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n *\n * Return 0 on success, nonzero (fatal) on failure. This iteration\n * does not generate per-box wrappers from declared signatures\n * (issue 307's optional advanced mode) — every C box uses the\n * fixed signature above. Wrapper generation can land as a follow-on\n * once we have a box whose declared types diverge from the byte-\n * array shape.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define C_CACHE_SIZE 32\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker dlopen cache */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *path;     /* strdup'd; identifies the cache entry         */\n    void *dl;       /* dlopen handle                                */\n} c_cache_entry_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    c_cache_entry_t entries[C_CACHE_SIZE];\n    int             count;\n} c_handle_t;\n\ntypedef int (*c_box_fn_t)(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n                          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_init() */\nstatic void *c_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    c_handle_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_teardown() */\nstatic void c_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (h->entries[i].dl) dlclose(h->entries[i].dl);\n        free(h->entries[i].path);\n    }\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ get_or_load() — find a cached .so or dlopen and add */\nstatic void *get_or_load(c_handle_t *h, const char *path)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(h->entries[i].path, path) == 0) return h->entries[i].dl;\n    }\n    if (h->count >= C_CACHE_SIZE) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen cache full (%d entries)\\n\", C_CACHE_SIZE);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    void *dl = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!dl) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen('%s'): %s\\n\", path, dlerror());\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    h->entries[h->count].path = strdup(path);\n    h->entries[h->count].dl   = dl;\n    h->count++;\n    return dl;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_invoke() */\nstatic int c_invoke(void *handle,\n                    const char  *file_path,    /* path to a .so */\n                    const char  *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data,\n                    const int   *input_sizes,\n                    int          n_inputs,\n                    void        *out_buf,\n                    int          out_capacity,\n                    int         *out_size)\n{\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    if (!h || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    void *dl = get_or_load(h, file_path);\n    if (!dl) return -1;\n\n    /* dlsym returns void*, but the cast to a function pointer is\n     * formally implementation-defined;           "old_string":"- Spawn-on-input-ready chaining: each push to a consumer slot\n  triggers a check, which may spawn the consumer's next task.",
          "new_string":"- Spawn-on-input-ready chaining: each push to a consumer slot\n  triggers a check, which may spawn the consumer's next task.\n\n### Plain-call dispatch + spawn-on-ready — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/012-dispatch.c` now has a real action body. For each task:\n1. Look up the box from the graph.\n2. Read every input port via `slot_peek` into a heap buffer.\n3. Dispatch on `box->kind`:\n   - **BOX_CALL** — resolve the per-worker spec handle via\n     `pool_current_worker->handles[box->spec_idx]`, call\n     `spec->invoke(handle, ref_path, fn_name, inputs, sizes,\n     n_present, out_buf, out_cap, &out_size)`.\n   - **BOX_DATA** — open `map_dir/box->path`, read up to\n     `out_capacity` bytes into the output buffer.\n   - **BOX_FILE_WRITE** — read inputs \"path\" and \"text\",\n     `fwrite` text to the resolved path.\n4. Capture the output for inspection (optional), push to every\n   outgoing connection's input slot, and fire\n   `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` on each consumer.\n5. Emit `task_start` / `task_end` events through the optional\n   event queue (issue 311) with monotonic-clock durations.\n\nThree end-to-end fixture maps cover the major paths:\n\n- `tests/maps/calc/` — single Lua call box with two literal\n  inputs. `add(17, 25) = \"42\"`.\n- `tests/maps/hello/` — two-box data → Lua pipeline.\n  `who → \"World\"` → `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`.\n- `tests/maps/pipeline/` — five-box multilang chain.\n  `data \"5\" → Lua double \"10\" → C addone \"11\" →\n  Bash shout \"11!\" → file_write` writes `11!` to disk.\n\nFour dispatch tests in `tests/012-dispatch-test.c` exercise the\ncalc fixture (with and without literals), a counter-burst\nverifying many concurrent tasks against the same box, and the\nskeleton dispatch path.\n\nStill ahead inside 304:\n- **Iterator multi-spawn.** Each iterator task should re-spawn\n  itself when its input queue still has values; that needs the\n  N-cell pop-mode slot shape from 302 and a different\n  `box_ever_spawned` rule.\n- **Routing kinds beyond plain.** Comparator routes by output\n  value; iterator/randomizer/weighted/distributor route by the\n  atomic counter or downstream fill. The hooks in `box->routing`\n  are populated by 305; only the dispatch branch picker is\n  missing.\n- **Variable-size payloads via the large-value heap** (issue 302).",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md"
        }
      }],

The mutex queue is a","+  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.","+- Opt-in slot events and per-task input/output dumps.","+- The integration-test harness with fixture maps and a runner","+  script that diffs normalized JSONL output against expected."],
        "oldStart":306

    "newString":"(`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`), inputs/outputs opt-in\n(`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`), the MPSC ring + writer thread, and\nthe integration-test harness map fixtures.\n\n### Multi-producer event queue + writer thread — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/014-event-queue.{c,h}` ships the producer-side queue and the\ndedicated writer thread. Producers (worker threads + the main\nthread) call `event_queue_run_start` / `task_submit` / `task_start`\n/ `task_end` / `run_end`; each emit appends a small fixed-size\nevent record under a brief mutex and signals a CV. The writer\nthread sleeps on the CV, snapshots the queue head into a local\nbatch under the lock, then drains the batch outside the lock —\nJSON encoding + fwrite happen with zero producer contention.\n\nFour unit tests in `tests/014-event-queue-test.c` cover single\nproducer / multi-thread burst (8 producers × 250 events each =\n2000 lines, all round-trip through the JSON parser) / shutdown-\ndrain / pending-count.\n\nThe dispatch action (issue 304) opt-in emits task_start and\ntask_end events with monotonic-clock durations via the queue;\nthe pool runner emits run_start and run_end. `soramech-pool`\nwrites to `map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl` when that directory\nexists, falling back to `/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl`.\n\nWhat's still ahead inside 311:\n- Lock-free Vyukov MPSC ring with sequence numbers — the\n  architecture doc's preferred design. The mutex queue is a\n  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.\n- Opt-in slot events and per-task input/output dumps.\n- The integration-test harness with fixture maps and a runner\n  script that diffs normalized JSONL output against expected."
  },

    "newString":"        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */\n        b->spec_idx = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && specs) {\n            b->spec_idx = resolve_spec_for_box(b, (spec_registry_t *)specs);\n            if (b->spec_idx < 0) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': no spec found for \"\n                                        \"lang='%s' / ref='%s'\",\n                                        b->id, b->lang ? b->lang : \"(null)\",\n                                        b->ref ? b->ref : \"(null)\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n         * concurrent-safe semantics. Randomizer and weighted\n         * routing kinds also rely on this slot once they land. */\n        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) {\n            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}"

        "lines":["      * defaults (-1 / NULL) by graph_load alone. */","     int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */","     int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */","+    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */"," } box_t;"," /* }}} */"," "],
        "oldStart":124
      }],
    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* For routing kinds that need them later — weights, thresholds —\n     * the parser leaves their fields zero in this iteration and adds\n     * them when those kinds are implemented. */\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics;         },
        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (c->to_box_idx < 0) continue;\n        const box_t *dst = graph_box(ctx->graph, c->to_box_idx);\n        if (!dst || !dst->input_slot_ids) continue;\n        if (c->to_input_idx < 0 || c->to_input_idx >= dst->n_inputs) continue;\n        if (slot_push(ctx->slots, dst->input_slot_ids[c->to_input_idx],\n                      out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' → '%s'.%s: push failed\\n\",\n                    b->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(ctx, c->to_box_idx, 0);\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ push_one_connection() — push to a single connection's slot */\nstatic int push_one_connection(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                               const connection_t *c,\n                               const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    if (c->to_box_idx < 0) return 0;\n    const box_t *dst = graph_box(ctx->graph, c->to_box_idx);\n    if (!dst || !dst->input_slot_ids) return 0;\n    if (c->to_input_idx < 0 || c->to_input_idx >= dst->n_inputs) return 0;\n    if (slot_push(ctx->slots, dst->input_slot_ids[c->to_input_idx],\n                  out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' → '%s'.%s: push failed\\n\",\n                b->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(ctx, c->to_box_idx, 0);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_branch() — push only to outgoing connections matching `branch` */\n/* `branch` is one of \"lt\" / \"eq\" / \"gt\" / \"out_<n>\". Connections\n * whose from_branch is NULL (plain) are skipped; connections whose\n * from_branch equals `branch` fire. */\nstatic int push_branch(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const char *branch,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    int fired = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (!c->from_branch) continue;\n        if (strcmp(c->from_branch, branch) != 0) continue;\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, c, out_bytes, out_size) != 0) return -1;\n        fired++;\n    }\n    return fired;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, &b->connections[i],\n                                out_bytes, out_size) != 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_double() — parse a NUL-bounded byte run as a double */\nstatic double parse_double(const void *bytes, int size)\n{\n    char tmp[64];\n    int n = size < 63 ? size : 63;\n    if (n > 0) memcpy(tmp, bytes, (size_t)n);\n    tmp[n] = '\\0';\n    return strtod(tmp, NULL);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_routed() — branch picker over routing.kind, then push */\nstatic int push_routed(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    /* Data and file_write boxes don't carry a routing kind; their\n     * output fans plain. Same for call boxes with no routing set\n     * (treated as plain). */\n    if (b->kind != BOX_CALL) return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n    switch (b->routing.kind) {\n        case ROUTING_PLAIN:\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            const char *branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER:\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED:\n        case ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR:\n        default:\n            /* Not yet implemented in the dispatch layer; fall back\n             * to plain so the runtime doesn't deadlock. */\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/012-dispatch.c"
        }

{
  "userType":"external",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-14T00:50:09.438Z",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",

  "parentUuid":"944b1ded-6132-4eb6-8123-e15a6d9ab1dc",
