  "sessionId":"585b6e65-7287-44e7-b133-8bdf3479a266",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "type":"assistant",
  "uuid":"11fe26d5-cada-4e6b-9ff1-1612152f0eab",
  "requestId":"req_011Cb1bNRTwfk3UgZqZRgceK",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "id":"toolu_01NL7v8kqg9k7EATkRmZtRkW",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_comparator_routing() */\n/* The comparator fixture's classify box returns its literal input\n * unchanged. With v=\"8\" and comparand=5, dispatch should route\n * along the \"gt\" branch — only high fires, low and mid don't. */\nstatic int test_comparator_routing(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/comparator\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int classify = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"classify\");\n    int low      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"low\");\n    int mid      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"mid\");\n    int high     = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"high\");\n    ASSERT(classify >= 0 && low >= 0 && mid >= 0 && high >= 0);\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, classify, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* classify ran; only the \"gt\" branch (high) ran behind it. */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify], \"8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high], \"HIGH:8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[low] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[mid] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_single_fire() */\n/* First invocation of an iterator with counter=0 picks branch\n * out_0. Subsequent firings would advance to out_1 / out_2, but\n * this iteration's dispatch doesn't multi-spawn. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_single_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* counter=0 → out_0 → a. */\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[iter], \"hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_round_robin() */\n/* Manually spawn the iterator three times (bypassing the single-\n * spawn guard via dispatch_spawn). Each spawn picks the next\n * branch via the atomic counter; a/b/c all fire across the three\n * invocations. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_round_robin(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    /* Three direct spawns; counter advances 0 → 1 → 2 → 0. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* a/b/c all captured an output. The \"v\" inputs are 1-cell peek,\n     * so the most-recent capture survives — that's \"A:hi\", \"B:hi\",\n     * \"C:hi\". */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b], \"B:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c], \"C:hi\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_round_robin);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

    "originalFile":"/* tests/012-dispatch-test.c — dispatch layer tests, including\n * the first end-to-end run of a real map through the runtime.\n *\n * Setup that every test shares: graph_load → slot_store_create →\n * spec_registry_load → pool_create → pool_set_worker_init →\n * graph_attach_runtime → dispatch_ctx_init → pool_init_barrier.\n * The teardown is the reverse.\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() — wire spec registry into pool worker init */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime — bundles every piece of phase 3 state */\ntypedef struct {\n    graph_t         *graph;\n    slot_store_t    *slots;\n    spec_registry_t *specs;\n    pool_t          *pool;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n} runtime_t;\n\nstatic int runtime_setup(runtime_t *rt, const char *map_dir,\n                         int n_workers, int capture_outputs)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    memset(rt, 0, sizeof *rt);\n\n    rt->graph = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!rt->graph) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    rt->slots = slot_store_create();\n    rt->specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!rt->specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    rt->pool = pool_create(n_workers);\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(rt->graph, rt->slots, rt->specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_attach_runtime: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&rt->ctx, rt->graph, rt->slots, rt->specs,\n                          rt->pool, capture_outputs, &err) != 0) {\n        free(err); return -1;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(rt->pool, spec_pool_init_cb, rt->specs);\n    if (pool_init_barrier(rt->pool) != 0) return -1;\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void runtime_teardown(runtime_t *rt)\n{\n    if (rt->pool) pool_destroy(rt->pool);\n    dispatch_ctx_destroy(&rt->ctx);\n    if (rt->specs) spec_registry_destroy(rt->specs);\n    if (rt->slots) slot_store_destroy(rt->slots);\n    if (rt->graph) graph_destroy(rt->graph);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_dispatch_skeleton_run() */\n/* The original skeleton test: a dispatch run that's only checking\n * the action plumbing. Now uses the proper setup so the dispatch\n * action's real logic is exercised (even though the hello fixture\n * needs file IO for the data box, which we don't push literals\n * for — the data box just reads names.txt). We expect at least\n * the data box dispatch to run. */\nstatic int test_dispatch_skeleton_run(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    /* hello has a data box that reads names.txt. We don't ship\n     * that file in the fixture, so the data box will fail to\n     * read it. That's expected — we only want to verify the\n     * dispatch ran (counter incremented). */\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/hello\", 2, 0) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n\n    /* Spawn the data box manually (no inputs, would be entry). */\n    int who = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"who\");\n    ASSERT(who >= 0);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, who, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&rt.ctx.tasks_dispatched) >= 1);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_end_to_end_calc() — the headline test */\n/* Load the calc fixture (one Lua call box with two literal inputs),\n * push literals, spawn the entry box, wait for quiescence, verify\n * the captured output is \"42\" (17 + 25). */\nstatic int test_end_to_end_calc(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/calc\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    /* The entry box should now have all its inputs ready. */\n    int entry = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"add\");\n    ASSERT(entry >= 0);\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, entry, 0);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&rt.ctx.tasks_dispatched) == 1);\n\n    /* Captured output for the add box must be \"42\". */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry], \"42\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_calc_mul() — same fixture, different function */\n/* Re-load the calc map, override one input via direct slot_push,\n * and call M.mul instead of M.add to exercise re-use. We just\n * load the calc map, but build a different result by writing\n * different literal values manually (skipping push_literals). */\nstatic int test_calc_mul(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/calc\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n\n    /* Push our own literal values: 6 and 7, expecting 42. */\n    int entry = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"add\");\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(rt.graph, entry);\n    ASSERT(b);\n    ASSERT(b->n_inputs == 2);\n\n    const char *six = \"6\", *seven = \"7\";\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, b->input_slot_ids[0], six,   1, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, b->input_slot_ids[1], seven, 1, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* The function name is fixed in the box JSON (\"add\"); we just\n     * verify add(6, 7) = \"13\". */\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, entry, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry], \"13\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_dispatch_counter_burst() */\nstatic int test_dispatch_counter_burst(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/calc\", 4, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    int entry = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"add\");\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    /* Force-spawn 8 add-box tasks (bypass the single-spawn guard\n     * via dispatch_spawn). All read the same input slots\n     * (1-cell peek), all compute 17 + 25 = 42. */\n    enum { N = 8 };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, entry, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&rt.ctx.tasks_dispatched) == N);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[entry], \"42\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

With v=\"8\" and comparand=5, dispatch should route\n * along the \"gt\" branch — only high fires, low and mid don't. */\nstatic int test_comparator_routing(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/comparator\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int classify = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"classify\");\n    int low      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"low\");\n    int mid      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"mid\");\n    int high     = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"high\");\n    ASSERT(classify >= 0 && low >= 0 && mid >= 0 && high >= 0);\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, classify, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* classify ran; only the \"gt\" branch (high) ran behind it. */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify], \"8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high], \"HIGH:8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[low] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[mid] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_single_fire() */\n/* First invocation of an iterator with counter=0 picks branch\n * out_0. Subsequent firings would advance to out_1 / out_2, but\n * this iteration's dispatch doesn't multi-spawn. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_single_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* counter=0 → out_0 → a. */\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[iter], \"hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_round_robin() */\n/* Manually spawn the iterator three times (bypassing the single-\n * spawn guard via dispatch_spawn). Each spawn picks the next\n * branch via the atomic counter; a/b/c all fire across the three\n * invocations. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_round_robin(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    /* Three direct spawns; counter advances 0 → 1 → 2 → 0. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* a/b/c all captured an output. The \"v\" inputs are 1-cell peek,\n     * so the most-recent capture survives — that's \"A:hi\", \"B:hi\",\n     * \"C:hi\". */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b], \"B:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c], \"C:hi\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_round_robin);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/012-dispatch-test.c"
  },

          "new_string":"/* Registry key for the per-worker file → module-table cache. The\n * key is a string in the Lua registry; the value is a Lua table\n * keyed by file path.     "originalFile":"/* langs/lua/spec.c — Lua language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a `lua_State` with the standard libraries\n * opened. Invocation convention: the box's source file is expected\n * to return a Lua table (`return M` at the bottom), and the\n * fn_name is a key into that table. Inputs arrive as byte arrays;\n * each one is pushed as a Lua string. The function's single return\n * value is converted to a string (via tostring semantics) and\n * memcpy'd into the caller's output buffer.\n *\n * Designed in issue 306. Implementation choices that matter:\n *\n *  - One lua_State per worker thread. lua_State is not\n *    thread-safe, but per-thread requires no locking.\n *  - The state's stack is rewound to its baseline depth at every\n *    invoke entry/exit so cross-call leaks don't accumulate.\n *  - File caching (luaL_loadfile once, replayed via lua_call) is\n *    deferred — this iteration loads the chunk on every invoke.\n *    Lands as a follow-on once profiling justifies it.\n *  - The chunk's side effects run on every invoke too (since\n *    we re-load and re-execute).     "originalFile":"/* langs/lua/spec.c — Lua language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a `lua_State` with the standard libraries\n * opened.     "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",
    "userModified":false,

The\n  architecture doc lists this as cached via the registry; the\n  cache lands when call rate justifies it.\n- **Rich return types.** The current invoke serializes the return\n  with `lua_tolstring`, which handles strings/numbers/booleans/\n  nil via tostring semantics. Tables, closures, and other\n  structured values land with the fast-path work in issue 312.",
    "structuredPatch":[{
        "oldLines":10,

        "lines":[" the pool runner will consume."," "," Deferred:","-- **File caching.** `luaL_loadfile` runs on every invoke. The","-  architecture doc lists this as cached via the registry; the","-  cache lands when call rate justifies it."," - **Rich return types.** The current invoke serializes the return","   with `lua_tolstring`, which handles strings/numbers/booleans/","   nil via tostring semantics. Tables, closures, and other","   structured values land with the fast-path work in issue 312.","+","+### Per-worker module cache — 2026-05-12","+","+`lua_init` now seeds an empty Lua table at","+`LUA_REGISTRYINDEX[LUA_CACHE_KEY]`. `lua_invoke` looks up the","+box's `file_path` in that table; on a hit it skips the","+`luaL_loadfile + lua_pcall` round-trip and uses the cached","+module table directly; on a miss it loads, runs the chunk,","+verifies the module table shape, and stashes the result in the","+cache before proceeding.","+","+The cache is per-worker (each worker has its own `lua_State`),","+which means no locking. It's also per-file-path string, so two","+boxes that share a source file share a module table on each","+worker — calling `M.greet` from one box doesn't reload the","+chunk when another box later calls `M.farewell` on the same","+file.","+","+Cache invalidation is intentionally absent for now: once a file","+is loaded, its module table sticks for the run. If the box","+source changes mid-run, the worker won't notice. Fine for the","+read-once-then-execute usage; revisit when there's a use case","+for hot-reload."],
        "oldStart":289
      }],
    "newString":"Deferred:\n- **Rich return types.** The current invoke serializes the return\n  with `lua_tolstring`, which handles strings/numbers/booleans/\n  nil via tostring semantics. Tables, closures, and other\n  structured values land with the fast-path work in issue 312.\n\n### Per-worker module cache — 2026-05-12\n\n`lua_init` now seeds an empty Lua table at\n`LUA_REGISTRYINDEX[LUA_CACHE_KEY]`. `lua_invoke` looks up the\nbox's `file_path` in that table; on a hit it skips the\n`luaL_loadfile + lua_pcall` round-trip and uses the cached\nmodule table directly; on a miss it loads, runs the chunk,\nverifies the module table shape, and stashes the result in the\ncache before proceeding.\n\nThe cache is per-worker (each worker has its own `lua_State`),\nwhich means no locking. It's also per-file-path string, so two\nboxes that share a source file share a module table on each\nworker — calling `M.greet` from one box doesn't reload the\nchunk when another box later calls `M.farewell` on the same\nfile.\n\nCache invalidation is intentionally absent for now: once a file\nis loaded, its module table sticks for the run. If the box\nsource changes mid-run, the worker won't notice. Fine for the\nread-once-then-execute usage; revisit when there's a use case\nfor hot-reload."
  },

The hooks in `box->routing`\n  are populated by 305; only the dispatch branch picker is\n  missing.\n- **Variable-size payloads via the large-value heap** (issue 302).\n\n### Comparator + iterator routing — 2026-05-12\n\n`push_routed(ctx, b, bytes, size)` now branches on\n`b->routing.kind`:\n- **PLAIN** — fan to every outgoing connection (existing behavior).\n- **COMPARATOR** — parse the output as a double via `strtod`,\n  compare against `b->routing.comparand`, push to the\n  matching `lt` / `eq` / `gt` connection only.\n- **ITERATOR** — `slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n  n_outputs)` picks the branch index, then push to the\n  `out_<idx>` connection only.\n- **RANDOMIZER / WEIGHTED / DISTRIBUTOR** — fall back to plain\n  for now; deferred to follow-ons.\n\nA new `push_branch(ctx, b, branch, bytes, size)` helper filters\nconnections by `from_branch` and pushes to each match (also\nfiring the spawn-on-input-ready check on each consumer).\n\nThe randomizer/weighted/distributor enum values stay reserved\nin the routing-kind table; the dispatch falls through to plain\nso nothing deadlocks.\n\nTwo fixture maps cover the two routing kinds end-to-end:\n\n- `tests/maps/comparator/` — `classify` (lua, comparator,\n  `comparand=5`) feeds three sinks `low`/`mid`/`high` via\n  `from_branch=\"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"`. With literal `v=\"8\"`, only the\n  `high` sink runs and captures `\"HIGH:8\"`.\n- `tests/maps/iter-route/` — `iter` (lua, iterator,\n  `n_outputs=3`) feeds three sinks `a`/`b`/`c` via\n  `from_branch=\"out_0\"/\"out_1\"/\"out_2\"`. First invocation\n  (counter=0) routes to `a`; manual `dispatch_spawn` calls then\n  walk through `b` and `c` as the counter advances.\n\nThree new tests in `tests/012-dispatch-test.c`: comparator\nrouting, single-fire iterator routing, and a 3-call round-robin\niterator covering all three branches.\n\n### Task-id correlation — 2026-05-12\n\n`dispatch_task_t` gained a `task_id` field assigned at\n`dispatch_spawn` time (atomic fetch-add on\n`ctx->next_task_id`). The same id correlates the\n`task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` events emitted\nthrough the event queue. `task_submit` lands on the spawning\nthread (worker_idx = -1 since the task hasn't been picked up\nyet); start/end land on the dispatching worker with its real\n`thread_idx`.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md"
        }
      }],

          "old_string":"Deferred:\n- **File caching.** `luaL_loadfile` runs on every invoke. The\n  architecture doc lists this as cached via the registry; the\n  cache lands when call rate justifies it.\n- **Rich return types.** The current invoke serializes the return\n  with `lua_tolstring`, which handles strings/numbers/booleans/\n  nil via tostring semantics. Tables, closures, and other\n  structured values land with the fast-path work in issue 312.",
          "new_string":"Deferred:\n- **Rich return types.** The current invoke serializes the return\n  with `lua_tolstring`, which handles strings/numbers/booleans/\n  nil via tostring semantics. Tables, closures, and other\n  structured values land with the fast-path work in issue 312.\n\n### Per-worker module cache — 2026-05-12\n\n`lua_init` now seeds an empty Lua table at\n`LUA_REGISTRYINDEX[LUA_CACHE_KEY]`. `lua_invoke` looks up the\nbox's `file_path` in that table; on a hit it skips the\n`luaL_loadfile + lua_pcall` round-trip and uses the cached\nmodule table directly; on a miss it loads, runs the chunk,\nverifies the module table shape, and stashes the result in the\ncache before proceeding.\n\nThe cache is per-worker (each worker has its own `lua_State`),\nwhich means no locking. It's also per-file-path string, so two\nboxes that share a source file share a module table on each\nworker — calling `M.greet` from one box doesn't reload the\nchunk when another box later calls `M.farewell` on the same\nfile.\n\nCache invalidation is intentionally absent for now: once a file\nis loaded, its module table sticks for the run. If the box\nsource changes mid-run, the worker won't notice. Fine for the\nread-once-then-execute usage; revisit when there's a use case\nfor hot-reload.",

Five fixture maps running end-to-end.**\n\n```\n009-slot-store-test       12\n010-graph-loader-test     11\n011-spec-registry-test     5\n012-dispatch-test          7   (was 4: +comparator, +iter single, +iter round-robin)\n013-jsonl-events-test      3\n014-event-queue-test       4\n301-pool-test             11\n303-pool-spec-init-test    2\n306-lua-spec-test          5\n307-c-spec-test            5\n308-bash-spec-test         5\n314-json-test             22\n```\n\n**Fixture maps:**\n\n| fixture | result | what it exercises |\n|--|--|--|\n| `calc` | `add → 42` | single Lua call with literal inputs |\n| `hello` | `greet → Hello, World!` | data → Lua pipeline |\n| `comparator` | `high → HIGH:8` | comparator routes 8 > 5 to `gt` branch only |\n| `iter-route` | `a → A:hi` | iterator picks `out_0` (counter=0) |\n| `pipeline` | file `11!` | data → Lua → C → Bash → file_write |\n\n**Progress now:**\n\n| Issue | Status |\n|-------|--------|\n| 301 | in progress · pool skeleton done |\n| 302 | in progress · core complete |\n| 303 | in progress · registry + per-worker init + pool hook done |\n| 304 | in progress · plain + comparator + iterator routing, multilang end-to-end |\n| 305 | in progress · parse + schema + topology + cycles + slot/spec attach + counter slots |\n| 306 | in progress · init + invoke + teardown + per-worker module cache done |\n| 307 | in progress · compile + invoke + lazy .c→.so done, typed wrapper deferred |\n| 308 | in progress · fork+exec invoke done, persistent socket deferred |\n| 309 | in progress · scaffolding done |\n| 310 | in progress · API + ordering done |\n| 311 | in progress · writer + emitters + MPSC queue + writer thread + task_id correlation |\n| 314 | in progress · parser + writer complete |\n\n**Highlights:**\n- **304 routing kinds** — `push_routed` branches on `routing.kind`. Comparator parses output as a double and picks `lt`/`eq`/`gt`; iterator reads `slot_read_inc` on its counter slot and picks `out_<idx>`. Three new fixture-driven dispatch tests verify each path including a 3-call round-robin that walks the iterator counter through all branches.\n- **305 atomic counter slots** — `graph_attach_runtime` allocates a `SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot for each iterator-routing box and stores its id on `box->counter_slot_id`.\n- **306 Lua module cache** — per-worker `LUA_REGISTRYINDEX[LUA_CACHE_KEY]` holds module tables keyed by file path. Subsequent invokes skip `luaL_loadfile + lua_pcall` entirely. Per-worker means no locking.\n- **311 task_id correlation** — `task_id` assigned at `dispatch_spawn` time and threaded through `task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` so the JSONL log can correlate them. The submit event has worker_idx=-1 (not yet picked up); start/end have the dispatching worker's index.\n\nWant another round?"
      }],

    "newString":"/* {{{ propagate_multi_spawn() — BFS forward from iterators */\n/* A box is \"multi_spawn\" if it's an iterator OR if any producer\n * feeding one of its inputs is itself multi_spawn. The marker\n * propagates forward through the connection graph. */\n#define MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS 16\n\nstatic void propagate_multi_spawn(graph_t *g)\n{\n    /* Seed: every iterator-routing call box is multi_spawn. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->multi_spawn = (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n                          b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    /* Fixed-point: as long as any new box gets marked, iterate. The\n     * graph is small (≤ a few hundred boxes in practice), so the\n     * O(n × edges) bound is fine. */\n    int changed = 1;\n    while (changed) {\n        changed = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n            if (!b->multi_spawn) continue;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n                int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n                if (dst < 0) continue;\n                if (!g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn) {\n                    g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn = 1;\n                    changed = 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_attach_runtime() — phase 5 + 7 */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int default_cell_bytes,\n                         char **err)\n{\n    if (!g || !slots) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_attach_runtime: NULL graph or slots\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (default_cell_bytes <= 0) default_cell_bytes = 4096;\n\n    /* Mark multi-spawn boxes via forward BFS from iterators so we\n     * can pick the right slot mode for each input port below. */\n    propagate_multi_spawn(g);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n\n        /* Allocate slots per input port. Multi-spawn boxes get\n         * N-cell pop rings so producers' multiple pushes accumulate\n         * and each task drains one cell. Single-spawn boxes get\n         * 1-cell peek slots (the legacy fast path). */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory allocating input slots\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS : 1;\n            int mode    = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_MODE_POP : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n                slot_id_t id = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots,\n                                          default_cell_bytes, n_cells, 0);\n                if (id == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                    if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': failed to allocate \"\n                                            \"slot for input '%s'\",\n                                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                b->input_slot_ids[j]   = (int)id;\n                b->input_slot_modes[j] = mode;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */\n        b->spec_idx = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && specs) {\n            b->spec_idx = resolve_spec_for_box(b, (spec_registry_t *)specs);\n            if (b->spec_idx < 0) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': no spec found for \"\n                                        \"lang='%s' / ref='%s'\",\n                                        b->id, b->lang ? b->lang : \"(null)\",\n                                        b->ref ? b->ref : \"(null)\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n         * concurrent-safe semantics. */\n        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) {\n            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */"

    "newString":"/* {{{ box_is_ready() — every required input has a value */\nstatic int box_is_ready(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id)\n{\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, box_id);\n    if (!b) return 0;\n    if (b->n_inputs == 0) return 1;\n    if (!b->input_slot_ids) return 0;        /* runtime not attached */\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (b->inputs[i].optional) continue;\n        if (!slot_has_value(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i])) return 0;\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ box_pop_ready() — every POP input has at least one cell */\n/* For multi-spawn boxes, we want to re-spawn so long as every POP\n * input still has a queued value. PEEK inputs are always available\n * after their initial push, so they don't gate continuation. */\nstatic int box_pop_ready(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id)\n{\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, box_id);\n    if (!b || !b->input_slot_modes) return 0;\n    int saw_pop = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (b->input_slot_modes[i] != SLOT_MODE_POP) continue;\n        if (b->inputs[i].optional) continue;\n        saw_pop = 1;\n        if (!slot_has_value(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i])) return 0;\n    }\n    return saw_pop;\n}\n/* }}} */"

          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ read_inputs() — peek every input slot into buffers */\n/* Returns the number of inputs read (== b->n_inputs). For each\n * input port, the consumer task gets the bytes via slot_peek\n * (head doesn't advance — that's the 1-cell peek model). Sets\n * *failed nonzero if any required input was missing or oversized. */\nstatic int read_inputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       char **bufs, const void **datas, int *sizes,\n                       int per_buf_cap, int *failed)\n{\n    *failed = 0;\n    if (b->n_inputs == 0 || !b->input_slot_ids) return 0;\n    int n_present = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        bufs[i] = malloc((size_t)per_buf_cap);\n        if (!bufs[i]) { *failed = 1; return n_present; }\n        int got = slot_peek(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i],\n                            bufs[i], per_buf_cap);\n        if (got < 0) {\n            /* Missing or wrong type. Optional ports get skipped\n             * (shorter n_inputs to the spec); required ports are an\n             * error. */\n            free(bufs[i]); bufs[i] = NULL;\n            if (!b->inputs[i].optional) { *failed = 1; return n_present; }\n            continue;\n        }\n        datas[n_present] = bufs[i];\n        sizes[n_present] = got;\n        n_present++;\n    }\n    return n_present;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ read_inputs() — peek or pop every input slot into buffers */\n/* Returns the number of inputs read (== b->n_inputs). The read\n * mode per port comes from b->input_slot_modes — PEEK leaves the\n * cell in place (subsequent tasks re-read the same value), POP\n * drains the head cell (the queue advances). Sets *failed nonzero\n * if any required input was missing or oversized. */\nstatic int read_inputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       char **bufs, const void **datas, int *sizes,\n                       int per_buf_cap, int *failed)\n{\n    *failed = 0;\n    if (b->n_inputs == 0 || !b->input_slot_ids) return 0;\n    int n_present = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        bufs[i] = malloc((size_t)per_buf_cap);\n        if (!bufs[i]) { *failed = 1; return n_present; }\n        int got;\n        int mode = b->input_slot_modes ? b->input_slot_modes[i] : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n        if (mode == SLOT_MODE_POP) {\n            got = slot_pop(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i],\n                           bufs[i], per_buf_cap);\n        } else {\n            got = slot_peek(ctx->slots, b->input_slot_ids[i],\n                            bufs[i], per_buf_cap);\n        }\n        if (got < 0) {\n            free(bufs[i]); bufs[i] = NULL;\n            if (!b->inputs[i].optional) { *failed = 1; return n_present; }\n            continue;\n        }\n        datas[n_present] = bufs[i];\n        sizes[n_present] = got;\n        n_present++;\n    }\n    return n_present;\n}\n/* }}} */",

          "old_string":"/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_round_robin() */\n/* Manually spawn the iterator three times (bypassing the single-\n * spawn guard via dispatch_spawn). Each spawn picks the next\n * branch via the atomic counter; a/b/c all fire across the three\n * invocations. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_round_robin(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    /* Three direct spawns; counter advances 0 → 1 → 2 → 0. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* a/b/c all captured an output. The \"v\" inputs are 1-cell peek,\n     * so the most-recent capture survives — that's \"A:hi\", \"B:hi\",\n     * \"C:hi\". */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b], \"B:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c], \"C:hi\");\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c], \"C:hi\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_iterator_multi_fire() */\n/* The iterator's input is an N-cell POP slot. Push three values\n * directly into it, then spawn the iterator once; auto-re-spawn\n * pops them one by one and the atomic counter walks through every\n * branch. All three sinks a/b/c fire. */\nstatic int test_iterator_multi_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int bx   = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    const box_t *iter_box = graph_box(rt.graph, iter);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->multi_spawn == 1);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->n_inputs == 1);\n    /* Push two more values so the queue has the literal plus two:\n     * \"hi\", \"hi2\", \"hi3\". The literal already landed via\n     * dispatch_push_literals. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi2\", 3, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi3\", 3, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* One spawn is enough: the dispatch action will re-spawn itself\n     * as long as POP inputs still have queued values. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a],  \"A:hi\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx], \"B:hi2\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c],  \"C:hi3\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/012-dispatch-test.c"
        }
      }],
    "role":"assistant",
    "id":"msg_01DQFJixFfeMmnqtTLAzTXgq",

Each spawn picks the next\n * branch via the atomic counter; a/b/c all fire across the three\n * invocations. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_round_robin(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    /* Three direct spawns; counter advances 0 → 1 → 2 → 0. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* a/b/c all captured an output.         "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_multi_fire);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_iterator_multi_fire() */\n/* The iterator's input is an N-cell POP slot. Push two extra\n * values (beyond the literal), then spawn the iterator once. The\n * dispatch action auto-re-spawns while POP inputs remain, so the\n * atomic counter walks 0 → 1 → 2 and each branch fires once. */\nstatic int test_iterator_multi_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int bx   = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    const box_t *iter_box = graph_box(rt.graph, iter);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->multi_spawn == 1);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->n_inputs == 1);\n\n    /* Queue two more values on top of the literal — \"hi\", \"hi2\",\n     * \"hi3\" — so the iterator has three to walk through. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi2\", 3, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi3\", 3, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* One spawn — auto-re-spawn handles the rest. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a],  \"A:hi\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx], \"B:hi2\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c],  \"C:hi3\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_multi_fire);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/012-dispatch-test.c"
        }
      }],

The","+ * dispatch action auto-re-spawns while POP inputs remain, so the","+ * atomic counter walks 0 → 1 → 2 and each branch fires once. */","+static int test_iterator_multi_fire(void)","+{","+    runtime_t rt;","+    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {","+        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;","+    }","+    char *err = NULL;","+    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);","+","+    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");","+    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");","+    int bx   = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");","+    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");","+","+    const box_t *iter_box = graph_box(rt.graph, iter);","+    ASSERT(iter_box->multi_spawn == 1);","+    ASSERT(iter_box->n_inputs == 1);","+","+    /* Queue two more values on top of the literal — \"hi\", \"hi2\",","+     * \"hi3\" — so the iterator has three to walk through. */","+    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi2\", 3, 0) == 0);","+    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi3\", 3, 0) == 0);","+","+    /* One spawn — auto-re-spawn handles the rest. */","+    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);","+    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);","+","+    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a]  != NULL);","+    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx] != NULL);","+    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c]  != NULL);","+    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a],  \"A:hi\")  == 0);","+    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx], \"B:hi2\") == 0);","+    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c],  \"C:hi3\") == 0);","+","+    runtime_teardown(&rt);","+    return 1;","+}","+/* }}} */","+"," /* {{{ main() */"," int main(void)"," {"],
        "oldStart":281
      }],
    "newString":"/* {{{ test_iterator_multi_fire() */\n/* The iterator's input is an N-cell POP slot. Push two extra\n * values (beyond the literal), then spawn the iterator once. The\n * dispatch action auto-re-spawns while POP inputs remain, so the\n * atomic counter walks 0 → 1 → 2 and each branch fires once. */\nstatic int test_iterator_multi_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int bx   = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    const box_t *iter_box = graph_box(rt.graph, iter);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->multi_spawn == 1);\n    ASSERT(iter_box->n_inputs == 1);\n\n    /* Queue two more values on top of the literal — \"hi\", \"hi2\",\n     * \"hi3\" — so the iterator has three to walk through. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi2\", 3, 0) == 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(rt.slots, iter_box->input_slot_ids[0], \"hi3\", 3, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* One spawn — auto-re-spawn handles the rest. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c]  != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a],  \"A:hi\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[bx], \"B:hi2\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c],  \"C:hi3\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_multi_fire);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */"
  },

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\t@if [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh; fi\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines.           "old_string":"### Task-id correlation — 2026-05-12\n\n`dispatch_task_t` gained a `task_id` field assigned at\n`dispatch_spawn` time (atomic fetch-add on\n`ctx->next_task_id`). The same id correlates the\n`task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` events emitted\nthrough the event queue. `task_submit` lands on the spawning\nthread (worker_idx = -1 since the task hasn't been picked up\nyet); start/end land on the dispatching worker with its real\n`thread_idx`.",
          "new_string":"### Task-id correlation — 2026-05-12\n\n`dispatch_task_t` gained a `task_id` field assigned at\n`dispatch_spawn` time (atomic fetch-add on\n`ctx->next_task_id`). The same id correlates the\n`task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` events emitted\nthrough the event queue. `task_submit` lands on the spawning\nthread (worker_idx = -1 since the task hasn't been picked up\nyet); start/end land on the dispatching worker with its real\n`thread_idx`.\n\n### Iterator multi-spawn + N-cell pop reads — 2026-05-12\n\nThree pieces together unlock real iteration:\n\n1. **Per-input slot mode.** `box->input_slot_modes[i]` is set by\n   `graph_attach_runtime` to either `SLOT_MODE_PEEK` (single-cell,\n   the legacy path) or `SLOT_MODE_POP` (multi-cell ring; each\n   read drains one cell). `read_inputs` picks `slot_pop` or\n   `slot_peek` based on the mode.\n2. **multi_spawn propagation.** Iterators are marked\n   `multi_spawn = 1`; a forward BFS propagates the flag through\n   the connection graph so every box reachable from an iterator\n   is also `multi_spawn`. Multi-spawn boxes get N-cell pop slots\n   (currently 16 cells); single-spawn boxes keep their 1-cell\n   peek slots.\n3. **Auto-re-spawn.** After a multi-spawn box's action completes\n   successfully, it calls `dispatch_spawn` on itself if any POP\n   input still has queued values. That's how a single push wakes\n   the entire chain — an iterator with three queued inputs walks\n   the counter through all three branches without external\n   intervention.\n\nThe single-spawn guard now applies only to single-spawn boxes.\nMulti-spawn ones spawn on every push; the per-slot atomic-flag\nspinlock serializes pops so two concurrent tasks each get a\ndistinct cell.\n\n`test_iterator_multi_fire` in `tests/012-dispatch-test.c` is the\nnew headline test: push three values to the iterator's input slot,\nspawn once, all three branches a/b/c fire with the right tagged\noutput. The atomic counter walks 0 → 1 → 2 across the\nauto-re-spawned tasks.",

        }

          "new_string":"What's still deferred:\n- **Language enumeration on the graph.** We resolve per-box but\n  don't expose the distinct set of languages a map uses, so\n  workers init every spec rather than only the ones in use.\n\n### Per-input slot modes + multi-spawn propagation — 2026-05-12\n\n`graph_attach_runtime` now picks the slot mode per input port:\n- A new BFS pass (`propagate_multi_spawn`) seeds every iterator-\n  routing call box as `multi_spawn = 1` and propagates the flag\n  forward through the connection graph. A","+proper per-wire classification (an iterator-rooted wire is","+multi-push regardless of the immediate consumer's status) would","+allow finer-grained mode picks; the current rule is conservative","+in the right direction (slots that *could* be POP are POP)."],
        "oldStart":379
      }],
    "newString":"What's still deferred:\n- **Language enumeration on the graph.** We resolve per-box but\n  don't expose the distinct set of languages a map uses, so\n  workers init every spec rather than only the ones in use.\n\n### Per-input slot modes + multi-spawn propagation — 2026-05-12\n\n`graph_attach_runtime` now picks the slot mode per input port:\n- A new BFS pass (`propagate_multi_spawn`) seeds every iterator-\n  routing call box as `multi_spawn = 1` and propagates the flag\n  forward through the connection graph. Every box reachable from\n  an iterator is now flagged.\n- For multi-spawn boxes, each input slot is allocated as a\n  16-cell pop ring. For single-spawn boxes, the legacy 1-cell\n  peek slot is used.\n- `box->input_slot_modes[]` carries the per-port mode\n  (`SLOT_MODE_PEEK` / `SLOT_MODE_POP`) so the dispatch action\n  picks the right read op.\n\nThis is the compile-time wire classification the architecture\ndoc described, with a single-step forward propagation rule. A\nproper per-wire classification (an iterator-rooted wire is\nmulti-push regardless of the immediate consumer's status) would\nallow finer-grained mode picks; the current rule is conservative\nin the right direction (slots that *could* be POP are POP)."
  },

          "new_string":"### Task-id correlation — 2026-05-12\n\n`dispatch_task_t` gained a `task_id` field assigned at\n`dispatch_spawn` time (atomic fetch-add on\n`ctx->next_task_id`). The same id correlates the\n`task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` events emitted\nthrough the event queue. `task_submit` lands on the spawning\nthread (worker_idx = -1 since the task hasn't been picked up\nyet); start/end land on the dispatching worker with its real\n`thread_idx`.\n\n### Iterator multi-spawn + N-cell pop reads — 2026-05-12\n\nThree pieces together unlock real iteration:\n\n1. **Per-input slot mode.** `box->input_slot_modes[i]` is set by\n   `graph_attach_runtime` to either `SLOT_MODE_PEEK` (single\n   cell, the legacy path) or `SLOT_MODE_POP` (multi-cell ring;\n   each read drains one cell). `read_inputs` picks `slot_pop`\n   or `slot_peek` based on the mode.\n2. **multi_spawn propagation.** Iterators are marked\n   `multi_spawn = 1`; a forward BFS propagates the flag through\n   the connection graph so every box reachable from an iterator\n   is also `multi_spawn`. Multi-spawn boxes get N-cell pop slots\n   (currently 16 cells); single-spawn boxes keep their 1-cell\n   peek slots.\n3. **Auto-re-spawn.** After a multi-spawn box's action completes\n   successfully, it calls `dispatch_spawn` on itself if any POP\n   input still has queued values. The atomic counter walks 0 → 1 → 2 across the\nauto-re-spawned tasks.",

          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# langs/bash/bash-server.sh — persistent bash subprocess, one per\n# worker thread, that talks to the C spec over a Unix-domain\n# socketpair connected to stdin/stdout.\n#\n# Designed in issue 308. Replaces the fork+exec-per-call model\n# with a long-lived process: process startup happens once at\n# pool init, every box invocation reuses the same bash state\n# (and the sourced module cache).\n#\n# Protocol — line-oriented, all values UTF-8:\n#\n#   Request:\n#     <n_args>\\n            (or \"QUIT\" to terminate)\n#     <file_path>\\n\n#     <fn_name>\\n\n#     <arg1>\\n              (n_args of these)\n#     <arg2>\\n\n#     ...\n#\n#   Response:\n#     <exit_status>\\n        (0 on success)\n#     <output_length>\\n      (decimal byte count, no newline at end of payload)\n#     <output_bytes>         (output_length bytes, NOT followed by \\n)\n#\n# Limitations of this iteration:\n#   - Arguments cannot contain literal newlines (line-oriented protocol).\n#   - Output is read as bytes — newlines inside the payload are fine,\n#     but trailing newlines from bash builtins like `echo` are part\n#     of the output. Box functions use `printf '%s' \"$x\"` to avoid them.\n#\n# Caching: each box file is sourced on first use and remembered in\n# the `sourced` associative array; subsequent invocations skip the\n# `source` and reuse the loaded functions. Per-worker, no locking.\n\nset -u\n\ndeclare -A sourced\n\nwhile IFS= read -r n_args; do\n    [[ \"$n_args\" == \"QUIT\" ]] && break\n\n    IFS= read -r file_path\n    IFS= read -r fn_name\n\n    args=()\n    for ((i = 0; i < n_args; i++)); do\n        IFS= read -r a\n        args+=(\"$a\")\n    done\n\n    if [[ ! -f \"$file_path\" ]]; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    if [[ -z \"${sourced[$file_path]:-}\" ]]; then\n        # shellcheck disable=SC1090\n        if ! source \"$file_path\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            printf '126\\n0\\n'\n            continue\n        fi\n        sourced[$file_path]=1\n    fi\n\n    # Capture function output and exit status. The function name\n    # itself failing (not a callable) surfaces as exit 127.\n    if ! declare -F \"$fn_name\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    out=$(\"$fn_name\" \"${args[@]}\" 2>/dev/null)\n    status=$?\n    n=${#out}\n    printf '%d\\n%d\\n' \"$status\" \"$n\"\n    printf '%s' \"$out\"\ndone\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/langs/bash/bash-server.sh"
        }
      }],

```json
{

        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* langs/bash/spec.c — Bash language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Persistent-subprocess model: each worker thread spawns one bash\n * process at init() and keeps it alive for the run, communicating\n * over a Unix-domain socketpair. Every invoke writes a\n * line-oriented request to the bash side and reads a framed\n * response — orders of magnitude faster than fork+exec per call.\n *\n * Designed in issue 308. The previous iteration's fork+exec path\n * lives only in git history now; this file replaces it wholesale.\n *\n * Protocol details, including the bash-side loop, are in\n * `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`. The C side here is just enough\n * machinery to spawn the subprocess and read/write the framing.\n *\n * Limitations:\n *  - Arguments containing literal newlines are not supported in\n *    this iteration (line-oriented protocol). Most bash boxes\n *    don't need them; binary data should be base64-encoded\n *    upstream.\n *  - The protocol is single-request/single-response; a slow box\n *    serializes calls behind it on the same worker. Multi-worker\n *    pools dispatch in parallel anyway, so this is rarely\n *    the bottleneck.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/socket.h>\n#include <sys/types.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH \"langs/bash/bash-server.sh\"\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker handle */\ntypedef struct {\n    int     fd;      /* parent-side socketpair fd */\n    pid_t   pid;     /* bash subprocess */\n} bash_handle_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ server_path() — locate bash-server.sh */\n/* For now, allow override via the SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER env var; the\n * default is relative to the cwd (the project root). The proper design is a persistent bash","- * subprocess per worker thread, connected by a Unix domain socket","- * with length-prefix framing. This iteration ships the simpler","- * fork+exec model: every invoke fork()s, exec()s bash with an","- * inline -c script that sources the box file and calls the named","- * function with the inputs as positional arguments, and reads the","- * child's stdout back through a pipe.","+ * Persistent-subprocess model: each worker thread spawns one bash","+ * process at init() and keeps it alive for the run, communicating","+ * over a Unix-domain socketpair. Every invoke writes a","+ * line-oriented request to the bash side and reads a framed","+ * response — orders of magnitude faster than fork+exec per call.","  *","- * That's slow (process spawn per call), but it lets a graph with","- * bash boxes actually run end-to-end.
