    "originalFile":"/* langs/bash/spec.c — Bash language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Persistent-subprocess model: each worker thread spawns one bash\n * process at init() and keeps it alive for the run, communicating\n * over a Unix-domain socketpair. Every invoke writes a\n * line-oriented request to the bash side and reads a framed\n * response — orders of magnitude faster than fork+exec per call.\n *\n * Designed in issue 308. The previous iteration's fork+exec path\n * lives only in git history now; this file replaces it wholesale.\n *\n * Protocol details, including the bash-side loop, are in\n * `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`. The C side here is just enough\n * machinery to spawn the subprocess and read/write the framing.\n *\n * Limitations:\n *  - Arguments containing literal newlines are not supported in\n *    this iteration (line-oriented protocol). Most bash boxes\n *    don't need them; binary data should be base64-encoded\n *    upstream.\n *  - The protocol is single-request/single-response; a slow box\n *    serializes calls behind it on the same worker. Multi-worker\n *    pools dispatch in parallel anyway, so this is rarely\n *    the bottleneck.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/socket.h>\n#include <sys/types.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH \"langs/bash/bash-server.sh\"\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker handle */\ntypedef struct {\n    int     fd;      /* parent-side socketpair fd */\n    pid_t   pid;     /* bash subprocess */\n} bash_handle_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ server_path() — locate bash-server.sh */\n/* For now, allow override via the SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER env var; the\n * default is relative to the cwd (the project root). A more\n * polished version locates the script next to the spec.so via\n * /proc/self/exe, landing with issue 309's spec discovery work. */\nstatic const char *server_path(void)\n{\n    const char *p = getenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER\");\n    return (p && *p) ? p : DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_all() — write n bytes, retrying on partial writes */\nstatic int write_all(int fd, const void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    const char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t w = write(fd, p, left);\n        if (w < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w == 0) return -1;\n        p    += w;\n        left -= (size_t)w;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_exact() — read exactly n bytes from fd */\nstatic int read_exact(int fd, void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, p, left);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        p    += r;\n        left -= (size_t)r;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_line() — read up to cap bytes including a trailing \\n */\n/* Returns the number of bytes read (including the newline), or -1\n * on error / EOF. The newline is overwritten with '\\0' so the\n * line is a NUL-terminated C string of length (return-1). */\nstatic int read_line(int fd, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    while (n < cap - 1) {\n        char c;\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, &c, 1);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        if (c == '\\n') {\n            buf[n] = '\\0';\n            return n + 1;\n        }\n        buf[n++] = c;\n    }\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    return -1;     /* line longer than buffer */\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_init() — spawn the subprocess */\nstatic void *bash_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    int sv[2];\n    if (socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, sv) != 0) return NULL;\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        close(sv[0]); close(sv[1]);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: route the child-side socket fd to stdin+stdout. */\n        close(sv[0]);\n        if (dup2(sv[1], STDIN_FILENO)  < 0) _exit(126);\n        if (dup2(sv[1], STDOUT_FILENO) < 0) _exit(126);\n        close(sv[1]);\n\n        /* Ignore SIGPIPE so the parent dying doesn't immediately\n         * kill us — let the read on stdin return EOF and exit cleanly. */\n        signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);\n\n        execlp(\"bash\", \"bash\", server_path(), (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    /* Parent. */\n    close(sv[1]);\n    bash_handle_t *h = malloc(sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) { close(sv[0]); return NULL; }\n    h->fd  = sv[0];\n    h->pid = pid;\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_teardown() — graceful shutdown */\nstatic void bash_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n    /* Send \"QUIT\" so the bash loop exits cleanly; then close the\n     * socket and wait for the child. */\n    if (h->fd >= 0) {\n        (void)write_all(h->fd, \"QUIT\\n\", 5);\n        close(h->fd);\n    }\n    if (h->pid > 0) {\n        int status = 0;\n        /* Give the child a chance to exit on its own; if it doesn't,\n         * SIGTERM it. The waitpid loop handles EINTR. */\n        for (int tries = 0; tries < 200; tries++) {\n            pid_t r = waitpid(h->pid, &status, WNOHANG);\n            if (r == h->pid) goto done;\n            if (r < 0 && errno != EINTR) break;\n            struct timespec ts = { 0, 5 * 1000 * 1000 };  /* 5 ms */\n            nanosleep(&ts, NULL);\n        }\n        kill(h->pid, SIGTERM);\n        waitpid(h->pid, &status, 0);\n    }\ndone:\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ send_request() — write the request frame */\nstatic int send_request(int fd, const char *file_path, const char *fn_name,\n                        const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes,\n                        int n_inputs)\n{\n    char header[64];\n    int n = snprintf(header, sizeof header, \"%d\\n\", n_inputs);\n    if (n < 0 || n >= (int)sizeof header) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, header, (size_t)n)              < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, file_path, strlen(file_path))   < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1)                        < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, fn_name, strlen(fn_name))       < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1)                        < 0) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (write_all(fd, input_data[i], (size_t)input_sizes[i]) < 0) return -1;\n        if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1) < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_invoke() */\nstatic int bash_invoke(void *handle,\n                       const char  *file_path,\n                       const char  *fn_name,\n                       const void **input_data,\n                       const int   *input_sizes,\n                       int          n_inputs,\n                       void        *out_buf,\n                       int          out_capacity,\n                       int         *out_size)\n{\n    if (!handle || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n\n    if (send_request(h->fd, file_path, fn_name,\n                     input_data, input_sizes, n_inputs) != 0) {\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Response: status\\n out_len\\n out_bytes. */\n    char line[64];\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int status = atoi(line);\n\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int n = atoi(line);\n\n    if (n > out_capacity) {\n        /* Drain the output to keep the protocol synced, then fail. */\n        char drop[1024];\n        int left = n;\n        while (left > 0) {\n            int chunk = left < (int)sizeof drop ? left : (int)sizeof drop;\n            if (read_exact(h->fd, drop, (size_t)chunk) < 0) return -1;\n            left -= chunk;\n        }\n        fprintf(stderr, \"bash spec: %s:%s returned %d bytes; buffer is %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, n, out_capacity);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (n > 0) {\n        if (read_exact(h->fd, out_buf, (size_t)n) < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_size) *out_size = n;\n\n    if (status != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"bash spec: %s:%s exited with status %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name     = \"bash\",\n    .file_ext = \".sh\",\n    .init     = bash_init,\n    .teardown = bash_teardown,\n    .compile  = 0,\n    .invoke   = bash_invoke,\n};\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,

    "originalFile":"/* langs/bash/spec.c — Bash language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Persistent-subprocess model: each worker thread spawns one bash\n * process at init() and keeps it alive for the run, communicating\n * over a Unix-domain socketpair. Every invoke writes a\n * line-oriented request to the bash side and reads a framed\n * response — orders of magnitude faster than fork+exec per call.\n *\n * Designed in issue 308. The previous iteration's fork+exec path\n * lives only in git history now; this file replaces it wholesale.\n *\n * Protocol details, including the bash-side loop, are in\n * `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`. The C side here is just enough\n * machinery to spawn the subprocess and read/write the framing.\n *\n * Limitations:\n *  - Arguments containing literal newlines are not supported in\n *    this iteration (line-oriented protocol). Most bash boxes\n *    don't need them; binary data should be base64-encoded\n *    upstream.\n *  - The protocol is single-request/single-response; a slow box\n *    serializes calls behind it on the same worker. Multi-worker\n *    pools dispatch in parallel anyway, so this is rarely\n *    the bottleneck.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/socket.h>\n#include <sys/types.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <time.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH \"langs/bash/bash-server.sh\"\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker handle */\ntypedef struct {\n    int     fd;      /* parent-side socketpair fd */\n    pid_t   pid;     /* bash subprocess */\n} bash_handle_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ server_path() — locate bash-server.sh */\n/* For now, allow override via the SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER env var; the\n * default is relative to the cwd (the project root). A more\n * polished version locates the script next to the spec.so via\n * /proc/self/exe, landing with issue 309's spec discovery work. */\nstatic const char *server_path(void)\n{\n    const char *p = getenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER\");\n    return (p && *p) ? p : DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_all() — write n bytes, retrying on partial writes */\nstatic int write_all(int fd, const void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    const char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t w = write(fd, p, left);\n        if (w < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w == 0) return -1;\n        p    += w;\n        left -= (size_t)w;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_exact() — read exactly n bytes from fd */\nstatic int read_exact(int fd, void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, p, left);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        p    += r;\n        left -= (size_t)r;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_line() — read up to cap bytes including a trailing \\n */\n/* Returns the number of bytes read (including the newline), or -1\n * on error / EOF. The newline is overwritten with '\\0' so the\n * line is a NUL-terminated C string of length (return-1). */\nstatic int read_line(int fd, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    while (n < cap - 1) {\n        char c;\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, &c, 1);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        if (c == '\\n') {\n            buf[n] = '\\0';\n            return n + 1;\n        }\n        buf[n++] = c;\n    }\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    return -1;     /* line longer than buffer */\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_init() — spawn the subprocess */\nstatic void *bash_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    int sv[2];\n    if (socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, sv) != 0) return NULL;\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        close(sv[0]); return NULL; }\n    h->fd  = sv[0];\n    h->pid = pid;\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_teardown() — graceful shutdown */\nstatic void bash_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n    /* Send \"QUIT\" so the bash loop exits cleanly; then close the\n     * socket and wait for the child. */\n    if (h->fd >= 0) {\n        (void)write_all(h->fd, \"QUIT\\n\", 5);\n        close(h->fd);\n    }\n    if (h->pid > 0) {\n        int status = 0;\n        /* Give the child a chance to exit on its own; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (write_all(fd, input_data[i], (size_t)input_sizes[i]) < 0) return -1;\n        if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1) < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_invoke() */\nstatic int bash_invoke(void *handle,\n                       const char  *file_path,\n                       const char  *fn_name,\n                       const void **input_data,\n                       const int   *input_sizes,\n                       int          n_inputs,\n                       void        *out_buf,\n                       int          out_capacity,\n                       int         *out_size)\n{\n    if (!handle || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n\n    if (send_request(h->fd, file_path, fn_name,\n                     input_data, input_sizes, n_inputs) != 0) {\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Response: status\\n out_len\\n out_bytes. */\n    char line[64];\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int status = atoi(line);\n\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int n = atoi(line);\n\n    if (n > out_capacity) {\n        /* Drain the output to keep the protocol synced, then fail. */\n        char drop[1024];\n        int left = n;\n        while (left > 0) {\n            int chunk = left < (int)sizeof drop ? left : (int)sizeof drop;\n            if (read_exact(h->fd, drop, (size_t)chunk) < 0) return -1;\n            left -= chunk;\n        }\n        fprintf(stderr, \"bash spec: %s:%s returned %d bytes; buffer is %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, n, out_capacity);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (n > 0) {\n        if (read_exact(h->fd, out_buf, (size_t)n) < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_size) *out_size = n;\n\n    if (status != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"bash spec: %s:%s exited with status %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name     = \"bash\",\n    .file_ext = \".sh\",\n    .init     = bash_init,\n    .teardown = bash_teardown,\n    .compile  = 0,\n    .invoke   = bash_invoke,\n};\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* src/008-pool-runner.c — phase 3 runner entry point.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C binary that loads a map\n * directory, stands up the slot store + spec registry + thread\n * pool, runs the dispatch loop to quiescence, and prints what\n * each box produced.\n *\n * As of this iteration the runner actually runs maps end-to-end:\n *\n *   1. Load and validate the graph (305).\n *   2. Create the slot store (302) and spec registry (303).\n *   3. Create the thread pool (301) and register a per-worker\n *      init callback that populates each worker's handles[]\n *      with the spec registry (303 pool hook).\n *   4. Attach runtime — allocate one slot per input port and\n *      resolve each call box's spec (305 phase 5+7).\n *   5. Initialize the dispatch context with output capture.\n *   6. pool_init_barrier — releases workers from their init\n *      stage into the task loop.\n *   7. Push literal input values to slots, then spawn every box\n *      that's ready (every input either literal or optional).\n *      Wired-input boxes spawn automatically when an upstream\n *      push triggers spawn-on-ready.\n *   8. pool_wait_quiescent.\n *   9. Print each box's captured output, tear down.\n *\n * The JSONL run log (issue 311) and the dispatch action's\n * iterator multi-spawn path (issue 304) are still ahead.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <time.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() / spec_pool_teardown_cb() */\n/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language\n * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker; the teardown\n * callback is the symmetric release path that fires at worker\n * exit so subprocess specs (e.g. bash) shut down cleanly. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n\nstatic void spec_pool_teardown_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, ctx->handles, spec_registry_size(r));\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ now_secs() */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ open_event_queue() — try map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl */\n/* Falls back to /tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl when there's no tmp/\n * subdir in the map. Returns NULL silently if even the fallback\n * can't be opened — the runner works without a run log. */\nstatic event_queue_t *open_event_queue(const char *map_dir,\n                                       char *path_out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(path_out, cap, \"%s/tmp/last-run.jsonl\", map_dir);\n    char tmpdir[4096];\n    snprintf(tmpdir, sizeof tmpdir, \"%s/tmp\", map_dir);\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(tmpdir, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        snprintf(path_out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\");\n    }\n    return event_queue_create(path_out);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g       = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots   = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs   = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool    = NULL;\n    event_queue_t   *events  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int              ctx_initialised = 0;\n    char             jsonl_path[4096] = {0};\n\n    struct timespec  ts_start;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_start);\n    long start_us = (long)ts_start.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_start.tv_nsec / 1000;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 6b. Open the run-log event queue and emit run_start. */\n    events = open_event_queue(map_dir, jsonl_path, sizeof jsonl_path);\n    if (events) {\n        ctx.events = events;\n        event_queue_run_start(events, now_secs(),\n                              graph_name(g), pool_n_workers(pool));\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n    if (events) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run log → %s\\n\", jsonl_path);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    struct timespec ts_end;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_end);\n    long end_us = (long)ts_end.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_end.tv_nsec / 1000;\n    if (events) {\n        event_queue_run_end(events, now_secs(),\n                            end_us - start_us, ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    }\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s) in %ld µs).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched, end_us - start_us);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (events) event_queue_destroy(events);    /* drains + joins writer */\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);",
    "newString":"    pool_set_worker_init    (pool, spec_pool_init_cb,     specs);\n    pool_set_worker_teardown(pool, spec_pool_teardown_cb, specs);",

  },

    "originalFile":"/* src/008-pool-runner.c — phase 3 runner entry point.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C binary that loads a map\n * directory, stands up the slot store + spec registry + thread\n * pool, runs the dispatch loop to quiescence, and prints what\n * each box produced.\n *\n * As of this iteration the runner actually runs maps end-to-end:\n *\n *   1. Load and validate the graph (305).\n *   2. Create the slot store (302) and spec registry (303).\n *   3. Create the thread pool (301) and register a per-worker\n *      init callback that populates each worker's handles[]\n *      with the spec registry (303 pool hook).\n *   4. Attach runtime — allocate one slot per input port and\n *      resolve each call box's spec (305 phase 5+7).\n *   5. Initialize the dispatch context with output capture.\n *   6. pool_init_barrier — releases workers from their init\n *      stage into the task loop.\n *   7. Push literal input values to slots, then spawn every box\n *      that's ready (every input either literal or optional).\n *      Wired-input boxes spawn automatically when an upstream\n *      push triggers spawn-on-ready.\n *   8. pool_wait_quiescent.\n *   9. Print each box's captured output, tear down.\n *\n * The JSONL run log (issue 311) and the dispatch action's\n * iterator multi-spawn path (issue 304) are still ahead.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <time.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() */\n/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language\n * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ now_secs() */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ open_event_queue() — try map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl */\n/* Falls back to /tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl when there's no tmp/\n * subdir in the map. Returns NULL silently if even the fallback\n * can't be opened — the runner works without a run log. */\nstatic event_queue_t *open_event_queue(const char *map_dir,\n                                       char *path_out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(path_out, cap, \"%s/tmp/last-run.jsonl\", map_dir);\n    char tmpdir[4096];\n    snprintf(tmpdir, sizeof tmpdir, \"%s/tmp\", map_dir);\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(tmpdir, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        snprintf(path_out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\");\n    }\n    return event_queue_create(path_out);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g       = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots   = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs   = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool    = NULL;\n    event_queue_t   *events  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int              ctx_initialised = 0;\n    char             jsonl_path[4096] = {0};\n\n    struct timespec  ts_start;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_start);\n    long start_us = (long)ts_start.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_start.tv_nsec / 1000;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 6b. Open the run-log event queue and emit run_start. */\n    events = open_event_queue(map_dir, jsonl_path, sizeof jsonl_path);\n    if (events) {\n        ctx.events = events;\n        event_queue_run_start(events, now_secs(),\n                              graph_name(g), pool_n_workers(pool));\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n    if (events) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run log → %s\\n\", jsonl_path);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    struct timespec ts_end;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_end);\n    long end_us = (long)ts_end.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_end.tv_nsec / 1000;\n    if (events) {\n        event_queue_run_end(events, now_secs(),\n                            end_us - start_us, ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    }\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s) in %ld µs).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched, end_us - start_us);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (events) event_queue_destroy(events);    /* drains + joins writer */\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

Current queue is plain FIFO."," "," Neither blocks 304 (dispatch) from starting.","+","+### Per-worker teardown hook — 2026-05-12","+","+Symmetric counterpart to `pool_set_worker_init`. Registered via","+`pool_set_worker_teardown(p, cb, user)`; the worker thread runs","+the callback right before exiting, after the task loop drains.","+The runner uses it to call `spec_registry_teardown_worker`,","+which sends bash subprocesses `QUIT`, closes their socket fds,","+and waitpids them. Without this, soramech-pool was leaking","+orphan bash processes (16 per run) that piled up across runs","+and slowed startup. Verified: zero orphans after a fresh run."],
        "oldStart":240
      }],
    "newString":"Neither blocks 304 (dispatch) from starting.\n\n### Per-worker teardown hook — 2026-05-12\n\nSymmetric counterpart to `pool_set_worker_init`. Registered via\n`pool_set_worker_teardown(p, cb, user)`; the worker thread runs\nthe callback right before exiting, after the task loop drains.\nThe runner uses it to call `spec_registry_teardown_worker`,\nwhich sends bash subprocesses `QUIT`, closes their socket fds,\nand waitpids them. Without this, soramech-pool was leaking\norphan bash processes (16 per run) that piled up across runs\nand slowed startup. Verified: zero orphans after a fresh run."
  },

        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"### fork+exec invoke — 2026-05-12\n\nFirst-pass implementation: every invoke forks bash with an inline\n`-c` script that sources the box file and calls the named\nfunction with the inputs as positional args. Child's stdout is\nread through a pipe — that becomes the output bytes. Slow (~1 ms\nper call), but it gets bash boxes running end-to-end. The\npersistent Unix-domain-socket model lands as a follow-on.\n\nLimitations: inputs containing NUL bytes can't be passed as\npositional args (base64-encode if needed); output is bounded by\n`out_capacity`.\n\n`tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh` ships three fixture functions.\nFive tests in `tests/308-bash-spec-test.c` cover happy paths\nplus the missing-function failure mode.",
          "new_string":"### fork+exec invoke — 2026-05-12\n\nFirst-pass implementation: every invoke forks bash with an inline\n`-c` script that sources the box file and calls the named\nfunction with the inputs as positional args. Child's stdout is\nread through a pipe — that becomes the output bytes. Slow (~1 ms\nper call), but it gets bash boxes running end-to-end. The\npersistent Unix-domain-socket model lands as a follow-on.\n\n### Persistent socketpair + line-protocol — 2026-05-12\n\nReplaced the fork+exec path with a persistent bash subprocess per\nworker thread. Each worker's `bash_init` does\n`socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC)`, forks bash,\nand execs `langs/bash/bash-server.sh` with the child-side socket\nfd dup'd to stdin and stdout. The `SOCK_CLOEXEC` flag is load-\nbearing: without it, concurrent worker forks would inherit each\nother's parent-side fds, the bash subprocesses would never see\nEOF, and orphan processes would pile up.\n\nThe on-the-wire protocol is line-oriented:\n\n```\nRequest:                          Response:\n  <n_args>\\n        (or QUIT)       <exit_status>\\n\n  <file_path>\\n                     <output_length>\\n\n  <fn_name>\\n                       <output_bytes>\n  <arg1>\\n\n  <arg2>\\n\n  ...\n```\n\n`bash-server.sh` keeps an associative array of sourced files so a\nbox source is sourced exactly once per worker — analogous to the\nLua spec's per-worker module cache (issue 306).\n\nPer-worker teardown plumbed through the pool (issue 301's new\n`pool_set_worker_teardown` callback) sends `QUIT\\n`, closes the\nparent fd, and `waitpid`s the subprocess with a 1-second\nshort-poll fallback to `SIGTERM`. Verified: zero orphan bash\nprocesses after a `soramech-pool` run.\n\nLimitations of the current protocol:\n- Arguments containing literal newlines are not supported\n  (line-oriented framing). Box authors who need them base64-encode.\n- Single-request/single-response; long-running bash boxes\n  serialize behind themselves on the same worker. Multi-worker\n  pools dispatch in parallel, so this is rarely the bottleneck.\n\n`tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh` ships three fixture functions.\nFive tests in `tests/308-bash-spec-test.c` cover happy paths\nplus the missing-function failure mode; all pass against the\npersistent-subprocess implementation.",

Line-oriented protocol: `n_args / file_path / fn_name / args` request, `status / out_len / out_bytes` response. `bash-server.sh` runs the loop and caches sourced files per worker (the bash analogue of 306's Lua module cache). All five bash-spec tests pass against the new model.\n\n- **The CLOEXEC bug** — without `SOCK_CLOEXEC`, concurrent worker forks would inherit each other's parent-side fds and the bash subprocesses would never see EOF. Fixed at socket creation.\n\n- **301 per-worker teardown hook** — `pool_set_worker_teardown(p, cb, user)` runs the symmetric counterpart to `pool_set_worker_init` right before each worker exits. The runner uses it to call `spec_registry_teardown_worker`, which `QUIT`s bash, closes its socket, and `waitpid`s with a 1s short-poll fallback to `SIGTERM`. **Verified zero orphan bash processes after a `soramech-pool` run.**\n\nThe bash spec is now properly out-of-process at the speed the architecture intended. Want another round?"

    "newString":"        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n         * concurrent-safe semantics. */\n        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) {\n            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes. Stored as\n     * a small array of arena-owned string pointers; the pool init\n     * can use it to skip specs no box in this map uses. */\n    free(g->languages);\n    g->languages   = NULL;\n    g->n_languages = 0;\n    if (g->n_boxes > 0) {\n        g->languages = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, sizeof(const char *));\n        if (!g->languages) {\n            if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n            if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n            int seen = 0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_languages; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(g->languages[k], b->lang) == 0) { seen = 1; break; }\n            }\n            if (!seen) g->languages[g->n_languages++] = b->lang;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */"

Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Data boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (data only)          */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing;     "originalFile":"/* src/011-spec-registry.h — language spec registry, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: scans langs/<name>/ at startup,\n * dlopens every spec.so it finds, and exposes a name- and\n * extension-keyed lookup to the rest of the runtime.\n *\n * Designed in issue 303. Returns NULL on failure with *err set. */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err);\n\n/* dlclose every handle, free the registry. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid             spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r);\n\nint              spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r);\n\n/* Look up by spec.name (\"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\"). NULL if not found. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name);\n\n/* Look up by file_ext (\".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\"). NULL if not\n * found. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext);\n\n/* Enumerate registered specs by index for diagnostics / iteration. */\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i);\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker init / teardown\n *\n * The pool's `worker_main` calls these once per worker between TLS\n * setup and the init barrier. For each spec in the registry, calls\n * spec->init(worker_idx) and stashes the returned handle in the\n * caller-provided handles array. Specs whose init pointer is NULL get a NULL handle.\n *\n * Returns the number of handles filled (== registry size) on\n * success, -1 on the first spec init that returns NULL when its\n * init pointer was non-NULL.\n *\n * teardown_worker walks the array in reverse and calls each\n * spec's teardown with the corresponding handle. Safe to call\n * with a partially-populated handles array. */\nint  spec_registry_init_worker     (spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                                    void **handles, int handles_capacity);\nvoid spec_registry_teardown_worker (spec_registry_t *r,\n                                    void **handles, int n_handles);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_SPEC_REGISTRY_H */\n",

          "new_string":"/* {{{ spec_registry_init_worker() — init every spec */\nint spec_registry_init_worker(spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                              void **handles, int handles_capacity)\n{\n    return spec_registry_init_worker_filtered(r, worker_idx,\n                                              handles, handles_capacity,\n                                              NULL, 0);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_init_worker_filtered() */\nint spec_registry_init_worker_filtered(spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                                       void **handles, int handles_capacity,\n                                       const char **langs, int n_langs)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return -1;\n    if (handles_capacity < r->count) return -1;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) handles[i] = NULL;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n\n        /* Filter: if `langs` is non-NULL, skip specs whose name\n         * isn't in the list.     "originalFile":"/* src/011-spec-registry.c — language spec registry, implementation.\n *\n * Scans the langs/ directory at startup, dlopens every <name>/spec.so\n * it finds, reads the exported `soramech_lang_spec` symbol, and\n * stores name + file_ext + dl handle + spec pointer. Registry stays\n * alive for the run; spec_registry_destroy walks the entries and\n * dlcloses every handle.\n *\n * Per-worker spec init (running each spec's init callback once per\n * worker thread) lives in the pool, not here — issue 301's worker_main\n * gets the hook in a follow-on. This file just produces the lookup\n * table that the hook will iterate.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal entry */\ntypedef struct spec_entry {\n    void             *dl_handle;\n    const lang_spec_t *spec;\n} spec_entry_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Registry */\nstruct spec_registry {\n    int           count;\n    int           capacity;\n    spec_entry_t *entries;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ grow_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_if_needed(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (r->count < r->capacity) return 0;\n    int new_cap = r->capacity ? r->capacity * 2 : 4;\n    spec_entry_t *grown = realloc(r->entries, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(spec_entry_t));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    r->entries  = grown;\n    r->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ try_load_one() — open one langs/<name>/spec.so */\n/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with *err set. Skips entries\n * that don't contain a spec.so silently (a subdirectory without a\n * built spec just means that language isn't available). */\nstatic int try_load_one(spec_registry_t *r, const char *langs_dir,\n                        const char *name, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s/spec.so\", langs_dir, name);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"spec path too long: %s/%s\", langs_dir, name);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) return 0;   /* no spec.so; silent skip */\n\n    /* RTLD_LOCAL keeps symbols from one spec from leaking into\n     * another — a spec's internal helpers shouldn't be visible to\n     * any other dlopen'd module. RTLD_NOW catches missing-symbol\n     * errors immediately rather than deferring them to the first\n     * call. */\n    void *h = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!h) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"dlopen('%s') failed: %s\", path, dlerror());\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* dlerror's \"clear the queue\" idiom: call it once before dlsym\n     * to flush any pending error, then again after to read it. */\n    (void)dlerror();\n    const lang_spec_t *spec = dlsym(h, \"soramech_lang_spec\");\n    const char *dl_err = dlerror();\n    if (!spec || dl_err) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' is missing 'soramech_lang_spec': %s\",\n                       path, dl_err ? dl_err : \"symbol not found\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (!spec->name || !spec->file_ext) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' exports a spec with NULL name or file_ext\", path);\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    if (grow_if_needed(r) != 0) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    r->entries[r->count].dl_handle = h;\n    r->entries[r->count].spec      = spec;\n    r->count++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_load() */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err)\n{\n    if (err) *err = NULL;\n    if (!langs_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"spec_registry_load: NULL langs_dir\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(langs_dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open langs directory '%s'\", langs_dir);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof *r);\n    if (!r) {\n        closedir(d);\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        /* Probe the subdir as a directory; ignore plain files. */\n        char sub[4096];\n        int w = snprintf(sub, sizeof sub, \"%s/%s\", langs_dir, e->d_name);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub) continue;\n        struct stat st;\n        if (stat(sub, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) continue;\n\n        char *one_err = NULL;\n        if (try_load_one(r, langs_dir, e->d_name, &one_err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            spec_registry_destroy(r);\n            if (err) *err = one_err;\n            else     free(one_err);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return r;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_destroy() */\nvoid spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!r) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (r->entries[i].dl_handle) dlclose(r->entries[i].dl_handle);\n    }\n    free(r->entries);\n    free(r);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nint spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    return r ? r->count : 0;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name)\n{\n    if (!r || !name) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->name, name) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext)\n{\n    if (!r || !file_ext) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->file_ext, file_ext) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_init_worker() */\nint spec_registry_init_worker(spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                              void **handles, int handles_capacity)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return -1;\n    if (handles_capacity < r->count) return -1;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) handles[i] = NULL;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (!s->init) continue;          /* spec opts out of init */\n        void *h = s->init(worker_idx);\n        if (!h) {\n            /* Teardown anything we've already created. */\n            spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, handles, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        handles[i] = h;\n    }\n    return r->count;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_teardown_worker() */\nvoid spec_registry_teardown_worker(spec_registry_t *r,\n                                   void **handles, int n_handles)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return;\n    if (n_handles > r->count) n_handles = r->count;\n    /* Walk in reverse — symmetric with init order. */\n    for (int i = n_handles - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (s->teardown && handles[i]) {\n            s->teardown(handles[i]);\n        }\n        handles[i] = NULL;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* src/008-pool-runner.c — phase 3 runner entry point.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C binary that loads a map\n * directory, stands up the slot store + spec registry + thread\n * pool, runs the dispatch loop to quiescence, and prints what\n * each box produced.\n *\n * As of this iteration the runner actually runs maps end-to-end:\n *\n *   1. Load and validate the graph (305).\n *   2. Create the slot store (302) and spec registry (303).\n *   3. Create the thread pool (301) and register a per-worker\n *      init callback that populates each worker's handles[]\n *      with the spec registry (303 pool hook).\n *   4. Attach runtime — allocate one slot per input port and\n *      resolve each call box's spec (305 phase 5+7).\n *   5. Initialize the dispatch context with output capture.\n *   6. pool_init_barrier — releases workers from their init\n *      stage into the task loop.\n *   7. Push literal input values to slots, then spawn every box\n *      that's ready (every input either literal or optional).\n *      Wired-input boxes spawn automatically when an upstream\n *      push triggers spawn-on-ready.\n *   8. pool_wait_quiescent.\n *   9. Print each box's captured output, tear down.\n *\n * The JSONL run log (issue 311) and the dispatch action's\n * iterator multi-spawn path (issue 304) are still ahead.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <time.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() / spec_pool_teardown_cb() */\n/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language\n * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker; the teardown\n * callback is the symmetric release path that fires at worker\n * exit so subprocess specs (e.g. bash) shut down cleanly. */\nstatic int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,\n                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;\n}\n\nstatic void spec_pool_teardown_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;\n    spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, ctx->handles, spec_registry_size(r));\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ now_secs() */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ open_event_queue() — try map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl */\n/* Falls back to /tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl when there's no tmp/\n * subdir in the map. Returns NULL silently if even the fallback\n * can't be opened — the runner works without a run log. */\nstatic event_queue_t *open_event_queue(const char *map_dir,\n                                       char *path_out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(path_out, cap, \"%s/tmp/last-run.jsonl\", map_dir);\n    char tmpdir[4096];\n    snprintf(tmpdir, sizeof tmpdir, \"%s/tmp\", map_dir);\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(tmpdir, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        snprintf(path_out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\");\n    }\n    return event_queue_create(path_out);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g       = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots   = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs   = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool    = NULL;\n    event_queue_t   *events  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int              ctx_initialised = 0;\n    char             jsonl_path[4096] = {0};\n\n    struct timespec  ts_start;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_start);\n    long start_us = (long)ts_start.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_start.tv_nsec / 1000;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    specs = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    pool_set_worker_init    (pool, spec_pool_init_cb,     specs);\n    pool_set_worker_teardown(pool, spec_pool_teardown_cb, specs);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 6b. Open the run-log event queue and emit run_start. */\n    events = open_event_queue(map_dir, jsonl_path, sizeof jsonl_path);\n    if (events) {\n        ctx.events = events;\n        event_queue_run_start(events, now_secs(),\n                              graph_name(g), pool_n_workers(pool));\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n    if (events) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run log → %s\\n\", jsonl_path);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    struct timespec ts_end;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_end);\n    long end_us = (long)ts_end.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_end.tv_nsec / 1000;\n    if (events) {\n        event_queue_run_end(events, now_secs(),\n                            end_us - start_us, ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    }\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s) in %ld µs).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched, end_us - start_us);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (events) event_queue_destroy(events);    /* drains + joins writer */\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

0 : -1;\n}\n\nstatic void spec_pool_teardown_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    struct spec_init_args *a = (struct spec_init_args *)user;\n    spec_registry_teardown_worker(a->registry, ctx->handles,\n                                  spec_registry_size(a->registry));\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ find_langs_dir() — locate the langs/ directory at runtime\n *\n * Precedence: SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR env var > sibling of the\n * binary (via /proc/self/exe) > \"langs\" relative to cwd.\n * `buf` is a scratch buffer the resolved path may live in. */\nstatic const char *find_langs_dir(char *buf, size_t cap)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR\");\n    if (env && *env) return env;\n\n    char exe[4096];\n    ssize_t n = readlink(\"/proc/self/exe\", exe, sizeof exe - 1);\n    if (n > 0 && n < (ssize_t)(sizeof exe - 1)) {\n        exe[n] = '\\0';\n        char *slash = strrchr(exe, '/');\n        if (slash) {\n            *slash = '\\0';\n            snprintf(buf, cap, \"%s/langs\", exe);\n            struct stat st;\n            if (stat(buf, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) return buf;\n        }\n    }\n    return \"langs\";\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ now_secs() */\nstatic double now_secs(void)\n{\n    struct timespec ts;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ open_event_queue() — try map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl */\n/* Falls back to /tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl when there's no tmp/\n * subdir in the map. Returns NULL silently if even the fallback\n * can't be opened — the runner works without a run log. */\nstatic event_queue_t *open_event_queue(const char *map_dir,\n                                       char *path_out, size_t cap)\n{\n    snprintf(path_out, cap, \"%s/tmp/last-run.jsonl\", map_dir);\n    char tmpdir[4096];\n    snprintf(tmpdir, sizeof tmpdir, \"%s/tmp\", map_dir);\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(tmpdir, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        snprintf(path_out, cap, \"/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl\");\n    }\n    return event_queue_create(path_out);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ print_outputs() */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int   rc  = 1;\n\n    graph_t         *g       = NULL;\n    slot_store_t    *slots   = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *specs   = NULL;\n    pool_t          *pool    = NULL;\n    event_queue_t   *events  = NULL;\n    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;\n    int              ctx_initialised = 0;\n    char             jsonl_path[4096] = {0};\n\n    struct timespec  ts_start;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_start);\n    long start_us = (long)ts_start.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_start.tv_nsec / 1000;\n\n    /* 1. Load the graph. */\n    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */\n    slots = slot_store_create();\n    if (!slots) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    char langs_buf[4096];\n    const char *langs_dir = find_langs_dir(langs_buf, sizeof langs_buf);\n    specs = spec_registry_load(langs_dir, &err);\n    if (!specs) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"spec load failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!pool) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: pool_create failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    /* spec_init_args bundles the registry + the map's language\n     * list. We populate it after graph_attach_runtime so the\n     * language enumeration is in place. */\n    struct spec_init_args sia = { specs, NULL, 0 };\n    pool_set_worker_init    (pool, spec_pool_init_cb,     &sia);\n    pool_set_worker_teardown(pool, spec_pool_teardown_cb, &sia);\n\n    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */\n    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"attach runtime failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */\n    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"dispatch_ctx_init failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    ctx_initialised = 1;\n\n    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */\n    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: worker init failed\\n\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n\n    /* 6b. Open the run-log event queue and emit run_start. */\n    events = open_event_queue(map_dir, jsonl_path, sizeof jsonl_path);\n    if (events) {\n        ctx.events = events;\n        event_queue_run_start(events, now_secs(),\n                              graph_name(g), pool_n_workers(pool));\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(pool));\n    if (events) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run log → %s\\n\", jsonl_path);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever\n     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by\n     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */\n    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"push literals failed\");\n        goto cleanup;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);\n    }\n\n    /* 8. Quiesce. */\n    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);\n\n    struct timespec ts_end;\n    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts_end);\n    long end_us = (long)ts_end.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts_end.tv_nsec / 1000;\n    if (events) {\n        event_queue_run_end(events, now_secs(),\n                            end_us - start_us, ctx.tasks_dispatched);\n    }\n\n    /* 9. Report. */\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s) in %ld µs).\\n\",\n            ctx.tasks_dispatched, end_us - start_us);\n    fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: outputs:\\n\");\n    print_outputs(&ctx);\n\n    rc = 0;\n\ncleanup:\n    free(err);\n    if (events) event_queue_destroy(events);    /* drains + joins writer */\n    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);\n    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);\n    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);\n    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);\n    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

We need\n     * a flat array of const char* — copy each language pointer\n     * into a small stack buffer. The graph owns the strings. */\n    const char *lang_ptrs[POOL_LANG_SLOTS];\n    int n_langs = graph_n_languages(g);\n    if (n_langs > POOL_LANG_SLOTS) n_langs = POOL_LANG_SLOTS;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_langs; i++) lang_ptrs[i] = graph_language(g, i);\n    sia.languages   = lang_ptrs;\n    sia.n_languages = n_langs;",

    "originalFile":"/* src/013-jsonl-events.c — phase 3 run-log event writer.\n *\n * Each emit serializes one event into a 512-byte buffer via the\n * bounded JSON writer (issue 314), appends a newline, then writes\n * the line to the underlying FILE under a per-writer mutex. The\n * mutex is what the MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread\n * will replace once dispatch is producing events at rate.\n *\n * Buffer size is fixed at 512 bytes. Every event the architecture\n * doc defines fits comfortably; if a future event needs more it\n * can be bumped or made dynamic.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#define EVENT_BUF 512\n\n/* {{{ Writer struct */\nstruct jsonl_writer {\n    FILE            *fp;\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_open() */\njsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    jsonl_writer_t *w = calloc(1, sizeof *w);\n    if (!w) { fclose(fp); return NULL; }\n    w->fp = fp;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&w->mtx, NULL) != 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        free(w);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return w;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_close() */\nvoid jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    if (w->fp) { fflush(w->fp); fclose(w->fp); w->fp = NULL; }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&w->mtx);\n    free(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ flush_line() — finalize the writer, append \\n, write under lock */\nstatic int flush_line(jsonl_writer_t *w, json_writer_t *jw, char *buf)\n{\n    int n = json_writer_finish(jw);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    if (n >= EVENT_BUF) return -1;   /* would overrun the newline byte */\n    buf[n] = '\\n';\n    int total = n + 1;\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    int written = 0;\n    if (w->fp) {\n        written = (int)fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)total, w->fp);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    return (written == total) ? 0 : -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ emit helpers — common event prologue */\nstatic void begin_event(json_writer_t *jw, const char *type, double ts)\n{\n    json_writer_object(jw);\n    json_writer_key(jw, \"event\");
