    "originalFile":"/* src/014-event-queue.c — multi-producer event queue with a\n * dedicated writer thread.\n *\n * Design: singly-linked queue under one mutex; one CV the writer\n * thread sleeps on when the queue is empty. Producers lock just\n * long enough to append a node and signal the CV. The writer\n * thread snapshots `head` (atomically swaps it with NULL) under\n * the lock, then drains the snapshot outside the lock — so the\n * serialization + fwrite work happens with zero producer\n * contention.\n *\n * The architecture doc's MPSC ring with Vyukov-style sequence\n * numbers is the next refinement once profiling shows the brief\n * append-mutex contention is the bottleneck. The shape of the\n * API stays the same.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Event record */\ntypedef enum {\n    EV_RUN_START,\n    EV_TASK_SUBMIT,\n    EV_TASK_START,\n    EV_TASK_END,\n    EV_RUN_END,\n} event_kind_t;\n\n#define MAP_BUF_SZ    128\n#define BOX_ID_BUF_SZ 64\n\ntypedef struct event_node {\n    struct event_node *next;\n    event_kind_t       kind;\n    double             ts;\n    union {\n        struct {\n            char map[MAP_BUF_SZ];\n            int  n_workers;\n        } run_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            char box_id[BOX_ID_BUF_SZ];\n            int  worker_idx;\n        } task_submit;\n\n        struct {\n            int task_id;\n            int worker_idx;\n        } task_start;\n\n        struct {\n            int  task_id;\n            int  worker_idx;\n            long duration_us;\n            int  output_size;\n        } task_end;\n\n        struct {\n            long duration_us;\n            int  n_tasks;\n        } run_end;\n    } u;\n} event_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Queue struct */\nstruct event_queue {\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   cv;\n    event_node_t    *head;\n    event_node_t    *tail;\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    pthread_t        writer_thread;\n    jsonl_writer_t  *writer;\n\n    _Atomic int      pending;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ copy_str_bounded() — strncpy + always-NUL-terminate */\nstatic void copy_str_bounded(char *dst, const char *src, size_t cap)\n{\n    if (cap == 0) return;\n    if (!src) { dst[0] = '\\0'; return; }\n    size_t n = strlen(src);\n    if (n >= cap) n = cap - 1;\n    memcpy(dst, src, n);\n    dst[n] = '\\0';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ enqueue() — append a node, signal the writer */\nstatic void enqueue(event_queue_t *q, event_node_t *n)\n{\n    n->next = NULL;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    if (q->tail) q->tail->next = n;\n    else         q->head       = n;\n    q->tail = n;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&q->cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&q->pending, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_one() — serialize one event through jsonl_emit_* */\nstatic void write_one(event_queue_t *q, const event_node_t *n)\n{\n    switch (n->kind) {\n        case EV_RUN_START:\n            jsonl_emit_run_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                 n->u.run_start.map,\n                                 n->u.run_start.n_workers);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_SUBMIT:\n            jsonl_emit_task_submit(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.task_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.box_id,\n                                   n->u.task_submit.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_START:\n            jsonl_emit_task_start(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                  n->u.task_start.task_id,\n                                  n->u.task_start.worker_idx);\n            break;\n        case EV_TASK_END:\n            jsonl_emit_task_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                                n->u.task_end.task_id,\n                                n->u.task_end.worker_idx,\n                                n->u.task_end.duration_us,\n                                n->u.task_end.output_size);\n            break;\n        case EV_RUN_END:\n            jsonl_emit_run_end(q->writer, n->ts,\n                               n->u.run_end.duration_us,\n                               n->u.run_end.n_tasks);\n            break;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ writer_main() — drain loop */\nstatic void *writer_main(void *arg)\n{\n    event_queue_t *q = (event_queue_t *)arg;\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n        while (!q->head && !atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&q->cv, &q->mtx);\n        }\n        event_node_t *batch = q->head;\n        q->head = NULL;\n        q->tail = NULL;\n        int shutting = atomic_load_explicit(&q->shutdown, memory_order_acquire);\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n\n        /* Drain the batch outside the lock — zero contention with\n         * producers while we encode + fwrite. */\n        while (batch) {\n            event_node_t *next = batch->next;\n            write_one(q, batch);\n            free(batch);\n            atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&q->pending, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n            batch = next;\n        }\n        if (shutting) {\n            /* Catch any stragglers that arrived between the snapshot\n             * and reading the shutdown flag. */\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n            batch = q->head; q->head = q->tail = NULL;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n            while (batch) {\n                event_node_t *next = batch->next;\n                write_one(q, batch);\n                free(batch);\n                atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&q->pending, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n                batch = next;\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_create() */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    event_queue_t *q = calloc(1, sizeof *q);\n    if (!q) return NULL;\n\n    q->writer = jsonl_writer_open(path);\n    if (!q->writer) { free(q); return NULL; }\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&q->mtx, NULL) != 0)        goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&q->cv,  NULL) != 0)        goto fail_cv;\n    atomic_init(&q->shutdown, 0);\n    atomic_init(&q->pending,  0);\n\n    if (pthread_create(&q->writer_thread, NULL, writer_main, q) != 0)\n        goto fail_thread;\n    return q;\n\nfail_thread:\n    pthread_cond_destroy(&q->cv);\nfail_cv:\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\nfail:\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_destroy() */\nvoid event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    /* Signal shutdown, wake the writer if it's parked. */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&q->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&q->cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&q->mtx);\n\n    pthread_join(q->writer_thread, NULL);\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&q->mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&q->cv);\n    jsonl_writer_close(q->writer);\n    free(q);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ event_queue_pending() */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q)\n{\n    return q ? atomic_load_explicit(&q->pending, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit functions */\nvoid event_queue_run_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n copy_str_bounded(n->u.run_start.map, map, MAP_BUF_SZ);\n    n->u.run_start.n_workers = n_workers;\n    enqueue(q, n);\n}\n\nvoid event_queue_task_submit(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n event_queue_task_start(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                            int task_id, int worker_idx)\n{\n    if (!q) return;\n    event_node_t *n = calloc(1, sizeof *n);\n    if (!n)     "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* For routing kinds that need them later — weights, thresholds —\n     * the parser leaves their fields zero in this iteration and adds\n     * them when those kinds are implemented. */\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). With\n     * our current specs (which all leave invoke_native NULL), the\n     * fallback runs and behaviour is unchanged — but the\n     * infrastructure is in place for future specialisation. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) {\n            b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n            continue;\n        }\n        b->use_native_invoke = 1;\n        /* Check outgoing connections: every call-box consumer must\n         * share my language. */\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections && b->use_native_invoke; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) continue;\n            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n            if (c->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n            if (!c->lang || strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) != 0) {\n                b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n            }\n        }\n        if (!b->use_native_invoke) continue;\n        /* Check incoming: every call-box producer feeding any of\n         * my inputs must share my language. */\n        for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && b->use_native_invoke; p++) {\n            const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n            for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections && b->use_native_invoke; k++) {\n                if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i) continue;\n                if (prod->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n                if (!prod->lang || strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) != 0) {\n                    b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes. Stored as\n     * a small array of arena-owned string pointers; the pool init\n     * can use it to skip specs no box in this map uses. */",

    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* For routing kinds that need them later — weights, thresholds —\n     * the parser leaves their fields zero in this iteration and adds\n     * them when those kinds are implemented. */\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx;           "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER:\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED:\n        case ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR:\n        default:\n            /* Not yet implemented in the dispatch layer; fall back\n             * to plain so the runtime doesn't deadlock. */\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n    }\n}",
          "new_string":"        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id, UINT32_MAX);\n            /* Mix the monotonic counter so consecutive invocations\n             * don't go to consecutive branches. xorshift32-like, no\n             * crypto pretensions. */\n            uint32_t h = i;\n            h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85ebca6bu;\n            h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xc2b2ae35u;\n            h ^= h >> 16;\n            uint32_t branch_idx = h % (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs;\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1 ||\n                !b->routing.weights) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to\n             * PRECISION. The last band absorbs floating-point\n             * rounding so the bands always sum to the whole range. */\n            enum { WEIGHTED_PRECISION = 1000 };\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                       (uint32_t)WEIGHTED_PRECISION);\n            double total = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                total += b->routing.weights[k];\n            }\n            if (total <= 0.0) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            int branch_idx = b->routing.n_outputs - 1;\n            double acc = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                acc += (b->routing.weights[k] / total) * WEIGHTED_PRECISION;\n                if ((double)i < acc) { branch_idx = k; break; }\n            }\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%d\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR:\n        default:\n            /* Distributor inspects downstream slot fill levels; not\n             * yet implemented. Fall back to plain so the runtime\n             * doesn't deadlock. */\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n    }\n}",

        }

          "new_string":"        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Mix the monotonic counter so consecutive invocations\n             * don't go to consecutive branches. xorshift32-style,\n             * no crypto pretensions. */\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id, UINT32_MAX);\n            uint32_t h = i;\n            h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85ebca6bu;\n            h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xc2b2ae35u;\n            h ^= h >> 16;\n            uint32_t branch_idx = h % (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs;\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1 ||\n                !b->routing.weights) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to a\n             * fixed precision. The last band absorbs floating-point\n             * rounding so the bands sum to the whole range. */\n            enum { WEIGHTED_PRECISION = 1000 };\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                       (uint32_t)WEIGHTED_PRECISION);\n            double total = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                total += b->routing.weights[k];\n            }\n            if (total <= 0.0) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            int branch_idx = b->routing.n_outputs - 1;\n            double acc = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < b->routing.n_outputs; k++) {\n                acc += (b->routing.weights[k] / total) * WEIGHTED_PRECISION;\n                if ((double)i < acc) { branch_idx = k; break; }\n            }\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%d\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR:\n        default:\n            /* Distributor inspects downstream slot fill levels; not\n             * yet implemented. Fall back to plain so the runtime\n             * doesn't deadlock. */\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n    }\n}",

All emits are thread-safe. */\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_start  (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           const char *map, int n_workers);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_submit(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *box_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_start (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_end   (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int worker_idx,\n                           long duration_us, int output_size);\n\nint jsonl_emit_run_end    (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           long duration_us, int n_tasks);\n\n/* Verbose events (opt-in via SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1).\n * `data` is logged as a string with the JSON writer's standard\n * escaping. Bytes containing NUL aren't supported; truncate to\n * the first NUL or the architecture's 4 KB cap. */\nint jsonl_emit_task_input (jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, int port_index,\n                           const char *data, int size);\n\nint jsonl_emit_task_output(jsonl_writer_t *w, double ts,\n                           int task_id, const char *data, int size);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_JSONL_EVENTS_H */\n",

The\n * mutex is what the MPSC ring buffer + dedicated writer thread\n * will replace once dispatch is producing events at rate.\n *\n * Buffer size is fixed at 512 bytes. Every event the architecture\n * doc defines fits comfortably; if a future event needs more it\n * can be bumped or made dynamic.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311.\n */\n\n#include \"013-jsonl-events.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#define EVENT_BUF 512\n\n/* {{{ Writer struct */\nstruct jsonl_writer {\n    FILE            *fp;\n    pthread_mutex_t  mtx;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_open() */\njsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)\n{\n    if (!path) return NULL;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    if (!fp) return NULL;\n    jsonl_writer_t *w = calloc(1, sizeof *w);\n    if (!w) { fclose(fp); return NULL; }\n    w->fp = fp;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&w->mtx, NULL) != 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        free(w);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return w;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ jsonl_writer_close() */\nvoid jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)\n{\n    if (!w) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&w->mtx);\n    if (w->fp) { fflush(w->fp); fclose(w->fp); w->fp = NULL; }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&w->mtx);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&w->mtx);\n    free(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ flush_line() — finalize the writer, append \\n, write under lock */\nstatic int flush_line(jsonl_writer_t *w, json_writer_t *jw, char *buf)\n{\n    int n = json_writer_finish(jw);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    if (n >= EVENT_BUF) return -1;     "originalFile":"/* src/014-event-queue.h — multi-producer event queue with a\n * dedicated writer thread.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: every worker thread (and the main\n * thread) calls into one of the emit functions; the queue\n * appends a small event record under a brief mutex and signals\n * the writer thread, which drains the queue in batches and writes\n * each event as a JSONL line to a file.\n *\n * Designed in issue 311. Decouples event emission from the JSON\n * encoding + fwrite hot path: every producer's critical section\n * is one node allocation plus a couple of pointer updates. The\n * MPSC-ring-with-sequence-numbers variant from the design doc is\n * the next refinement once profiling justifies it.\n *\n * Lifecycle: `event_queue_create(\"tmp/last-run.jsonl\")` opens the\n * file, spawns the writer thread, and is ready to receive events.\n * `event_queue_destroy` signals shutdown, joins the writer thread,\n * closes the file, and frees the queue. Any events still in the\n * queue at shutdown drain to the file before the thread exits.\n *\n * The emit functions are non-blocking from the producer's\n * perspective (modulo brief mutex contention). They never write to\n * the file directly.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n#define SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\ntypedef struct event_queue event_queue_t;\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Open `path` for writing (truncates), spawn the writer thread.\n * Returns NULL on failure. */\nevent_queue_t *event_queue_create(const char *path);\n\n/* Signal shutdown, drain remaining events, join the writer thread,\n * fflush+fclose, free the queue. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid           event_queue_destroy(event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emit (producer side) */\n/* Every emit clones its arguments into the queued event record;\n * the caller's pointers don't need to outlive the call. Truncated at NUL or 4 KB. */\nvoid event_queue_task_input (event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, int port_index,\n                             const char *data, int size);\n\nvoid event_queue_task_output(event_queue_t *q, double ts,\n                             int task_id, const char *data, int size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Inspection */\n/* Best-effort: returns the count of events currently queued\n * (between produce and drain). Mostly useful for diagnostics. */\nint event_queue_pending(const event_queue_t *q);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_EVENT_QUEUE_H */\n",

          "new_string":"    /* 6b. Open the run-log event queue and emit run_start. */\n    events = open_event_queue(map_dir, jsonl_path, sizeof jsonl_path);\n    if (events) {\n        ctx.events = events;\n        /* Verbose logging gates are opt-in per the architecture doc;\n         * off by default to keep the log small even for iteration-\n         * heavy maps. */\n        const char *lv = getenv(\"SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES\");\n        ctx.log_values = (lv && lv[0] && lv[0] != '0') ? 1 : 0;\n\n        event_queue_run_start(events, now_secs(),\n                              graph_name(g), pool_n_workers(pool));\n\n        /* Slot allocator events — one per input slot, plus one per\n         * iterator counter slot, all fired right after attach so\n         * the run log records the full slot layout up front. */\n        const char *ls = getenv(\"SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS\");\n        if (ls && ls[0] && ls[0] != '0') {\n            double ts = now_secs();\n            for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {\n                const box_t *b = graph_box(g, i);\n                if (b->input_slot_ids) {\n                    int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? 16 : 1;\n                    for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n                        event_queue_slot_alloc(events, ts,\n                            b->input_slot_ids[j], 4096, n_cells,\n                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n                    }\n                }\n                if (b->counter_slot_id >= 0) {\n                    event_queue_slot_alloc(events, ts,\n                        b->counter_slot_id, 4, 1, b->id, \"<counter>\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/008-pool-runner.c"

          "old_string":"/* {{{ test_load_branching() — comparator + iterator routing kinds */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_native_invoke_classification() */\n/* Verifies issue 312's same-language fast-path classification:\n * a call box whose every adjacent call box shares its language\n * is marked use_native_invoke; otherwise not. */\nstatic int test_native_invoke_classification(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n\n    /* hello: data box feeds greet (lua). greet's only producer is\n     * a data box (no lang), no consumers — eligible. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n        const box_t *who   = graph_box_by_id(g, \"who\");\n        ASSERT(greet->use_native_invoke == 1);\n        ASSERT(who->use_native_invoke   == 0);   /* who is BOX_DATA */\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n\n    /* comparator: all four boxes are lua, no cross-language wires\n     * → every call box is native-eligible. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/comparator\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"classify\")->use_native_invoke == 1);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"low\")     ->use_native_invoke == 1);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"mid\")     ->use_native_invoke == 1);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"high\")    ->use_native_invoke == 1);\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n\n    /* pipeline: lua → c → bash chain → no call box stays inside\n     * one language → none should be native-eligible. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/pipeline\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"double\")->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"addone\")->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"shout\") ->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_randomizer_weighted_parsing() */\n/* Verifies issue 304's randomizer and weighted routing schemas\n * load cleanly with the right per-kind fields. */\nstatic int test_randomizer_weighted_parsing(void)\n{\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-routing-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    ASSERT(dir);\n\n    char path[4096];\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"r\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"rnd\\\"}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir); mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/rnd.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"rnd\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"lang\\\":\\\"lua\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"ref\\\":\\\"r.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"r\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"randomizer\\\",\\\"n_outputs\\\":4}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/wtd.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"wtd\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"lang\\\":\\\"lua\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"ref\\\":\\\"r.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"w\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"weighted\\\",\\\"weights\\\":[0.8,0.2]}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    const box_t *rnd = graph_box_by_id(g, \"rnd\");\n    const box_t *wtd = graph_box_by_id(g, \"wtd\");\n    ASSERT(rnd->routing.kind      == ROUTING_RANDOMIZER);\n    ASSERT(rnd->routing.n_outputs == 4);\n    ASSERT(wtd->routing.kind      == ROUTING_WEIGHTED);\n    ASSERT(wtd->routing.n_outputs == 2);\n    ASSERT(wtd->routing.weights   != NULL);\n    ASSERT(wtd->routing.weights[0] == 0.8);\n    ASSERT(wtd->routing.weights[1] == 0.2);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n\n    /* Cleanup. */\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/rnd.json\", dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/wtd.json\", dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\",     dir); unlink(path);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\",         dir); rmdir(path);\n    rmdir(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_branching() — comparator + iterator routing kinds */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/010-graph-loader-test.c"
        }
      }],

        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ push_one_connection() — push to a single connection's slot */\nstatic int push_one_connection(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                               const connection_t *c,\n                               const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    if (c->to_box_idx < 0) return 0;\n    const box_t *dst = graph_box(ctx->graph, c->to_box_idx);\n    if (!dst || !dst->input_slot_ids) return 0;\n    if (c->to_input_idx < 0 || c->to_input_idx >= dst->n_inputs) return 0;\n    if (slot_push(ctx->slots, dst->input_slot_ids[c->to_input_idx],\n                  out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' → '%s'.%s: push failed\\n\",\n                b->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(ctx, c->to_box_idx, 0);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_branch() — push only to outgoing connections matching `branch` */\n/* `branch` is one of \"lt\" / \"eq\" / \"gt\" / \"out_<n>\". Connections\n * whose from_branch is NULL (plain) are skipped; connections whose\n * from_branch equals `branch` fire. */\nstatic int push_branch(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const char *branch,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    int fired = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (!c->from_branch) continue;\n        if (strcmp(c->from_branch, branch) != 0) continue;\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, c, out_bytes, out_size) != 0) return -1;\n        fired++;\n    }\n    return fired;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, &b->connections[i],\n                                out_bytes, out_size) != 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ push_one_connection() — push to a single connection's slot */\n/* The `tag` is the ordering hint for cell-tagged consumer slots\n * (issue 304's iterator-ordering rule). Key Technical Concepts:\n   - C thread pool with pthreads, init barrier (3-stage), per-worker init/teardown hooks\n   - Per-input-port slot store with three modes: 1-cell peek, N-cell pop ring, atomic counter\n   - Cell tagging for parallel iterator ordering (`SLOT_TAGGED` flag)\n   - Per-slot atomic_flag spinlock\n   - Language spec registry with dlopen of `langs/<name>/spec.so`, `lang_spec_t` C contract\n   - Per-worker spec handles (`worker_ctx_t.handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS]`)\n   - SOCK_CLOEXEC for fork+exec correctness\n   - Persistent bash subprocess via socketpair + line protocol (n_args/file/fn/args request, status/length/bytes response)\n   - C box compile via gcc -shared -fPIC; lazy .c→.so via path hashing\n   - Lua per-worker module cache in `LUA_REGISTRYINDEX`\n   - JSON DOM parser with chunked-bump arena, recursive descent, BMP + surrogate pair handling\n   - JSON streaming writer with depth stack for bracket/comma placement\n   - JSONL run-log events: `run_start`, `task_submit`, `task_start`, `task_end`, `run_end`, `task_input`, `task_output`, `slot_alloc`\n   - MPSC event queue with dedicated writer thread (mutex-based, drains in batches outside lock)\n   - Dispatch action: read inputs → invoke spec → routing-aware push → spawn-on-input-ready\n   - Routing kinds: plain, comparator (lt/eq/gt), iterator (atomic counter), randomizer (xorshift hash), weighted (cumulative bands), distributor (deferred)\n   - Iterator multi-spawn re-fire when POP inputs remain\n   - Multi-spawn propagation BFS from iterators forward through connection graph\n   - Same-language fast path (`use_native_invoke` classification, `invoke_native`/`invoke_json`/bridge callbacks)\n   - Language-filtered worker init (skip specs the map doesn't use)\n   - Spec discovery via /proc/self/exe\n   - Verbose logging gates: `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`, `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`\n\n3. Files and Code Sections:\n   - `langs/lang-spec.h`: Extended `lang_spec_t` with `invoke_native`, `invoke_json`, `native_to_json`, `json_to_native` callbacks. Defines `lang_invoke_fn` and `lang_bridge_fn` typedefs.\n   - `src/008-pool-runner.c`: The main entry point. Full lifecycle: load graph, create slot store + spec registry, attach runtime, set worker init/teardown callbacks with language-filtered spec init, init barrier, open event queue, push literals, spawn ready boxes, wait quiescent, emit run_end, teardown. Added `find_langs_dir()` for `/proc/self/exe`-based spec discovery. Added `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1` slot_alloc emit loop. Has `struct spec_init_args { spec_registry_t *registry; const char **languages; int n_languages; }`.\n   - `src/009-slot-store.{c,h}`: Slot store with all three modes, cell tagging, per-slot spinlock.\n   - `src/010-graph-loader.{c,h}`: Graph loader with parse, validate, topology, cycles, slot allocation, spec resolution, multi-spawn propagation, language enumeration, and **312 fast-path classification** now in graph_load (moved from graph_attach_runtime). Box_t has `use_native_invoke`, `multi_spawn`, `input_slot_modes`, `counter_slot_id`, `spec_idx`, `input_slot_ids`. Routing_t has `comparand`, `n_outputs`, `weights` (malloc'd, freed in graph_destroy).\n   - `src/011-spec-registry.{c,h}`: Registry with dlopen, added `spec_registry_init_worker_filtered(r, idx, handles, cap, langs, n_langs)`.\n   - `src/012-dispatch.{c,h}`: Full dispatch action. Auto-re-spawn for multi-spawn boxes with POP inputs. dispatch_ctx_t has `events`, `log_values`, `next_task_id`. **Recent change**: invoke resolution picks invoke_native > invoke_json > invoke based on `b->use_native_invoke`.\n   - `src/013-jsonl-events.{c,h}`: JSONL event writers. Added `jsonl_emit_task_input`, `jsonl_emit_task_output`, `jsonl_emit_slot_alloc`. Uses 8KB buffer for verbose events.\n   - `src/014-event-queue.{c,h}`: Event queue with writer thread. Verbose events bypass queue and write directly through writer's mutex.\n   - `libs/json/json.{c,h}`: JSON parser/writer. Recent fix: parse_number rejects `0\\d+` (strict leading zero, RFC 8259).\n   - `libs/task-pool/pool.{c,h}`: Pool with `pool_set_worker_init` and `pool_set_worker_teardown` callbacks. 3-stage init barrier (init_starting, workers_ready, init_released).\n   - `langs/lua/spec.c`: Lua spec with per-worker module cache via LUA_REGISTRYINDEX.\n   - `langs/c/spec.c`: C spec with gcc compile + dlopen + lazy .c→.so via hash_path.\n   - `langs/bash/spec.c`: Bash spec with persistent socketpair + SOCK_CLOEXEC + line protocol.\n   - `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`: Persistent bash subprocess.\n   - `langs/{lua,c,bash}/Makefile`: Recent fix — added `$(DIR)/langs/lang-spec.h` as dependency so spec.so rebuilds when header changes.\n   - `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c`: 13 tests including new `native_invoke_classification` and `randomizer_weighted_parsing`.\n   - `tests/012-dispatch-test.c`: 7 tests including comparator_routing, iterator_routing_single_fire, iterator_multi_fire.\n   - `scripts/run-tests.sh`: Integration runner verifying all 5 fixtures.\n   - `tests/maps/{calc,hello,comparator,iter-route,pipeline}/`: 5 working fixture maps.\n   - `issues/phase-3-progress.md`: Tracking table.\n\n4.       "content":"/* {{{ push_routed() — branch picker over routing.kind, then push */\nstatic int push_routed(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    /* Data and file_write boxes don't carry a routing kind; their\n     * output fans plain. Same for call boxes with no routing set\n     * (treated as plain). */\n    if (b->kind != BOX_CALL) return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n    switch (b->routing.kind) {\n        case ROUTING_PLAIN:\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            const char *branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Mix the monotonic counter so consecutive invocations\n             * don't go to consecutive branches. xorshift32-style,\n             * no crypto pretensions. */\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id, UINT32_MAX);\n            uint32_t h = i;\n            h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85ebca6bu;\n            h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xc2b2ae35u;\n            h ^= h >> 16;\n            uint32_t branch_idx = h % (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs;\n            char branch[24];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", branch_idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1 ||\n                !b->routing.weights) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to a\n             * fixed precision.       "content":"/* {{{ slot_has_value() */\nint slot_has_value(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r) return 0;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return 1;\n\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        /* Tagged: any filled cell counts. Cheap scan; tagged slots\n         * are usually small. */\n        lock_slot(r);\n        int found = 0;\n        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r->n_cells; i++) {\n            if (cell_filled(r, i) != 0) { found = 1; break; }\n        }\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return found;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n    return head != tail;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_fill_count() */\nint32_t slot_fill_count(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    slot_rec_t *r = get_slot(s, id);\n    if (!r)                                  return 0;\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) return 0;\n\n    if (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) {\n        lock_slot(r);\n        int32_t n = 0;\n        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r->n_cells; i++) {\n            if (cell_filled(r, i) != 0) n++;\n        }\n        unlock_slot(r);\n        return n;\n    }\n\n    uint32_t head = atomic_load_explicit(&r->head, memory_order_acquire);\n    uint32_t tail = atomic_load_explicit(&r->tail, memory_order_acquire);\n    return (int32_t)(tail - head);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]];         "input":{
          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ link the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A symlink keeps the artifact small and lets a rebuild of the runner\n# propagate automatically. If the user wants a fully detached copy\n# they can replace the link with a cp afterwards.\nln -sf \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/soramech-compile.sh"
        }
      }],

    "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ link the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A symlink keeps the artifact small and lets a rebuild of the runner\n# propagate automatically. If the user wants a fully detached copy\n# they can replace the link with a cp afterwards.\nln -sf \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",

Copying keeps the compiled artifact","+# self-describing and portable.","+cp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"","+chmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\""," # }}}"," "," # {{{ write manifest.json"],

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ link the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A symlink keeps the artifact small and lets a rebuild of the runner\n# propagate automatically. If the user wants a fully detached copy\n# they can replace the link with a cp afterwards.\nln -sf \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"# {{{ link the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A symlink keeps the artifact small and lets a rebuild of the runner\n# propagate automatically. If the user wants a fully detached copy\n# they can replace the link with a cp afterwards.\nln -sf \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}",
    "newString":"# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}",

A more\n * polished version locates the script next to the spec.so via\n * /proc/self/exe, landing with issue 309's spec discovery work. */\nstatic const char *server_path(void)\n{\n    const char *p = getenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER\");\n    return (p && *p) ? p : DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_all() — write n bytes, retrying on partial writes */\nstatic int write_all(int fd, const void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    const char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t w = write(fd, p, left);\n        if (w < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w == 0) return -1;\n        p    += w;\n        left -= (size_t)w;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_exact() — read exactly n bytes from fd */\nstatic int read_exact(int fd, void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, p, left);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        p    += r;\n        left -= (size_t)r;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
