        "content":"1\t# 302 — Per-task slot store with wire-held references\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\tWire values are passed through stdout pipes and transient strings. Values\n8\thave no addressable location, no reference count, and no cross-language\n9\taccessibility. Each value vanishes once the pipe is drained.\n10\t\n11\t## Concept\n12\t\n13\t### Slots belong to input ports, not tasks\n14\t\n15\tEach box has **one slot per input port**, allocated when the graph\n16\tloads and persisting for the life of the run. A wire is a routing\n17\tdeclaration: \"the producer's output port pushes a copy of its value\n18\tinto this consumer's named input slot.\" The producer never owns a\n19\tslot — its output is a routing event, not a stored value.\n20\t\n21\tWhen a producer fires, the dispatch layer copies the value into\n22\tevery downstream input slot wired to that output. Fan-out is N\n23\tpushes (one per consumer); fan-in is N producers all pushing into\n24\tthe same consumer's slot. Both behaviors fall out of the same\n25\tpush-into-input-slot mechanic.\n26\t\n27\tSlots live in process heap memory, accessible to every worker\n28\tthread. Cross-process visibility is not required: language specs\n29\t(issue 303) only ever receive byte pointers — never raw slot\n30\taddresses — so out-of-process specs (Bash) work via sockets, not\n31\tshared memory.\n32\t\n33\t### Tasks are ephemeral; box state is durable\n34\t\n35\tA **task** is one invocation: pop one value from each of the box's\n36\tinput slots, run the box's logic, push the output to every\n37\tdownstream input slot. Tasks have no persistent identity — they're\n38\tjust stack frames on workers. Tasks are spawned dynamically by the\n39\tdispatch layer when a box's input set is ready (every input slot\n40\tholds at least one value).\n41\t\n42\tThe **box** is the durable thing: it owns its input port slots, any\n43\tcounter state (for iterators), its language spec handle, and so\n44\ton. The box exists from graph load until run end. Tasks come and\n45\tgo.\n46\t\n47\tThis is uniform across iterator and non-iterator boxes. Both run N\n48\ttimes where N depends on how many invocations their inputs supply\n49\t(possibly 1, possibly thousands). The difference is just what the\n50\ttask does:\n51\t- **Plain call task**: invoke spec on the popped values, push the\n52\t  return to outputs.\n53\t- **Iterator task**: read box's counter, route the popped value to\n54\t  output port `iterator_outputs[counter]`, increment counter mod N.\n55\t  No spec invocation.\n56\t- **Comparator task**: invoke spec on the popped values, compare\n57\t  the return against `comparand`, route to the matching `lt` /\n58\t  `eq` / `gt` branch.\n59\t\n60\t### All slots are ring buffers; read mode varies\n61\t\n62\tThere is one slot type. It is a ring buffer of `n_cells` cells,\n63\teach of `cell_capacity` bytes. The number of cells (`n_cells`) and\n64\tthe read mode are both compile-time properties of the input port:\n65\t\n66\t- **1-cell + peek mode**: the value the producer wrote stays in the\n67\t  cell. Tasks read via `slot_peek` — read without draining — and\n68\t  every subsequent task on this consumer reads the same value\n69\t  unless the producer overwrites it. Used for **single-push wires**\n70\t  (a literal, or a wire from a producer box whose invocation count\n71\t  is exactly 1). Multiple consumer tasks read the value as many\n72\t  times as needed; the cell is never empty.\n73\t- **N-cell + pop mode**: a queue. Producers push; consumers\n74\t  `slot_pop` — drain one cell per task. Used for **multi-push wires**:\n75\t  any wire whose producer has more than one task invocation\n76\t  during the run. The producer's pushes accumulate, the consumer\n77\t  drains in pop order.\n78\t\n79\tCompile-time analysis classifies each wire. A producer is\n80\t\"runs-once\" if no transitive ancestor is an iterator; otherwise\n81\tit's \"runs-N-times.\" Wires from runs-once producers get 1-cell\n82\tpeek slots; wires from runs-N-times producers get N-cell pop slots.\n83\t\n84\t`n_cells` for pop slots is sized for worst-case backlog (or a\n85\tdefault like 64 with growth on demand). Lists grow if the producer\n86\toutruns the consumer past the pre-allocation.\n87\t\n88\tFan-in: multiple producers pushing into the same N-cell pop slot\n89\tland in arrival order. The consumer pops FIFO unless the cell\n90\tcarries an ordering tag (see \"Cell tagging\" below).\n91\t\n92\t### Atomic-counter slot mode\n93\t\n94\tA slot allocated with `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` carries a single\n95\t4-byte unsigned integer cell, read via a special op:\n96\t\n97\t```c\n98\tuint32_t slot_read_inc(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, uint32_t mod);\n99\t// Returns the current value mod `mod`, then atomically increments\n100\t// the underlying counter. Concurrent readers each get a distinct\n101\t// value. Counter wraps at 2^32; mod handles N-branch routing.\n102\t```\n103\t\n104\tUsed for iterator counters (issue 304): the iterator box has an\n105\tauto-allocated `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot at load time; the\n106\tdispatch action calls `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_branches)`\n107\tto pick its output branch. Multiple iterator tasks can read\n108\tconcurrently from the same counter slot in parallel — each gets a\n109\tunique routing index — without any per-box mutable state and\n110\twithout the serial dependency of a self-push counter.\n111\t\n112\tThe slot's \"cell\" is just an `atomic_uint32_t`. No push is ever\n113\tperformed; reads do the work. From the dispatch action's\n114\tperspective it's just another slot; from the slot store's\n115\tperspective the read op is special-cased.\n116\t\n117\t### Cell tagging (for parallel-iterator ordering)\n118\t\n119\tA cell can optionally carry a 4-byte ordering tag alongside its\n120\tsize and data:\n121\t\n122\t```\n123\tCell layout (N-cell pop slot)\n124\tOffset  Size  Field\n125\t------  ----  -----\n126\t0       4     filled_size\n127\t4       4     tag      (0 if untagged; iterator counter snapshot otherwise)\n128\t8       …     data\n129\t```\n130\t\n131\tSlots created for wires from parallel iterators (issue 304) are\n132\ttagged. Pop on a tagged slot returns the cell with the lowest tag,\n133\tnot the head cell — preserving iterator-counter order across pushes\n134\tthat arrived out of order from parallel iterator workers.\n135\t\n136\tUntagged slots default tag to 0 and pop FIFO at no extra cost. The\n137\ttag-aware pop is a per-slot mode flag set at allocation time.\n138\t\n139\t### Asynchrony\n140\tThe store is fully asynchronous. Slots are allocated, filled, read, and\n141\tfreed at any time, on any thread, with no global lock. Synchronization\n142\tis per-slot. There is no central allocator-wide mutex.\n143\t\n144\t## Slot layout\n145\t\n146\tEach slot is a header followed by `n_cells` cells, each `cell_capacity`\n147\tbytes. The header tracks ring-buffer state and lifetime:\n148\t\n149\t```\n150\tSlot header\n151\tOffset  Size  Field\n152\t------  ----  -----\n153\t0       4     cell_capacity   (bytes per cell, set at allocation)\n154\t4       4     n_cells         (ring size, set at allocation)\n155\t8       4     head            (read index, mod n_cells)\n156\t12      4     tail            (write index, mod n_cells; cells_filled = tail - head)\n157\t16      1     touched         (per-slot lock: 0=free, 1=another thread mutating)\n158\t17      3     _pad\n159\t20      …     cells           (n_cells * (4-byte size + cell_capacity bytes))\n160\t```\n161\t\n162\tEach cell stores a 4-byte filled-size followed by `cell_capacity`\n163\tbytes of value data. Cells have wildly different capacities across\n164\tslots — capacity is per-slot, not global. The C convention of passing\n165\tsizes alongside arrays applies: the task that allocates a slot knows\n166\thow big it needs the cells.\n167\t\n168\t`touched` is a single-byte flag toggled around any header mutation\n169\t(push, pop, refcount changes). A reader that finds `touched == 1`\n170\tspins until it clears. This is the simplest possible per-slot lock —\n171\tif contention proves to matter, replace with a proper mutex without\n172\tchanging the API.\n173\t\n174\tWrites to a cell complete with a memory barrier before `tail` is\n175\tadvanced, so a reader that observes `head < tail` is guaranteed to\n176\tsee the complete value at the head cell.\n177\t\n178\t## Lifetime\n179\t\n180\tSlots are owned by the box that holds the input port. They live\n181\tfrom graph load until run end. There is no per-slot reference\n182\tcounting and no end-of-stream propagation — the slot is freed\n183\twhen the run ends, alongside its owning box.\n184\t\n185\tRun termination is governed entirely by the pool's active-task\n186\tcounter (issue 301): when no task is running and no further spawns\n187\tare pending, the run is over. There's nothing the slot store needs\n188\tto track to make this work.\n189\t\n190\t### No wait lists\n191\t\n192\tTasks never park on slots. Tasks are spawned by the dispatch\n193\tlayer's spawn-on-input-arrival rule and run to completion; they\n194\tnever block. A slot that has no value yet simply means the\n195\tspawn rule hasn't fired for that consumer yet. No wait list,\n196\tno per-slot wake-up traversal — just a check after each push.\n197\t\n198\t## Backing store\n199\t\n200\tSlots are allocated from process heap memory. The slot store owns a\n201\tper-run allocator (described under \"Allocation strategy\" below) that\n202\thands out memory chunks to slots. Plain `malloc`-class memory is\n203\tsufficient — every worker thread in the process can read and write\n204\tit, and no spec ever needs to access it from a child process.\n205\t\n206\tSynchronization within a slot uses the per-slot `touched` flag for\n207\theader mutations. There is no allocator-wide mutex on the\n208\tread/write path; only the per-size-class free lists in the\n209\tallocator have their own locks.\n210\t\n211\t## Slot creation\n212\t\n213\tSlot creation happens at **graph load**, not per task. The graph\n214\tloader walks every box, allocates one ring buffer per input port,\n215\tand parks the slot on the box's per-port slot table. The dispatch\n216\tlayer never allocates new slots at runtime in the steady state —\n217\tall slots that will ever exist are created up front.\n218\t\n219\t```c\n220\tslot_id_t slot_alloc(slot_store_t *store, int cell_capacity, int n_cells);\n221\t```\n222\t\n223\t`cell_capacity` and `n_cells` come from compile-time analysis of\n224\tthe graph. Boxes downstream of iterators get larger `n_cells` to\n225\tabsorb the iterator's worst-case backlog.\n226\t\n227\tIf a slot's pre-allocated `n_cells` proves too small at runtime\n228\t(producer outpaces consumer beyond the pre-allocation), the slot's\n229\tring grows — see \"Allocation strategy\" below.\n230\t\n231\t## C API surface\n232\t\n233\t```c\n234\tslot_id_t slot_alloc       (slot_store_t *s, int cell_capacity, int n_cells, int flags);\n235\tvoid      slot_push        (slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, const void *data, int size, uint32_t tag);\n236\tint       slot_peek        (slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, void *buf, int buf_size); // 1-cell: read without draining\n237\tint       slot_pop         (slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, void *buf, int buf_size); // N-cell: drain head (or lowest-tag)\n238\tuint32_t  slot_read_inc    (slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id, uint32_t mod);            // SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER only\n239\tint       slot_has_value   (slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id);                          // for spawn-rule check\n240\t```\n241\t\n242\tFlags include:\n243\t- `SLOT_TAGGED`: cells carry ordering tags; `slot_pop` returns the\n244\t  lowest-tag cell.\n245\t- `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`: slot holds a single atomic uint32; reads\n246\t  via `slot_read_inc` only. `slot_push` / `slot_peek` / `slot_pop`\n247\t  are not valid on atomic-counter slots.\n248\t\n249\tPush always takes a `tag` argument; untagged slots ignore it (or\n250\ttreat 0 as \"no order\").\n251\t\n252\t1-cell peek slot use: producer `push` once at startup (literal) or\n253\twhen its single invocation completes (single-push wire). All\n254\tconsumer tasks `peek` to read the value as many times as their box\n255\truns. The cell is never empty after the initial push.\n256\t\n257\tN-cell pop slot use: producers `push` repeatedly. Consumer tasks\n258\t`pop` one cell each. For tagged slots, `pop` returns the\n259\tlowest-tag cell; for untagged, FIFO. Pop on an empty slot is a\n260\tbug — the spawn rule guarantees the slot is non-empty before a\n261\ttask spawns.\n262\t\n263\tThere is no `slot_ref` / `slot_unref` — slot lifetime is the run.\n264\t\n265\t## Submission timing\n266\t\n267\tTasks are spawned dynamically in response to slot pushes. Each box\n268\thas small per-box state used by the dispatch layer:\n269\t\n270\t```\n271\tbox_runtime_state {\n272\t    slot_id_t  *input_slots;     // one per input port (set at load)\n273\t    int        *port_modes;      // PEEK or POP, per input port\n274\t    int         n_inputs;\n275\t    slot_id_t   counter_slot;    // iterator only: SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER slot;\n276\t                                 // 0 / unused otherwise\n277\t};\n278\t```\n279\t\n280\tThe spawning rule:\n281\t- When a producer pushes to one of a box's input slots, the\n282\t  dispatch layer checks **does every input slot have a value\n283\t  available?** \"Available\" means:\n284\t  - For peek-mode (1-cell) slots: cell has been written at least\n285\t    once. Once a peek slot is filled, it stays available — every\n286\t    subsequent spawn-check on this box passes the peek-port check.\n287\t  - For pop-mode (N-cell) slots: queue is non-empty.\n288\t- If yes, spawn a `dispatch_task_t` and submit to the pool. The\n289\t  task pops (or peeks) one value from each input slot when it\n290\t  runs.\n291\t- Each push that completes the input set triggers exactly one\n292\t  spawn. Multiple pushes accumulate in pop slots; each pop\n293\t  consumes one, and if more remain, the next push (or check)\n294\t  re-fires the spawn rule.\n295\t\n296\tThis makes the pool's queue the rate buffer: pushes accumulate\n297\tin pop slots (possibly multiple per slot), and one task per\n298\taccumulated value gets spawned.\n299\t\n300\tTasks never block on slots. They're spawned after inputs are\n301\tready, run to completion, and disappear. Blocking-and-waking\n302\tmachinery is unnecessary — the spawn-on-arrival rule is the\n303\tsynchronization primitive.\n304\t\n305\tThe pool's queue is the only queue. There is no separate \"blocked\n306\ttasks\" structure.\n307\t\n308\t## Allocation strategy: size-class free lists with coalescing fallback\n309\t\n310\tThe slot store uses a segregated free-list allocator. The map is\n311\tanalyzed at compile time to enumerate every distinct slot size the\n312\tgraph will need (each call box declares its output slot size; each\n313\tqueued-input ring declares its total size from cell capacity × queue\n314\tdepth). The allocator builds one free list per distinct size class.\n315\t\n316\tVariable-size and unknown-size payloads (a long LLM response, an\n317\tarray whose length is not known until runtime) are handled by a\n318\tseparate **large-value heap** described below — not by allocating\n319\thuge slots up front.\n320\t\n321\t### The lists\n322\tEach size class is an array (or linked list) of free slots of exactly\n323\tthat size. At startup, each list is pre-populated with enough slots\n324\tto cover the static box count for that size. Lists grow during the\n325\trun if demand exceeds the pre-allocation.\n326\t\n327\tEach list has its own mutex — allocation and deallocation in different\n328\tsize classes never contend with each other.\n329\t\n330\t### Allocation\n331\tGiven a request for size N bytes:\n332\t1. Find the smallest size class with `class_size ≥ N`.\n333\t2. If that class has a free slot, pop it. Done.\n334\t3. Otherwise, try the next larger size class. Repeat.\n335\t4. If a larger class hits, the slot is oversized for the request.\n336\t   Try to slice the unused tail into a residual slot. If the residual\n337\t   is at least as large as the smallest size class, push it onto that\n338\t   class's list. Otherwise skip the slice — oversize the allocation\n339\t   and live with the waste until the slot is freed.\n340\t5. If no size class has a free slot, attempt to coalesce: walk the\n341\t   address-ordered chunk list looking for adjacent free chunks that\n342\t   together meet the requested size. If found, merge them and return\n343\t   the combined chunk.\n344\t6. If coalescing fails, grow the region (see \"Growth\" below) and\n345\t   append the new slots to the appropriate lists. Then try again.\n346\t7. After steps 5 or 6 complete, queue a deferred cleanup task on the\n347\t   pool. Cleanup runs on a worker thread later and walks the\n348\t   chunk list to opportunistically coalesce contiguous free chunks\n349\t   into the largest possible chunks. Cleanup is best-effort — it\n350\t   does not block any other thread. If memory fragments faster than\n351\t   cleanup can keep up, the next allocation grows the heap; that's\n352\t   fine.\n353\t\n354\t### Deallocation\n355\tWhen refcount drops to zero, the slot is pushed onto its size class's\n356\tfree list. The deallocator also performs a cheap eager-coalesce step:\n357\tcheck the slot's two physical neighbors; if either is free, merge\n358\tthem and push the combined chunk onto the appropriate size class.\n359\tThis is O(1) given the doubly-linked chunk list (see below) and keeps\n360\tsmall-scale fragmentation in check without needing the deferred\n361\tcleanup task to run.\n362\t\n363\t### Physical-order chunk list (for coalescing)\n364\tCoalescing needs to know which chunks are physically adjacent in\n365\tmemory. The size-class free lists don't carry that information.\n366\t\n367\tTwo viable representations:\n368\t\n369\t- **Doubly-linked list** of all chunks (free and allocated) in\n370\t  address order. Splits and merges are O(1) given the chunk pointer.\n371\t  Neighbor lookup is O(1). Pointer chasing is the cost.\n372\t- **Two parallel arrays** (`start[i]`, `end[i]`) sorted by start\n373\t  address. Lookup by binary search is O(log N), but inserts and\n374\t  deletes are O(N) without an additional index. Cache-friendly to\n375\t  scan.\n376\t\n377\tThe linked list is simpler and has the right asymptotic behavior for\n378\tsplits/merges, which dominate. Start there. If profiling later shows\n379\tlist traversal is hot, switch to the array form with an auxiliary\n380\tindex — the API doesn't change.\n381\t\n382\t### Large-value heap (variable-size payloads)\n383\t\n384\tFor values whose size is not known at compile time — long LLM\n385\tresponses, dynamically-sized arrays, anything where the upper bound\n386\tis not a useful number to allocate — the slot does not hold the value\n387\tdirectly. Instead, the slot holds a small fixed-size handle:\n388\t\n389\t```\n390\t{ uint32_t size; uint32_t lvh_offset; }\n391\t```\n392\t\n393\t`lvh_offset` points into a separate **large-value heap**, a\n394\tplain `malloc`-backed region used only for variable-size payloads.\n395\tWhen a box produces a 4 MB LLM response, the dispatch layer:\n396\t1. Allocates 4 MB in the large-value heap.\n397\t2. Writes the bytes there.\n398\t3. Stores the handle (size = 4 MB, offset = …) in the slot.\n399\t\n400\tThe consumer reads the handle from the slot, follows the offset,\n401\tcopies the bytes (or works with them in place). When the slot's\n402\trefcount hits zero, the slot's deallocator also frees the\n403\tlarge-value-heap region.\n404\t\n405\tThe slot allocator is unchanged — it always sees fixed-size slots.\n406\tThe two-tier approach keeps the hot path simple while still\n407\tsupporting unbounded outputs.\n408\t\n409\tA box opts into large-value output by declaring its output as\n410\t\"variable-size\" in the graph. Compile-time-known outputs use the\n411\tfixed-size path with no indirection.\n412\t\n413\t### Growth\n414\tWhen all size-class lists are exhausted and coalescing cannot satisfy\n415\ta request, the allocator grows by calling `malloc` for a new region,\n416\tdividing it into slots, and appending them to the relevant size-class\n417\tlists. Plain heap memory is fine — no spec needs cross-process access\n418\tto slot memory.\n419\t\n420\t### Why this design\n421\t- Compile-time enumeration makes every common allocation a single\n422\t  pop from a list. No size-comparison loops, no walks of free space.\n423\t- Slicing residuals cannot fragment beyond the granularity of the\n424\t  smallest declared size class, since smaller residuals are simply\n425\t  not split.\n426\t- Coalescing is the safety valve for unusual allocation patterns,\n427\t  and it costs nothing on the common path.\n428\t- Growth is rare — if pre-allocation matches static demand, it never\n429\t  fires.\n430\t\n431\t## No type tags\n432\t\n433\tSlots store opaque bytes. The producer wrote N bytes; the consumer\n434\treads N bytes. What those bytes mean is the language spec's business\n435\ton each side, and the wire's metadata in the graph (issue 219's\n436\tcompiler can check producer-output type vs consumer-input type at\n437\tbuild time). The slot store does not interpret values — it does not\n438\tneed to know if they are strings, numbers, JSON, images, or anything\n439\telse. Removed the type-tag field from the header for that reason.\n440\t\n441\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n442\t1. Write `src/slot-store.h` and `src/slot-store.c` — the C API above.\n443\t2. Unit test single-value slots: thread A writes, thread B reads,\n444\t   refcount decrements, slot freed when last ref dropped.\n445\t3. Unit test ring-buffer slots: multiple producers push, single consumer\n446\t   drains in order, no values lost or duplicated.\n447\t4. Integrate into `src/008-pool-runner.c`: shared memory created at\n448\t   startup, store handle passed to the dispatch layer.\n449\t\n450\t## Relevant files\n451\t- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — pool entry point, owns the shared memory region\n452\t- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — pool API (refcounting is complementary)\n453\t- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n454\t- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — task dispatch reads/writes slots\n455\t- `issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md` — queued input model that\n456\t  ring-buffer slots implement\n457\t- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — IPC options; shm_open + mmap is Option 2\n458\t\n459\t## Implementation log\n460\t\n461\t### Core milestone — 2026-05-12\n462\t\n463\tWhat shipped:\n464\t- `src/009-slot-store.h` — the public API exactly as the design\n465\t  describes: `slot_alloc` / `slot_push` / `slot_peek` / `slot_pop` /\n466\t  `slot_read_inc` / `slot_has_value` / `slot_fill_count`. Plus the\n467\t  store lifecycle pair and a small inspection helper for tests.\n468\t- `src/009-slot-store.c` — implementation. Plain-malloc per slot\n469\t  (size-class free lists deferred); ring slots and atomic-counter\n470\t  slots both supported; the SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED variant of pop scans\n471\t  for the lowest-tag filled cell. Per-slot spinlock via\n472\t  `atomic_flag`. Atomic counter via `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`,\n473\t  no lock.\n474\t- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — 12 unit tests covering peek\n475\t  semantics, FIFO pop, tagged pop ordering (in-order and\n476\t  interleaved), atomic counter (sequential + 8-thread concurrent),\n477\t  bad-argument paths, ring-full / empty edge cases, and a\n478\t  multi-thread producer/consumer race over 5000 values.\n479\t- Makefile additions: `test` target builds test binaries via a\n480\t  pattern rule and runs them. Per-test prerequisites listed\n481\t  explicitly so each binary links the minimal set of source `.o`s.\n482\t- File index counter advanced to `009`.\n483\t\n484\tVerified clean build and 12/12 tests pass in `make STRICT=1`\n485\t(`-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic`).\n486\t\n487\tWhat's deferred to a follow-on within 302:\n488\t- **Size-class free lists with coalescing.** The current\n489\t  implementation `malloc`s each slot independently. That's correct\n490\t  but unoptimized. Slots are allocated once at graph load and never\n491\t  freed until run end, so under the current usage pattern free-list\n492\t  reuse buys nothing. Lands once profiling justifies it (or once\n493\t  long-running maps surface allocation pressure).\n494\t- **Large-value heap for variable-size payloads.** Slots currently\n495\t  store fixed-size cells; very large outputs (multi-MB LLM\n496\t  responses, dynamically-sized arrays) will need the two-tier\n497\t  scheme described under \"Large-value heap\" above. Blocks no\n498\t  in-flight phase 3 work until a graph wants variable-size outputs.\n499\t\n500\tNeither deferred item blocks 301 / 304 / 305 / 306 / 307 / 308.\n501\t"
      }],

    "file":{
      "content":"/* src/009-slot-store.h — per-input-port slot store, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: a thread-safe pool of ring-buffer\n * slots, allocated at graph load time, used by the phase 3\n * dispatch layer to route values between boxes.\n *\n * Slots belong to input ports, not tasks. Each box has one slot\n * per input port; the slot persists for the whole run. A wire is\n * a routing declaration — when a producer's task finishes, the\n * dispatch layer pushes copies of the output into every\n * downstream input slot. Fan-out is N pushes; fan-in is N\n * producers pushing into one slot. Designed in issue 302.\n *\n * Three slot modes, chosen via flags at slot_alloc:\n *\n *   1-cell peek (n_cells == 1, no flags)\n *     — for literals and wires from producers that run exactly\n *       once. Push once at startup. Every consumer task peeks\n *       without draining; the cell stays filled.\n *\n *   N-cell pop (n_cells > 1, no flags)\n *     — for wires whose producer runs many times (iterators,\n *       queued inputs). Push appends to tail; pop drains head\n *       FIFO. Consumer task pops one cell per spawn.\n *\n *   N-cell pop, tagged (SLOT_TAGGED)\n *     — same shape as N-cell pop, but pop returns the cell with\n *       the lowest tag, not the head. Used downstream of parallel\n *       iterators where push order is non-deterministic but\n *       consumption order must follow the iterator counter.\n *\n *   atomic counter (SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER, n_cells and cell_capacity\n *     ignored)\n *     — single atomic uint32. Read-and-increment via\n *       slot_read_inc(). Used for iterator / randomizer /\n *       weighted-routing counters. Concurrent reads each get a\n *       distinct value mod the caller-supplied bound.\n *\n * Synchronization is per-slot. There is no allocator-wide lock on\n * the hot read/write path. The atomic-counter slot uses\n * atomic_fetch_add; the ring-buffer slots use a per-slot spinlock\n * around header mutation (one byte, atomic_flag).\n *\n * Lifetime is the run. Slots are freed when the store is\n * destroyed at the end of the run — there is no per-slot refcount\n * and no end-of-stream propagation. Run termination is governed\n * by the pool's active-task counter (issue 301).\n *\n * Errors: a return of -1 from a read/write op means the operation\n * could not be performed (empty pop, buffer too small, type\n * mismatch). The store does not assert or abort; the dispatch\n * layer is expected to check return codes. The hard-crash policy\n * applies at the language-spec layer, not here.\n *\n * What's NOT in this version:\n *  - Size-class free lists and coalescing. The design in issue 302\n *    describes a segregated allocator with eager-coalesce; this\n *    initial implementation uses plain malloc per slot. The pattern\n *    is \"allocate once at graph load, free at run end\", so free-list\n *    optimization buys nothing for the current usage. Lands as a\n *    follow-on if profiling justifies it.\n *  - Large-value heap for variable-size payloads. Slots store\n *    fixed-size cells; very large outputs (LLM responses) will\n *    use a separate two-tier scheme. Follow-on within 302.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_SLOT_STORE_H\n#define SORAMECH_SLOT_STORE_H\n\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types & flags */\ntypedef struct slot_store slot_store_t;\ntypedef int32_t           slot_id_t;\n\n#define SLOT_INVALID  ((slot_id_t)-1)\n\n/* slot_alloc flags */\nenum {\n    SLOT_FLAG_NONE           = 0,\n    SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED         = 1 << 0,\n    SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER = 1 << 1,\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Store lifecycle */\n/* Construct an empty store. Returns NULL on allocation failure. */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void);\n\n/* Free every slot and the store itself. Safe to call on NULL. */\nvoid          slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Slot lifecycle */\n/* Allocate a slot.\n *\n *   cell_capacity — bytes per cell. Ignored for SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *   n_cells       — ring size (1 for peek slots, >1 for pop). Ignored for\n *                   SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *   flags         — zero, SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED, or SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *\n * Returns the new slot's id, or SLOT_INVALID on allocation failure or\n * invalid arguments. Ids are stable for the lifetime of the store. */\nslot_id_t     slot_alloc(slot_store_t *s,\n                         int32_t cell_capacity,\n                         int32_t n_cells,\n                         int32_t flags);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Ring-buffer ops */\n/* Push a value into the slot's next free cell.\n *\n *   data, size — value bytes. size must be <= cell_capacity.\n *   tag        — ordering tag. Each cell is a 4-byte\n7\t *     filled_size, optionally a 4-byte tag (for SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED),\n8\t *     then cell_capacity bytes of payload. Untagged slots use the\n9\t *     standard head/tail ring discipline; tagged slots use head/tail\n10\t *     for the bookkeeping of \"where to put the next push\" but pop\n11\t *     scans for the lowest-tag filled cell.\n12\t *\n13\t *   - Atomic-counter slots — no header bookkeeping, no payload cells;\n14\t *     just one atomic_uint that slot_read_inc fetches-and-adds. No\n15\t *     lock needed.\n16\t *\n17\t * Per-slot concurrency is a single atomic_flag spinlock for the\n18\t * ring-buffer slots. Inside the lock the header and cells are mutated\n19\t * without atomics; outside the lock no header bytes are touched.\n20\t *\n21\t * The store itself owns a flat array of slot pointers indexed by\n22\t * slot_id_t. The array grows on demand. Ids are never reused — there\n23\t * is no slot_free; slots live for the run.\n24\t *\n25\t * Designed in issue 302. This file implements the API declared in\n26\t * 009-slot-store.h. Free-list optimization and the large-value heap\n27\t * are deferred per the header's \"what's not in this version\" note.\n28\t */\n29\t\n30\t#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n31\t\n32\t#include <stdatomic.h>\n33\t#include <stdint.h>\n34\t#include <stdlib.h>\n35\t#include <string.h>\n36\t\n37\t/* {{{ Internal slot record */\n38\ttypedef struct slot_rec {\n39\t    uint32_t    cell_capacity;   /* bytes per cell payload (ring slots) */\n40\t    uint32_t    n_cells;         /* ring size (ring slots)              */\n41\t    _Atomic uint32_t head;       /* read index, mod n_cells             */\n42\t    _Atomic uint32_t tail;       /* write index, mod n_cells            */\n43\t    atomic_flag lock;            /* per-slot spinlock for header+cells  */\n44\t    uint32_t    flags;           /* SLOT_FLAG_*                         */\n45\t    uint32_t    cell_record;     /* derived: 4 (+4 if tagged) + cap     */\n46\t\n47\t    /* For atomic-counter slots: a single atomic uint, used by\n48\t     * slot_read_inc. Lives separately from `cells` so the two slot\n49\t     * shapes don't share storage interpretation. */\n50\t    _Atomic uint32_t counter;\n51\t\n52\t    /* For ring slots: n_cells * cell_record bytes. Flexible array. */\n53\t    uint8_t     cells[];\n54\t} slot_rec_t;\n55\t/* }}} */\n56\t\n57\t/* {{{ Internal store */\n58\tstruct slot_store {\n59\t    slot_rec_t **slots;        /* dynamic array, indexed by slot_id_t */\n60\t    int32_t      count;\n61\t    int32_t      capacity;\n62\t};\n63\t/* }}} */\n64\t\n65\t/* {{{ Local helpers — locking */\n66\tstatic inline void lock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n67\t{\n68\t    while (atomic_flag_test_and_set_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_acquire)) {\n69\t        /* spin — contention is expected to be brief because the\n70\t         * locked section is just a header update plus a memcpy. */\n71\t    }\n72\t}\n73\t\n74\tstatic inline void unlock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n75\t{\n76\t    atomic_flag_clear_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_release);\n77\t}\n78\t/* }}} */\n79\t\n80\t/* {{{ Local helpers — cell layout */\n81\t/* Pointer to the i-th cell within the slot's flexible array. The cell\n82\t * record layout for ring slots is:\n83\t *\n84\t *   bytes 0..3   : filled_size (uint32_t; 0 means empty)\n85\t *   bytes 4..7   : tag         (uint32_t; only if SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED)\n86\t *   bytes (4|8)..: payload     (cell_capacity bytes)\n87\t */\n88\tstatic inline uint8_t *cell_ptr(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n89\t{\n90\t    return r->cells + (size_t)i * r->cell_record;\n91\t}\n92\t\n93\tstatic inline uint32_t cell_filled(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n94\t{\n95\t    uint32_t v;\n96\t    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i), sizeof v);\n97\t    return v;\n98\t}\n99\t\n100\tstatic inline uint32_t cell_tag(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n101\t{\n102\t    uint32_t v;\n103\t    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i) + 4, sizeof v);\n104\t    return v;\n105\t}\n106\t\n107\tstatic inline uint8_t *cell_data(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n108\t{\n109\t    return cell_ptr(r, i) + ((r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) ? 8 : 4);\n110\t}\n111\t/* }}} */\n112\t\n113\t/* {{{ slot_store_create() */\n114\tslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)\n115\t{\n116\t    slot_store_t *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);\n117\t    if (!s) return NULL;\n118\t    s->capacity = 16;\n119\t    s->slots    = calloc((size_t)s->capacity, sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n120\t    if (!s->slots) { free(s); return NULL; }\n121\t    return s;\n122\t}\n123\t/* }}} */\n124\t\n125\t/* {{{ slot_store_destroy() */\n126\tvoid slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)\n127\t{\n128\t    if (!s) return;\n129\t    for (int32_t i = 0; i < s->count; i++) {\n130\t        free(s->slots[i]);\n131\t    }\n132\t    free(s->slots);\n133\t    free(s);\n134\t}\n135\t/* }}} */\n136\t\n137\t/* {{{ slot_store_size() */\n138\tint32_t slot_store_size(slot_store_t *s)\n139\t{\n140\t    return s ? s->count : 0;\n141\t}\n142\t/* }}} */\n143\t\n144\t/* {{{ Local helper — grow_store_if_needed() */\n145\tstatic int grow_store_if_needed(slot_store_t *s)\n146\t{\n147\t    if (s->count < s->capacity) return 0;\n148\t    int32_t new_cap = s->capacity * 2;\n149\t    slot_rec_t **grown = realloc(s->slots, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n150\t    if (!grown) return -1;\n151\t    memset(grown + s->capacity, 0,\n152\t           (size_t)(new_cap - s->capacity) * sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n153\t    s->slots    = grown;\n154\t    s->capacity = new_cap;\n155\t    return 0;\n156\t}\n157\t/* }}} */\n158\t\n159\t/* {{{ slot_alloc() */\n160\tslot_id_t slot_alloc(slot_store_t *s,\n161\t                     int32_t cell_capacity,\n162\t                     int32_t n_cells,\n163\t                     int32_t flags)\n164\t{\n165\t    if (!s) return SLOT_INVALID;\n166\t\n167\t    size_t bytes_cells = 0;\n168\t    uint32_t cell_record = 0;\n169\t\n170\t    if (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) {\n171\t        /* Atomic-counter slot: no ring cells. cell_capacity and\n172\t         * n_cells are ignored. */\n173\t        bytes_cells = 0;\n174\t    } else {\n175\t        if (cell_capacity <= 0 || n_cells <= 0) return SLOT_INVALID;\n176\t        cell_record = (uint32_t)(4\n177\t                                  + ((flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED) ? 4 : 0)\n178\t                                  + cell_capacity);\n179\t        bytes_cells = (size_t)n_cells * cell_record;\n180\t    }\n181\t\n182\t    slot_rec_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof(slot_rec_t) + bytes_cells);\n183\t    if (!r) return SLOT_INVALID;\n184\t\n185\t    r->cell_capacity = (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) ? 0 : (uint32_t)cell_capacity;\n186\t    r->n_cells       = (flags & SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER) ? 0 : (uint32_t)n_cells;\n187\t    r->cell_record   = cell_record;\n188\t    r->flags         = (uint32_t)flags;\n189\t    atomic_init(&r->head,    0u);\n190\t    atomic_init(&r->tail,    0u);\n191\t    atomic_init(&r->counter, 0u);\n192\t    /* atomic_flag has no atomic_flag_init in C11; ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT is\n193\t     * for initializers. Clearing it leaves it in the \"not set\" state. */\n194\t    atomic_flag_clear(&r->lock);\n195\t\n196\t    if (grow_store_if_needed(s) != 0) { free(r); return SLOT_INVALID; }\n197\t    slot_id_t id = s->count++;\n198\t    s->slots[id] = r;\n199\t    return id;\n200\t}"
      }],

        "name":"Write",

        },
        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/015-large-value-heap.h — variable-size payload allocator.\n *\n * The large-value heap is a chunked arena: a linked list of malloc'd\n * chunks where each allocation bump-allocates within the current\n * chunk. When a chunk fills up, a new chunk is allocated and prepended.\n * Allocations are never individually freed — the entire heap is\n * destroyed at run end (same lifetime model as the slot store).\n *\n * Why a separate heap, not just bigger slot cells:\n *\n *   The slot store gives every cell a fixed cell_capacity decided at\n *   slot_alloc time. For values whose size is not known at compile\n *   time — long LLM responses, dynamically-sized arrays, binary\n *   blobs of unbounded length — there is no useful upper bound to\n *   bake into cell_capacity.\n *\n *   The large-value heap solves this by decoupling cell size from\n *   payload size. A slot allocated with SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE\n *   (issue 302) stores only a handle in its cell; the payload bytes\n *   live in the large-value heap and the cell carries a stable\n *   pointer to them. Push allocates a heap region of the requested\n *   size; pop follows the pointer.\n *\n * Why stable pointers matter: the heap may grow by appending new\n * chunks, but existing chunks never move, so a pointer returned by\n * lvh_alloc remains valid for the life of the heap. This is what\n * makes the design safe for concurrent producers and consumers —\n * the consumer's pointer doesn't get invalidated by a later\n * producer's allocation.\n *\n * Concurrency: lvh_alloc is thread-safe via an internal mutex.\n * Reads of returned pointers need no synchronization beyond what\n * the slot store already provides at the cell level.\n *\n * Cleanup: allocations are not individually freed. The heap is\n * monotonic-growth for the duration of a run. For long-running\n * graphs with iterators producing large values in a tight loop,\n * this means the heap grows in proportion to total bytes produced\n * — not in proportion to peak live bytes. That's a known trade-off;\n * a proper free-on-pop allocator is a future iteration. Track\n * total_allocated() to surface when it matters.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H\n#define SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Type */\ntypedef struct lvh lvh_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Construct a new heap.\n *\n *   default_chunk_size — bytes per new chunk when the heap grows.\n *                        Pass 0 to use the built-in default (64 KB).\n *\n * Returns NULL on allocation failure. */\nlvh_t  *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size);\n\n/* Free every chunk and the heap struct. Safe on NULL. After this\n * call, all pointers returned by lvh_alloc on this heap are\n * invalid. */\nvoid    lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Allocation */\n/* Allocate `size` bytes of unspecified contents. The returned\n * pointer is stable for the life of the heap. Returns NULL on\n * allocation failure (out of memory at the malloc layer; the\n * heap itself doesn't pre-cap).\n *\n * Allocations larger than `default_chunk_size` get a dedicated\n * chunk sized exactly to the request — no waste, no fragmentation\n * of the regular chunks. Allocations smaller or equal share the\n * current bump chunk. */\nvoid   *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats (test / debug) */\n/* Sum of every chunk's capacity (the working-set ceiling). */\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h);\n\n/* Sum of bytes returned to callers via lvh_alloc. */\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h);\n\n/* Count of chunks currently in the heap. */\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H */\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/015-large-value-heap.h"
        }
      }],

    "content":"/* src/015-large-value-heap.h — variable-size payload allocator.\n *\n * The large-value heap is a chunked arena: a linked list of malloc'd\n * chunks where each allocation bump-allocates within the current\n * chunk. When a chunk fills up, a new chunk is allocated and prepended.\n * Allocations are never individually freed — the entire heap is\n * destroyed at run end (same lifetime model as the slot store).\n *\n * Why a separate heap, not just bigger slot cells:\n *\n *   The slot store gives every cell a fixed cell_capacity decided at\n *   slot_alloc time. For values whose size is not known at compile\n *   time — long LLM responses, dynamically-sized arrays, binary\n *   blobs of unbounded length — there is no useful upper bound to\n *   bake into cell_capacity.\n *\n *   The large-value heap solves this by decoupling cell size from\n *   payload size. A slot allocated with SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE\n *   (issue 302) stores only a handle in its cell; the payload bytes\n *   live in the large-value heap and the cell carries a stable\n *   pointer to them. Push allocates a heap region of the requested\n *   size; pop follows the pointer.\n *\n * Why stable pointers matter: the heap may grow by appending new\n * chunks, but existing chunks never move, so a pointer returned by\n * lvh_alloc remains valid for the life of the heap. This is what\n * makes the design safe for concurrent producers and consumers —\n * the consumer's pointer doesn't get invalidated by a later\n * producer's allocation.\n *\n * Concurrency: lvh_alloc is thread-safe via an internal mutex.\n * Reads of returned pointers need no synchronization beyond what\n * the slot store already provides at the cell level.\n *\n * Cleanup: allocations are not individually freed. The heap is\n * monotonic-growth for the duration of a run. For long-running\n * graphs with iterators producing large values in a tight loop,\n * this means the heap grows in proportion to total bytes produced\n * — not in proportion to peak live bytes. That's a known trade-off;\n * a proper free-on-pop allocator is a future iteration. Track\n * total_allocated() to surface when it matters.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H\n#define SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Type */\ntypedef struct lvh lvh_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Construct a new heap.\n *\n *   default_chunk_size — bytes per new chunk when the heap grows.\n *                        Pass 0 to use the built-in default (64 KB).\n *\n * Returns NULL on allocation failure. */\nlvh_t  *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size);\n\n/* Free every chunk and the heap struct. Safe on NULL. After this\n * call, all pointers returned by lvh_alloc on this heap are\n * invalid. */\nvoid    lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Allocation */\n/* Allocate `size` bytes of unspecified contents. The returned\n * pointer is stable for the life of the heap. Returns NULL on\n * allocation failure (out of memory at the malloc layer; the\n * heap itself doesn't pre-cap).\n *\n * Allocations larger than `default_chunk_size` get a dedicated\n * chunk sized exactly to the request — no waste, no fragmentation\n * of the regular chunks. Allocations smaller or equal share the\n * current bump chunk. */\nvoid   *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats (test / debug) */\n/* Sum of every chunk's capacity (the working-set ceiling). */\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h);\n\n/* Sum of bytes returned to callers via lvh_alloc. */\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h);\n\n/* Count of chunks currently in the heap. */\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_LARGE_VALUE_HEAP_H */\n",
    "type":"create",

          "content":"/* src/015-large-value-heap.c — variable-size payload allocator.\n *\n * Chunked arena. Every chunk is a single malloc; the chunk's\n * capacity and used-watermark live in the chunk header, the payload\n * bytes follow as a flexible array. The heap holds the chunk list\n * head and a mutex serializing alloc / grow.\n *\n * The single mutex is intentional: large-value allocations are\n * relatively coarse (kilobytes-to-megabytes), and the time spent in\n * the lock is dominated by the memcpy that the caller performs\n * *outside* the lock. A per-chunk lock would add complexity for\n * negligible win. If profiling later shows the mutex is hot, the\n * upgrade path is a try-lock-with-thread-local-chunk scheme.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's \"Large-value heap (variable-size\n * payloads)\" section; landed 2026-05-19 as a follow-on within 302.\n */\n\n#include \"015-large-value-heap.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ Defaults */\n#define LVH_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE  (64u * 1024u)\n#define LVH_ALIGN               (16u)  /* generous alignment for any payload type */\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Chunk record */\ntypedef struct lvh_chunk {\n    struct lvh_chunk *next;\n    size_t            cap;     /* bytes available in `data` */\n    size_t            used;    /* bytes bump-allocated so far */\n    /* The flexible array begins at the alignment boundary — gcc\n     * naturally aligns to 8 on x86-64; LVH_ALIGN is enforced inside\n     * align_up() to give consumers a generous guarantee. */\n    uint8_t           data[];\n} lvh_chunk_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Heap record */\nstruct lvh {\n    lvh_chunk_t    *head;\n    pthread_mutex_t mu;\n    size_t          default_chunk_size;\n\n    /* Stats. Atomic so callers can read without taking the mutex. */\n    _Atomic uint64_t total_allocated;  /* sum of chunk capacities */\n    _Atomic uint64_t total_used;       /* sum of used bytes        */\n    _Atomic uint32_t chunk_count;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — align_up() */\n/* Round `n` up to the next multiple of LVH_ALIGN. Aligning here\n * means any pointer we hand out is at least 16-byte aligned, which\n * is enough for any standard C scalar or vector type. */\nstatic inline size_t align_up(size_t n)\n{\n    return (n + (LVH_ALIGN - 1u)) & ~(size_t)(LVH_ALIGN - 1u);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — alloc_chunk() */\n/* Allocate a new chunk with at least `min_cap` bytes available.\n * Returns NULL on allocation failure. Updates the stats counters. */\nstatic lvh_chunk_t *alloc_chunk(lvh_t *h, size_t min_cap)\n{\n    size_t cap = h->default_chunk_size;\n    if (min_cap > cap) {\n        /* Caller asked for more than a default chunk holds. Give it\n         * its own oversized chunk sized to exactly fit; this keeps\n         * the default chunks from being permanently bloated by one\n         * unusual allocation. */\n        cap = min_cap;\n    }\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = malloc(sizeof(lvh_chunk_t) + cap);\n    if (!c) return NULL;\n    c->next = NULL;\n    c->cap  = cap;\n    c->used = 0;\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->total_allocated,\n                              (uint64_t)cap,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->chunk_count, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    return c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_create() */\nlvh_t *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    h->default_chunk_size = (default_chunk_size > 0)\n                            ? default_chunk_size\n                            : LVH_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&h->mu, NULL) != 0) {\n        free(h);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    atomic_init(&h->total_allocated, 0u);\n    atomic_init(&h->total_used,      0u);\n    atomic_init(&h->chunk_count,     0u);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_destroy() */\nvoid lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    if (!h) return;\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = h->head;\n    while (c) {\n        lvh_chunk_t *next = c->next;\n        free(c);\n        c = next;\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_alloc() */\nvoid *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    if (size == 0) {\n        /* Zero-byte allocation: return a non-NULL \"this is intentional\"\n         * pointer. Hand out a stable address that nobody else will\n         * see — the head of an allocation of LVH_ALIGN bytes, which\n         * we waste deliberately. This keeps callers from special-\n         * casing the empty case while still letting NULL mean\n         * \"failure\". */\n        size = 1;\n    }\n\n    size_t need = align_up(size);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&h->mu);\n\n    /* Fast path: current chunk has room. */\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = h->head;\n    if (!c || c->used + need > c->cap) {\n        lvh_chunk_t *fresh = alloc_chunk(h, need);\n        if (!fresh) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        fresh->next = h->head;\n        h->head     = fresh;\n        c           = fresh;\n    }\n\n    void *p = c->data + c->used;\n    c->used += need;\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->total_used,\n                              (uint64_t)need,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats accessors */\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->total_allocated,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->total_used,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->chunk_count,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"/* src/015-large-value-heap.c — variable-size payload allocator.\n *\n * Chunked arena. Every chunk is a single malloc; the chunk's\n * capacity and used-watermark live in the chunk header, the payload\n * bytes follow as a flexible array. The heap holds the chunk list\n * head and a mutex serializing alloc / grow.\n *\n * The single mutex is intentional: large-value allocations are\n * relatively coarse (kilobytes-to-megabytes), and the time spent in\n * the lock is dominated by the memcpy that the caller performs\n * *outside* the lock. A per-chunk lock would add complexity for\n * negligible win. If profiling later shows the mutex is hot, the\n * upgrade path is a try-lock-with-thread-local-chunk scheme.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's \"Large-value heap (variable-size\n * payloads)\" section; landed 2026-05-19 as a follow-on within 302.\n */\n\n#include \"015-large-value-heap.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ Defaults */\n#define LVH_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE  (64u * 1024u)\n#define LVH_ALIGN               (16u)  /* generous alignment for any payload type */\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Chunk record */\ntypedef struct lvh_chunk {\n    struct lvh_chunk *next;\n    size_t            cap;     /* bytes available in `data` */\n    size_t            used;    /* bytes bump-allocated so far */\n    /* The flexible array begins at the alignment boundary — gcc\n     * naturally aligns to 8 on x86-64; LVH_ALIGN is enforced inside\n     * align_up() to give consumers a generous guarantee. */\n    uint8_t           data[];\n} lvh_chunk_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Heap record */\nstruct lvh {\n    lvh_chunk_t    *head;\n    pthread_mutex_t mu;\n    size_t          default_chunk_size;\n\n    /* Stats. Atomic so callers can read without taking the mutex. */\n    _Atomic uint64_t total_allocated;  /* sum of chunk capacities */\n    _Atomic uint64_t total_used;       /* sum of used bytes        */\n    _Atomic uint32_t chunk_count;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — align_up() */\n/* Round `n` up to the next multiple of LVH_ALIGN. Aligning here\n * means any pointer we hand out is at least 16-byte aligned, which\n * is enough for any standard C scalar or vector type. */\nstatic inline size_t align_up(size_t n)\n{\n    return (n + (LVH_ALIGN - 1u)) & ~(size_t)(LVH_ALIGN - 1u);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — alloc_chunk() */\n/* Allocate a new chunk with at least `min_cap` bytes available.\n * Returns NULL on allocation failure. Updates the stats counters. */\nstatic lvh_chunk_t *alloc_chunk(lvh_t *h, size_t min_cap)\n{\n    size_t cap = h->default_chunk_size;\n    if (min_cap > cap) {\n        /* Caller asked for more than a default chunk holds. Give it\n         * its own oversized chunk sized to exactly fit; this keeps\n         * the default chunks from being permanently bloated by one\n         * unusual allocation. */\n        cap = min_cap;\n    }\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = malloc(sizeof(lvh_chunk_t) + cap);\n    if (!c) return NULL;\n    c->next = NULL;\n    c->cap  = cap;\n    c->used = 0;\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->total_allocated,\n                              (uint64_t)cap,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->chunk_count, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    return c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_create() */\nlvh_t *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    h->default_chunk_size = (default_chunk_size > 0)\n                            ? default_chunk_size\n                            : LVH_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&h->mu, NULL) != 0) {\n        free(h);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    atomic_init(&h->total_allocated, 0u);\n    atomic_init(&h->total_used,      0u);\n    atomic_init(&h->chunk_count,     0u);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_destroy() */\nvoid lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    if (!h) return;\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = h->head;\n    while (c) {\n        lvh_chunk_t *next = c->next;\n        free(c);\n        c = next;\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lvh_alloc() */\nvoid *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    if (size == 0) {\n        /* Zero-byte allocation: return a non-NULL \"this is intentional\"\n         * pointer. Hand out a stable address that nobody else will\n         * see — the head of an allocation of LVH_ALIGN bytes, which\n         * we waste deliberately. This keeps callers from special-\n         * casing the empty case while still letting NULL mean\n         * \"failure\". */\n        size = 1;\n    }\n\n    size_t need = align_up(size);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&h->mu);\n\n    /* Fast path: current chunk has room. */\n    lvh_chunk_t *c = h->head;\n    if (!c || c->used + need > c->cap) {\n        lvh_chunk_t *fresh = alloc_chunk(h, need);\n        if (!fresh) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        fresh->next = h->head;\n        h->head     = fresh;\n        c           = fresh;\n    }\n\n    void *p = c->data + c->used;\n    c->used += need;\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->total_used,\n                              (uint64_t)need,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats accessors */\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->total_allocated,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->total_used,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->chunk_count,\n                                    memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

Used by the slot store\n(009-slot-store) for `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE` slots — the cell\nholds a stable pointer into this heap; the actual bytes live here.\nDesigned in issue 302; implemented 2026-05-19.\n\n## Mental model\n\nA chunked arena. The heap is a singly-linked list of `malloc`'d\nchunks. Each `lvh_alloc` either bump-allocates within the current\n(head) chunk or, if the request doesn't fit, allocates a fresh\nchunk and prepends it.\n\nAllocations are **never individually freed**. The entire heap is\ndestroyed at run end (matching the slot store's lifetime).\n\nPointers returned by `lvh_alloc` are stable — chunks don't move\nonce allocated, so a consumer's pointer outlives any number of\nlater producer allocations.\n\n## API\n\n```c\nlvh_t   *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size);   /* 0 → 64 KB */\nvoid     lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h);\n\nvoid    *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size);        /* stable, 16-byte aligned */\n\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h);           /* sum of chunk caps */\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h);                /* sum of used bytes */\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h);\n```\n\n## Behaviors worth knowing\n\n- **Thread-safe.** A single internal mutex serializes `lvh_alloc`.\n  The user's memcpy of payload bytes runs outside the lock —\n  contention is brief.\n- **Oversized allocations get their own chunk.** A 5 MB request\n  with a 64 KB default chunk size produces a 5 MB chunk, not a\n  bump within a 64 KB chunk. This keeps fragmentation predictable\n  and stops one large value from pinning a chunk forever.\n- **Zero-size allocations succeed.** They return a stable non-NULL\n  pointer (1 byte rounded to 16 alignment), so callers don't need\n  to special-case empty payloads. NULL strictly means \"out of\n  memory\".\n- **No free.** Long iterator loops that produce large values\n  monotonically grow the heap. Track `lvh_total_used` to detect.\n  A proper free-on-pop allocator is a future iteration.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Per-allocation free (`lvh_free`).\n- Cross-process visibility (heap is in-process; out-of-process\n  language specs receive bytes via existing socket plumbing).\n- Concurrent chunk allocation with no mutex (thread-local chunk\n  scheme is the planned upgrade path if profiling justifies it).\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/015-large-value-heap-test.c`:\n- `create_destroy` — round-trip with no allocations.\n- `single_alloc_within_chunk` — write/read bytes through the\n  returned pointer.\n- `multiple_allocs_within_chunk` — independent pointers, no\n  overlap.\n- `oversized_alloc` — request larger than chunk size; verify it\n  gets its own chunk.\n- `pointer_stability_across_growth` — alloc, fill chunks past\n  default size to force growth, original pointer still readable.\n- `zero_size_alloc` — non-NULL return, no crash.\n- `concurrent_alloc` — eight threads each doing 1000 allocs;\n  every returned pointer is unique and writable.\n- `stats_match_reality` — total_used / chunk_count line up with\n  what was asked for.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/015-large-value-heap.info.md"
        }
      }],

    "content":"# 015-large-value-heap.info.md\n\nVariable-size payload allocator. Used by the slot store\n(009-slot-store) for `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE` slots — the cell\nholds a stable pointer into this heap; the actual bytes live here.\nDesigned in issue 302; implemented 2026-05-19.\n\n## Mental model\n\nA chunked arena. The heap is a singly-linked list of `malloc`'d\nchunks. Each `lvh_alloc` either bump-allocates within the current\n(head) chunk or, if the request doesn't fit, allocates a fresh\nchunk and prepends it.\n\nAllocations are **never individually freed**. The entire heap is\ndestroyed at run end (matching the slot store's lifetime).\n\nPointers returned by `lvh_alloc` are stable — chunks don't move\nonce allocated, so a consumer's pointer outlives any number of\nlater producer allocations.\n\n## API\n\n```c\nlvh_t   *lvh_create(size_t default_chunk_size);   /* 0 → 64 KB */\nvoid     lvh_destroy(lvh_t *h);\n\nvoid    *lvh_alloc(lvh_t *h, size_t size);        /* stable, 16-byte aligned */\n\nuint64_t lvh_total_allocated(lvh_t *h);           /* sum of chunk caps */\nuint64_t lvh_total_used(lvh_t *h);                /* sum of used bytes */\nuint32_t lvh_chunk_count(lvh_t *h);\n```\n\n## Behaviors worth knowing\n\n- **Thread-safe.** A single internal mutex serializes `lvh_alloc`.\n  The user's memcpy of payload bytes runs outside the lock —\n  contention is brief.\n- **Oversized allocations get their own chunk.** A 5 MB request\n  with a 64 KB default chunk size produces a 5 MB chunk, not a\n  bump within a 64 KB chunk. This keeps fragmentation predictable\n  and stops one large value from pinning a chunk forever.\n- **Zero-size allocations succeed.** They return a stable non-NULL\n  pointer (1 byte rounded to 16 alignment), so callers don't need\n  to special-case empty payloads. NULL strictly means \"out of\n  memory\".\n- **No free.** Long iterator loops that produce large values\n  monotonically grow the heap. Track `lvh_total_used` to detect.\n  A proper free-on-pop allocator is a future iteration.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Per-allocation free (`lvh_free`).\n- Cross-process visibility (heap is in-process; out-of-process\n  language specs receive bytes via existing socket plumbing).\n- Concurrent chunk allocation with no mutex (thread-local chunk\n  scheme is the planned upgrade path if profiling justifies it).\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/015-large-value-heap-test.c`:\n- `create_destroy` — round-trip with no allocations.\n- `single_alloc_within_chunk` — write/read bytes through the\n  returned pointer.\n- `multiple_allocs_within_chunk` — independent pointers, no\n  overlap.\n- `oversized_alloc` — request larger than chunk size; verify it\n  gets its own chunk.\n- `pointer_stability_across_growth` — alloc, fill chunks past\n  default size to force growth, original pointer still readable.\n- `zero_size_alloc` — non-NULL return, no crash.\n- `concurrent_alloc` — eight threads each doing 1000 allocs;\n  every returned pointer is unique and writable.\n- `stats_match_reality` — total_used / chunk_count line up with\n  what was asked for.\n",
    "type":"create",

          "content":"/* tests/015-large-value-heap-test.c — unit tests for the\n * variable-size payload allocator (issue 302 follow-on, lvh).\n *\n * The tests cover the three properties that the slot store relies\n * on at the layer above:\n *   1. Pointers returned by lvh_alloc are stable across further\n *      allocations (chunks don't move).\n *   2. Concurrent allocations from many threads never produce\n *      overlapping regions.\n *   3. Allocations larger than the default chunk size succeed.\n *\n * The miscellaneous tests cover the stats accessors and the\n * zero-size convention.\n */\n\n#include \"../src/015-large-value-heap.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Local mini test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"  ASSERT failed at %s:%d: %s\\n\", \\\n                __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\n#define RUN(test) do { \\\n    int ok = test(); \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s %s\\n\", #test, ok ? \"ok\" : \"FAIL\"); \\\n    if (ok) g_pass++; else g_fail++; \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(0);\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 0);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_allocated(h) == 0);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_used(h) == 0);\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n\n    /* destroy on NULL is safe */\n    lvh_destroy(NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_single_alloc_within_chunk() */\nstatic int test_single_alloc_within_chunk(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(4096);\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n\n    void *p = lvh_alloc(h, 100);\n    ASSERT(p != NULL);\n\n    /* Write through the pointer; read it back. */\n    memset(p, 0xAB, 100);\n    unsigned char *q = (unsigned char *)p;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) ASSERT(q[i] == 0xAB);\n\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 1);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_allocated(h) >= 4096);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_used(h) >= 100);\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_multiple_allocs_within_chunk() */\nstatic int test_multiple_allocs_within_chunk(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(4096);\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n\n    void *a = lvh_alloc(h, 100);\n    void *b = lvh_alloc(h, 100);\n    void *c = lvh_alloc(h, 100);\n    ASSERT(a && b && c);\n    ASSERT(a != b && b != c && a != c);\n\n    /* Write different bytes to each; verify no overlap. */\n    memset(a, 0x11, 100);\n    memset(b, 0x22, 100);\n    memset(c, 0x33, 100);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)a)[0] == 0x11);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)b)[0] == 0x22);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)c)[0] == 0x33);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)a)[99] == 0x11);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)b)[99] == 0x22);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)c)[99] == 0x33);\n\n    /* Still one chunk. */\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 1);\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_oversized_alloc() */\nstatic int test_oversized_alloc(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(1024);  /* small chunks on purpose */\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n\n    /* Request more than a chunk holds. */\n    void *p = lvh_alloc(h, 100 * 1024);  /* 100 KB */\n    ASSERT(p != NULL);\n\n    /* Writable end-to-end. */\n    memset(p, 0xCD, 100 * 1024);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)p)[0]            == 0xCD);\n    ASSERT(((unsigned char *)p)[100*1024 - 1] == 0xCD);\n\n    /* One chunk, sized for the oversized request (>= 100KB). */\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 1);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_allocated(h) >= 100u * 1024u);\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_pointer_stability_across_growth() */\n/* This is the property the slot store relies on: an earlier\n * consumer's pointer must not be invalidated when a later\n * producer's allocation forces a chunk grow. */\nstatic int test_pointer_stability_across_growth(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(1024);\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n\n    void *first = lvh_alloc(h, 64);\n    ASSERT(first != NULL);\n    memset(first, 0xEE, 64);\n    uintptr_t first_addr = (uintptr_t)first;\n\n    /* Push another ~20 KB through the heap, forcing several\n     * chunks. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {\n        void *p = lvh_alloc(h, 128);\n        ASSERT(p != NULL);\n    }\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) > 1);\n\n    /* Original pointer still has its bytes. */\n    ASSERT((uintptr_t)first == first_addr);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {\n        ASSERT(((unsigned char *)first)[i] == 0xEE);\n    }\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_zero_size_alloc() */\nstatic int test_zero_size_alloc(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(0);\n    void *p = lvh_alloc(h, 0);\n    ASSERT(p != NULL);  /* non-NULL is the convention */\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_stats_match_reality() */\nstatic int test_stats_match_reality(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(4096);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_used(h) == 0);\n    ASSERT(lvh_total_allocated(h) == 0);\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 0);\n\n    lvh_alloc(h, 100);\n    /* Used is 16-aligned; lower bound 112, upper bound 128 (the\n     * exact value depends on LVH_ALIGN). */\n    uint64_t used = lvh_total_used(h);\n    ASSERT(used >= 100 && used <= 128);\n\n    lvh_alloc(h, 200);\n    used = lvh_total_used(h);\n    ASSERT(used >= 300 && used <= 400);\n\n    ASSERT(lvh_chunk_count(h) == 1);\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Concurrent alloc test scaffolding */\n#define N_THREADS    8\n#define N_PER_THREAD 1000\n#define ALLOC_SIZE   64\n\ntypedef struct {\n    lvh_t *h;\n    void  *ptrs[N_PER_THREAD];\n    int    thread_idx;\n} worker_arg_t;\n\nstatic void *concurrent_worker(void *vp)\n{\n    worker_arg_t *w = vp;\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n        void *p = lvh_alloc(w->h, ALLOC_SIZE);\n        if (!p) { w->ptrs[i] = NULL; continue; }\n        /* Write something thread-specific so unique-pointer checks\n         * later are paired with non-overlap evidence. */\n        memset(p, (unsigned char)(w->thread_idx + 1), ALLOC_SIZE);\n        w->ptrs[i] = p;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_alloc() */\n/* Eight threads, 1000 allocs each. Every returned pointer must be\n * unique, every memset must survive (no overlap), and the chunk\n * count + total_used must reflect reality. */\nstatic int test_concurrent_alloc(void)\n{\n    lvh_t *h = lvh_create(4096);\n    ASSERT(h != NULL);\n\n    pthread_t   threads[N_THREADS];\n    worker_arg_t args[N_THREADS];\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        args[t].h          = h;\n        args[t].thread_idx = t;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, concurrent_worker, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n    }\n\n    /* Verify each pointer still contains the byte its thread wrote.\n     * If two threads' regions had overlapped, at least some bytes\n     * would be the other thread's marker. */\n    int n_alloced = 0;\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < N_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n            void *p = args[t].ptrs[i];\n            if (!p) continue;\n            n_alloced++;\n            unsigned char expect = (unsigned char)(t + 1);\n            for (int k = 0; k < ALLOC_SIZE; k++) {\n                ASSERT(((unsigned char *)p)[k] == expect);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    ASSERT(n_alloced == N_THREADS * N_PER_THREAD);\n\n    /* Pairwise uniqueness — a quadratic check, but for 8000\n     * pointers it's still well under a second and it gives us the\n     * strongest evidence. */\n    void **all = malloc((size_t)n_alloced * sizeof(void *));\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < N_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n            if (args[t].ptrs[i]) all[n++] = args[t].ptrs[i];\n        }\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {\n            ASSERT(all[i] != all[j]);\n        }\n    }\n    free(all);\n\n    lvh_destroy(h);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"015-large-value-heap-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(test_create_destroy);\n    RUN(test_single_alloc_within_chunk);\n    RUN(test_multiple_allocs_within_chunk);\n    RUN(test_oversized_alloc);\n    RUN(test_pointer_stability_across_growth);\n    RUN(test_zero_size_alloc);\n    RUN(test_stats_match_reality);\n    RUN(test_concurrent_alloc);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
