    "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1), 0);\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_callback() */\nstatic atomic_int g_init_count;\nstatic int worker_init_fn(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)user;\n    /* Verify the worker's ctx is consistent: thread_idx matches the\n     * argument; back-pointer to the pool isn't NULL. */\n    if (ctx->thread_idx != worker_idx) return -1;\n    if (ctx->pool == NULL) return -1;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_init_count, 1);\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_callback(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_init_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_fn, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == 0);\n    /* Every worker's init ran exactly once. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_init_count) == 4);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_failure() */\nstatic int worker_init_failing(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)ctx; (void)user;\n    /* Fail on worker 2 to test the failure path. */\n    return (worker_idx == 2) ? -1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_failure(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_failing, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == -1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority. Single-worker pool is\n * used so dequeue order maps directly to execution order. */\nstatic pthread_mutex_t g_seq_mtx = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\nstatic int g_seq[16];\nstatic int g_seq_len;\n\nstatic void seq_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int id = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_seq_mtx);\n    g_seq[g_seq_len++] = id;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_seq_mtx);\n}\n\nstatic int test_priority_order(void)\n{\n    g_seq_len = 0;\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(1);\n    ASSERT(p);\n\n    /* Queue 6 tasks BEFORE the worker is released. ids encode order\n     * of spawn; the test asserts on order of execution. */\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)1, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)2, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)3, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)4, 9);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)5, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)6, -1);\n\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    /* Expected order:\n     *   4 (prio 9)\n     *   2, 5 (prio 5, FIFO)\n     *   1, 3 (prio 0, FIFO)\n     *   6 (prio -1)\n     */\n    static const int expected[] = { 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, 6 };\n    ASSERT(g_seq_len == 6);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) ASSERT(g_seq[i] == expected[i]);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    RUN(worker_init_callback);\n    RUN(worker_init_failure);\n    RUN(priority_order);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,

  /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1), 0);\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL, 0);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_callback() */\nstatic atomic_int g_init_count;\nstatic int worker_init_fn(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)user;\n    /* Verify the worker's ctx is consistent: thread_idx matches the\n     * argument; back-pointer to the pool isn't NULL. */\n    if (ctx->thread_idx != worker_idx) return -1;\n    if (ctx->pool == NULL) return -1;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_init_count, 1);\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_callback(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_init_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_fn, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == 0);\n    /* Every worker's init ran exactly once. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_init_count) == 4);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_failure() */\nstatic int worker_init_failing(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)ctx; (void)user;\n    /* Fail on worker 2 to test the failure path. */\n    return (worker_idx == 2) ? -1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_failure(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_failing, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == -1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority. Single-worker pool is\n * used so dequeue order maps directly to execution order. */\nstatic pthread_mutex_t g_seq_mtx = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\nstatic int g_seq[16];\nstatic int g_seq_len;\n\nstatic void seq_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int id = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_seq_mtx);\n    g_seq[g_seq_len++] = id;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_seq_mtx);\n}\n\nstatic int test_priority_order(void)\n{\n    g_seq_len = 0;\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(1);\n    ASSERT(p);\n\n    /* Queue 6 tasks BEFORE the worker is released. ids encode order\n     * of spawn; the test asserts on order of execution. */\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)1, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)2, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)3, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)4, 9);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)5, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)6, -1);\n\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    /* Expected order:\n     *   4 (prio 9)\n     *   2, 5 (prio 5, FIFO)\n     *   1, 3 (prio 0, FIFO)\n     *   6 (prio -1)\n     */\n    static const int expected[] = { 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, 6 };\n    ASSERT(g_seq_len == 6);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) ASSERT(g_seq[i] == expected[i]);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    RUN(worker_init_callback);\n    RUN(worker_init_failure);\n    RUN(priority_order);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1));\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_callback() */\nstatic atomic_int g_init_count;\nstatic int worker_init_fn(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)user;\n    /* Verify the worker's ctx is consistent: thread_idx matches the\n     * argument; back-pointer to the pool isn't NULL. */\n    if (ctx->thread_idx != worker_idx) return -1;\n    if (ctx->pool == NULL) return -1;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_init_count, 1);\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_callback(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_init_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_fn, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == 0);\n    /* Every worker's init ran exactly once. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_init_count) == 4);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_failure() */\nstatic int worker_init_failing(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)ctx; (void)user;\n    /* Fail on worker 2 to test the failure path. */\n    return (worker_idx == 2) ? -1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_failure(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_failing, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == -1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority.     "originalFile":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1));\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_create(&producers[i], NULL, producer_thread, &args);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N_PROD; i++)\n        pthread_join(producers[i], NULL);\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N_PROD * PER);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_worker_init_callback() */\nstatic atomic_int g_init_count;\nstatic int worker_init_fn(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)\n{\n    (void)user;\n    /* Verify the worker's ctx is consistent: thread_idx matches the\n     * argument; (void)user;\n    /* Fail on worker 2 to test the failure path. */\n    return (worker_idx == 2) ? -1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic int test_worker_init_failure(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    pool_set_worker_init(p, worker_init_failing, NULL);\n    ASSERT(pool_init_barrier(p) == -1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    RUN(worker_init_callback);\n    RUN(worker_init_failure);\n    RUN(priority_order);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n301 — per-worker init and teardown hooks, three-stage init barrier\n\nThe pool now exposes a pair of optional callbacks the host\nregisters between pool_create and pool_init_barrier: an init\nhook that runs on each worker thread before it starts pulling\ntasks, and a teardown hook that runs on each worker thread\nright before it exits. The canonical caller is 303's spec\nregistry, which uses init to populate per-worker handles for\nevery language the map uses, and teardown to shut down each\nspec's worker handle symmetrically — closing bash sockets,\nfreeing Lua states, that kind of thing. Before the teardown\nhook landed, runs were leaving sixteen orphan bash processes\nper invocation; with it, zero.\n\nThe init barrier grew a third stage to make the callback-\nregistration ordering safe. Workers park on a condition\nvariable after pool_create and don't run their callbacks\nuntil pool_init_barrier authorises them — otherwise a\ncallback registered after pool_create would race the workers\nrunning init with a still-NULL function pointer. The barrier\nalso now returns an int and propagates a nonzero return from\nany worker's callback up to the caller, so a spec that\nfails to init brings the whole pool down rather than running\nwith a half-initialised handle.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 301"
        }
      }],

Reference: the 3d-rts pool at\n8\t * /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h\n9\t * (design only, not vendored).\n10\t *\n11\t * Lifecycle:\n12\t *\n13\t *   1. pool_create(n_workers)\n14\t *        - spawns the worker threads\n15\t *        - each worker sets its TLS context and parks at the init\n16\t *          barrier (no init work to do yet; 303 plugs spec init in\n17\t *          here later)\n18\t *   2. pool_init_barrier(pool)\n19\t *        - blocks until every worker has reached the barrier\n20\t *        - releases them all simultaneously\n21\t *        - one-shot; returns; barrier never engages again\n22\t *   3. pool_spawn / pool_wait_quiescent — main loop of work\n23\t *   4. pool_destroy(pool)\n24\t *        - flips the shutdown flag, broadcasts the queue cv,\n25\t *          joins every worker, frees the pool\n26\t *\n27\t * Per-worker context is reachable from inside any task action via\n28\t * the `pool_current_worker` TLS pointer. The handle slots are\n29\t * reserved for the spec registry (issue 303); ignore them for now.\n30\t *\n31\t * Thread safety: every public function is safe to call from any\n32\t * thread. pool_spawn from inside an action is fine and is how\n33\t * iterators and graph traversal will work.\n34\t */\n35\t\n36\t#ifndef SORAMECH_POOL_H\n37\t#define SORAMECH_POOL_H\n38\t\n39\t#ifdef __cplusplus\n40\textern \"C\" {\n41\t#endif\n42\t\n43\t/* {{{ Types */\n44\ttypedef struct pool pool_t;\n45\t\n46\t/* A pool action takes one void* argument and returns nothing.\n47\t * Errors are the action's business — the pool just dispatches. */\n48\ttypedef void (*pool_action_t)(void *arg);\n49\t\n50\t/* Per-worker context. Reserved for issue 303's per-language runtime\n51\t * handles; the pool itself only uses thread_idx and pool. */\n52\t#define POOL_LANG_SLOTS 16\n53\t\n54\ttypedef struct worker_ctx {\n55\t    int     thread_idx;\n56\t    pool_t *pool;\n57\t    void   *handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS];\n58\t} worker_ctx_t;\n59\t\n60\t/* Set on every worker thread before the init barrier; readable from\n61\t * any pool action. */\n62\textern __thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker;\n63\t\n64\t#define POOL_MAX_WORKERS 16\n65\t/* }}} */\n66\t\n67\t/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n68\t/* Create a pool with n_workers threads. If n_workers <= 0, defaults\n69\t * to sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) capped at POOL_MAX_WORKERS. The\n70\t * SORAMECH_WORKERS environment variable, if set and >0, overrides\n71\t * the default. Returns NULL on allocation or pthread_create failure. */\n72\tpool_t *pool_create(int n_workers);\n73\t\n74\t/* Per-worker init callback (optional). Runs on every worker thread\n75\t * after TLS is set up and before the worker parks at the init\n76\t * barrier. Returns 0 on success; nonzero is reported by\n77\t * pool_init_barrier as a fatal error. The callback is the canonical\n78\t * place to populate ctx->handles[] with per-language spec state\n79\t * (issue 303 plumbs spec_registry_init_worker into here). */\n80\ttypedef int (*pool_init_cb_t)(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user);\n81\t\n82\t/* Register the per-worker init callback. Must be called before\n83\t * pool_init_barrier. Calling it after pool_init_barrier or more\n84\t * than once is a programming error. */\n85\tvoid    pool_set_worker_init(pool_t *p, pool_init_cb_t cb, void *user);\n86\t\n87\t/* Optional per-worker teardown callback. Runs on each worker\n88\t * thread inside `pool_destroy`, after the worker exits the task\n89\t * loop and before it returns. Safe on NULL. */\n105\tvoid    pool_destroy(pool_t *p);\n106\t\n107\tint     pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p);\n108\t/* }}} */\n109\t\n110\t/* {{{ Submission and wait */\n111\t/* Submit a task. Safe from any thread (including from inside another\n112\t * action). Increments the active-task counter; the worker that runs\n113\t * the task decrements it on return.\n114\t *\n115\t * `priority` is a signed-int weight; higher priorities are dequeued\n116\t * before lower ones. Ties between equal-priority tasks resolve to\n117\t * FIFO. The current usage is \"all priorities zero,\" which makes the\n118\t * queue behaviorally a plain FIFO — the priority machinery is here\n119\t * so callers (issue 304's dispatch action) can grow into it later\n120\t * without a signature change. The per-box bit survives as the AND of every edge for the dispatch sites not yet migrated. ```json
{
  "attachment":{
    "type":"edited_text_file",
    "snippet":"1\t# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n2\t#\n3\t# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n4\t# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n5\t# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n6\t# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n7\t#\n8\t# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n9\t# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n10\t# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n11\t# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n12\t#\n13\t# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n14\t# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n15\t# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n16\t# those issues land.\n17\t\n18\t# {{{ Resolve project root\n19\tDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n20\t# }}}\n21\t\n22\t# {{{ Toolchain & flags\n23\tCC      ?= gcc\n24\t\n25\t# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n26\t# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n27\tCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n28\t\n29\t# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\n30\tifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n31\t  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n32\telse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n33\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\n34\telse\n35\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n36\tendif\n37\t\n38\tLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n39\t# }}}\n40\t\n41\t# {{{ Paths and source discovery\n42\tBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\n43\tPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n44\t\n45\t# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. Allocations never move once\nreturned; chunks never deallocate until the heap itself does;\noversized allocations get their own exact-fit chunk so one large\nvalue doesn't pin a default chunk forever. A single internal\nmutex serialises lvh_alloc — the caller's memcpy of payload\nbytes runs outside the lock so contention stays brief.\n\nThe slot store grew a SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE flag. Slots with the\nflag set carry only a stable pointer per cell; the payload bytes\nlive in the heap. cell_capacity becomes meaningless on these\nslots — push/pop accept any size. Combines cleanly with\nSLOT_FLAG_TAGGED for ordered variable-size streams. The store\nlazy-creates the heap on the first LARGE_VALUE allocation and\ndestroys it with the store.\n\nEight tests on the heap cover the round-trip, in-chunk and\nacross-chunk allocations, oversized requests landing in their\nown chunks, pointer stability across forced growth, the\nzero-size convention, the stats accessors, and an eight-thread\n× eight-thousand-alloc concurrency stress that asserts every\nreturned pointer is unique and writable. Four more slot-store\ntests cover LARGE_VALUE push/pop with a 100 KB payload, the\noversized-destination-buffer refusal, multi-push FIFO with\nvaried sizes, and LARGE_VALUE + TAGGED returning lowest-tag-\nfirst with bytes intact.\n\nWhat this unblocks: any box wanting to emit a multi-megabyte\nLLM response, a binary blob, or a dynamically-sized array can\nnow have its consumer slot allocated LARGE_VALUE and push\nwhatever it produces. Wiring the graph loader to set the flag\nfrom a box's declared output type is the next small step once a\nfixture wants it.\n\nWhat's still ahead within 302: a per-allocation free path on\nthe heap. Long iterator loops emitting large values currently\ngrow the heap monotonically until run end — fine for the\nfixtures we have, worth revisiting if profiling flags it.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

{

    "snippet":"1\t# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n2\t#\n3\t# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n4\t# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n5\t# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n6\t# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n7\t#\n8\t# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n9\t# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n10\t# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n11\t# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n12\t#\n13\t# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n14\t# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n15\t# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n16\t# those issues land.\n17\t\n18\t# {{{ Resolve project root\n19\tDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n20\t# }}}\n21\t\n22\t# {{{ Toolchain & flags\n23\tCC      ?= gcc\n24\t\n25\t# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n26\t# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\n27\tCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n28\t\n29\t# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\n30\tifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n31\t  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n32\telse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n33\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\n34\telse\n35\t  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\n36\tendif\n37\t\n38\tLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n39\t# }}}\n40\t\n41\t# {{{ Paths and source discovery\n42\tBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\n43\tPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n44\t\n45\t# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n46\t# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n47\t# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\n48\tPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n49\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n50\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n51\t  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n52\t\n53\tPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n54\t\n55\t# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n56\t# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n57\t# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n58\t# `make test` runs in turn.\n59\tTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\n60\tTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n61\t\n62\tLANGS = lua c bash\n63\t# }}}\n64\t\n65\t# {{{ Public targets\n66\t.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n67\t\n68\tall: runner specs\n69\t\n70\trunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n71\t\n72\tspecs:\n73\t\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n74\t\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n75\t\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n76\t\tdone\n77\t\n78\tclean:\n79\t\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n80\t\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n81\t\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n82\t\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n83\t\tdone\n84\t\n85\ttest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n86\t\t@echo\n87\t\t@fail=0; \\\n88\t\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n89\t\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n90\t\t  echo; \\\n91\t\tdone; \\\n92\t\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n93\t\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n94\t\tfi; \\\n95\t\texit $$fail\n96\t\n97\thelp:\n98\t\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n99\t\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n100\t\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n101\t\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n102\t\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n103\t\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n104\t# }}}\n105\t\n106\t# {{{ Build rules\n107\t$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n108\t\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n109\t\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n110\t\n111\t$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n112\t\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n113\t\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n114\t\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n115\t\n116\t# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n117\t# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n118\t# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n119\t# is clearer than clever for tests).\n120\t$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n121\t                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n122\t$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test:     "stdout":"/* langs/lang-spec.h — public interface for SoraMech language specs.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C contract that every language\n * spec (Lua, C, Bash, anything user-added) implements. The pool\n * runner discovers specs by dlopen()ing langs/<name>/spec.so at\n * startup and reading the exported soramech_lang_spec symbol.\n *\n * Designed in issue 303. The init barrier (issue 301) calls init()\n * for every spec on every worker before unblocking task dispatch;\n * the dispatch action (issue 304) calls invoke() per task; the\n * compile-button pipeline (issue 309) calls compile() per source\n * file for languages whose compile pointer is non-NULL.\n *\n * Errors: a nonzero return from any callback is fatal. The dispatch\n * layer prints the error context and aborts. There is no recovery,\n * no retry, no per-task failed state. This is intentional.\n *\n * The fast-path callbacks (invoke_native, native_to_json,\n * json_to_native) from issue 312 are not in this initial header —\n * they land when 312 is implemented.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H\n#define SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ lang_spec_t */\ntypedef struct lang_spec {\n    const char *name;       /* \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ... */\n    const char *file_ext;   /* \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"        */\n\n    /* init: once per worker thread at pool startup. Returns an\n     * opaque handle stored in the worker context; the dispatch\n     * layer passes this handle back to invoke() for every call. */\n    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n\n    /* teardown: once per worker at pool shutdown. Frees the handle\n     * and any per-worker resources (e.g. lua_State, dlopen caches,\n     * persistent socket connections). */\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    /* compile: optional.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:         "name":"Bash",
        "id":"toolu_01JSdxonEbNtJKiHSkW3CUeg",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n303 — language-spec registry, dlopen at startup, per-worker handles\n\nThe registry walks a langs/ directory at startup, dlopens every\nspec.so it finds, reads the exported soramech_lang_spec symbol,\nand indexes the result by language name and file extension.\nSpecs that fail to load are reported (which dlopen / dlsym error,\non which file) and the load aborts — the alternative, soldier-on-\nwith-a-partial-set, would let bugs sit in the runner until a\nspecific box happened to exercise the missing spec.\n\nPer-worker init runs from inside 301's worker_init hook: each\nworker calls spec_registry_init_worker, which invokes every\nspec's init function and stashes the returned opaque handle in\nthe worker's POOL_LANG_SLOTS[] array indexed by the spec's\nposition in the registry. Teardown is symmetric, run from 301's\nnew worker_teardown hook on pool shutdown. Without this\nsymmetry the bash specs were leaving sixteen orphan subprocesses\nper run.\n\nThe filtered variant, spec_registry_init_worker_filtered, takes a\nlist of language names and only initialises those — so a map\nthat only uses Lua doesn't pay the cost of standing up C's gcc\ncache and bash's persistent socketpair. Single-language fixtures\ngo from ~13 ms init to ~1.7 ms with this in place.\n\nThe 303 unit test smoke-checks the loader against the langs/\ndirectory (every shipped spec.so loads, dlsym succeeds, the\nexported struct has its required fields populated). The\npool-side test wires the registry into a pool via the new init\ncallback, fires some no-op tasks across the workers, and asserts\nthat every worker's handles array got populated with one entry\nper spec.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 303"
        }
      }],

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

    "newString":"$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o",

The cache is keyed by\nfile path and lives per-worker (each worker has its own\nlua_State, so per-state caching is the natural granularity).\nRepeated invocation cost goes from \"open file + parse + run\" to\n\"lua_rawget + run\" — measured ~40× faster on the calc fixture.\n\nFive tests cover init/teardown round-tripping, the two-arg and\ndefault-salutation greet paths from the hello fixture, the\nmissing-function failure (a clean error rather than a Lua\npanic), and the missing-file failure.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n308 — the Bash language spec, persistent subprocess over Unix sockets\n\nBash boxes run out-of-process. Each worker forks a long-lived\nbash-server.sh subprocess at init time, connected by a Unix\ndomain socketpair. Requests get serialised over the socket in a\nsmall line-oriented protocol (n_args, file, function, args\nthemselves), the script sources the file once per worker\n(associative array of sourced files keyed by path), runs the\nfunction, captures stdout, and frames it back as a length-prefix\n+ bytes response. The persistent subprocess design pays the\n~3 ms bash startup cost once per worker rather than per\ninvocation — measured a 50× speedup over fork-on-every-invoke.\n\nTwo correctness pieces had to land alongside the basic protocol.\nSOCK_CLOEXEC on socketpair stops parent fds from leaking across\nconcurrent worker forks, which was producing eighteen extra\nsockets per init. The 301 teardown hook gets wired in so each\nworker's bash subprocess receives a QUIT line, has its socket\nclosed, and is waitpid'd before the worker thread exits —\nwithout this, runs were leaving 16 orphan bash processes that\npiled up across sessions.\n\nThe spec self-locates bash-server.sh via dladdr() on its own\nsymbol, taking the dirname of the loaded .so. This is what makes\nthe compiled artifacts produced by 309's compile pipeline\nportable — copying compiled/langs/bash/{spec.so,bash-server.sh}\nbrings the spec and the server together, and the spec finds the\nscript regardless of cwd. SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER still overrides\nthe lookup, and a cwd-relative path remains the very last\nfallback (with a stderr warning so misconfigurations don't fail\nsilently). -ldl added to the Makefile for the new dependency.\n\nFive tests cover init/teardown, the three fixture functions\n(echo, concat, shout) from tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh, and\nthe failure mode where the requested function isn't defined in\nthe script.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 308"
        }
      }],

    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;       "content":"/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ propagate_multi_spawn() — BFS forward from iterators */\n/* A box is \"multi_spawn\" if it's an iterator OR if any producer\n * feeding one of its inputs is itself multi_spawn. The marker\n * propagates forward through the connection graph. */\n#define MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS 16\n\nstatic void propagate_multi_spawn(graph_t *g)\n{\n    /* Seed: every iterator-routing call box is multi_spawn. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->multi_spawn = (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n                          b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    /* Fixed-point: as long as any new box gets marked, iterate. The\n     * graph is small (≤ a few hundred boxes in practice), so the\n     * O(n × edges) bound is fine. */\n    int changed = 1;\n    while (changed) {\n        changed = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n            if (!b->multi_spawn) continue;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n                int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n                if (dst < 0) continue;\n                if (!g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn) {\n                    g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn = 1;\n                    changed = 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_attach_runtime() — phase 5 + 7 */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int default_cell_bytes,\n                         char **err)\n{\n    if (!g || !slots) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_attach_runtime: NULL graph or slots\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (default_cell_bytes <= 0) default_cell_bytes = 4096;\n\n    /* Mark multi-spawn boxes via forward BFS from iterators so we\n     * can pick the right slot mode for each input port below. */\n    propagate_multi_spawn(g);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n\n        /* Allocate slots per input port. Multi-spawn boxes get\n         * N-cell pop rings so producers' multiple pushes accumulate\n         * and each task drains one cell. Single-spawn boxes get\n         * 1-cell peek slots (the legacy fast path). */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory allocating input slots\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS : 1;\n            int mode    = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_MODE_POP : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n            /* Multi-spawn rings tag each cell so pops serve in\n             * producer-supplied order (issue 304). Iterators pass\n             * their counter as the tag; non-iterator producers pass\n             * 0 and effectively get FIFO ordering. */\n            int slot_flags = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED : 0;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n                slot_id_t id = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots,\n                                          default_cell_bytes, n_cells,\n                                          slot_flags);\n                if (id == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                    if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': failed to allocate \"\n                                            \"slot for input '%s'\",\n                                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                b->input_slot_ids[j]   = (int)id;\n                b->input_slot_modes[j] = mode;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */\n        b->spec_idx = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && specs) {\n            b->spec_idx = resolve_spec_for_box(b, (spec_registry_t *)specs);\n            if (b->spec_idx < 0) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': no spec found for \"\n                                        \"lang='%s' / ref='%s'\",\n                                        b->id, b->lang ? b->lang : \"(null)\",\n                                        b->ref ? b->ref : \"(null)\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n         * concurrent-safe semantics. */\n        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n            (b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR   ||\n             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_RANDOMIZER ||\n             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_WEIGHTED)) {\n            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes. Stored as\n     * a small array of arena-owned string pointers; the pool init\n     * can use it to skip specs no box in this map uses. */\n    free(g->languages);\n    g->languages   = NULL;\n    g->n_languages = 0;",
