      "content":"/* {{{ test_native_invoke_classification() */\n/* Verifies issue 312's per-edge fast-path classification:\n *\n *  - input_edge_native[port]  is 1 iff every producer feeding\n *    that port is a call box in the consumer's language.\n *    Literals and data-box producers count as NOT native — they\n *    emit JSON text the consumer's spec must parse.\n *  - output_edge_native[edge] is 1 iff the consumer at the other\n *    end of that connection is a call box in this box's language.\n *  - use_native_invoke remains as the per-box AND of every edge,\n *    used by dispatch sites not yet migrated to per-edge. */\nstatic int test_native_invoke_classification(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n\n    /* hello: greet (lua) has a literal-fed input → input edge is\n     * JSON. greet has no outgoing connections in this fixture.\n     * Per-edge: input 0 not native; vacuous all-outs. Per-box AND\n     * = 0 because the input is a JSON edge. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n        const box_t *who   = graph_box_by_id(g, \"who\");\n        ASSERT(greet->n_inputs == 2);\n        ASSERT(greet->input_edge_native != NULL);\n        ASSERT(greet->input_edge_native[0] == 0);  /* fed by data box `who` */\n        ASSERT(greet->input_edge_native[1] == 0);  /* literal */\n        ASSERT(greet->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(who->use_native_invoke   == 0);     /* who is BOX_DATA */\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n\n    /* comparator: classify (lua) has a literal input but its\n     * three outgoing edges all feed lua call boxes → outputs are\n     * native, input is JSON. low/mid/high have no outgoing\n     * connections and their input comes from classify (a Lua call\n     * box) → input native, vacuous outs, all-native = use_native. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/comparator\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        const box_t *classify = graph_box_by_id(g, \"classify\");\n        const box_t *low      = graph_box_by_id(g, \"low\");\n\n        ASSERT(classify->input_edge_native[0]  == 0);  /* literal */\n        ASSERT(classify->n_connections         == 3);\n        ASSERT(classify->output_edge_native[0] == 1);  /* lt → low (lua) */\n        ASSERT(classify->output_edge_native[1] == 1);  /* eq → mid (lua) */\n        ASSERT(classify->output_edge_native[2] == 1);  /* gt → high (lua) */\n        ASSERT(classify->use_native_invoke     == 0);  /* per-box AND fails on input */\n\n        /* low has two inputs: port 0 \"tag\" (literal) and port 1\n         * \"v\" (fed by classify, a Lua call box). */\n        ASSERT(low->n_inputs               == 2);\n        ASSERT(low->input_edge_native[0]   == 0);   /* literal \"tag\"      */\n        ASSERT(low->input_edge_native[1]   == 1);   /* lua classify → \"v\" */\n        /* use_native_invoke is the AND across all ports, so the\n         * literal port keeps it at 0 even though the lua input\n         * is native. */\n        ASSERT(low->use_native_invoke      == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"mid\") ->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"high\")->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n\n    /* pipeline: lua → c → bash chain. Every adjacent edge crosses\n     * a language boundary; per-edge bits are 0 across the board. */\n    {\n        graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/pipeline\", &err);\n        ASSERT(g);\n        const box_t *dbl = graph_box_by_id(g, \"double\");  /* lua */\n        ASSERT(dbl->n_connections >= 1);\n        ASSERT(dbl->output_edge_native[0] == 0);          /* → addone (c) */\n        ASSERT(dbl->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"addone\")->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        ASSERT(graph_box_by_id(g, \"shout\") ->use_native_invoke == 0);\n        graph_destroy(g);\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_randomizer_weighted_parsing() */\n/* Verifies issue 304's randomizer and weighted routing schemas\n * load cleanly with the right per-kind fields. */\nstatic int test_randomizer_weighted_parsing(void)\n{\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-routing-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    ASSERT(dir);\n\n    char path[4096];\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", dir);\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"r\\\",\\\"entry_box_id\\\":\\\"rnd\\\"}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes\", dir); mkdir(path, 0755);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/rnd.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"rnd\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"lang\\\":\\\"lua\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"ref\\\":\\\"r.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"r\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"randomizer\\\",\\\"n_outputs\\\":4}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/boxes/wtd.json\", dir);\n    fp = fopen(path, \"w\");\n    fputs(\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"wtd\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\\\"lang\\\":\\\"lua\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"ref\\\":\\\"r.lua\\\",\\\"fn\\\":\\\"w\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"routing\\\":{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"weighted\\\",\\\"weights\\\":[0.8,0.2]}}\", fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",
    "userModified":false,

          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n305 — topology resolution, cycle detection, slot-store / spec-registry attach\n\nThe graph loader gains the three passes that turn a directory of\nparsed box files into something the dispatch action can run on:\n\n1. resolve_topology fills in to_box_idx and to_input_idx on every\n   outgoing connection. Errors are explicit and quote the\n   offending box's id plus the missing reference, rather than a\n   numeric index — the message goes to the human writing the\n   map, not the runtime.\n\n2. detect_cycles refuses any cycle in the dataflow except cycles\n   that pass through an iterator box. The iterator exception is\n   how phase 3's loop construct gets expressed in a strictly\n   topology-sortable language — iterators introduce a barrier,\n   so the cycle is structurally bounded. Non-iterator cycles\n   would deadlock the dispatch's spawn-on-input-ready rule, so\n   they're a load-time error rather than a runtime hang.\n\n3. graph_attach_runtime ties the now-validated graph to the\n   actual runtime resources: every input port gets a slot\n   allocated from the slot store (1-cell peek for this baseline;\n   issues 304 and 312 grow this into pop rings and tagged slots),\n   and every call box gets its spec resolved by language + file\n   extension against the 303 registry. The pass also enumerates\n   the distinct languages the graph uses so the spec init can\n   skip languages no box in this map references.\n\nSix tests gained alongside the existing parse coverage: two for\nunresolved connection endpoints (nonexistent box, nonexistent\ninput), two for the cycle rule (non-iterator cycle rejected,\niterator cycle allowed), and one for the duplicate-id case the\nprevious parse layer didn't catch on its own.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 305"
        }
      }],
    "role":"assistant",
    "id":"msg_01A63t86xL5tbyeLmJG2hZq7",

Aligned to the unified routing schema\n9\t * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n10\t * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n11\t * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n12\t * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n13\t *\n14\t * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n15\t * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n16\t * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n17\t * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n18\t * one call.\n19\t *\n20\t * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n21\t * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n22\t * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n23\t * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n24\t * whether to abort or surface the error.\n25\t *\n26\t * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n27\t * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n28\t * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n29\t * routing schema validated).\n30\t *\n31\t * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n32\t *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n33\t *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n34\t *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n35\t *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n36\t *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n37\t *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n38\t *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n39\t *\n40\t * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n41\t */\n42\t\n43\t#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n44\t#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n45\t\n46\t#include <stddef.h>\n47\t\n48\t#ifdef __cplusplus\n49\textern \"C\" {\n50\t#endif\n51\t\n52\t/* {{{ Box kinds */\n53\ttypedef enum {\n54\t    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n55\t    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n56\t    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n57\t} box_kind_t;\n58\t/* }}} */\n59\t\n60\t/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\n61\ttypedef enum {\n62\t    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n63\t    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n64\t    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n65\t    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n66\t    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n67\t    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n68\t} routing_kind_t;\n69\t\n70\ttypedef struct {\n71\t    routing_kind_t kind;\n72\t    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n73\t    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n74\t    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n75\t     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n76\t    const double  *weights;\n77\t} routing_t;\n78\t/* }}} */\n79\t\n80\t/* {{{ Input port declaration */\n81\ttypedef struct {\n82\t    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n83\t    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n84\t    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n85\t    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n86\t} input_decl_t;\n87\t/* }}} */\n88\t\n89\t/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n90\t/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n91\t * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n92\t * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\n93\ttypedef struct {\n94\t    const char *to_box;     "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". A box is \"native-eligible\" iff every adjacent call box —\n     * any producer feeding its inputs AND any consumer reading its\n     * output — shares the box's language. Data boxes and\n     * file_write boxes don't constrain (they emit/consume raw\n     * bytes that any spec interprets uniformly).\n     *\n     * Computed in graph_load (not graph_attach_runtime) because\n     * it's purely topology-derived and doesn't need the slot\n     * store or registry. The dispatch action picks\n     * `spec->invoke_native` when this flag is set, falling back to\n     * `invoke_json` or `invoke`. Our current specs all leave\n     * invoke_native NULL so the fallback runs and behaviour is\n     * unchanged — but the infrastructure is in place. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n        b->use_native_invoke  = 0;\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n\n        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n         * explicitly below. */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n         * language. Only true\n         * when EVERY edge in both directions is native. */\n        b->use_native_invoke = (all_ins_native && all_outs_native) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    return g;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

      "content":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). When\n     * 1 and `events` is non-NULL, dispatch_action also emits\n     * task_input / task_output events with the byte payloads\n     * (truncated to 4 KB per the architecture doc). */\n    int                   log_values;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). When\n     * 1 and `events` is non-NULL, dispatch_action also emits\n     * task_input / task_output events with the byte payloads\n     * (truncated to 4 KB per the architecture doc). */\n    int                   log_values;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

This is how an iterator \"loops\"\n         * over its input queue without the upstream needing to\n         * push twice. */\n        if (b->multi_spawn && box_pop_ready(ctx, t->box_id)) {\n            dispatch_spawn(ctx, t->box_id, 0);\n        }\n    } else if (b) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: box '%s' failed (rc=%d)\\n\", b->id, rc);\n    }\n\n    long end_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events) {\n        event_queue_task_end(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx,\n                             end_us - start_us, out_size);\n    }\n\n    free(out_buf);\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

ctx->default_out_capacity : 4096;\n619\t    char *out_buf = malloc((size_t)out_capacity);\n620\t    int rc = -1;\n621\t    if (out_buf && b) {\n622\t        switch (b->kind) {\n623\t            case BOX_CALL:\n624\t                rc = do_call_box(ctx, b, task_id, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n625\t                break;\n626\t            case BOX_DATA:\n627\t                rc = do_data_box(ctx, b, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n628\t                break;\n629\t            case BOX_FILE_WRITE:\n630\t                rc = do_file_write_box(ctx, b, task_id, &out_size);\n631\t                break;\n632\t        }\n633\t    }\n634\t\n635\t    if (rc == 0 && b) {\n636\t        capture(ctx, t->box_id, out_buf, out_size);\n637\t        /* Verbose: emit the task's output payload before push (so\n638\t         * the log entries land in computation order). */\n639\t        if (ctx->log_values && ctx->events) {\n640\t            event_queue_task_output(ctx->events, now_secs(),\n641\t                                    task_id, out_buf, out_size);\n642\t        }\n643\t        /* file_write boxes don't push (they're sinks). */\n644\t        if (b->kind != BOX_FILE_WRITE) {\n645\t            push_routed(ctx, b, out_buf, out_size);\n646\t        }\n647\t        /* Iterator-style re-spawn: if this is a multi-spawn box and\n648\t         * any POP input still has queued values, schedule another\n649\t         * task on the same box.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/307-c-spec-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/308-bash-spec-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/314-json-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n\n# Pattern: link a test binary. $^ collects the .o files declared\n# above plus the test's own .o file.\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%.o\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n# }}}\n",

Spawn-on-input-ready means\nthe very push that completes a consumer's input set triggers\nthe consumer's spawn — no thread blocks on a slot, no central\nscheduler walks the graph.\n\nRouting kinds shipped: plain (fan to every connection),\ncomparator (lt/eq/gt against a comparand), iterator (atomic\ncounter picks the branch), randomizer (hash the counter so\nconsecutive invocations land on different branches), and\nweighted (cumulative-band lookup against a normalised weight\nlist). Each kind reads its branch from the box's outgoing\nconnections by from_branch name; the parser already validates\nthem at load time.\n\nIterators add a multi-spawn rule: a forward BFS from every\niterator marks every reachable box as multi-spawn. Multi-spawn\nboxes get N-cell pop ring slots instead of 1-cell peek so a\nsingle iterator firing can push three values that three\nseparate consumer tasks each drain in turn. After a multi-spawn\ntask completes, dispatch checks whether any of its pop inputs\nstill have queued values and auto-respawns if so — a single\nproducer push wakes the whole chain without external scheduling.\n\nIterator slots are tagged: the iterator's counter snapshot rides\nwith each push as a 4-byte ordering tag. The consumer's slot is\nSLOT_FLAG_TAGGED, so pops serve the lowest-tag cell first. Two\niterator tasks racing on different workers produce ordered\noutput at the consumer regardless of which finishes first.\n\nThe integration-style tests cover the happy path through the\nhello, calc, comparator, and iter-route fixtures; the\ncomparator routing test asserts only the matching branch fired;\nthe iterator tests cover both single-fire (one value, one\nbranch) and multi-fire (three values walk the counter through\nall three branches).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

    "snippet":"1\t/* src/012-dispatch.c — task dispatch layer, implementation.\n2\t *\n3\t * The pool action does five things, in order:\n4\t *\n5\t *   1. Look up the box from the graph.\n6\t *   2. Read each input port's value from its slot (peek mode for\n7\t *      this iteration; pop mode + iterator multi-spawn land later).\n8\t *   3. Do the box's work:\n9\t *        - BOX_CALL — invoke the resolved language spec via the\n10\t *          worker's per-language handle.\n11\t *        - BOX_DATA — read the file at `box->path` (resolved\n12\t *          relative to `graph_map_dir` if non-absolute) and use\n13\t *          its contents as the output.\n14\t *        - BOX_FILE_WRITE — write the second input (\"text\") to the\n15\t *          path given by the first input or by box->path.\n16\t *   4. Push the resulting bytes to every outgoing connection's\n17\t *      consumer input slot.\n18\t *   5. For each consumer, fire the spawn-on-input-ready check,\n19\t *      which spawns the consumer iff it has all required inputs\n20\t *      and hasn't been spawned yet (single-spawn guard via an\n21\t *      atomic CAS).\n22\t *\n23\t * The optional `capture_outputs` mode also memcpy's the output\n24\t * bytes into `ctx->last_outputs[box_id]` so tests can verify\n25\t * what each box produced after the pool quiesces.\n26\t *\n27\t * Designed in issue 304.\n28\t */\n29\t\n30\t#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n31\t\n32\t#include <stdarg.h>\n33\t#include <stdio.h>\n34\t#include <stdlib.h>\n35\t#include <string.h>\n36\t#include <sys/stat.h>\n37\t#include <time.h>\n38\t\n39\t/* {{{ now_secs() / mono_us() — timestamps */\n40\tstatic double now_secs(void)\n41\t{\n42\t    struct timespec ts;\n43\t    clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);\n44\t    return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;\n45\t}\n46\t\n47\tstatic long mono_us(void)\n48\t{\n49\t    struct timespec ts;\n50\t    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);\n51\t    return (long)ts.tv_sec * 1000000L + ts.tv_nsec / 1000;\n52\t}\n53\t/* }}} */\n54\t\n55\t/* {{{ err_fmt() — malloc'd diagnostic string */\n56\t__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\n57\tstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n58\t{\n59\t    char buf[512];\n60\t    va_list ap;\n61\t    va_start(ap, fmt);\n62\t    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n63\t    va_end(ap);\n64\t    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n65\t    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n66\t    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n67\t    if (!out) return NULL;\n68\t    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n69\t    out[len] = '\\0';\n70\t    return out;\n71\t}\n72\t/* }}} */\n73\t\n74\t/* {{{ dispatch_ctx_init() */\n75\tint dispatch_ctx_init(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n76\t                      const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n77\t                      spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n78\t                      int enable_output_capture, char **err)\n79\t{\n80\t    if (!ctx || !g) {\n81\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"dispatch_ctx_init: NULL ctx or graph\");\n82\t        return -1;\n83\t    }\n84\t    memset(ctx, 0, sizeof *ctx);\n85\t    ctx->graph = g;\n86\t    ctx->slots = s;\n87\t    ctx->specs = r;\n88\t    ctx->pool  = p;\n89\t    atomic_init(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 0);\n90\t    atomic_init(&ctx->next_task_id,     0);\n91\t    ctx->n_boxes              = graph_n_boxes(g);\n92\t    ctx->default_out_capacity = 4096;\n93\t    ctx->events               = NULL;     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:           "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n311 — last-run.jsonl event log and the integration test runner\n\nEvery soramech-pool run now writes one JSONL event per\ninteresting thing that happened: a run_start at the top, one\ntask_submit when the dispatch enqueues a task, task_start when\na worker picks it up, task_end on completion with elapsed\nmicroseconds, and run_end at the bottom. Two opt-in verbose\ngates ride on the same plumbing — SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1 adds\ntask_input / task_output payloads (truncated to 4 KB so a\nmulti-megabyte LLM response doesn't bury the log), and\nSORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1 adds slot_alloc events so the slot store's\nallocation pattern can be inspected for a given map.\n\nThe write path is a dedicated single-thread MPSC queue\n(src/014-event-queue) drained by a writer thread that\nserialises events with the JSON writer from 314. Producers do\nnot block on disk; events accumulate in the queue under a\nmutex and the writer drains in batches outside the lock.\nVerbose events bypass the queue and serialise straight through\nthe writer's mutex, since they're rare and their payloads are\nlarge enough that double-buffering them through the queue\nwould chew memory.\n\nIntegration tests live in scripts/run-tests.sh — a small shell\nrunner that invokes soramech-pool against every fixture map\nunder tests/maps/, captures stdout, and asserts on expected\nsubstrings. Five fixtures shipped:\n\n  - calc       — single-box arithmetic, smoke test for Lua\n  - hello      — data box → Lua call, with a literal default\n  - comparator — three-way routing on a literal input\n  - iter-route — iterator with three branches drained one each\n  - pipeline   — Lua → C → Bash → file_write end-to-end chain\n\nThe pipeline fixture also exercises the file_write box kind by\nasserting the output file contains exactly \"11!\" after the run.\nThe Makefile's `test` target invokes run-tests.sh as the final\nstep, so a single `make test` covers both the in-process unit\ntests and the full multi-language integration matrix.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 311"
        }
      }],

          "command":"git -C /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n312 — per-edge same-language classification, plus the spec contract for it\n\nThree pieces land together:\n\nThe lang_spec_t contract grows two typedef'd function-pointer\nslots a spec may specialise: invoke_native (callable when every\nadjacent wire on this box stays in this language) and\ninvoke_json (callable when the wire is JSON). Both share the\nsame signature as the canonical invoke and are NULL by default\n— specs that haven't specialised silently fall through to the\nJSON-bridge invoke. Two bridges round out the contract:\nnative_to_json and json_to_native, for the boundary case where\na value has to cross a language line mid-graph.\n\nThe graph loader computes, per call box, two parallel bit\narrays: input_edge_native[port] is true iff every producer\nfeeding that port is a call box in the consumer's language, and\noutput_edge_native[edge] is true iff the consumer on the other\nend of each outgoing connection is a call box in this box's\nlanguage. Literals and data-box producers count as JSON edges\non the input side — they emit text the consumer's spec has to\nparse — so a Lua box fed by a literal correctly classifies its\ninput edge as non-native even though the box itself runs Lua.\nThe earlier per-box use_native_invoke bit survives as the AND\nacross every edge, used by the dispatch sites not yet migrated\nto per-edge consultation. Five tests on three fixtures cover\nthe hello/comparator/pipeline cases — mixed-language pipeline,\nall-Lua comparator with literal inputs, single-box hello.\n\nThe dispatch layer picks invoke_native vs invoke_json vs invoke\non every call. Current specs have all four NULL'd except for\ninvoke, so the fallback runs end-to-end and behaviour is\nunchanged from before — the infrastructure is in place, the\nspecialised serialisations land per-spec once the contract is\nreal.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 312"
        }

The script walks\nevery box file to enumerate the languages the map actually uses,\ncopies meta.json + boxes/ + src/ + data/ + the top-level\nfixture files verbatim, copies one spec.so per used language\ninto compiled/langs/<lang>/, copies bash-server.sh alongside the\nbash spec when bash is in use, pre-compiles every C box source\ninto compiled/bin/ so packaging errors surface at compile time\nrather than at run time, drops a real copy of the soramech-pool\nbinary as compiled/pool-runner, and writes a small manifest\nwith the n_boxes / languages / compiled_at stats.\n\nTwo correctness points worth recording. The pool-runner inside\nthe artifact has to be a real copy and not a symlink: the\nrunner discovers its sibling langs/ via readlink(\"/proc/self/exe\"),\nwhich follows symlinks to their canonical target, so a\nsymlinked pool-runner inside compiled/ would resolve back to\nthe project tree and pick up the wrong langs/. And the bash\nspec's bash-server.sh location is found via dladdr() on a local\nsymbol — without that, the script falls back to a cwd-relative\npath that the compiled artifact can't satisfy.\n\n.gitignore picks up the per-map compiled/ pattern so the\nartifacts never get tracked, and a core.* pattern so kernel\ncoredumps that land at the project root don't either.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 309"

        "text":"Ha, yeah — it does sound like a lot. But the 21 commits aren't 21 distinct issues. Breaking it down:\n\n- **10 issues with one commit each**: 301, 302, 304, 305, 306, 308, 309, 310, 311, 314 — the substantive ones\n- **3 issues with two commits each**: 303 (impl + a missed test-file addendum), 307 (the \"language never bends to SoraMech\" rule strengthening as a design refinement, then the actual C spec implementation), 312 (per-edge design refinement, then the implementation)\n- **3 design-only new issues**: 315 (refcounted artifacts), 316 (test runner), 317 (data-box JSON bridge) — these had no code, just the spec\n- **2 non-issue commits**: the phase-3 progress doc reflection, and the soramech-pool integration capstone\n\nSo **16 distinct issue files touched**, **15 of phase 3's 17 issues now have committed implementations** (only 313 — research-stage, parked — and 315/316/317 — fresh designs — remain unimplemented). The big number partly reflects that a lot of accumulated work had piled up uncommitted across multiple sessions before the slicing started, and partly that strictness multiplies commits (every nuance of a design refinement gets its own commit so the diff stays scoped).\n\nWhat it really represents is: **phase 3 is essentially built**. The pool runner runs multi-language maps end-to-end. The compile pipeline produces portable artifacts. The JSONL run log is wired. All five fixtures pass. The remaining work is mostly polish (315/316/317) and the deferred deep-optimization items (real native serializations for 312, size-class allocator for 302, typed C wrapper for 307)."

  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The critical path to \"phase 3 done\" runs through four blockers from the phase-3 goal checklist that aren't checked off yet. Everything else is parallel or deferrable.\n\n### Critical path\n\n**1. Wire SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE into the graph loader** *(small)*\nThe LVH foundation is in place (issue 302's follow-on landed in commit `079bc3a`), but `graph_attach_runtime` doesn't yet set `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE` on consumer slots when the producer declares `output_capacity: 0`. A few lines in the loader + one fixture (a box producing a kilobyte-scale string, asserted downstream) closes the checklist item.\n\n**2. Issue 317 — data-box JSON bridge** *(substantial)*\nEvery spec gains `native_to_json` and `json_to_native`. The Lua spec walks a `lua_State` stack value; the C spec leans on 307's type system; the bash spec validates JSON pass-through. Without this, data boxes can only emit hand-written JSON literals or file contents. With it, a Lua data box returns an idiomatic table and the rest of the graph reads structured JSON. **This is foundational for any of the 6 remaining integration fixtures that want non-trivial data authoring.**\n\n**3. Six more integration fixtures** *(medium)*\nThe phase-3 checklist names \"all 11 integration test maps.\" Five fixtures ship today (calc, hello, comparator, iter-route, pipeline). The missing six should exercise corners the current fixtures don't touch:\n- variable-size output through LVH (depends on step 1)\n- many-to-one fan-in into a single consumer slot\n- nested iterators (iterator feeding another iterator)\n- error-path box (a function that returns nonzero) — surfaces whether dispatch failure is recoverable or fatal as designed\n- cross-language data box (depends on step 2)\n- file_write with a computed (non-literal) path input\nEach new fixture will likely surface a bug or design gap that needs fixing as a sub-commit.\n\n**4. Phase 3 demo map** *(small)*\nA showpiece map that ties everything together — multi-language, iterator, comparator, file_write, variable-size output. Goes in `issues/completed/demos/` per the CLAUDE.md phase-demo convention. Runnable from the project-root demo selector script.\n\n**5. Phase 2 retirement** *(small)*\nDelete `src/004-executor.lua`, `src/007-runner-main.lua`, `src/003-loader.lua`, `drivers/*.sh`. Update docs / README to point at `soramech-pool` as the entry point. This is the final commit of phase 3.\n\n### Parallel tracks (any order, none block the path)\n\n- **316 test runner** — `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh`. ~1 session. Pure quality-of-life for the dev loop.\n- **315 refcounted compiled artifacts** — `scripts/soramech-ref.sh` plus the fork-on-live-refs logic in `soramech-compile.sh`. ~2 sessions. Matters once anyone actually pins to a compiled artifact across time; not before.\n- **307 typed C wrapper** — code-generator that lifts plain C functions into `sm_box_entry` wrappers. ~2-3 sessions. Real product-quality boost for C-box authors; not strictly required for the demo if you write the spec ABI by hand.\n- **306 rich Lua return types** — multi-value and table returns from Lua boxes. ~1 session. Convenience.\n\n### Deferred indefinitely (performance or research)\n\n- **302 size-class allocator** — current `malloc`-per-slot pattern is fine for static-graph workloads.\n- **302 per-allocation free in LVH** — only matters if a long iterator loop emits large values; revisit when profiling demands.\n- **304 distributor routing** — argmin over downstream slot fill. Niche; the four implemented routing kinds cover every fixture we have.\n- **312 real native serializations** — every spec's `invoke_native` aliases `invoke` right now; the per-edge infrastructure is in place, the binary formats are spec-author work. Pure perf.\n- **313 whole-program same-language merge** — research, parked.\n\n### Suggested sequencing\n\nDo **1 → 2 → 3** sequentially (each unlocks the next), then **4 → 5** to close out the phase. Spin **316** off whenever you want a faster dev loop. Treat the rest as opportunistic.\n\nEstimated effort to close the critical path: **7–10 focused sessions**, dominated by 317 and the six fixtures."
      }],

        "text":"Good catch. Let me explain, fix it, then we'll move on to 317.\n\n### What \"wire SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE into the graph loader\" actually means\n\nIssue **302** (the slot store) has two layers:\n\n- **The mechanism** — `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE` on the slot store, plus `src/015-large-value-heap.{c,h}`. Already shipped (commit `079bc3a`). A slot allocated with that flag holds payload bytes in the heap instead of inline, so the cell can be any size.\n\n- **The policy** — *when* should a slot get that flag? The design rule is: any slot whose producer declares `output_capacity: 0` (variable-size) needs `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE`, because the producer's pushes won't fit in a fixed-size cell. That decision lives in `graph_attach_runtime`.\n\nThe mechanism shipped without the policy. The 302 commit message even noted it:\n\n> Wiring the graph loader to set the flag from a box's declared output type is the next small step once a fixture wants it.\n\nSo it's the deferred half of 302. Belongs in 302's issue file. Fixing it now."

      "content":"        /* Allocate slots per input port. Multi-spawn boxes get\n         * N-cell pop rings so producers' multiple pushes accumulate\n         * and each task drains one cell. Single-spawn boxes get\n         * 1-cell peek slots (the legacy fast path). */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory allocating input slots\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS : 1;\n            int mode    = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_MODE_POP : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n            /* Multi-spawn rings tag each cell so pops serve in\n             * producer-supplied order (issue 304). Iterators pass\n             * their counter as the tag; non-iterator producers pass\n             * 0 and effectively get FIFO ordering. */\n            int slot_flags = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED : 0;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n                slot_id_t id = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots,\n                                          default_cell_bytes, n_cells,\n                                          slot_flags);\n                if (id == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                    if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': failed to allocate \"\n                                            \"slot for input '%s'\",\n                                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                b->input_slot_ids[j]   = (int)id;\n                b->input_slot_modes[j] = mode;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */",

          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_variable_size_producer_lvh_wiring() */\n/* 302 follow-on: graph_attach_runtime sets SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE on\n * any input slot whose producer declares variable-size output\n * (output_capacity == 0). The hello fixture pairs greet (call,\n * output_capacity=256) with who (data box, output_capacity defaults\n * to 0). After attach, greet's input port 0 (`name`, fed by who)\n * should accept a push that exceeds the slot's normal cell\n * capacity, while port 1 (`salutation`, literal-only) should not. */\nstatic int test_variable_size_producer_lvh_wiring(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g);\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    ASSERT(s);\n    /* Tight default cell so the discriminator (push 2 KB) is well\n     * outside it — without LARGE_VALUE the push would fail. */\n    ASSERT(graph_attach_runtime(g, s, r, 512, &err) == 0);\n\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet && greet->n_inputs == 2);\n\n    char big[2048];\n    memset(big, 'A', sizeof big);\n\n    /* Port 0 (`name`) is fed by data box `who` → LARGE_VALUE. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, greet->input_slot_ids[0], big, sizeof big, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Port 1 (`salutation`) has only a literal — no variable-size\n     * producer → fixed-size slot → 2 KB push exceeds cell capacity\n     * and fails. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, greet->input_slot_ids[1], big, sizeof big, 0) == -1);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/010-graph-loader-test.c"
        }
      }],

After attach, greet's input port 0 (`name`, fed by who)\n * should accept a push that exceeds the slot's normal cell\n * capacity, while port 1 (`salutation`, literal-only) should not. */\nstatic int test_variable_size_producer_lvh_wiring(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    ASSERT(g);\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r);\n\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    ASSERT(s);\n    /* Tight default cell so the discriminator (push 2 KB) is well\n     * outside it — without LARGE_VALUE the push would fail. */\n    ASSERT(graph_attach_runtime(g, s, r, 512, &err) == 0);\n\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet && greet->n_inputs == 2);\n\n    char big[2048];\n    memset(big, 'A', sizeof big);\n\n    /* Port 0 (`name`) is fed by data box `who` → LARGE_VALUE. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, greet->input_slot_ids[0], big, sizeof big, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Port 1 (`salutation`) has only a literal — no variable-size\n     * producer → fixed-size slot → 2 KB push exceeds cell capacity\n     * and fails. */\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, greet->input_slot_ids[1], big, sizeof big, 0) == -1);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{"
  },

        },
        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"What this unblocks: any box that wants to emit a variable-size\noutput can now declare its downstream consumer slots with\nSLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE and produce payloads whose size isn't\nknown at graph-load time. The wiring from declared box output\ntype to the LARGE_VALUE flag in `graph_attach_runtime` lands as\na follow-on once a fixture or real graph requires it; the\nfoundation is in place.\n\nWhat's still deferred within 302:",
          "new_string":"What this unblocks: any box that wants to emit a variable-size\noutput can now declare its downstream consumer slots with\nSLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE and produce payloads whose size isn't\nknown at graph-load time. The wiring from declared box output\ntype to the LARGE_VALUE flag in `graph_attach_runtime` lands as\na follow-on once a fixture or real graph requires it; the\nfoundation is in place.\n\n### Producer-driven LARGE_VALUE wiring — 2026-05-19\n\nThe \"wiring from declared box output type\" deferred above is\nnow in place. During `graph_attach_runtime`, each consumer\ninput slot's flags get OR'd with `SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE` if any\nproducer feeding that port declares `output_capacity == 0`. The\nrule covers both data boxes (which default to 0 because the\nfield isn't in their JSON schema) and call boxes that opt into\nvariable-size output by setting `\"output_capacity\": 0`. The discriminator is the slot's capacity:\nwithout LARGE_VALUE the 2 KB push exceeds 512 and is rejected;\nwith it the heap absorbs the bytes and the push lands.\n\nThe remaining phase-3 checklist item \"Variable-size outputs\nwork via the large-value heap\" is now satisfied end-to-end at\nthe slot-store boundary. A graph fixture that exercises the\npath on the dispatch side — a Lua box returning a multi-KB\nstring and a downstream box reading it — is a one-line fixture\naddition and lands with the 6-more-integration-fixtures task.\n\nWhat's still deferred within 302:",

Filling in the\nmissing half — graph_attach_runtime now OR's SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE\nonto any input slot whose producer reports output_capacity == 0.\nData boxes get that for free since they don't set the field;\ncall boxes opt in by writing \"output_capacity\": 0 in their box\nJSON. Fan-in mixing fixed-size and variable-size producers\nupgrades the whole slot to LARGE_VALUE — conservative since the\nslot can only carry one format, and the heap path handles small\npayloads fine.\n\nA new test in 010-graph-loader-test pins the discriminator:\nattach the hello fixture with default_cell_bytes deliberately\nnarrow (512), assert a 2 KB push succeeds on greet's `name`\nport (fed by data box `who`) and fails on greet's `salutation`\nport (literal only).         "type":"text",
        "text":"Done. The deferred half of 302 is closed; the phase-3 checklist item is checked off; 114 tests green under STRICT.\n\n### Onward to 317 — data-box JSON bridge\n\n317 is substantial. Quick orienting recap before we dive in:\n\n**What 317 promises:**\n- Every spec gets two new callbacks: `native_to_json` (lift the spec's native value into JSON text) and `json_to_native` (the inverse).\n- Data boxes gain optional `lang` + `ref` fields. With them set, the runner loads the file *via the spec*, gets a native value, and asks the spec to serialise it. Without them, the existing inline-`data` path applies unchanged.\n- The user's data file is idiomatic. A Lua data box is a Lua file that `return`s a table. A C data box is a C function that returns a struct. No SoraMech glue.\n\n**Per-spec work required:**\n- **Lua**: walk the value at a `lua_State` stack index, recurse into tables, emit JSON via `libs/json/json.c`'s writer. Handle the array-vs-object distinction (contiguous 1-indexed integer keys → array). Refuse functions, threads, userdata.\n- **Bash**: near-identity. The script already prints text; validate it parses as JSON.\n- **C**: depends on a type system. For step one, support scalars (`int`, `double`, `string`). Anything richer waits for 307's typed wrapper.\n\n**Order of attack I'd suggest:**\n1. Extend `lang_spec_t` with the new typedefs and document the native-handle contract per spec.\n2. Implement the Lua `native_to_json` and `json_to_native` first (most useful, most idiomatic).\n3. Implement Bash next (small, near-identity).\n4. Implement C scalars-only (depth-limit it; full struct support lives with 307).\n5. Extend the data-box dispatch path in `src/012-dispatch.c` to consult `lang` / `ref` when present and route through the spec.\n6. Build a `tests/maps/cross-lang-data/` fixture exercising the path end-to-end.\n\nReady to start? I'd open with the `lang_spec_t` extension (a small commit on its own — pure contract, no behavior change), then commit the Lua impl next. Sound right, or do you want a different starting wedge?"
      }],

{

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Yes — 317 is genuinely four-to-five distinct system pieces, each meaningful as a blueprint on its own. The sub-issue convention (per CLAUDE.md) names them `{PHASE}{ID}{INDEX}-{DESCR}`, so `317a-…`, `317b-…`, etc.\n\nProposed split:\n\n- **317a — spec contract** (the `lang_spec_t` extension). Pure design: the two typedefs (`lang_native_to_json_fn`, `lang_json_to_native_fn`), the native-handle shape documented per spec (Lua = stack index, C = typed pointer, Bash = text). Zero implementation. This is the foundation everything else builds on, and it's contained enough that a reader gets the whole concept from one file. It also flushes the question of whether the existing 312 fields should be repurposed or whether 317 introduces new typedefs.\n\n- **317b — Lua spec implementation.** The reference implementation. Walks values on `lua_State`, recurses tables, handles the array-vs-object distinction, refuses unserializable types (functions/userdata/threads). Drives whatever ambiguity remained in 317a's contract.\n\n- **317c — Bash + C spec implementations.** Bash's bridge is a near-identity (the script already produces text; validate-and-pass-through). C's bridge handles scalars (`int`, `double`, `string`, maybe `bytes`); rich struct support is explicitly deferred until 307's typed wrapper lands. Paired because each is small and they share the \"smaller spec, fewer types\" story.\n\n- **317d — data-box dispatch path.** The integration: when a data box has `lang` and `ref`, the runner loads the file via the spec, gets a native value, calls the spec's `native_to_json`, and emits the JSON bytes as the box's output. Plus the cross-language test fixture (`tests/maps/cross-lang-data/`) that exercises Lua data box → C consumer end-to-end.\n\nEach sub-issue stands as its own blueprint. Each commits independently in dependency order (a → b → c → d), and an outside reader can pick up any one without needing the others open.\n\nWant me to write the four sub-issue files? Or would you split it differently — maybe just two (contract + Lua together, then everything else)?"
      }],

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-19T18:03:47.073Z",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",

  "gitBranch":"master",
  "parentUuid":"a03fa827-918e-4316-b3a8-3384a5ecc214",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"585b6e65-7287-44e7-b133-8bdf3479a266",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "type":"assistant",
  "uuid":"3e413b1d-07bb-47f0-b970-56074e1b2d36",
  "requestId":"req_011CbCRDmpBfay2H1zCn79nU",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"307's promise is the same rule 317 enforces, just for *call* boxes instead of data boxes: **the box author writes idiomatic code in their language, and SoraMech adapts to it.**\n\n### What 307 is for\n\nToday a C-box author has to write a function with the SoraMech ABI:\n\n```c\nint my_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size) {\n    /* unpack bytes from inputs[i]/sizes[i] by hand,\n     * do the actual work,\n     * pack result back into out_buf,\n     * set *out_size */\n}\n```\n\nThat's project-specific boilerplate. The function can't be tested standalone, can't be linted by a normal C tool, can't be called by another non-SoraMech program. 307 wants the user to write what they'd write anyway:\n\n```c\nint classify(const char *text, int weight) {\n    if (text[0] >= '0' && text[0] <= '9') return weight * 1;\n    return weight * 2;\n}\n```\n\n…and declare the signature in the box JSON:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"classify\", \"lang\": \"c\", \"ref\": \"classify.c\", \"fn\": \"classify\",\n  \"inputs\":  [{\"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\"}, {\"name\": \"weight\", \"type\": \"int\"}],\n  \"returns\": \"int\" }\n```\n\nThe C spec then generates a wrapper `.c` next to the user's source, with a fixed entry point `sm_box_entry`. The wrapper unpacks bytes into typed C arguments per the JSON declaration, calls `classify(text, weight)`, serializes the return into the output buffer. The user's source stays pristine.\n\nThe same machinery unlocks **library functions as boxes**:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"compress\", \"lang\": \"c\", \"fn\": \"compress2\",\n  \"headers\": [\"<zlib.h>\"], \"link_libs\": [\"z\"],\n  \"inputs\":  [{\"name\": \"src\", \"type\": \"bytes\"}, {\"name\": \"level\", \"type\": \"int\"}],\n  \"returns\": \"bytes\" }\n```\n\nNo user `.c` file at all. The wrapper `#include`s `<zlib.h>`, calls `compress2`, the linker pulls in `libz` via `-lz`. Any C library with a header becomes a box.\n\n### What's already shipped under 307\n\nThe boring half: gcc invocation as the compile callback (`-shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall`), dlopen cache per worker, lazy `.c → .so` compile on first invoke, error reporting from gcc's stderr. Five tests cover compile + invoke + missing-symbol + bad-source.\n\n### What's deferred\n\nThe typed wrapper generation. That's the actual product feature. It's substantial:\n\n- A small type system maps JSON `\"type\"` strings to C types and a serialization rule each (`int` → 4 bytes little-endian, `string` → length-prefixed UTF-8 or null-terminated, `bytes` → length-prefixed raw, `double` → IEEE 754 8-byte). Each type has paired unpack/pack functions in a tiny runtime header.\n- A code generator (probably in `langs/c/wrapper-gen.c`) reads the box JSON's declared `inputs` and `returns`, emits a `.c` file declaring `extern` to the user's function and defining `sm_box_entry` that calls it.\n- The compile step orchestrates: emit wrapper, run gcc against `wrapper.c + user.c` with `-l<libname>` for any declared `link_libs`, produce one `.so`.\n\n### How 307 ties into 317\n\n317's C spec needs `native_to_json` for data boxes. To serialize an arbitrary native value, it needs to know its type — that type comes from the same JSON declaration 307's wrapper consumes. Once 307's type system exists, 317's C bridge reuses it: walk the typed struct, emit JSON per the type.\n\nUntil 307 lands, 317c handles only scalars (`int`/`double`/`string`/`bytes`). Rich C-struct data boxes wait for 307.\n\n### Effort estimate\n\n307 is two to three focused sessions: a half-day for the type system, a session for the code generator, a session for tests + the library-function path. Compares to maybe 4-5 sessions for 317 as a whole.\n\n### Whether 307 is critical-path\n\nIt's parallel. The phase-3 demo could ship with hand-written-ABI C boxes if needed (ugly but works). Most maps wouldn't have C boxes anyway. So 307 lives in the *quality-of-life* track unless a demo specifically wants idiomatic C authoring.\n\nWant me to also break 307 into sub-issues before we start 317? It naturally factors into **307a — type system + serialization runtime**, **307b — wrapper code generator**, **307c — library-function-as-box (no `ref`)**."
      }],

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-19T18:12:13.394Z",
